Count the living Village claims before picking a Katana target; the Yakuza killed the real Oracle the night after she guessed Grace's Diviner role correctly, so an Oracle who is still alive after a correct guess on a Yakuza is the first kill to make.

Check whether a Katana attack actually happened by its visit trail: a Lookout's single visitor on a victim is strong evidence, but the Diviner's own group shows only who was near the target, so do not treat group membership as a visit.

Fortune Teller numbers (for example 2 and 2) are only a consistency check: they count visited players and visitors without saying which is which. Use them to reject claims that imply more visits than the numbers allow, not to confirm a single named visit.

Publicly revealing or claiming a Yakuza-only role such as Diviner, or posting Yakuza-chat-style group results, is a near-certain tell. If you must reveal, do it only when a Good claimant would make the same claim, and never invent a result that a Village role could contradict.

Do not whip votes privately on a single unverified claim. Private messages are visible as trails and get quoted publicly; when the Village is split, make the case in public and ask for a second source before asking anyone to vote.

A player who self-nominates, votes Yes for themselves, and then argues for their own trial may be a Jester who wins by hanging. Before voting Guilty on that pattern, check whether the hang gives them a win, and weigh that more than the contradictions they are accused of.

Investigators who learn a true result should write it into their will, labelled as results. Bob's will carried his real Lookout watches after death and was the only visit evidence the Village could still use.

If your result confirms a Jester or Executioner, reveal it publicly before the nomination vote, or at the latest in your trial speech. Protecting your role is worth far less than stopping a hang that hands Neutrals a win and triggers revenge kills.
evidence: Carol knew Judy was the Jester after Night 1 but only voted Innocent with a vague 'a hanged Jester wins'. Judy was hanged 10-1. Dave won, and the revenge attacks killed Erin and Mallory, which put the Yakuza at half the table.

tip: Treat a player who self-nominates and asks for the rope as a probable Jester or Executioner target. Hanging them costs a Village life to revenge, and maybe two if an Executioner rides along. Hang only on a mechanical result. If you must hang, keep the Guilty side a bare majority so fewer Village are in the revenge pool.
evidence: Judy self-nominated on Day 1 and on trial said 'I'd rather hang on a fair read'. Ten players voted Guilty, and two random Guilty voters (Erin, Mallory) died to the Jester and Executioner revenge attacks.

tip: Count factions before every vote. Once Evil holds half the living votes, the Village can no longer pass nominations. Once Evil holds a majority, Evil can hang anyone. The Village must avoid losing numbers to wasted hangs before that point. Evil should press its advantage the moment the count allows.
evidence: On Day 3 (6 alive, 3 Yakuza) Heidi, Ivan and Grace voted No and Bob's nomination of Grace failed at 3 Yes, despite strong evidence. On Day 4 (5 alive) Grace nominated Frank and the Yakuza hanged him 3-2.

tip: When a Lookout's visit result and a Yakuza-only role claim both point at one player, the players who vote No in lockstep to protect them are the likeliest teammates. Name them publicly and record it in your will so the information outlives you.
evidence: Heidi and Ivan both voted No on Grace and kept repeating 'need a second source' after Grace had posted Diviner results. That pattern identified the whole Yakuza team, but nobody named the trio together.

tip: Never post results from a Yakuza-only role, and never flatly deny a visit a Lookout may have seen. Prepare a Village cover claim with a cover action in night chat. Only being at parity saved Grace here.
evidence: Grace published her Diviner groups on Day 3 and then denied visiting Alice, whom Bob's Lookout had watched. Frank and Carol immediately read her as Yakuza, and Carol's Night 3 Oracle guess confirmed it.

tip: Open with a mild, friendly private message to your target, then let them make themselves suspicious. Build the case on their own odd plays rather than inventing claims. Nominate when the room is already irritated with them.
evidence: Dave PM'd Judy on Day 1, absorbed the early heat calmly, then nominated Judy on Day 2 over her unexplained PMs and self-nomination. The nomination passed 10-1 and he won.

tip: Don't claim an information role on Day 1 just because someone demands results. Claim when you have a result that does work, ideally one that catches someone. An early claim with no payoff just marks you as the Katana target.
evidence: Alice claimed Scout on Day 1 when Mallory pressed her, posted an uninformative Night 1 result, and was the Yakuza's first kill on Night 2, explicitly 'because she's the live Scout'.

tip: A group result centred on one player does not show who visited whom; spend a map token on a player outside the suspected trio early, before the group is used as a case, because the trio alone cannot separate the holder from a visitor.

Yakuza with a visible Katana holder should avoid reusing the same holder and public-facing targets night after night, since a Cartographer or Fortune Teller can triangulate the holder from repeated visit patterns.

When a claimant posts numbers or results, ask for the night-numbered details immediately and treat repeated dodging as a read, not a result; judge trials on concrete contradictions and votes, not on who pushed the case loudest.

Keep an explicit tally of who has been attacked by which role; an Arsonist dousing many players and igniting at once can kill several living Village in a single night, so a late-game doused list should be checked against deaths.
A Fortune Teller's two numbers do not reveal visits by the Fortune Teller; check whether a claimant's numbers are compatible with the public deaths before relying on them to convict or clear anyone.

Before a kill, check whether the target's death would actually be a useful signal. Here Yakuza killed Carol, Erin, Alice, Ivan and Grace, and each death removed information but left the Arsonist free to finish the team; keep a fallback plan for a second killer.

Claimed-role stories that generate testable counts (Accountant totals, Fortune Teller numbers, Cartographer groups) are risky. Only fake a count you can keep consistent across nights, because public players will check every number against the visit record.

Refuted or retracted accusations (Mallory's Judy claim, Dave's Ivan visit claim) were the main drivers of hangs. Before a Guilty vote, ask whether the key premise has been retracted, and do not let a dead player's PM steer your vote.

A Katana holder who kills a claimant and a teammate's Arsonist ignite can make the Yakuza look dead while one team member survives. Track which kills were Katana and which were Arsonist, since the win condition only counts living players.

Keep public and night-chat stories consistent across days. Repeated refusals to answer a plain yes/no question became the central case against Bob, so give a short true-or-false answer that you can defend, rather than a dodge.

Guessing a role as an Oracle is a one-shot Astral Visit with a yes/no answer; a Village power role should only guess when the guess would be a useful test, since a dead Oracle's will is public and the Yakuza can read it.

With a Katana holder and an Arsonist both alive, the Yakuza should not cover for the Arsonist's kills; Heidi's Arsonist ignited with three dousers and killed three at once, so Yakuza should track which living player is doused before choosing a night target.
A Cartographer group only shows links, not who visited whom; a player who must answer a plain visit question but dodges is a lead, not a mechanical contradiction, so hang only on checkable results.
Claimed roles that die to the Katana on their first night are common; before trusting any claim, ask the claimant for a night-numbered result that a Yakuza could not have forged.
A Fortune Teller's pair counts alone cannot be checked against the visits you can see; ask for the whole pair and the visit they imply rather than accepting or rejecting a bare number.

A Cartographer or Scout group is an undirected link, not a visit record. A trio centred on a player is consistent with many visit patterns, so test a link with a result from outside the group before hanging anyone on it.

Track which claimants the Katana and Arsonist kill each night. When the kills hit the players who asked the sharpest questions, treat the killer's targets as a lead to check against the claims and night results.

Do not cast a lone Guilty vote on a dodge. Once you find you have no concrete contradiction, retract early; my unsupported Guilty vote on Bob cost me credibility and later made me the easiest trial target.

For each unverified numbers claim, write down every visit pattern that fits it and ask the claimant to name the one they assume. A claim that fits all patterns settles nothing, and one that fits none is a real contradiction.
Keep repeated no-news posts to one short line. Long echo messages spend budget you need for the trial turn, where your defense and last word matter most.
A zero-token result from a player who plausibly holds no tokens (Vanilla, Sheriff, Tracker) tells you nothing. Audit players whose roles really hold tokens, since a zero there is a real lead.
Publicly claiming a power role on Day 2 made me the Katana's target that same night. Claim only when the result is useful right away, and expect a live Yakuza holder to target the claimant.
A Cartographer or Scout link means only that two players touched. Your own visit links you too, so before accusing a group member, check whether your own action or a teammate's explains the link.
A Neutral Arsonist can win after the Yakuza die. Track who was doused and who the ignition hit, and do not treat a Neutral as cleared because the Katana is still with the Yakuza.

Use swaps on the night a threat is known, not at the end. Both of Frank's swap tokens died unused, but a swap can move an Arsonist's douse or a Katana hit onto a planned partner. Agree the swap in night chat before the threat lands.

Don't nominate or vote Guilty on the same non-teammate as your teammates on consecutive Days. Frank's Day 4 nomination of Ivan, with Bob and Judy voting Guilty, made a visible bloc. Split the nominators and vary the Guilty votes, or let a Village player carry the case.

Don't leave the Katana on one holder all game. Bob held it Nights 1 to 5, and Alice's Erin map plus elimination pointed at him. Move it to a low-link member on any night a map, visit or count could expose the holder.

Visit-count numbers and group sizes give totals, not identities. Before a Guilty vote, ask the claimant to name the specific visitors and targets behind the numbers. A pair like 2,2 is explained only by named visits, and a refusal to name them is a lead, not a contradiction.

Check each night's deaths against the known Katana attack. A death with no Katana attack means a second killer exists, such as an Arsonist's ignite that kills every doused player at once. Look for that third killer before hanging anyone.
Use shots early on a mechanical or claim-conflict lead. I held 3 tokens, never fired, and was killed by the Katana on Night 5, so unused tokens were wasted.
Claimants were Katana targets every night (Carol, Erin, Alice, Ivan). Claim only when the claim is backed by posted, night-numbered results, and write results into your will in case you die.
Group and map results (Cartographer, Surveyor, Diviner) show links, not visits. Before treating a link as a kill record, get a second independent result, or the trio can stall the whole Day.
A refusal to answer a plain yes/no is not a contradiction. Hanging on dodges and retracted claims (Bob, Dave) cost Village players, so vote on a named mechanical result.
If several players die on one night with no Katana explanation, suspect an Arsonist ignite (an Astral Visit, so it leaves no visit trail) and keep Arsonists alive in the suspect pool.

Douse quietly on separate nights and ignite (Astral Visit) once 3 or more living players are doused. One ignite kills every doused player at once, and the douses stay hidden until then. Here Frank, Ivan and Judy all died on one night.

A Cartographer or group result is an undirected link, so a trio like Bob, Dave and Erin only shows that someone in it touched someone else. Test the link with a result on a player outside the trio before treating it as a visit record.

Require one named mechanical contradiction before any Guilty vote. Trials on Bob and Ivan went Innocent when the Guilty case rested on a dodge or an unanswered question, and the case-makers were later exposed.
With two players alive, a trial needs both votes Guilty and a nomination needs both Yes. A lone accuser can never hang anyone, so the other player's own vote decides the endgame. Plan around that.

Do not answer a plain yes or no question about a night visit with 'I won't post my choices'. Bob's refusal to answer the Erin visit question for days became the town's main case, and it got him hanged on Day 6.
Post your two numbers with their night number as soon as each night resolves. Withholding them for three Days made the claim look fake, and the Yakuza used that case to kill you on Night 4.

A Cartographer or Surveyor group is an undirected, centred cluster. A trio of links shows that someone in it touched someone else, not who holds the Katana. Ask for a test on a player outside the group before anyone is nominated on it.

Ask for one concrete contradiction before a Guilty vote, and retract publicly when the case you voted on is refuted. The Day 5 Dave trial and the Day 6 Bob trial both rested on claims that were later shown to be weak.
Several players repeated No nomination from me every round, which spent budget on nothing. Use one short line per round and save budget for the question that could decide a trial.

When both a Katana holder and an Arsonist are alive, expect stacked Night deaths and do not assume every death is from the same faction. Track who has been visited by which known kill, and keep unverified survivors in the suspect pool.

A rig is a one-shot token, so plan its Day in advance and spend it before death. I held mine unspent to the end and it died with me; a rig on a Day when the Village nominates a teammate-safe target would have forced an execution.

A Katana victim's Cartographer group always contains the holder, since the holder visited that victim. If a Cartographer or Tracker is alive, kill them first or move the Katana the same night, before their map points at the holder.

Arsonist ignite is an Astral Visit that kills every doused player at once, and doused players aren't told. A night with several deaths and no Katana on a doused player can mean a dousing role. Keep a running list of doused names in your notes.

With five or fewer alive, a lone Guilty vote or a self-nomination built on a group link is a read, not a contradiction. Name the concrete mechanical contradiction before a hang, or the Village can burn its own players while a neutral or Yakuza survives.
Repeating 'no nomination until a result' every round spends budget without adding information. Spend budget on a named target, a numbered result, or a concrete test instead.

A Cartographer group, Surveyor group or Diviner group is only a neighbourhood or a set of links. It shows that someone in it touched someone else, not who visited whom. Don't convict a player on a group alone; ask for a visit-based result or a second, independent check.

Before nominating someone on another player's claim, check that claim against the public record. Mallory nominated Bob on a Judy-visit claim that was never posted, and had to retract it after the trial. Verify the record before the nomination, not after.

Once an Arsonist may have several doused players, an ignite can kill them all in one night. Village should spend its hangs or shots on the likely Arsonist before the douse count reaches three, not after, since the ignite removes the doused players and the Village's voice with them.

When only two players are alive and a nomination needs both Yes votes, the trial can't convict unless the other player votes Guilty on themselves. Once it's clear that the last two can't reach a majority, stop spending speech on nominations and focus on checking which living player holds the Arsonist or Katana.

Protect the player most likely to be the Katana's next target, and alternate targets rather than repeating the same protection; my Judy protections on N2 and N4 were predictable and the Yakuza simply attacked her anyway, so the Katana holder kept choosing targets I was not protecting.

Track which claims are verified by independent checks. A count from an audit corroborated by a Lookout watch is stronger than an unsourced visit list; before voting, separate each claim into verified, self-reported, and unsourced.

Yakuza who vote together each night leave a clear pattern of Katana targets; a Village player can map a holder's attacks against Lookout and Tracker results, so vary the kill timing and avoid a target the Village already has a lead on.

Do not make a nomination or Guilty vote built on a token count alone or on a retracted visit list; a flipped role claim after a nomination is weak evidence in either direction, so ask for an actual visit or result.

Check the token rules before drawing conclusions: Clerk, Smuggler and Vanilla Villager tokens differ, and a Philanthropist gift can make a role's count look wrong, so verify whether the claimed role can hold that many tokens.

Spend the single archive token only when the 7-of-10 role list can be cross-checked; I spent it on Night 1 and then could not test the list, so my claim was just a number with no way to be challenged. Hold it until a second source can confirm or refute a listed role.

Build a claim-by-claim table early (claimed role, tokens, checkable results, who visited whom) and mark each claim as verified, contradicted or unverifiable. Discussion stalled for days because players argued about slot math from a single unverifiable source instead of testing claims against night results.

Do not nominate yourself after saying no nomination; the self-nomination became the Yakuza's stated reason to kill me and made my claim look unstable. If you change your stance, say so explicitly before acting, and avoid any public line that a later action can contradict.

Target the claimant whose slot math points at your teammates. The Katana kill on the Archivist removed the only source that could have exposed the Grunt/VV split, so kill the player whose list threatens the team rather than the one with the most obvious claim.

When a claim is flipped after a nomination, weigh it as a lie-or-mistake question: ask for the concrete action behind it rather than whether the flip was 'under pressure'. Both Clerk and Smuggler flips were treated as proof of guilt by some and as honest corrections by others, and this split the Village vote for days.

Before the Katana attacks a Medic-protected target, count protections: a Standard Katana fails against Standard Defense, so pick targets the Medic has not protected or switch to a Strong-capable plan.
Keep the Katana holder and target agreed in night chat, but avoid repeating the same holder-target pattern each night; the town tracks Katana visits from attack notices and Lookout watches.
Claim the lowest-risk role that explains your no-action record, and state it before any audit can contradict it; flipping roles after a nomination looks like a cover and got Carol and Mallory hanged.
Verify a visit-list claim against who could actually see it: a Medic sees only her own protection, so a full Night visit list from a Medic is a red flag worth pressing early.

Hang on a token count only when the count's role is reachable; Yakuza-only roles like Clerk and Smuggler make a count a strong claim check, but a flip after nomination should be treated as weak evidence.

Don't spend alert tokens on nights with no reason to expect a visit. My three empty alerts on N1-N3 gave no information and left no alert for N4-N5, when the Katana holder visited the Lookout and then the Accountant. Save at least one alert for the night after a power role is publicly exposed or after a Katana hit shows the holder is active.

A claimed role that cannot hold a count is a hard contradiction. A Vanilla Villager with a token audit, or a Medic whose tokens don't fit her protections, falsifies the claim. Check audits against each role's token kind before debating motives or slot math.

Corroborate visit claims with an independent source. A Lookout watch that sees exactly one visitor on a target backs up an Accountant or Medic visit. Discount visit lists from anyone who cannot see them, such as a Medic listing other players' visits, until their source is shown.

The Yakuza attacked claimants in a row (Fortune Teller, Archivist, Lookout, Accountant), so each Katana victim's visitors form a short suspect list. Ask who visited each victim, and protect the most useful claimant at the next night.

A role change made only after a nomination (Vanilla Villager to Clerk, then Smuggler) is weak evidence, but it is still testable. Treat the new claim by its token counts and visit records, and vote on those rather than on how the flip was made.

Before a teammate makes a public claim, check it against any token audit or visit list it implies. If a teammate's claim conflicts with an audit, agree a single cover story at night and a consistent vote line, rather than letting them flip alone under nomination pressure.

A Vanilla Villager claim is easily contradicted by any living Accountant's token count, since VV holds no tokens. When an Accountant may be alive, prefer a claim whose token count you can actually keep, or avoid a public claim that a token audit can check.
Avoid a Yes-then-Innocent pattern on the same teammate or a doomed player. The town reads that pattern as shielding, and it becomes the case against you after the teammate is hanged.

Rotate Katana targets instead of retrying one that a Medic is likely protecting. Confirm whether a Veteran is on alert and whether a Medic or Lookout has already been seen acting on the target before sending the holder out.

Cross-check token audits against roles that hold tokens. Vanilla Villager has no tokens, so a nonzero audit on a self-claimed VV is a near-proof contradiction. A Yakuza-only role claimed after a nomination should be weighed as a flip, not as a clean claim.

applies_to: Accountant, Lookout, Sheriff and other investigators
tip: Post each night result on the same Day it arrives, with names, instead of holding it for a later turn. Yakuza killed the Accountant the night after an audit, so an unposted result died with the player. Put the newest result in the first public message of the Day and in the will at each Day start.

A role claim that flips to a Yakuza-only role (Clerk, Smuggler) right after a nomination, after an earlier Village claim, is a strong Yakuza tell. A clean no-action record doesn't clear someone who flipped under pressure, because a Yakuza with no visits looks the same as a Village player with no visits.

Ask for the source of any visit list before trusting it. A Medic only sees her own protection, so a Medic who lists everyone's night visits is either guessing or has an information source the table should know about. Retractions after a nomination don't undo a push built on that list.

When the Katana kills a claimant, cross-check that player's last will against the public record. Yakuza used the Katana on each active claimant in turn, so the dead claimants' wills and claims are the main evidence left and should be checked as data, not accepted as proof.

When a count contradicts a claim, such as a Vanilla Villager showing tokens, name the exact count and the claim it breaks in the public log before the vote. Players who are Evil will call it a Philanthropist or a mistake, so settle that possibility with a second source before voting Guilty.

Separate what a claim predicts from what it proves: an audit or watch result only checks a claimant's token count or visit, so chase the one check that can actually refute a claim (e.g. Alice's visit list was unsourced, which I should have forced into the open on Day 3 rather than arguing about slot math).

Demand a source for any full-table information (archive slots, visit lists, numbers) before using it to nominate; a Bob-style slot-math argument that only its author can see is worth nothing until someone else can verify it.

Don't adopt the lead's case by reflex. On Day 4 and 5 the trials were run on a token count and the nominator's own record, and Yakuza-only role claims (Clerk, Smuggler) were accepted as proof of guilt when they were only consistent with the count; a flipped claim is not a visit.

Track which votes on a single trial were Yes-then-Innocent or No-then-Guilty across days; after a Yakuza flip, the players who shielded the flipped teammate (Innocent on the trial, No on the next nomination) are the strongest leads, and I should have pressed that pattern sooner.

Once the Katana holder is confirmed visiting a target every night, a Medic who self-protects or protects the same likely target repeatedly is predictable; rotate protection and share the target publicly only after it is no longer useful.

applies_to: investigators (Fortune Teller, Sheriff, Seer, Lookout, Archivist)
tip: Once you claim an information role, the Katana holder can target you the same night, and Heidi died that way the night after posting numbers. Before posting results publicly, get a Medic or other protection line, or at least make the claim when it helps the town more than it helps the Yakuza.

A claim that describes other players' visits (for example, a Medic listing every Night 1 visit) can't come from the claimant's own role. Ask for the source before using it, and weigh only claims that match what the role can actually see.

A claimed role flip after a nomination is not an action. Ask each accused player to name the visible action behind their vote or role, and wait for an independent result that corroborates the accusation before hanging.

Slot math on an archive only proves a listed role is taken once a holder claims it. Roles can repeat, so an unclaimed listed role is not evidence that a particular player is hiding it, and it shouldn't be used alone to nominate someone.

Before voting on a claimed role, check whether the claimed role even fits the public information (e.g. a Vanilla Villager cannot hold tokens); a single corroborated audit that contradicts a claim is stronger than a long slot-math argument built on an unverifiable archive.

Ask every claimant for the source of their information early; a Medic who lists other players' night visits is revealing that the list came from a claim, not from observation, and that should be flagged immediately rather than after several days.

Do not let a single teammate's stance decide the Katana holder vote without checking that they will still be alive and unblocked; a holder who is a visible Village-claimant (Dave on alert) was kept off-limits and the team lost tempo around them.

When your own vote flips between nomination and trial, say so explicitly and give the visible reason; unexplained flips were the main reason the town could not separate the Yakuza from honest players in the late game.

A Lookout watch that shows a single other visitor to the same victim as a known Katana attack is a strong lead; combine Lookout results with Medic protection and Veteran alert counts before any vote rather than voting on a claim count alone.

Watching a player who is later Katana-attacked or hanged gives you a visitor list you can check against deaths; repeated watches on the same Yakuza-adjacent claimants (Carol, Mallory, Erin) produced the only corroborated visits, so log every watch target and visitor result in your will as you go.

Treat a nominee's public claim flip made only after their nomination as weak evidence; check the audit or watch that contradicts the claim first, because multiple Yakuza-only claims (Clerk, Smuggler) fit token counts and cannot be disproved by a flip alone.

Ask a claimant for their night target and result early and in public, and punish silence or late retractions; the Yakuza here kept their Katana holder unseen by dodging these questions, so any player who refuses a direct check should count as a suspect.

A Katana kill with Standard Defense protection fails, so a protected Lookout surviving a Katana attack is strong evidence for a Medic claim; use survival-versus-protection pairs as checkable facts rather than debating claims.

Before voting for an elimination that removes the last checkable Yakuza-linked suspect, confirm which living players can still break a tie; hanging Mallory and Carol left a small Village pool where Erin's Innocent votes became the only dissent and the Yakuza survived to the end.

Never let the Katana holder or the team's attack target sit on an unresolved visit list; before choosing a Katana target, check whether any living Medic or Veteran could protect or punish that target and avoid predictable repeats (the team attacked the same protected Lookout twice in a row).

Do not pick a flip-prone Village-claim cover (e.g. Vanilla Villager on Day 1) when your team already has a visible, checkable token or visit record; a claim that the audit contradicts forces a flip under pressure, which is what got the Clerk and Smuggler hanged.

Audit and watch results that corroborate each other (e.g. Lookout watch plus Accountant audit on the same visit) are strong evidence; look at who pushed the hang on the earliest unverified claim before accepting a trial built on a single count.
A token count of 1 or 2 can be explained by several roles (Clerk, Seer, Smuggler, Philanthropist gifts); check which role claims match the full count before calling a flip a lie.
Keep the Katana holder and target agreement written in night chat with explicit reply-agree lines, and avoid having a teammate speak publicly about team-relevant claims on the same Day.

Combine a visit-group map with confirmed or credible no-action claims. If the victim's group holds only the victim, a Vanilla and one other player, and the victim's own visit explains the Vanilla's link, the other player is the Katana holder. Act on it the same Day; don't wait for a 'perfect' contradiction.
evidence: Alice's N2 map showed Bob, Dave and Erin. Erin audited Dave, and Bob was the holder. Mallory, Ivan and Alice all spelled this out, yet Bob was acquitted 1 to 7 on Day 4 and went on to kill Ivan and Grace.

tip: Reconcile visit counts nightly against the known visits. A recurring extra visit pair that no living claimant explains points to a hidden actor such as an Arsonist dousing or a Neutral killer. Treat it as a lead, not as proof the counter is lying.
evidence: Alice's sizes showed a 2-player group every night, and Ivan's N3 numbers were 2,2. Both came from Heidi dousing Frank, Ivan and Judy. Instead, Judy, Frank and Bob called Ivan's numbers 'unsupported' and nominated him.

tip: A strong mechanical case plus a suspect's refusal to answer a yes/no about their own visit is enough to vote Guilty. Don't let 'a dodge isn't a contradiction' become a shield. Never pad a case with a fact you haven't checked: one false detail lets the defense discredit the whole push.
evidence: Mallory wrongly said Judy had reported Bob visiting Alice. Grace caught it, and the Day 4 trial collapsed with only Dave voting Guilty, although Bob refused to answer about Erin all game.

tip: Use one-shot tokens while the team is alive and a vote can be swung. A Clerk rig on a Day when the town is already willing to nominate a power role turns the nomination into an execution. Swaps and early puppets can also shield the holder.
evidence: Ivan's Day 4 nomination passed 7 to 1, so a rig would have executed the Fortune Teller. Judy and Frank died to the ignite with Clerk and Smuggler tokens unused, and Bob's puppet came only on Day 6, when it couldn't change Heidi's vote.

tip: Douse quietly, stay non-committal in the daytime, and ignite once three or more players are doused. Then vote with whichever side keeps you alive into a one-on-one endgame. Hang the last Yakuza rather than a Villager who can't kill you.
evidence: Heidi ignited on N4, killing Frank, Ivan and Judy (two of them Yakuza). She helped hang Dave on Day 5, voted Guilty on Bob on Day 6 although her puppeted messages argued Innocent, then ignited Mallory to win.

tip: A credible map or visit result that narrows the holder to one suspect is a mechanical lead. Shoot that player rather than sitting on all your tokens. Village power unused by the endgame is wasted.
evidence: Grace held 3 Vigilante tokens and never fired, although Alice's map pointed at Bob from Day 3. She was killed on N5 having done nothing, after helping hang the Vanilla Dave.

tip: Post your results promptly and in full once you've claimed or been called out. Hinting at results you won't share draws suspicion and wastes a Day. Put exact targets in your will, such as whom you audited, so your death resolves links.
evidence: Ivan stalled for most of Day 4 and was nominated 7 to 1. Erin's will only said she would do 'a token-count check on one player', without naming Dave, which left Bob room to argue that Erin's audit might explain his own link.

tip: At low counts, map out which pairings can still win before you hang. With 5 alive, including a likely holder and a hidden killer, hanging a Villager loses outright. Hang the best-evidenced suspect, not the player whose arguments were weakest.
evidence: On Day 5 Bob, Grace and Heidi hanged Dave, a true Vanilla, partly on Heidi's false 'I know I'm not the holder' slip, which Mallory showed any player can say. The remaining 3 (Bob, Heidi, Mallory) could no longer produce a Village win.

applies_to: Yakuza with token roles (Clerk, Smuggler, Ritualist, Mortician, etc.)
tip: Once an Accountant (or any token-counting role) has claimed and is auditing, never fake-claim a tokenless role like Vanilla Villager. Either claim a Village role with a matching token count that no one can contradict, or make killing the Accountant the team's top priority.
evidence: Frank claimed Accountant on Day 2, yet Mallory claimed VV on Day 3 and Carol claimed VV on Day 3. Frank's audits found 1 token on Mallory (N3) and 2 on Carol (N4); both were hanged the next Day. Carol named Frank only as a 'fallback' target, and he wasn't killed until Night 5.

tip: Use limited tokens while the user is alive and the game is still contested. A Smuggler swap can redirect an Accountant's audit or a Lookout's watch, or send a Katana attack past a protector. A Clerk rig can hang a key investigator. A dead Yakuza's unused tokens are pure waste.
evidence: Carol died with 2 unused swap tokens and Mallory with an unused rig. Both said they were holding tokens 'for a Day we need it', and that Day never came before they were hanged.

tip: When a teammate's hang is already certain, vote Yes and Guilty with the town and keep your record clean. A lone Innocent or No vote saves no one and becomes the main case against you once the teammate flips Evil.
evidence: Erin voted Innocent on Mallory (lost 7-2) and No on Carol's nomination (passed 6-2). Every Guilty speech against Erin on Day 6 cited those two votes. Carol bused Mallory with a Guilty vote, so her own exposure came only from the audit.

tip: Don't announce which nights you'll alert. Publicly naming an alert night just tells the Katana to go elsewhere. Stay silent, or vaguely suggest you might alert, so attackers hesitate on every night instead of skipping only the announced one.
evidence: Dave said on Day 3 'I'll go on alert on Night 3 with my last token.' The Yakuza night chat explicitly ruled Dave out, and all three of his alerts drew zero visits.

tip: Check claims mechanically. Audit Vanilla Villager claimants and players who haven't claimed, since a token count that contradicts a claim is near-proof. Have a Lookout corroborate the auditor's visit so the town trusts the count.
evidence: Frank audited the late VV claimants Mallory and Carol, and Judy's N3 watch on Mallory independently saw Frank visit. Several players cited that corroboration when voting Guilty, and both hangs landed on Evil players.

tip: Keep protecting the most valuable confirmed investigator, especially one whose results have just hurt the Yakuza. A repeated protection is fine when that player is clearly the top Katana target.
evidence: Alice protected Judy on N2 and again on N4. On N4 the Yakuza attacked Judy and the Standard protection stopped the Katana. Judy survived to watch Erin on N5 and to nominate Erin on Day 6.

tip: Speak precisely. Never present inferred information as something your role observed, and never let a wording slip contradict your own claim. Slips get read as tells, and they discredit even correct information you share.
evidence: Alice's 'full Night 1 visit list' had to be retracted and dogged her for days. Bob's self-nomination right after saying 'no nomination' let Yakuza dismiss his correct slot math. Erin's 'Grunt-claim withheld' became the opening line of the nomination that hanged her.

tip: A Medic who publicly claims and protects one predictable target each night only forces the Katana to pick someone else. Rotate protections, keep Strong tokens for the likeliest holder target, and self-protect when the Katana's pattern points at you.

Do not trial a power role whose claim is corroborated by independent deaths unless a concrete contradiction exists. Hanging the only lethal night check (the Veteran) removed the Village's one test of visits, and the Yakuza benefited directly.
Track who stays silent on their role for several Days, then votes with the nominator. Co-nominations, joint Guilty votes and silence on role claims form a bloc to check against Katana kill patterns.

applies_to: Investigators (Lookout, Sheriff, Tracker, Fortune Teller, Accountant)
tip: Claiming a role publicly on Day 2 made Judy and Frank the next night's targets. Hold the target and details until a second check exists, and post results only once they are needed to resolve a claim.

applies_to: Archivist and any investigator with a sampled census
tip: A 7-of-10 census is a sample, so a role missing from it proves nothing about the players who were not drawn. Post the census as a list of possibilities, not as elimination, and do not let it carry a lean on one player.

The Katana killed the investigators who posted specific accusations or targets (Judy after her watch claim, Bob after his census lean). Share results plainly but keep any lean or nightly target out of public posts until the case is strong, so the Katana has less to aim at.

When a player's vague slip ('the Grunt it lists is me') draws a plain-answer demand, count their answer against their votes and night role. A plain 'Vanilla' costs a Yakuza nothing, so a slip alone should not carry a nomination. Require a vote-behaviour or mechanical contradiction before a trial.

Publicly announcing protections and alert counts tells the Yakuza which targets are safe and which visits are lethal. Keep tonight's protection secret; the Katana never visited the publicly alert Veteran, which made his alert a known blind spot the Yakuza could route around.

Before calling any visit count wrong, check whether the Lookout's own visit is excluded and whether a visit was a Katana strike or a role action. Most of the apparent 'open' visits in this game came from counting visits incorrectly rather than from missing information.

Rotate the Katana holder before the holder becomes the town's obvious suspect. Erin held it every night and her Grunt slip stayed open for five Days, which made the Katana trail easy to follow. Move the Katana to a less-exposed member once a slip or a repeated link appears.
When a teammate makes a visible slip about their role, have them give a plain answer at once in the Day, with a cover explanation ready. Leaving it unanswered let Village treat it as a standing lead.

Keep a swap for the night a Medic protects the Katana target. Swapping the protected player with a non-protected one moves the protection onto the other player, so the Katana can land. Plan this before the night, not after a failed attack.

Do not nominate on a soft read. A failed nomination from a teammate publicly marks them as active and gives the town a count of who wants whom gone. Let Village nominate and vote, and vote with them on evidence.

Alert only hits players who visit you, so a Yakuza team that learns your alert nights can simply stop visiting you. Announcing your alert plan in advance makes those nights predictable. Vary your timing, and hold the claim until a second source (a Medic protection or a Fortune Teller count) can corroborate it.

Do not cast a Yes on a nomination you would not defend at trial. My Day 3 Yes on Erin's slip-only nomination became the read-vote mismatch the Village used to hang me on Day 6. Before voting Yes, ask whether that vote will be quoted back at you.

When count claims (Fortune Teller, Accountant, Archivist, alert counts) start to close, list the remaining unexplained visits and assign each to a named player. Then ask each silent player for a yes or no on their role by a fixed day, and vote on that answer, not on an earlier slip or on silence.

A Standard Katana cannot beat Standard Defense, so Standard protections and alerts stop it. Check each target's Defense before submitting, and do not repeat a target that already failed without new information. Keep one holder steady only while the Village cannot tie that holder to a visible incident.

A teammate's wording slip (such as claiming a census role) becomes the Village's main case within a day. Correct it in your first public turn with a plain statement, and do not let it sit while claims pile up around it.

applies_to: Grunt or any Yakuza who makes a public slip
tip: When you misspeak about your role (e.g. saying a census Grunt 'is me'), retract it plainly and fully the same day. A vague 'wording slip' left a standing contradiction that a teammate later used to nominate you and gave the town a focal point.
Kill the information roles (Lookout, Fortune Teller, Archivist) early, before their counts can be cross-checked. Their deaths left the town with unverifiable claims and a Veteran it could not test.

A Standard Katana cannot beat a Standard-defended or Veteran-alert target. Do not visit a living Veteran on alert; let the town trial them, using their own votes, while the team stays out of their visit count.

Count the trial majority before each vote. With five alive, three Yakuza voting Guilty together is a majority, so a unified Guilty bloc on a power-role claimant decides the trial without needing Village votes.

Submit identical night votes on holder and target every night, and keep all team planning in night chat. No daytime private messages were sent, so no PM trail existed for the town to build a case from.

Audit a player who has publicly claimed a token role (or is the most suspicious silent player) early, because a token count of 0 or an unexpected count is the only hard data an Accountant gets, and I spent my N1 audit on the Grunt-slip suspect who had 0 tokens while my N2 audit on Dave confirmed the Veteran's 2 remaining tokens. Use the audit to test claims, not to confirm a player the town already trusts.

Count visits against every posted claim before voting: a Fortune Teller's two numbers only reconcile if each visit is attributed to a named actor, and a Lookout's watch target adds a visited name. Write the reconciliation in your notepad as a table; the Yakuza's kill pattern (Judy, Heidi, Bob, Grace, Ivan) followed the info-role claimants and the most active Village pushers, so a player who keeps pushing silence-based nominations while holding no role is a lead.

Do not let a single unverifiable lethal power role (here a Veteran) be hanged on a read-vote mismatch alone; the Yakuza used the Day 6 trial to remove the one player who could punish visits, and the Guilty bloc was Yakuza plus Mallory and Carol. When a trial bloc votes together and cites the same weak point, ask who gains if the claimant dies before voting.

A Grunt or silent Village-looking player who slips a role-specific phrase and then recants is fine, but the team should avoid nominating a silent, low-claim player like Grace or Ivan on a 'no role posted' pattern when the nomination itself is the tell; the Day 3 slip-only nomination by Carol was the clearest Yakuza-leaning action in the record.

The Veteran's alert kill reveals the visitor's role only through the visit count, not the identity; a visitor who dies to an alert that the Veteran reports publicly is still hidden from the town, so count each kill against the other claims rather than trusting the Veteran's word on who visited.

Build a visit-count ledger each night (who visited whom, from every reported result) and check it against Fortune Teller and Heidi-style counts before trusting any claim; the count closed only because someone named every visitor.

Do not let a single silent or slip-based nomination pass; a trial on a lethal night power (Veteran) should require a checkable contradiction, because hanging the only Village killer removes the one player who could punish Yakuza visits.
A Veteran's alert kills show who visited the Veteran, so once a Veteran is credible, keep them alive and use their public alert counts as the best check on which living players are Katana holders.

Expect Village to read silent players as suspicious; a Yakuza who stays quiet while pushing trials on others is exposed by vote patterns, so spread Guilty votes so teammates are not the only ones pushing.
Keep the Katana holder unnamed and rotate who holds it; the same holder across several nights with the same target made the Yakuza's pattern easy for the Village to see.

Post your two numbers with the exact night they cover and list the visits you can account for; the 3/3 and 4/4 counts were checkable against claims, but I never reconciled the unexplained visit before dying, so spell out which visits are still open each morning.

Treat a lethal Veteran or Strong-alert claim as a claim about visitors, not a verified fact: two alert kills corroborated only by the same self-reporting player leave the Veteran untestable, and a trial on him should rest on a concrete contradiction rather than the town's inability to check him.

Don't let a single unexplained slip (like Erin's Grunt line) drive a nomination; when one player pushes a case that fails and then leaves a living silent player, check who benefits from the lynch of the remaining power role before voting Guilty.

Before a trial, ask every voter to name one concrete contradiction; a Guilty majority built on a Veteran who can't be checked tends to remove the only lethal night power, which the Yakuza benefit from.

When the Katana holder is protected by a Standard-level Medic, a Standard Katana fails; plan targets so the holder's attack beats likely protection, and avoid predictable rotation of targets across nights.

With 5 alive and 3 Yakuza, any 3-vote trial belongs to the Yakuza. Before voting Guilty on a player with a lethal or unverifiable power token, count whether the Guilty bloc is the Yakuza bloc. Hanging Dave removed the only lethal check, and Village had no way to stop the Yakuza choosing the next trial.

A player who names a Yakuza role on a census and then retracts it as a wording slip is a lead to settle by a plain yes or no before the next votes, not to accept. The unresolved slip let the Yakuza keep cover for four Days.

Treat the Archivist census and token counts as exact arithmetic: after each claim, list which unclaimed roles remain alive, then ask each unclaimed player for one concrete role statement. Vague denials of a role ate Days 2 to 4.

The Katana holder is hidden, but Yakuza votes are not: the bloc voted identically on holder, target and action every night. Track which players always vote the same way on Katana actions and on trials. That co-voting is a stronger tell than speeches.

Repeating 'no nomination without a mechanical lead' across dozens of messages added nothing and burned budget. Spend budget on one specific question to one named player, with a stated consequence, so the answer is visible and checkable.

A Lookout's watch only shows visits to the target; your own visit is excluded. Watch the player the Katana is most likely to hit next (an active info role), not a random name, because the watch result is lost when you die that night.
Count visits per night against Fortune Teller numbers and each claimed action; an unexplained visit slot (like Judy's N2 watch target) is a concrete lead that a Yakuza may be hiding behind a claim.

Do not let a silence-based or slip-based nomination become the group's default. Two Yakuza who nominate a Village player early on a weak read can steer the trial pattern for days; vote only on a named contradiction.
Keep the Katana holder's vote and target agreed in night chat and avoid repeating a predictable target pattern; the Village saw the same holder every night, which made the Grunt slip a strong lead.

A Veteran's alert kills are verifiable only by the Veteran's own report; when a Village trial hangs a Veteran, the team loses the only lethal night role that can be checked, so weigh the cost before voting Guilty.

Don't hold a rig token for a perfect moment. Spend it on a Day when a non-teammate is likely to pass nomination and be executed, while the Village is still unsure. This game the Clerk token went unused all the way to the win.
Stay visibly active in public, even with no role. Silent players (me, Carol) became the target of silence-based nomination threats. Post short, concrete reads on other players' claims to avoid that.
Explain a teammate's wording slip the same day it is raised, with a cover story ready. Erin's 'the Grunt it lists is me' line stayed open for days and became the Village's main lean and a nomination.
Rotate the Katana holder when a Lookout or Tracker could be alive. The holder stayed Erin every night and nothing moved it, which is predictable if the Village ever gets an information role.

A Veteran's alert kills can only be checked against visit counts the Veteran reports. If a claimed Veteran is alive, avoid visiting them; the Katana never visited Dave, so his claim was never falsified.

Once a Veteran claim is public, never visit that player, with an audit, protection, watch or anything else. A Veteran on alert already has Standard Defense, so protecting them gains nothing and risks your life. If you need to verify the Veteran, use visit-free or Astral information, or simply wait for their alert results.
evidence: Dave announced on Day 2 that he would alert on Night 2, and Frank audited him and died. On Night 3 Alice protected Dave while he was alerting and died too. That is two of the Village's six deaths before the endgame, both self-inflicted.

tip: Do the parity math every day. When the Village can still pass a hang on its own and nobody is dying to mis-hangs, a no-hang day hands the Yakuza a free kill. Hang the strongest lead, such as a self-contradiction that fits a slot count, before the Yakuza can block votes. 'Only on a mechanical lead' is a losing policy when night kills are erasing your investigators faster than they produce results.
evidence: On Day 4 the four Village players (Bob, Dave, Grace, Ivan) could have passed a nomination and a Guilty vote without help. They had Erin's Grunt slip and Bob's slot math, yet nobody nominated. By Day 5 it was 3v3, and on Day 6 the Yakuza hanged Dave.

tip: Treat a player's slip that names their own evil role as a real contradiction, not as 'wording'. This is strongest when it matches a public role list and the player's token count. Pair it with pressure on players who never claim anything: an archive Grunt slot that has to sit among the unclaimed players makes those players the pool to hang from.
evidence: Erin said 'the Grunt it lists is me', then claimed Vanilla. Frank's audit had shown her at 0 tokens. Bob showed the Grunt had to be among Carol, Erin, Grace, Ivan or Mallory, and Carol and Mallory never claimed a role until Day 5. The Village still kept calling the slip a 'lean'.

tip: When a suspect's own nomination comes up, especially one started by someone else, vote Yes if you hold any real lead. Passing a nomination only opens a trial and costs nothing. Voting No on a strong suspect wastes the chance and protects the Yakuza.
evidence: On Day 3 Carol nominated Erin, but Grace, Heidi, Ivan and Alice voted No alongside Erin and Mallory, so it failed with 3 Yes. With those four Yes votes it would have passed, and a Village-majority trial could have hanged the Katana holder.

tip: Keep protecting the obvious information target, the claimed investigator whose results the town keeps citing. Don't switch to a player who has built-in protection, such as an alerting Veteran. Use your Strong tokens rather than dying with them unspent.
evidence: Alice protected Heidi (Fortune Teller) on Night 2 and then moved to Dave on Night 3. The Katana killed Heidi that night, and Alice died to Dave's alert with both medic tokens unspent.

tip: Coordinate fully at night, avoid daytime PMs, kill information roles in order of threat, and leave the Veteran alone. Then, once your votes control the day, hang the remaining power role while citing his own vote record. But never refer to your true role in public. One slip can be the whole case against you.
evidence: Unanimous Katana votes and zero PMs left the town no PM trail to follow. The Katana took Judy, Heidi and Bob, never visited Dave, and at 3v2 the Yakuza hanged him using his Day 3 Yes vote. Erin's 'the Grunt it lists is me' nearly undid all of this when Carol's nomination came up.

tip: A prosecution forces a trial with no Yes votes, so it is the one reliable way past a stalled Day. Spend the token on a suspect you have a concrete read on, and only on a Day where a Guilty majority is plausible, since a failed trial wastes it. My Night 2 and Night 3 prosecutions were spent before any evidence against Carol or Mallory had been checked.

When a player repeats or leaks information only insiders could know, such as a Katana holder, ask for the source at once. A withdrawal with no source is a confirmation of the leak, not a clearance, and it should count as a real lead.

A random Seer pair that reads DIFFERENT only says one player reads Evil and one does not. Check whether a Katana holder (who reads Good that night) or a Yakuza Diviner is in the pair before deciding that one member's read contradicts the other's claim.
Keep teammate-only facts such as who held the Katana out of day chat. Ivan's public remark gave the Village its strongest lead and cost the team its Pharmacist and, later, the Diviner's defence.

Repeated self-nominations and long pushes cost budget every round and stalled the Day for several rounds. A short, specific question naming one player and one check gets a faster and more useful answer than another full speech.

Before a Katana attack, check whether the target is a Lookout or Tracker claimant; Dave's visit-list claim exposed our night visits and his Lookout watch on Bob was a predictable threat, so consider moving the Katana off a holder the claimed watcher is likely to name.

Random pairs and random visits (Seer pair, Ex-Con visit) can be checked only against fixed facts; when a claim fits a random result, weigh it as neutral rather than as proof, and check whether the claimant's own read matches the mechanics before voting.

Don't let a single unsourced slip become the whole case; the table hanged Ivan on a withdrawn Katana remark and then hanged Carol and Bob on the same thread, which left the Jester pool and the Oracle claim unchallenged.

Avoid taking a visible stance (defending or attacking the Jester-looking nominator) that makes you the obvious vote target; Frank's repeated self-nominations drew votes away from the real threat while our own votes drew suspicion.

Check the Oracle's Astral guess and the Katana holder's Good read before using them in arguments; they are night-only facts that other players cannot verify, so both sides spent speaking budget on claims nobody could test.

Do not let a Katana holder's own role action be the only visible kill signal; coordinate the Katana target with a non-revealing action so a Seer or Tracker cannot easily pin the holder. Also avoid a Diviner visit on a player whose result would expose the team's own holder.

Never leak Yakuza-only information in public, even as a guess. Ivan's Katana remark was the single fact that got the Pharmacist and then the Diviner hanged, and the withdrawal only made it look worse.
A teammate's private message to a surviving player right before a trial (Carol to Bob) is a permanent link that the table will reuse. Avoid private messages to teammates on Day 3 and before a trial.

Test Oracle-style claims with the public record before they are used: an Astral guess that cannot be checked should not be the basis for a trial, and a verified hit on a second player is what separates a real power role from a bluff.

Repeated self-nomination by one player is a weak signal either way; vote on checkable contradictions in claims, votes and results rather than on the pushes, since a Jester and a Yakuza can both produce the same noise.
Watching the same player on consecutive nights (Mallory N1 and N2) only re-confirms the same visitor list; spread watches across different suspects or a corroborated pair to get new information.

A private message from a Yakuza-only information source (e.g. a Katana holder remark) is a strong tell; when someone states secret night info as fact, demand a source immediately and vote on it rather than on pushes.

Repeated self-nominations by one player are a Jester tell only if the Jester's win matters to the table; when a Jester claim exists, avoid being the one who hangs the Jester by accident and test the claim with checkable results first.
Do not PM a teammate who is about to be on trial with requests to stay quiet; that PM is public evidence (sender and recipient) and tied the Grunt to the Diviner's fall.
Count the living roles against the archive and claims each day; a verified power-role hit (like an Oracle guess that was correct) should be weighed above unverifiable Astral claims.

Since your visit is random and untold, a Lookout or Tracker watching a victim will show you as a visitor; stating your random-visit claim early with an explicit note that it can land on anyone avoids the suspicion of refusing to name a target.

Before accepting a claimed Oracle, Seer or similar guess result, check whether any mechanical fact (visit-based results, Katana holder alignment, archive slot math) can actually test it; untestable Astral claims should not carry a trial alone.
Never leak Yakuza-only information such as who holds the Katana in public chat; a single slip like Ivan's gave the Village a clear hanging case and cost a Pharmacist.

Vote on checkable contradictions in claims and results rather than on who pushed for a nomination; self-nominating repeatedly fits a Jester, and Village votes that followed pushes led to hanging teammates and the wrong players.
Track which Village claims are testable: a Lookout's visitor list and a Tracker's result that agree are two independent confirmations, so weigh them above a Seer pair built on random results.

A Jester who keeps self-nominating reads as a Jester hunting a hanging and gets the table to rally against them; vary the approach, e.g. push a trial only once a concrete suspect is named, so the nomination doesn't look like pure self-promotion.

Check whether a claim explains the public facts before accepting or rejecting it: a single unverifiable Oracle or Astral guess cannot be tested, but a confirmed Ex-Con visit or a Katana holder's secret leak can be cross-checked against who held the Katana and who was visited.
Never let a teammate reveal Yakuza-only information in public (such as who held the Katana) without a cover story ready; the slip exposes the whole team and invites hangings.
Track which players can still hold a role: the archive plus the public claims and deaths define the census, so once slots are full an unclaimed role must belong to a specific living player.

Voting Innocent on a player the table is already leaning against, while a teammate's PM or leak points at you, makes your votes look coordinated; vote on the record rather than defending a suspected teammate.

Archive slot math only works if you track which shown roles are dead; once claims fill the hidden slots, write the full census in your notepad each day so you can spot a claim that overflows the remaining slots.

A teammate's knowledge leaks when they reference Katana holder or night-chat facts; withdrawing such a remark without a source is worse than silence, because it marks the speaker as the leak to every town player.

When a player is asked for a source and dodges, don't let a repeated vote on pushes replace the check; vote only on a concrete contradiction, since Jester self-nominations and Yakuza defensive votes look identical until results come in.

The Katana holder reads Good at night's end and Ex-Con reads Evil, so a DIFFERENT Seer pair involving a Katana holder can look like a Yakuza while being a Good-reading holder; check which role reads which before building a case on alignment.
Avoid day PMs to teammates that a Carol-style pre-trial message can expose; the single private message Carol sent Bob before her trial became the main link the town used to hang him.

A Tracker that picks the same target every night gets a clean visit trail; switch targets only when a claim needs testing. Here my N1 and N3 Mallory tracks both showed no visits, which weakened the Mallory-as-Oracle-hit line I could have used earlier; track players making contested claims on the nights they make them.

Before voting Guilty on a leak-style remark, check whether the same accuser also had a teammate-protective vote pattern. Ivan's Katana slip was a real lead, but the table hanged him on one withdrawn remark while the Yakuza-aligned vote pattern (defending Carol, pushing Frank's trial) went less examined.

Run the archive and claim slot math each day, and mark which claimed roles are dead so the remaining Village/Yakuza split is clear; the Day 4 Bob trial rested on an unverified Prosecutor claim, so verify claims that carry the census before using them to hang.
Mass-piling onto one nominee with repeated identical reasons (as on Frank and Ivan) drew votes without new evidence; ask each voter for one concrete, checkable reason before you join the pile.

A teammate's private message right before a trial (Carol to Bob on Day 3) is a visible link; avoid day PMs that tie a living teammate to a dying one, since the table used exactly that link to hang Bob.

Decide the block target before Day 2 chat settles; I never blocked anyone, so the Katana and Diviner ran unchecked while my team lost its last Yakuza-side protection. A block on the lone Seer claim would have cut its pair info early.

Do not let one teammate make a public slip that exposes the team; Ivan's Katana remark (Yakuza-only info) got him hanged and cost the Katana-holder cover. If a teammate slips, distance yourself at once and vote consistently.
Keep votes consistent with the public line. Carol voted Innocent on Ivan after arguing against his leak and then flip-flopped on Erin; that inconsistency was the easiest lead for the town to follow.
Check claims against private-message traffic and vote history early. The Carol-to-Bob PM on Day 3 and Frank's repeated self-nominations were visible signals the town used, so manage who PMs whom.
Verify single untestable claims (Astral Oracle) by checking other claimants' results; Mallory's correct Oracle calls on Erin and Frank were what cleared Mallory and sealed Erin's innocence.

Your random pair is a fact about two players, not a read on either. Publicly claiming it with a live token on Day 2 made you the predictable Katana target on Night 2. Before claiming, decide whether the claim is worth more than the token, and keep the token for a choice-based check on a suspect that matters.

Before treating a self-claimed role as false, check whether the claim is consistent with a random or untestable result (for example an Ex-Con's random visit or an Astral Oracle guess). Table-wide time was lost on Erin's claim, which was consistent with the random pair and only got clearer once checked.

A teammate's leak of Yakuza-only information (such as who holds the Katana) is strong evidence. Ask who could have known it and whether the speaker can name a source, instead of accepting a withdrawal as cover.

Budget carries only 50% into the next Day and public messages get pricier each round, so the late-Day budget ran out before key trial arguments. Save budget for trial defenses and the decisive votes rather than spending it on repeated Day 1 pushes.
Hold the one-line counterclaim and the full log for your own trial or a critical vote. Repeating the same unverified claim each round without new information wastes the table's few checks.

An Astral guess leaves no visit and no tracker trail, so it can't be corroborated. Publish the exact guess and result early, then favour guesses or actions that other roles can check, rather than spending several rounds defending an untestable result.

If Day 1 has no information, stop demanding reads and push for checkable claims. A player who self-nominates repeatedly without new information is a Jester-shaped lead, so answer the pattern directly instead of letting it stall the Day.

Random results (a Seer random pair, a Diviner group draw) prove very little about any single member. Weigh them only alongside claim consistency, and remember that a Katana holder reads Good that night, which can flip what a pair means.

Private messages are visible to everyone as a link between two players, and a Day PM between teammates was the link that got Bob executed. Coordinate only at night and keep daytime contact public and innocuous.

Never state Yakuza-only information in public. A slip that is then withdrawn vaguely reads as confirmation, so if it happens, either give a plausible cover source at once or move on without repeating it.

Never state team-only facts in public, even as a 'mechanics check'. This includes who holds the Katana, who acted at night, and teammate results. If you need a mechanic to reconcile a result, phrase it as a hypothesis ('if Carol held the Katana, she'd read Good'), never as a fact about a named player.
evidence: Ivan said 'Carol held the Katana on N1' to explain Judy's pair. He could not source it, withdrew it, and was hanged 9-2. His Pharmacist flip then got Carol hanged the next day on the same remark.

tip: Don't PM teammates during the Day, and don't cast a futile Innocent vote for a doomed teammate. Do the vote math. If the hang is certain, vote Guilty to keep your cover.
evidence: Carol PM'd Bob just before her trial, and Bob voted Innocent in a 6-3 hang. On Day 4 Grace, Erin, Heidi, Mallory and Alice all cited 'Carol's PM to Bob plus his Innocent vote' to hang Bob, the last Yakuza.

tip: Use the Night 1 Katana attack. With a large town and many unclaimed investigators, a skipped kill lets every power role reach Day 2 and pool results.
evidence: The Yakuza chose no N1 attack. On Day 2 the Lookout, Tracker, Seer, Archivist and Oracle all claimed and cross-checked one another, and that consistent picture was what cornered Ivan, Carol and Bob.

tip: Post archive or survey lists early, then redo the slot math after every flip and claim. Once Neutrals are pinned by other results, an unclaimed player left over in a known Evil slot is the target.
evidence: Grace's N1 archive showed Grunt, Pharmacist and Diviner. After Ivan and Carol flipped, Alice claimed Prosecutor, and Mallory's Oracle made Frank the Jester. That left only Bob for Grunt, and he was hanged 6-1.

tip: When pressed for your night target, claim Ex-Con right away. Your random, untold visit and your Evil reading explain both a missing target and a 'different' Seer pair. Evasive non-answers just build a case against you.
evidence: For five rounds Erin said 'I can't give a target I'm sure of' and was nominated 9-2. Once she claimed Ex-Con at trial, the claim fit Judy's pair and Grace's archive, and she was acquitted 11-0.

tip: Repeated self-nominations and PMs asking to be voted onto trial mark you as a Jester almost at once. Play a believable, mildly suspicious villager and let others build the case against you.
evidence: Frank self-nominated six times and asked Dave by PM for a Yes vote. Dave publicly called it a Jester pattern on Day 1, and Mallory's Oracle confirmed it. No nomination of Frank got more than 4 Yes votes.

tip: Spend prosecutions on your strongest mechanical lead, not on a claimant whose results keep checking out. A prosecution that ends in acquittal also uses up one of the Day's three trials.
evidence: Alice's prosecution of Carol, which followed straight from Ivan's leak, produced a hang. Her N3 prosecution of Mallory, whose Oracle had already correctly called Frank, ended 6-1 Innocent and spent her last token, while unclaimed Bob was the real Grunt.

tip: Spend the map token on a suspect whose group you can then cross-check against a visit claim, and post the group size before the claim is tested; my N2 map on Bob showed a group that a Lookout claim could not square, but I only posted it after I died, so the info came too late to matter.

Undirected visit groups show who is linked, not who attacked. Treat a Katana kill as proof only that the holder is in the victim's group; do not let a single claim about who visited whom pin the holder without a second source.
Do not vote on a claim's internal wording slips alone (e.g. Yes votes versus ballots); check the trial record before pushing a nomination, and push only with a result that the table can test.

When several Good players can't agree on a trial, the Yakuza benefit from the split. Agree in advance on a checkable question (e.g. a Katana holder's group or a token count) and vote on the answer, not on who pushed first.
A role-blocked or unlucky night can look like innate Defense; a Standard Katana failing is not proof of a protector. Ask for a token or role-specific answer before hanging on it.

Before submitting a Katana target, check whether the target is a Good power role that a Medic or Vigilante could protect; a Katana kill that fails to kill (Heidi's Standard Defense) reveals an innate Defense role that a teammate can then test by claim.

A Lookout cover claim built on an undirected visit group breaks as soon as the group is checked; pick a cover that does not depend on one visit that the town can verify, such as a passive Lookout watch on an uninvolved player.

When a player posts a stated vote that contradicts their ballot, treat it as a slip only once; repeated mismatches toward Good hangs are a Yakuza-linked pattern, so ask for a concrete mechanical result before voting.
Keep the Katana holder's cover aligned with the holder's own night claims; Bob's Lookout claim made Bob the only possible holder once Alice's group was posted, so the team lost its best defender.
Visit groups from the Cartographer and Scout are undirected, so a group of three with one kill does not identify the holder; test directions with a separate visit result before any hang.

An exact-role guess only confirms the role you named; use it on a player who is hard to read (not already claimed by a suspect) and post the result promptly, since a dead Oracle's single check is lost. Spend it on the most dangerous unverified claim, not a Day 1 teammate-looking player.

Night-chat plans were posted in full and the Katana target list was predictable (the power claimant each night). Vary the target between claimants so Good players can't predict the next kill, and never leave a teammate's trial unanswered when the vote math could save them.

Before voting, check your ballot against your stated stance: two Good players hanged after posting one vote and casting the other. Re-read the trial record before you post, and if you slip, correct it before the next nomination.

Do not let a single unverifiable claim (a Fortune Teller naming visitors, a Lookout whose only visitor is a dead teammate) drive two hangs in a row. Ask each claimant for a checkable result, and move to a vote only when a mechanical result breaks the chain.

A Katana kill with no visible protector means the victim had innate Standard Defense (Arsonist, Serial Killer) or a Medic protected them. Track which roles can have Standard Defense before using a failed kill as proof of protection.
A Katana hit that fails on a target with no Medic claimed means innate Standard Defense (Arsonist or Serial Killer). Ask for that role early, before a claimed Lookout chain is treated as settled.

Check your ballot against your posted stance before you post, and say 'as of now' when you state a vote. Two posted-versus-ballot mismatches got a Good player hanged and made the rest of the table distrust the poster.

A Fortune Teller gets only unordered totals, so any claim naming who visited whom is fabricated or leaked night-chat info. Test the totals by rebuilding visits from public claims, then demand a named target and a result you could not have read elsewhere.
Keep daytime PMs and vote patterns from matching your teammate's. Frank and Judy voting together on every hang, plus PMs to the Village, made the two of them a visible bloc once three were alive.
Do not rest a Vanilla or innocence claim on a dead player's check alone. Once Carol died, my Vanilla status could not be re-checked, so my defense under the Day 7 trial had nothing to point to.

applies_to: Accountant, Oracle, Sheriff, Seer and other investigators
tip: Post each result as it comes, but don't promise a schedule of future targets. The Yakuza killed me the night after my audit of Grace, and their night chat named me as the live threat because my results were public. Keep the next target private and keep a will with the full log.

applies_to: Fortune Teller and everyone checking one
tip: A Fortune Teller gets only two unordered totals. Any claim that names who visited whom is either fake or night-chat knowledge. Ask the claimant which number came from which night and check their names against public visits before trusting the totals.

Don't hang on one unexplained visit or a wording slip. The town hanged several Good players on small reads, while the Yakuza survived by pushing those hangs and then voting with the majority. Before any vote, name the specific answer you need and which answer would clear the accused. Then check the pusher's own record.

applies_to: Yakuza and Village players checking for them
tip: A slip that reveals knowledge only night chat or a dead-role status could give is a strong tell. Frank's opener calling Judy the only Village player left was such a slip, but it went unpunished. When a player names who is Village, press them for the source before the vote.

Before posting a vote stance, check your ballot against it. Mallory posted Innocent twice and voted Guilty both times. The mismatch was a slip, but it was used to hang a Good player. Re-read your last vote before you publicly state a stance.

Our Clerk rig and two swap tokens sat unused for the whole game while we agreed on Katana targets every night. Plan a specific Day for the rig and use swaps on the night a Lookout or Tracker threatens the holder, not at the end when the tokens are worthless.

Never fake a visit-based claim (Lookout, Tracker) that names one other visitor to a victim who was actually visited by your holder. Bob's Lookout claim forced him to be the only possible attacker once any map linked him, and his claim was dead as soon as the group was public.

Innate Standard Defense (Arsonist or Serial Killer) makes a Standard Katana fail with no protector. If a Neutral target survives, do not retry the same Standard attack; use a Strong source or block or remove the player instead.

Village players who push nominations on unverified reads (Ivan, Heidi, Mallory, Dave) hang their own Good players. Vote with confident lone pushers rather than against them; you gain from their wrong hangs more than from arguing.

Under R17 a protected player is never told who protected them, so asking who protected you cannot be answered; ask for the player's Defense level or innate role instead. Likewise, a Lookout never sees its own visit, so a Lookout whose only named visitor is the victim's own attacker is contradicting itself.

Don't sit on untouched shots while the Katana kills one Village player per night. Set a concrete trigger on Day 1-2 (for example, shoot the lone visitor to a victim) and fire a Basic shot when it's met, because dying with 3 unused tokens gave the Yakuza free kills.

Check each player's stated stance against their recorded ballot after every trial. Mallory's posted 'Innocent' lines that were recorded as Guilty were checkable right away and should have triggered a vote-record check before the next nomination.

A nomination chain (Judy nominated Heidi, then Ivan, then Mallory nominated Judy) where each push rests on the previous push's claim is a sign of a Yakuza steering the Village. Demand a mechanical result from the nominator before voting Yes, and don't let one unexplained visit carry a trial.

Fortune Teller totals can't name who visited whom. A claimed Fortune Teller naming visitors is either fake or using night-chat information, so test the names against what the claimant could only know, not against the totals.

Yakuza Lookout or Tracker frames often rest on an undirected or self-visit gap, like 'the only other visitor was X'. Before accepting or rejecting that, list every visit the claimant could have made and check whether the Katana hit fits it.

Dousing a player reveals nothing to them, but it still shows as a visit; an Arsonist who only douses wastes nights while Yakuza build a case. Ignite sooner once 2-3 are doused, and keep a Standard-Defense self-claim ready rather than letting a Katana hit force the reveal.

A false role claim made under trial (Lookout after saying Neutral) is read as a lie and gets you hanged. Pick one consistent public role on Day 1 and defend it, even if it is a Neutral reveal, rather than switching under pressure.

Yakuza night chat that names a visit-target and a reason in public-sounding terms gets copied by town. Keep the Katana holder's public story independent of your team's night plan, and let the holder be someone with a clean public record.

When a player's public claim gets tested by a checkable visit, check the actual visit-count or token math yourself before voting. Several Village votes this game rested on repeated claims rather than new results, and the trial ballots did not match stated votes; always confirm your own ballot after posting it.
