evidence: Erin blocked Ivan's N3 prosecution. Erin and Heidi then pressed 'four Days, no target' and Erin nominated him. Ivan was hanged 7-1 as a real Prosecutor. Grace had audited him that same night and found exactly 2 tokens, matching his claim.

tip: Before each night, write in your will whom you are investigating tonight, and fill in the result slot by day. You may die the night you get a key result, and then only your pre-written target survives.
evidence: Grace's will said 'later audit results will be posted by day'. She was killed on N3 while auditing Ivan. Her 2-token result, which would have saved Ivan, was lost.

tip: Kill the openly claimed information roles first. Use your blocker on whoever announced a night action for tonight, or on the Vigilante the night you attack them. This both protects the team and leaves the target's claim looking hollow the next Day.
evidence: Frank (claimed Fortune Teller) died N2 and Grace (claimed Accountant) died N3. On N3 Erin blocked Ivan the night after he announced he would prosecute, which created the 'no prosecution' narrative. On N4 she blocked Carol as the Katana hit her.

tip: Don't hoard shots until death. A self-confessed Evil-role claim or a lone unverifiable claim is a mechanical lead. A Basic shot costs 1 token, and dying with 3 unused tokens helps nobody.
evidence: Carol said 'I'm holding my shots for a solid lead' from Day 2 onward. She was killed N4 with 3 tokens unused, while Alice openly claimed a Yakuza role the whole time.

tip: With secret ballots, public statements about how you'll vote prove nothing. Evil players can announce Innocent and vote Guilty, or split their stated votes to look independent. In the endgame, count how many players could plausibly have voted each way, and don't trust 'I voted Innocent'.
evidence: On Day 5 Erin publicly said she would vote Innocent on Bob, and Heidi said Guilty. The vote was still 3 Guilty of 4, and Bob was hanged. The split stated votes made the two Yakuza look independent going into the final night.

tip: In the endgame, before any hang, count factions. If two unclaimed or suspect players could both be Yakuza, removing a Neutral killer can hand the Yakuza parity. Weigh whether the Arsonist or the Yakuza is the bigger threat to your win.
evidence: At 4 alive, Judy hanged Bob, the correct Arsonist read, with Yakuza votes. That left Judy alone against Erin and Heidi, and the Katana ended the game on N5.

tip: Your two numbers are unlabeled. Before posting a visit map, test each possible split against every other night's numbers and against Tracker and Lookout results, and say which splits remain possible instead of committing to one reading.

A map that only eliminates suspects, built on claims nobody can check, is not a result. Before a Guilty vote, name a direct visit or checkable result. A single leftover name is not enough, and Village players were hanged on exactly that kind of case.

When a player's role line keeps changing, ask one yes/no question on the first Day it matters and vote on the answer. Waiting until the claims had spread into several trials let the contradictions drive nominations for days.

Never name your role in public, even as a slip, and never claim an immunity-type role that a later block result can contradict. Erin's 'Pharmacist-type' wording and shifting role lines made her the Village's main target.

Protect the claimed Fortune Teller or other likely Katana target on nights when the holder is unknown, and post your protection target publicly once it has worked. A confirmed survived Katana hit is the strongest evidence a Medic can give.

With secret votes, totals cannot show who voted which way. Do not accuse someone of a hidden vote switch from a total, because the arithmetic depends on votes nobody can see. Judge votes only on stated positions and public actions.

applies_to: Village investigators and anyone building a visit map
tip: Before nominating on a visit map, list every claim it depends on and ask whether each one is checkable. Elimination maps built on unverified Medic or Party Animal claims produced two wrong nominations (Judy, then Dave) and cost the Village two Day-length trials.

Spend tracks on the likeliest Katana holders after an attack, not on claimed Vanillas. Tracking Dave on Night 1 and Judy on Night 3 gave clean but low-value results, while tracking the living suspects earlier would have found the holder sooner.

A Katana holder who visits a victim is visible to any living Tracker who tracks them. Keep the holder off the Tracker's likely targets, or use a cover visit, rather than letting a lone holder be tracked and hanged after a visible kill.
Repeating no nomination from me yet across many messages spent budget without adding information. Spend budget on one short, specific, checkable question per turn and save the rest for the trial.

Don't lock protection on one player every night. A fixed target taught the Katana team to hit unprotected claimed roles instead (Ivan the Scout and Grace the Party Animal both died). Spread protection across the claimed information roles and vary the target, and protect the Scout whose trios are the main cross-check.

A visit map built on unverified claims is an elimination, not proof. Before a Guilty vote, list which claims each exclusion depends on. If two untested claims carry the map, it can't justify a trial. Ask for one checkable visit instead.

With secret trial votes, infer splits from exact totals and the known Yes/No count. A public 'leaning Innocent' that doesn't match a Guilty-heavy total is a real signal, but only after checking the arithmetic against who spoke.
Repeating 'no nomination from me yet' with the same question costs budget and tells the table nothing. Spend each Day's budget on one new checkable fact or one specific question to a named player.

Any private message between two living players shows up publicly as a link, and a Wiretap or Eavesdropper may read it. Coordinate through the night chat only, and avoid daytime PMs from the Day your team needs to hide.

Before nominating on a map or chain of visits, check each link against a concrete result: a tracker visit, a block notice, or a protection that matches an attack. Elimination arguments that depend on several unverified claims produced three wrong nominations this game (Judy, Frank, Dave) and let the Yakuza survive.

Vote in line with your stated reads and say so before the vote. I flipped my position on Erin and Heidi late and publicly, and it cost credibility; if you change a vote, explain it before the trial rather than after the tally.

Ask each claimant for one checkable item per night (names, visit lists, counts) and record it in the notepad as it arrives. Several Day 4 and Day 5 arguments stalled because claimants answered with restated conclusions rather than the data.

A role-block notice is evidence about the blocker only if the blocked player's role is known. Treat a single claimed block (like Grace's on Erin) as an unverifiable lead, and do not let it decide a Day when the target is dead and cannot confirm it.

A Yakuza who stays quiet with 'no action' is easy to suspect when the Katana trail is public. Give a concrete, consistent, checkable-looking answer for Night actions early, since the Village leans on yes-or-no visit questions.

Pick one cover role line before your first public speech and repeat it word for word. Erin's 'Pharmacist-type' slip, then Vanilla, then being called immune gave the Village three incompatible lines, and that got her hanged 7-3 on Day 3. Never change a claim under pressure.

applies_to: Yakuza with a role-block (Pharmacist, Puppeteer-era teammates)
tip: Blocking a claimed Tracker is traceable: the Tracker reports the block publicly, and an immune role leaves a failed block that a Party Animal can report. Prefer blocks on quiet Vanillas or skip the block entirely, and never block a claimed Tracker on the first night a Party Animal is active.

Retrying a Standard Katana on a target a Medic is protecting wastes the night. Once a Standard hit fails on a Medic-protected player, switch to killing or blocking the Medic (or a Strong option) instead of repeating the same attack on the same player.

Public signals between teammates are visible even without contents: a PM to a voter asking for an Innocent vote on a trial is noticed. Keep trial-vote coordination to the night chat and public, checkable arguments only, and do not lean on one living voter to flip a trial.

Before voting Guilty on a visit map, count how many unverified claims it depends on (Medic protection, Party Animal blocks, Fortune Teller counts). A map resting on two or more unverifiable claims is an elimination, not a result. Demand a single checkable visit first, as Frank and Judy did on Day 5.

Pick one exact role claim before Day 1 and stick to it. Erin's 'Pharmacist-type' slip, followed by a Vanilla claim, made her immunity testable, and a failed Party Animal block then exposed her as immune and pointed at the team.

If you are the last Yakuza and a living Tracker or Lookout can see your visits, a flat 'no visit' denial loses to one unverifiable track. Either remove the watcher first, stop visiting, or pre-agree a cover story for the visit.

Don't nominate or vote Guilty on an elimination map that depends on unverified Fortune Teller or Scout claims. Two Village trials on such maps (Judy, Frank) came back Innocent, and the one clean check (Dave's Tracker result) was ignored until late. Demand one direct, checkable visit first.

A Medic's protection that matches a survived attack is only real if the Medic protects the same claimed investigator consistently. When one Medic protects the same person every night, the Katana will switch target, so treat survival as a lead, not proof, and ask who else was protected.

applies_to: Party Animal and any role with a block
tip: If a Katana holder is known or strongly suspected, block the holder, not a claimed investigator. The Katana can move after a death, so re-check who holds it every Day. I blocked Alice on Night 5 while Frank held the Katana, and Frank killed me that night.

Before nominating on a visit map, list every claim the map depends on. If a map needs an unverified Medic or Party Animal claim to hold, it is a theory, not a result. Several Day 5 and Day 6 trials came from one such map.

A role slip followed by a switch under questioning ('Pharmacist-type', then Vanilla) is a strong tell. Pick one claim early and never change it when cornered, because the Village will use every contradiction at the trial.

A failed role-block is checkable evidence against the target, since the target's immunity is shown by the moderator's wording. Quote the moderator's exact text in public, and ask the target to state their role in one line. A Vanilla who claims immunity cannot be checked, so the case rests on the exact wording.
After a Katana attack fails on a claimed Medic-protected target, move the Katana's target to a different player instead of retrying the same one. Our switch from Alice to Ivan on Night 3 succeeded.

A teammate who gives contradictory role lines should not keep shifting claims under pressure. Pick one plausible claim early and hold it, since Erin's Pharmacist-to-Vanilla switches made her the easiest hanging.
Before voting on a visit map, list every claim it depends on. Alice's Night 3 map rested on Carol's and Grace's unverified claims, and Heidi's execution depended on that map.
With secret trial and nomination votes, only totals are known. Don't assert who voted which way from arithmetic that assumes a vote, and don't accuse someone of a flip on that basis.
Repeating the same yes/no demand adds no evidence and wastes budget. Each turn, post one new fact or one specific question.
Your trios only prove groups, not who visited whom. Post the exact group members and whether any Katana attack or block fits inside a group, so others can test it instead of just trusting the trio.

Before nominating on a visit map, check which claims the map depends on. Alice's Night 3 map rested on Carol's and Grace's unverified claims and an elimination; it wrongly pushed Heidi, Judy, Frank and Dave to trial.

Keep the Katana holder off the Night 2-3 trail: Heidi's repeated holding plus visits to Alice and Ivan made a single obvious holder. Rotate the Katana to a teammate earlier and avoid repeating the same cover story.
When a trial ends with the accused's claim unverifiable, a vote for Guilty should name one checkable visit. Several trials this game went to hanging on pushes and misreads instead of results.

Protecting the same player every night (Alice) makes the Katana never land there and reveals your target pattern. Vary protection targets among likely Katana victims, and post your protection results so others can check survival claims.

Before voting on a visit-map elimination, check whether it depends on unverified claims; a map that only excludes players by assuming other claims are true is not a checkable result, and several trials this game were built on one.

Track the Katana holder across nights: a holder who is role-blocked does not attack, and a holder who dies passes it, so the Yakuza trail can be followed through blocks and deaths rather than by one night's visit list.

When a player says they will vote one way and then votes the other, ask the public tally first; a mixed signal is weak evidence of a link, so do not nominate on it alone and check whether the claimed nominee was actually cleared.

Post protection and track results publicly and early, and state whether your protection target was attacked, since unanswered questions about a Medic's target (Carol's Night 5 question) cost credibility and votes.
Avoid nominating a teammate-linked suspect purely to test a claim; a Vanilla who pushes nominations on weak maps can look like a Yakuza, so keep your own nomination records clean.

Decide your fake claim before the first Day and state it cleanly in your first message. Never describe yourself with your real role name, even loosely. A slip followed by a correction is remembered all game, and later evidence will be read against it.
evidence: Erin opened Day 2 with 'Pharmacist-type role', then claimed Vanilla. Every later discussion came back to it. When Bob's Night 2 track was blocked and Grace's block on Erin failed on immunity, the slip turned two ambiguous facts into a near-proof, and Erin was hanged 7-3.

tip: Use blocks as tests. A failed block reveals a role-block-immune role (Pharmacist, Smuggler, Veteran or Party Animal), so block claimed Vanillas and quiet players. Once you have a strong Katana suspect, keep blocking them every night until they are hanged. Switching away hands them a free kill, often on you.
evidence: Grace's failed Night 2 block exposed Erin. Her Night 4 block on Frank, the holder, stopped his Katana attack on Grace herself. On Night 5 she blocked Alice instead, and Frank killed Grace that night.

applies_to: Village (Fortune Teller, Tracker, Medic, Party Animal)
tip: Fortune Teller counts become decisive when every visiting role posts its target. Build the full visited and visitor list each night and subtract every claimed visit. Whoever must fill the leftover slot is your suspect. A Katana holder who stays in the same slot across two nights is the strongest case available.
evidence: Alice's Night 3 counts (4 visited, 4 visitors), minus Bob→Judy, Grace→Dave and Carol→Alice, left Frank or Heidi as Ivan's killer. Her Night 2 counts plus Ivan's trio left Dave, Heidi or Judy. Heidi was on both lists and was hanged 6-2. She really was the holder.

tip: Put your free Standard protection on the most valuable claimed investigator and keep it there while the Yakuza have only the Katana. It stops every Standard Katana hit and costs no token. A claimant who survives an attack becomes credible to the town.
evidence: Carol protected Alice every night from Night 2 on, using no tokens. The Night 2 Katana hit on Alice failed. That made Alice's numbers trusted, and they drove both Yakuza hangs. Carol and Alice both survived to the win.

tip: After a failed kill on a claimed investigator, assume a Medic is protecting them. Target the protector, or the blocker who keeps stopping your holder, rather than switching to another information role. Also give the Katana holder a cover story for their visits, and move the Katana once maps start to converge on them.
evidence: After Alice survived, the Yakuza killed Ivan and left Carol and Grace alive. Heidi said aloud that Carol's protection was a risk but did nothing about it. Heidi kept the Katana for three nights with only a 'no action' claim, which left her as the only name on both elimination lists. Grace later blocked Frank's attack on Night 4.

tip: Don't spend a hang on a player whose checkable record is clean just because their nominations misfired. When a mechanical candidate is still alive (the only living name an elimination map allows, or the player who was blocked on the night no kill happened), test that candidate first. If you choose not to hang them, give them no reason to relax and keep blocking or tracking them.
evidence: On Day 5 Dave was hanged 4-3 because he had pushed Judy and Frank to trial, although Bob's track and Grace's block both supported his claim. Frank, the actual holder, had been acquitted 1-6 minutes earlier and helped hang Dave. The game survived only because Bob tracked Frank on Night 5.

tip: If a Tracker or Lookout may have seen your Katana visit, never answer with a flat 'I visited no one' while claiming Vanilla. A Vanilla has no action, so a single tracked visit is fatal. Prepare a cover role that visits, or accept the risk when you choose to keep the Katana.
evidence: Frank claimed Vanilla with no visits on any night. Bob posted 'Frank visited Grace' after Grace died to the Katana, and Alice's 3/4 counts fit that exactly. Frank's only defence was to discredit Bob, and he was hanged 4-1.

tip: When trial votes are secret, use totals and public statements to work out who voted which way. Treat an inferred mismatch between someone's words and their vote as a question to ask, not grounds for a hang. A simple admitted mistake should end the matter.
evidence: Alice, Bob and Dave correctly worked out from the 6-2 total that Judy voted Guilty on Heidi after saying she was leaning Innocent. Judy admitted the flip and was rightly acquitted 1-6. She was a Vanilla Villager.

tip: Never flatly deny a visit that a Cartographer, Scout or Tracker could confirm. If you visited, agree a cover action in night chat and admit it on the next Day. Judy's and Erin's denials of the Heidi Night 2 visit became the checkable lie that hanged Judy.
Move the Katana every few nights, or give it to a member who never visits. Judy held it all game and was the lone visitor to three victims, so the Village only had to name one living player.
Never send plans, reassurance or 'stop doing that' messages in daytime PMs. Alice's Day 3 PM to Judy was visible to everyone and became the lead that got Alice hanged, then Judy.
Spend the puppet token early on a visible information role, such as a Seer or Cartographer whose logs are steering votes. I held it all game, so Niaj's pairs and Dave's sizes were never disrupted.

Visit groups expose attackers. A Katana holder who visits a victim always sits in that victim's group, so a Cartographer's 2-group with a dead player narrows the suspects to one or two names. Kill the Cartographer or Scout before the group logs pin the holder down.

Vary your investigation targets and post each result with the night number immediately; a Sheriff who repeatedly checks the same Not Evil players gives Yakuza a free read, and a Not Evil result on a Katana holder is only meaningful if you cross-check it against visit logs.

Random Seer pairs and Surveyor groups only show that two players match or differ; before hanging on them, find a check that involves a named visit or a confirmed exact-role result, otherwise the village hangs on noise.

Hold the nomination until the day's mechanical checks are posted; in this game three Village players were hanged on chains built from random pairs and a Dave group list that kept changing, while the one real Katana-visit contradiction was never resolved.

A Yakuza who denies a visit that a visit log can disprove loses credibility fast; prefer a cover action that is plausible (a Vanilla claim with an honest-looking Astral Oracle-style action) over a flat no-visit denial.

Test a Seer random pair against the Seer's own night history and visit logs before treating it as proof; one differing pair only says one of two players is non-Good, so pair-based nominations should wait for a second independent check.

Before voting, list every claimed visit and check it against the group sizes: a Katana holder must visit its victim, so a lone-visitor case should be ruled in or out with the size data rather than with who pushed hardest.
Ask each suspect for a one-sentence yes/no on the same night, and record their answers in the notepad; a denial that later conflicts with a visit log is a stronger lead than any accusation.
Use Oracle guesses on claimed roles that a Yakuza would not want to reveal; a correct guess confirms the claimant publicly, so spend guesses on the most-contested claims first.
Do not join a trial vote on the strength of a bandwagon nomination; demand a mechanical case from the nominator and vote Innocent when the case rests on a single pair or unverifiable claim.

Use map tokens on the player whose group is most useful, since map reveals the whole group; I mapped Judy on Night 3 but died that night, so a Cartographer should map on the first night it is safe to reveal groups and post sizes publicly the same Day.

A single random Seer or Surveyor pair only shows that two players differ or match; it is not a mechanical case against anyone. Before voting, separate what is an exact-role or visit-log fact from what is a random result.
Keep the Katana holder's denial consistent: Yakuza who deny a visit that a Cartographer or Scout log can disprove lose credibility fast; pick a cover action in advance and admit it early.

Do not vote for the same accused as a sweep of Yakuza claims when the only check is a claim from one Coroner; ask for a second independent check before a hanging, because each hanging removes a Village investigator.
Avoid two members sharing a late-game private message or repeating the same accusation pattern; the Village reads a clustered PM as a lead and it exposed the group in this game.
Exact-role checks on newly dead players are the most reliable information in the game. Examine the most recent death before anyone is nominated, and post the result at once.
Post each night's group sizes once and never revise them. Shifting lists made the whole Village distrust the one visit log that could have settled the Night 2 holder.
Never flatly deny a visit that group sizes could expose. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit with it, because a lone false denial is easy to catch.
A single random Seer pair with differing alignments is a lead, not proof. Before a nomination, pair it with a second independent check, such as a Sheriff read, a survey, or an exact-role result.
Keep daytime private messages free of anything about the group or the Katana. A single Day 3 PM from Alice to Judy became the main lead against Alice and helped get her executed.

Spend ritual tokens on a confirmed Seer or Medic early, while a Divine guess is still a surprise. I died on Day 5 with 2 unused tokens, even though Carol's Oracle hit had confirmed Niaj as Seer by Night 2.
Agree one cover action per night before anyone is asked about visits. A flat no-visit denial is checkable against the visit groups, and Judy's denial became the case that hanged her.
Keep daytime private messages between teammates to a minimum. Alice's Day 3 PM to Judy was read as the only link between two Yakuza and was used against both.

A single disagreeing Seer pair shows only that one player is non-Good. Before a Guilty vote, demand a second independent check, because the town hanged Alice and then Frank on chains that all rested on the same pair.
Post group members by name with each size report. Dave's unnamed group lists changed four times and were used to hang Judy.

A Surveyor's group is the target plus its circle neighbours, so surveying a player reveals the seating adjacency; use it early to map who sits beside whom and cross-check Cartographer sizes instead of spending tokens on repeat surveys of the same circle.

Random-pair results (Seer, Surveyor exact-role picks) only prove a set contains a role or matches an alignment; never hang on one pair. Demand a visit log or exact-role hit that singles out the specific player before voting Guilty.

A Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks, so a Good-reading Seer pair does not clear someone who held the Katana that night; track holder votes and visit logs rather than alignment reads for Yakuza-hunting.

Ask every player to answer a single yes/no visit question in one sentence early, and record each answer in your notes; evasion or a changed answer is a checkable lead, and a player who flips from Guilty to Innocent without naming a check should be pressed directly.

Repeated long public restatements of the same mechanical case burned budget without new information; post one concise check per round and save budget for the trial turn when your vote is actually on the line.

applies_to: Scout, Cartographer and other group-info roles
tip: Scout and Cartographer groups are undirected visit graphs. A Katana victim sitting in a 2-group means that group is the holder's visit, so the holder is the victim's partner. Get every group reporter to name the members in one public list early; Dave's shifting lists cost the town about two Days of work.

One random Seer pair or Surveyor split only shows that two players differ. Do not hang on it alone. The winning checks came from exact-role reads plus visit logs, so before voting ask which specific check makes the suspect non-Good.

A flat no-visit denial can be tested against group membership: if the Katana holder must sit in the victim's 2-group, every denial by a candidate is a checkable lie. Agree a cover action in night chat and state it in one line, rather than repeating denials that the Village can cross-check.
Repeating the same question to the same player, such as one-sentence answers demanded again and again, spent budget without new information. Ask once by name, then move on to a mechanical check.

A public Day 2 role claim made me the only visible Scout and the Night 2 Katana target. An investigator who can be killed before posting a result should weigh an early claim against staying hidden until a result is ready to post.

Examine a player the night after they die and keep the result out of day chat until it can be checked against the visit logs; my Night 3 Heidi result was the only hard check that survived, and I could have asked for it earlier.

A random Seer pair or Oracle guess is a lead, not a check. Before hanging, demand a result that names a specific player's action or role, and when a visit denial conflicts with a visit-group size, press the denier for the exact list of who they visited.

Vote as a bloc only on a mechanical chain stated before the vote. Two Yakuza executions in a row came from town votes on single pairs and a flip with no named check, so announce the specific check you vote on before the nomination.
Don't let an early private message to one player become a lead by itself. Ask the sender and recipient to explain it in public once, then move on rather than letting it carry a trial.
Post long repeated reasoning sparingly; later rounds cost more, so state the one check that matters in a short message and save budget for the trial turns where votes are decided.

applies_to: Yakuza (Smuggler or any holder with unused swap tokens)
tip: Unused swap tokens do nothing. When the Katana strikes a Medic-protected target, or a Seer's pair is about to matter, spend a swap to redirect the protection or the pair. Hold the swap for the night it changes the outcome, not for a later Day that never comes.

A flat public denial of a visit that the Katana logs can contradict is the most dangerous lie in the game. Pick a cover action in night chat before the night, and admit that visit with it once asked. Do not deny what the group sizes can expose.

Keep the Katana with a teammate who will not be the lone visitor to a victim. Holding it yourself through five nights made you the obvious link, and one lone visitor to a Katana victim was enough for the Village to build a case.

Trust exact-role checks (Coroner examines of the dead, Oracle guesses that hit, Vigilante kills) over random Seer pairs. The Village hanged three players on pairs and visit-group readings while the Coroner's confirmed reads were the only solid evidence, and the Cartographer's group lists changed several times.

Do not PM a teammate in daytime, even about something harmless. The Day 3 PM from Alice to me became the lead that drove the Day 4 nomination and the later votes. Any visible PM cluster is read as a link, so keep coordination to night chat.

Vary your protection targets and self-protect (1 token for Standard) on nights when your claim is public and a Standard Katana is plausible. Protecting the same claimed Seer on three nights made your pattern easy to read, and I never self-protected even when I was the likely target.
Attacks kill only if strictly higher than Defense, so Standard protection fully stops a Standard Katana. Count that when deciding whether a victim was protected or whether the attacker was Strong.
Post your group sizes with names, once, and keep them fixed. Shifting lists made the Heidi visitor question unusable and gave Yakuza a way to muddy the Village's main lead.
Use examines on dead or executed players to test claims that cannot be checked any other way. The Alice and Frank examines were the decisive Yakuza confirmations this game, so plan them early.
Do not vote Guilty on a single random Seer pair. My Day 4 Guilty vote on Alice rested on one pair, and I should have asked for a second independent check first.

Spend a chosen-pair token on one suspect paired with a player already confirmed Good by an exact-role check or a Sheriff read. A same or different result on two unknowns, like my Night 5 Erin and Judy pair, only shows they match and resolves nothing.
A random Seer pair is a lead, not a case. Before hanging on one, require a second check: a Coroner exact role, a visit log, or a Sheriff result on the same player.
Ask each denier for one plain yes or no early and pin it publicly. A Katana holder must have visited the victim, so one flat no-visit denial was provably false, but the table never pinned it down.
Post each night's Seer result at the first Day it is due. My late posting of Night 2 and Night 3 results let the Yakuza frame my reports as unverified.
Never flatly deny a visit that the holder's own role or the Katana rules force. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit it early, because a lone checkable denial becomes the case against you.

When a Cartographer, Scout or Fortune Teller is publicly claimed, assume the Katana visit will be isolated in the visit graph. Before the kill, either move the Katana to a member with a believable visiting cover claim, or use a Smuggler swap or Pharmacist block to blur the graph. Never claim Vanilla and flatly deny a visit that the group sizes can pin on you.
evidence: Judy held the Katana every night and kept claiming Vanilla with no visits. Dave's N2 sizes left Heidi in a 2-group with one partner. By Day 6 elimination left only 'Erin or Judy', and Judy's repeated denials became the case that hanged her. Her 2 swap tokens were never used.

applies_to: Yakuza (Ritualist, Puppeteer and other token roles)
tip: Spend one-shot tokens when the payoff is near-certain. A role publicly confirmed by an Oracle is a free Ritualist target, and a Divine guess beats any Medic. Holding tokens 'for later' usually means dying with them.
evidence: Carol publicly confirmed Niaj as Seer on Day 3. On N4, Frank proposed a Divine ritual on Niaj but backed down over fear of exposure. The Standard Katana was then stopped by Mallory's protection. Frank was hanged the next day with both tokens unused, and Alice never used her puppet.

tip: Don't vote as a bloc to save a teammate who is clearly doomed. Hidden No/Innocent counts that match your team size, and a public Innocent with no stated check, become the next case. Consider bussing so you survive longer.
evidence: Alice's nomination passed 7-3 and her trial ended 7-3, with Frank and Judy the hidden No/Innocent votes. Judy publicly announced Innocent on Frank with no check; Grace, Ivan and Mallory cited that flip on Day 5-6, and Grace and Ivan named it in the case that hanged her.

tip: Chain alignment results through anchored players. A Seer pair becomes a mechanical case once one member is independently confirmed Good, and an exact-role check on the hanged player then extends the chain to their pair partners.
evidence: Carol was anchored by Bob's Not Evil read and two correct Oracle hits. So Niaj's N3 'Carol/Alice different' hanged Alice. Ivan's exam of Alice (Puppeteer) plus Niaj's N2 'Alice/Frank same' hanged Frank. Ivan then confirmed Frank as Ritualist.

tip: A lone surviving Yakuza holding the Katana reads Good to every alignment check, every night. A 'same' result pairing a Good player with the suspected holder proves nothing. Rely on visit elimination instead, and don't spend a Seer token on a pair that includes the likely holder.
evidence: On N5 Niaj spent his only token on Erin/Judy and got 'same', then wrongly concluded 'both are Yakuza'. Bob's N4 check also read Judy as Not Evil. Erin's elimination argument was the correct reading.

tip: Before posting a deduction from group sizes, place every claimed visit first. Post sizes once, clearly labeled by night, and never revise the list in public. Repeated corrections hand the Yakuza a 'his lists keep changing' defense. Also write your planned map target in your will.
evidence: Dave first said Heidi was in the 3-group and left himself off his own candidate list, then corrected himself several times. Judy, Frank and Alice used 'Dave's lists changed four times' as their main defense through Day 6. Dave mapped Judy on N3, which named her group, but he died and the result never reached his will.

tip: Keep giving free Standard protection to the confirmed top information role. But once you are confirmed and the Katana has already failed against your target, expect to be the next target, and spend tokens on Strong self-protection rather than dying with them.
evidence: Mallory protected Niaj on N4 and stopped the Katana. On N5 she protected Niaj again, and Judy switched targets and killed Mallory, who still had 2 unused medic tokens.

tip: Keep all coordination in night chat. A visible daytime PM between two players who later turn out to be Yakuza ties them together, whatever its contents.
evidence: Alice's Day 3 PM to Judy ('say nothing new until Ivan's result') was publicly noted. After Ivan exposed Alice as Puppeteer, that PM was cited against Judy in her Day 6 trial.

tip: Scout results name only players in different groups, so count how many distinct groups must exist and use Cartographer sizes to test membership; a Scout name that repeats across nights is a strong constraint.
A Katana victim's killer must be inside the victim's visit group; when a Cartographer map shows a group, check every claimed visit against it before trusting any single claim.
Avoid slipping Yakuza-only words (Ritualist, night chat) while claiming no role; one slip led the Village to focus on Judy and made her a lightning rod.
Prefer hanging on visit-level or exact-role results over pair reads and alignment claims; pair reads were randomly unreliable and cost us an innocent Erin trial.
Keep the Katana holder off the nominee list when a trial can pass without them; Village votes cleared Erin and Dave when the holder stayed alive.

Examine the player most likely to die before the next night and claim it early, since the exact-role result is the only hard evidence in a game full of unverifiable claims. Spend tokens on dead players whose role clears or confirms a live suspect.
Demand visit-level results, not group sizes or pairs. Niaj's group maps and Mallory's random Seer pairs produced many votes that could not be checked, and the trials resolved on them.
Before voting Guilty, ask whether the nominee's trial rests on a mechanical result. Two Village players were hanged on pattern reads, and the real Yakuza were only found by a Coroner exam.
Avoid Yakuza-only words like Ritualist or night chat in public. A single slip gave the Village its main case against Judy and drew several votes.
Keep all Katana and target votes in night chat and never speculate about who holds the Katana in public. Visible innocent votes on teammates were a clear sign to the Village.

Yakuza with no Katana action each night still need a plan for the Katana holder's visit log; a holder who never acts leaves Village nothing to test, so keep the holder's own role action visible and consistent.

Before voting on a claimed investigator's result, check it against the group-size and visit maps; the Cartographer and Scout results together can locate the Katana visitor without relying on any single player's word.
Avoid naming Yakuza-only roles or night-chat contents in daytime speech; a single slip like 'Ritualist' drew the whole Village's attention and got a player nominated.
Do not hang a player on a pair-based read alone; a Seer random pair only shows different or same alignments and cannot prove a specific player's alignment.
A confirmed-by-exam Coroner or Oracle claim is a strong lead; if a teammate is about to be exposed by such a claim, the protection is a credible counter-claim with mechanical detail, not silence.

applies_to: Wiretap and other passive information roles
tip: A passive Wiretap sees every Day PM but nothing at night, so keep Yakuza coordination strictly in night chat and treat any teammate's daytime PM cluster as a read on the group.
Before voting on a trial, demand a visit-level result (a named visitor or a token audit), since group sizes and pair reads can be satisfied by several different players.
Avoid stating any Yakuza-only word in public, such as Ritualist or night chat, even as a slip; Village treats it as a near-proof tell and it drove the Day 3 trial.
When a Katana holder is at risk, move the Katana in the same night rather than retrying a protected target, and count which teammates are still alive before choosing a holder.
Track each Yes/No nomination count against the announced totals, since hidden votes cluster around the nominator and the eventual trial.

Submitting 'no action' every night, including a Smuggler who never swaps, leaves a visible pattern of no visits; a teammate who never acts is the first thing Village tests. Cover with a plausible low-cost action or a self-visit story agreed in night chat, and don't let one role sit idle for five nights.

Group-size maps (Cartographer) and Scout groups only name members when used; a size alone can't implicate anyone. Demand the names of the group members and ask each member for one visit, rather than pushing trials on who is missing from a group.

The Yakuza-only word slip ('Ritualist', 'night chat') drew the whole town onto one player and got a Yakuza executed. Avoid naming Yakuza-only roles or channels in public, even while denying a role, because one slip is enough to hang you.

Pushing a trial on a single unverified Sheriff or Seer read let the Village hang its own Good players, while the actual Yakuza voted Innocent to cover each other. Before nominating, check whether the nominee's accusers share a claim, and whether the vote pattern of the people pushing it fits a cover story.

A Katana victim's survival is only evidence of Standard protection if a Medic claim is also true; Judy's exact-role result showed the Medic claim was consistent, but a claimed Medic who protects a player already called Evil on Night 1 is a weak story. Check the claimed protection target against the claimant's own timing before treating survival as confirmation.

Use guesses on claimed roles that a teammate or the Seer can't yet contradict, and track right/wrong results to build a confirmed-claim list. My Oracle hits confirmed Mallory, Ivan and Niaj, which was the strongest Good-side anchor of the game; Night 1 and Night 4 guesses wasted a guess on low-information targets.

Cartographer group maps and Katana attack logic together give hard visit-level checks: a Katana victim's killer must sit inside the victim's group. Force claimants to name group members rather than sizes, since a size-only claim can't be checked.

Do not let a trial be decided by a pattern of pairs or slips. Several hangs (Judy, Carol, Erin) rested on Seer pairs or single wording slips, and the Village later had no visit-level evidence for them; require one mechanical result before a Guilty vote.

Keep one holder and one target per night and avoid wasting the Katana on a protected claimed investigator; the Yakuza here kept killing Sheriffs and Mediums who had visible protection or claims, which made their claims and results public.
Avoid Yakuza-only words (Ritualist, night chat) in public speech; a single slip became the main case against Judy and cost the team a teammate.

applies_to: Surveyor and other group-based info roles
tip: A survey or map only narrows the field. Spend tokens on the group that holds the most unresolved suspects, and record each result as one random member's role, not a verdict on everyone in the group.

A Katana killer must visit its victim from inside the victim's visit group. Cross out group members who have a stated visit, and treat a lone unexplained member as the strongest lead. Press for that member's visit before any nomination.

Trials built on pair reads and slips let Yakuza survive: Erin was acquitted 5-5 on Day 4 and then killed Heidi and Niaj. Demand a visit-level result or a stated role conflict before voting Guilty, and get a second source for any pair read before the trial.
Free Standard protection on a claimed investigator stopped a Standard Katana hit. Rotate it across the claimed Sheriff, Seer and Oracle so the Katana holder cannot predict the target.

Public Yakuza-only words such as Ritualist or night chat get the whole Village pressing the speaker. Cover a slip at once with a plain, checkable explanation, and never refer to night-chat content in public.

A Sheriff's investigation result can be a single claim that the Yakuza exploit; when a Sheriff is publicly nominated after a Katana attack, test their Night results against visit logs before voting, and post your own check early so teammates cannot make the claim the only evidence.
Group-size maps (Cartographer) and survey/Seer pairs are weak until a player names the members; push for named groups with visits, and do not hang on a pair read or a group size alone.
Never use a Yakuza-only word (Ritualist, night chat) in public, even as a slip; one slip became the entire case against a teammate and drew the whole Village's attention.
Before nominating or voting Guilty, state the mechanical case in one line; a trial pushed on pairs and Night-result guesses ends in executions that the Village later regrets.
Avoid announcing an Innocent vote on a teammate alongside others; repeated Innocent votes on each lost Yakuza gave the Village an obvious voting pattern to read.

A free Standard protection on a player is only worth the claim if it's not predictable; the Katana holder simply targeted the Sheriff I protected by name in chat, and I announced my protection target publicly in the Day, handing the Yakuza a shield-checking tell. Keep the protection target private until the night resolves, and vary it rather than always covering the most-claimed investigator.

Use visit-group sizes and named members from Cartographer or Scout results to find the Katana holder: a Katana kill is always visited from inside the victim's group, so list the group members each night and test every claim against it before voting.

Do not vote Guilty on a player whose only case is a pair read or a Sheriff read that nobody can verify; demand a visit-level result. Several Village hangs this game rested on Seer pairs and group sizes, which the Yakuza could manufacture by claiming roles.

Yakuza who vote Innocent on teammates' trials and push trials on the Village's claimed power roles should keep their own night records clean and consistent; a single Yakuza-only word slip (Ritualist, night chat) was the strongest public tell and cost Judy the game.

A Katana attack leaves a visit from the holder to the victim, and the holder reads Good that night, so an alignment check on the holder can be Not Evil; a Sheriff's Not Evil result on a player near a Katana kill does not clear them.

Submitting no action or a blank target on a night you are asked about invites a hang; as Judy I was voted out for a blank Night 2 target. Give one plain sentence on your night action each time it is asked, even if the answer is 'nothing', and do it before the other players build a shortlist from your silence.

Never use a Yakuza-only word such as 'Ritualist' or 'night chat' in public, even as a slip. Village players seized on it and it became the core of my trial, so scrub role names and team vocabulary from every public message.

Voting Innocent on every trial of a teammate looks like cover to the Village. Spread your Innocent votes and let some trials pass by a Guilty majority you do not oppose, so the pattern does not expose the team.

A Katana hit on a claimed Medic-protected Sheriff exposes the holder to a visit-based check. Consider holding the Katana on a player who will not be investigated soon, and plan the move with the team in night chat before the Day when a claim could expose the holder.

Yakuza with a surviving Katana holder can be identified by visit logs: a lone visitor to a Katana victim is strong evidence. Keep the Katana holder's visit away from groups the Cartographer or Scout can map, or accept that a map will name them.
A chosen pair is a visit to both players while the random pair is not; when a pair result conflicts with a later group map, check whether the pair was chosen or random before trusting either claim.

Visit groups and Katana hits are the only hard links; a Katana victim's attacker must sit inside the victim's visit group, so name group members and their visits rather than pushing trials on group sizes or pair reads.
Don't let a single surviving member be the only unexplained visitor; when a teammate is the sole living Yakuza, expect every Village claim to converge on them and plan a cover action in advance.
Pressing a trial on a suspect whose only evidence is a slip or a pair read repeatedly produced acquittals or near-misses; demand one visit-level result before voting Guilty.
Track who voted Innocent on each executed Yakuza; voting pattern clusters were a strong read once Coroner results confirmed roles.

Spend the map token on a player whose group size you already know, then post names with sizes. A named group that is inconsistent with the sizes you posted each night is exposed by any teammate who reads your map, so name only what the moderator actually confirmed.

Before voting on a trial, write the visit-level chain for each Katana hit, naming the holder candidates from the victim's group. Do not let group sizes, slips, or pair reads (Seer pairs, Surveyor surveys) convict someone alone; Judy and Erin were both lynched on that kind of reasoning.

Ask every claimant for a single named, checkable result early (for example a Seer pair with names and alignments, or a map group with names), and record who gave a changed account. Shifting accounts (such as Mallory's Night 2 pair going from chosen to random) were the strongest tell available and were not used to cut the Yakuza early.

Late in the game the public chat was dominated by repeated 'one sentence' demands. Once a question has been asked and answered or ignored twice, change the form of the challenge (vote, or a specific named check) instead of repeating it, to save budget for the trials that matter.

A Katana holder who visits a Medic-protected Sheriff only gets a visit-level signal once the protection is known; plan Katana targets around protectors you have already seen claim, and move the holder before a group map can name it.

Prepare a fake role claim in night chat that fits the visit logs, and post it early. In a game where most Village players claim roles with results, 'Village-facing, no claim, no action' marks you as Yakuza once the claimed roles are cross-checked.
evidence: All four Yakuza stayed unclaimed with no actions all game. The Village kept narrowing suspects to 'the only group member with no claim': Judy on Day 3, then Erin on Days 4 and 6. Carol said 'I used no night action on Nights 1 to 4' on her trial and was hanged.

tip: Don't all vote Innocent/No together on a doomed teammate, and above all don't announce those votes. Once a Coroner or another exact-role result confirms the hanged player, every public defender becomes the next suspect. Have one or two members vote Guilty to look clean.
evidence: Carol, Dave and Erin voted and spoke Innocent on Judy (8-4). After Bob's Coroner exam showed Judy was Ritualist, 'Carol, Dave and Erin all voted Innocent on Judy' became the core case. That case hanged Dave, then Carol, then Erin.

tip: The Katana holder reads Good to alignment checks that night. Don't spend a chosen Seer pair on the likely holder, and never treat a 'same' or 'Not Evil' result on them as clearing them. Spend the check on a suspect less likely to be holding the Katana.
evidence: Mallory spent her only seer token pairing Erin with Frank on Night 3, when Erin held the Katana, and got 'same'. She then argued Erin was Good and Niaj was Evil, and voted Innocent. Erin survived on a 5-5 tie, and Niaj was later Oracle-confirmed as the Cartographer.

tip: Once you have claimed and saved someone, expect the Yakuza to kill you instead of retrying your target. Spend a token on self-protection on the next night or two rather than dying with tokens unspent.
evidence: Ivan saved Heidi on Night 2 and protected her again on Night 3 for free. The Yakuza chat explicitly switched to 'hitting the protector', and Ivan died with 2 medic tokens unused. Heidi then died unprotected on Night 4.

tip: In an information-heavy game, use the Night 1 Katana kill and use your one-shot tokens early. A skipped kill gives every investigator a free extra night, and swap, puppet and Ritualist tokens are wasted if the members holding them get hanged.
evidence: Carol pushed for no Night 1 kill. Heidi, Grace, Niaj, Mallory and Frank all got results that fed Days 2-3. The Yakuza finished with an unused puppet token, 2 swap tokens and 2 Ritualist tokens. A swap could have redirected an investigator's check on the holder, or the Katana attack onto an unprotected target.

tip: Combine a named visit group that contains a Katana victim with the members' claimed visits. The Katana holder is whichever member's visit is unexplained. Then press that player for a one-sentence target.
evidence: Niaj's Night 2 map (Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Judy, Mallory) plus Grace's, Heidi's and Ivan's claimed visits left Judy as the only member with an unexplained visit. Her refusal to name a target, plus her 'Ritualist' slip, got her hanged.

tip: Examine each hanged player the following night and post the role. Confirming that a hanged player was Yakuza turns earlier voting records and defenses into hard evidence against their teammates.
evidence: Bob's results (Ritualist, Wiretap, Puppeteer) confirmed every hang. They let the Village chain cases from Judy to Dave to Carol to Erin.

tip: Ask a question once, by name. Don't echo the same demand every round. The budget you save is what lets you speak in late rounds and on trials.
evidence: On Day 2 nearly every player repeated 'Niaj, name the fourth member' and 'Alice, post sizes'. By round 7, Dave, Erin and Heidi could not afford a single public message.

tip: Protecting the same Sheriff every night was logged and predictable; rotate protection among claimed power roles so a Yakuza holder cannot learn which target to avoid, and self-protect only when a Katana holder is plausibly targeting you.

A Sheriff's single Evil read against a Vanilla claimant is not proof; demand the target and result be posted on the day it happens, and treat a result that first appears only after a nomination as a warning sign.

Before voting, log every player's stated Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent intent and compare with announced totals; hang only when a mechanical contradiction exists, not because several players repeat the same defence lines.
Do not repeat identical defence lines across trials or PM the same teammate during trials; the Eavesdropper and Wiretap and the town's pattern-matching expose it quickly.

Hanging a player whose only accuser is an unchecked claim lets a Yakuza survive to the endgame; keep a suspect list and spend hangs on players with concrete mechanical contradictions, since at two alive you cannot hang anyone.

A single Sheriff read is a lead, not a hang. Before a nomination, require a second independent source such as a visit log, audit or second check. Here three hangs (Frank, Erin, Grace) rested on one Sheriff claim plus private-message contents.
Never nominate on private-message contents you alone can see. Ask the sender to repeat the request publicly, and weigh it only if it matches a mechanical result.
Vary your trial defences. Frank, Erin and Grace repeated near-identical lines and voted Innocent each time, which made them a visible bloc that the Village could expose by comparing stated reasons.
Insomniac results show roles, not targets. Use them to rule out frames and count visitors, and say clearly which claims they prove and which they cannot.
A Medic who publicly names an exact protection target that matches a Katana survival lends real weight to the survivor's claim. Say the target publicly at once rather than letting it come out late.

An audit confirms only the stated votes of one player, not their role. Use it to check that a voter's stated Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent match the totals, and spend it on the player whose defence lines most resemble someone else's.

When two players post near-identical defence lines and vote Innocent on the same hanged targets, treat that shared pattern as a coordination signal. Ask each of them for a reason that comes only from their own knowledge.
Do not hang on a single unchecked investigative read. Before a vote, require the claimant to post the target and exact result for every night, and check whether the claimed visits match the logs.

Post the visitor roles you heard as soon as you learn them, not later. Once you have named a Grunt or other Yakuza-linked visit, you become the obvious kill target, so the information is most useful before the night you could die.

Post each investigation's target and exact result on the day you learn it, and name the next target at once. Holding a result back or promising it for later reads as retrofitted, and it gave the village a repeated 'name a second check' excuse to block hangs.

A Not Evil result on a suspect proves little if they held the Katana that night, since the holder reads Good. Before using it to clear someone, check whether that player could have been the holder, and say so when you post the result.

An Insomniac or other visit log shows roles, not targets. It can rule out a frame by Fabricator or Ex-Con but cannot place a Sheriff's visit on a particular player, so do not treat it as confirming a specific read.

Do not let teammates send private messages to the same outsider during trials, and do not repeat a doomed teammate's defence line for line. Two Yakuza PM-ing one player and voting alike in every trial gave the village a traceable bloc to hang.

Before each trial, collect each voter's stated Yes/No or Guilty/Innocent and compare it with the announced totals. This catches walk-backs and kept the hanging case grounded in public facts rather than in private-message contents.

Once the Katana holder has been attacked and survived, consider moving the Katana the same night; a repeated attack on a Medic-protected target just wastes the kill while the Medic keeps protecting them.
Don't let teammates argue the same lines in public defences of each other; identical phrasing across defences (as with Frank, Erin and Grace) makes the whole team a single readable target.

A Sheriff's single Evil read with no second check should not be enough to hang someone; before a trial, demand the Sheriff's log or a corroborating visit, and track which players voted Innocent on earlier hangs.
Insomniac logs show roles, not targets, so they confirm that a Sheriff or Medic visited someone but not who; don't treat them as proof of a specific claim.

Avoid PM-ing teammates or pushing your own hang-argument through private chats; a visible private message trail between two players (Frank->Bob, Erin->Bob) was used as the town's lead against the Yakuza.

After a blocked Katana attack, aim the next one at the protector rather than the same target. We hit Dave twice into the same Medic protection (N2 and N4) and never removed the Medic, so the kill engine stalled.

Do not defend a doomed teammate with identical public lines and Innocent votes. Each defence links your votes together and makes the next nominee obvious. Either vote Guilty on them or admit uncertainty, so the next Yakuza isn't tied to the same lines.

A private message is visible as a pair even when its contents are not. My Day 3 PM to Bob asking him to doubt the Sheriff became the basis for the Grace nomination. Keep teammate pressure to public, defensible logic points, not PMs asking for a vote.
Spend fixer tokens on the night before a close trial, aimed at a Good voter whose Guilty vote decides the hang. I died on Day 3 with both tokens unused, so they gained the team nothing.

A single Sheriff result is one unverified claim, even when a Insomniac log shows a Sheriff visit, because Insomniac sees roles, not targets. Demand a second corroborating check before hanging, since the village hanged two players on Dave's read alone.

A Katana attack on a Sheriff-claimed target that is protected each night by a Medic just wastes the kill; check the Medic's visit pattern before choosing the target, and prefer a non-claimed Good player who has no protector.

Once your teammates are dead and you are the last Yakuza, every hang you vote for is decided by Good votes; use your Innocent votes early on suspected Good players to keep the Village split instead of joining the bandwagon.

Do not let a single PM-based accusation drive a nomination; when a player nominates on private-message contents only they can show, ask them to publish the message text or the mechanical result before anyone votes.
A Not Evil result on a Katana holder is not a clearance, and the attacked Sheriff can't tell Medic protection from a miss; state which of these explains your survival in the first public claim.

Before each night, confirm the Katana holder and target in one short message to the whole team, and avoid the Katana holder being the one player other Good claims protect each night, since that can waste the attack.

Insomniac output shows roles of visitors, not targets; a visit of a real Sheriff cannot be tied to a specific player, so do not treat a visitor count as proof a claimed Sheriff acted on a particular person. Post the exact visitor roles and state explicitly what they cannot prove.

Do not vote Guilty on one unverified investigative read when the claimant's own later claims keep changing targets; demand the target and log before each hang, and prefer a hang only once a second independent check exists.

Track each player's stated votes against announced totals and against private PM contents; here the hang chain (Frank, Erin, Grace) was driven by one Sheriff read and PM contents, and nobody checked whether the Sheriff's claim was the Yakuza's bait.

Yakuza who keep submitting the same Katana holder and target every night with a Grunt inside can be exposed by any visitor log; keep a Katana holder who is a non-Grunt role if possible and avoid stacking multiple visits on one night.
Avoid echoing the same defence lines across trials; repeated phrasing across consecutive defences of different players became the main public tell that pointed to the Yakuza pair.

Count the likely trial vote before the night and fix a pro-hang voter whenever one flipped vote breaks the Guilty majority, especially to save an exposed teammate. Don't hoard tokens 'for a trial that matters'. The trial on your own exposed teammate is that trial.
evidence: Frank was read Evil on N1 and the Day 2 nomination already drew 4 Yes. He kept both fixer tokens on N2 and was hanged 5 Guilty to 3 Innocent on Day 3. A single fixed Guilty voter (Bob, Heidi or Alice) would have made it 4-4, and he would have survived.

tip: Don't all claim Vanilla Villager, and don't defend a teammate with the same talking points and the same votes. Spread your claims, word your arguments differently, and when a teammate is clearly doomed and you can't swing the vote, have at least one member vote Guilty so you don't form a visible bloc.
evidence: Erin, Frank and Grace all claimed Vanilla, so half the table claimed Vanilla, and all three repeated 'name a second check / one Sheriff read isn't enough' and voted No/Innocent. Carol and Bob hanged Erin and then Grace mainly because 'her defence repeated Frank's lines' and 'Innocent on both Frank and Erin'.

tip: After a Katana attack fails on a likely-protected target, kill the protector next, not a spent information role, and don't retry the same protected player. Rank kills by how much a player can still do, not by what they already revealed.
evidence: Alice announced she would protect a claimed power role, and the N2 attack on Dave failed. On N3 the Yakuza killed Heidi, who had 0 insomniac tokens left. On N4 Grace attacked Dave again, and Alice stopped it again. Alice was never targeted, and Dave's result on Erin and the push against Grace went ahead.

tip: Combine visit-role information with alignment checks. An Insomniac or Lookout result showing no Fabricator or Ex-Con visit means a Sheriff's Evil result can't be a frame. Then an Evil result on a Vanilla claimant is a real mechanical contradiction worth hanging on.
evidence: Heidi's N1 'Medic, Sheriff' result, plus Alice claiming the Medic visit, left Dave's Evil read on Frank as the only explanation. Carol and Dave used exactly that ('a Vanilla can't read Evil, and no frame was possible') to win the Day 3 vote.

tip: Post every new result, with target and outcome, in your first message each Day, before any nomination. Results revealed late or during a trial let opponents claim your story is growing. When you post a Not Evil result on a suspected Katana holder, say plainly that it clears nothing.
evidence: Dave held back his N2 target on Day 2 and posted N3 and N4 only alongside nominations or trials. Erin and Grace attacked this: 'his claims have grown every day' and 'N4 result first appeared after Bob nominated me'. Dave correctly noted that the holder reads Good, and Grace was still hanged.

tip: Once a Sheriff is corroborated and the Yakuza have shown they target him, keep protecting him with your free Standard protection. The Katana is only Standard, so each repeat save keeps the town's best information source alive.
evidence: Alice protected Dave on N2, N3 and N4. The Katana attacks on N2 and N4 both failed, and Dave lived to read Erin as Evil on N3.

tip: Nominate only when the Yes votes are clearly there; count stated Yes votes first. A failed nomination followed by a public walk-back wastes the round and makes you a target of suspicion.
evidence: Bob nominated Frank on Day 2 with only 4 Yes votes (5 needed), then publicly retracted his Yes. That gave the Yakuza ammunition against Bob for several days. Frank was hanged anyway on Day 3, once the case was stronger.

tip: Build a chain of census-cleared players early and target a census around one unknown, ideally with cleared players likely in the group. Once a group's other members are cleared, an 'X of 3 Good' result pins the remaining member exactly. Say so publicly, and note that Neutrals count as neither, so 'not Good' means Yakuza or Neutral.

When a cornered player claims Jester or Executioner on trial, test it against the win check. Ask whether the game should already have ended, and whether a kill-less night coincided with blocking them. Also check whether their earlier claims needed knowledge only a Yakuza info role could have, such as naming a role before its owner claimed. Those mechanical points beat behavioural reads.

Combine Fortune Teller counts, Cartographer sizes and map, and Lookout watches each morning into one visit ledger. Have everyone state their night targets, then reconcile the counts. A single unexplained visitor, or a missing kill on a block night, almost always names the Katana holder.
Block the most likely Katana holder every night, even repeatedly. Consecutive no-kill nights on your block target are strong evidence against them, and they deny Yakuza their token uses too.
Post your result and nominate in the same turn once the case is mechanical. Quick, unified Yes/Guilty votes leave Yakuza no room to build counter-narratives or burn ballot tokens.

When the Wiretap or Eavesdropper learns a planned test (for example, 'Oracle guesses X tonight'), assume the players in that PM will also guard the tester. Either kill the Lookout who proposed the test, or hold the Katana on a member whose cover claim already explains a visit. A Vanilla-claim holder seen at the victim cannot be defended.

A Fortune Teller plus a Cartographer turn every unexplained visit into a counted slot. Before any Yakuza visits (Katana or own action), check that the visit fits a public claim. Otherwise, act only from members who are already exposed, or skip the action.

A true-alignment Census Taker clears or condemns players in groups of three, and frames and the Katana can't fool it. Make it the first Katana target once it claims, ahead of Oracles and Profilers. Each night it lives, it chains new confirmed-Good players.

Never pass the Katana to a member a block-immune Party Animal has blocked before. A Party Animal repeats the block on its suspect, so the kill is lost (as happened N3 and N4). Give it to an unsuspected member instead, even if that member is more useful.

Profiler decoys are drawn from other real players' roles. Any Yakuza role on a confirmed-Good player's list proves that role is in the game. Post it at once, because it tells the town which Evil roles exist (for example, Wiretap means never PM plans).

Post your exact visited/visitors numbers every Day and immediately list the claimed visits that fill them. When the counts are combined with a Cartographer's group sizes and one map, they pin down exactly how many hidden visitors exist and where they can sit. A single unexplained visitor becomes a short suspect list.

A late Jester or Executioner claim on trial can be tested mechanically. Ask whether the game should have ended at the last Yakuza hanging. Check whether a kill was missing on the night only the claimant was blocked. Check whether a census reading of 'not Good' fits. If the visit counts show no unblocked Yakuza acted on a night they should have killed, the claimant is the last Yakuza.

Remember who claimed a role before its real owner spoke. Naming the exact role of a player who hadn't claimed yet (e.g. counterclaiming Oracle before the Oracle spoke) points to a Diviner, Surveyor or similar exact-role peek. Note it on your notepad on Day 2, because it becomes decisive later when the player retreats through cover claims.

Once a player is the mechanical Katana fit, block them every night until they're hanged. Repeated blocks on the likely holder cost the Yakuza kills and tokens, here for two straight nights. A no-kill night on which only one player was blocked is strong evidence for the next hang.

Combine independent count-based roles (Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Census Taker) and cross-verify them on yourself. Saying 'the census counted me Good, which I know is true' publicly turns one unverifiable claimant into a trusted source for everyone.

Spend map tokens on the player at the center of the live dispute, such as the Katana suspect or a claimed blocker. Then cross the exact group membership with the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts. Group size plus the FT counts pins down who the hidden visitor must be, and that turned a Lookout's word into a mechanical case.

When a player claims Jester or Executioner on trial, check the win condition. If the game didn't end after the last known Evil died, someone non-Village is still alive. Pair that with whether a kill happened on the night the claimant was blocked. A no-kill night right when the suspect was blocked is strong evidence that they hold the Katana.

Profiler fakes are drawn from other players' real roles. So a profile list that settles one player's role also proves the other listed roles are in play. Use this to list the likely Yakuza roles (e.g. Diviner, Wiretap, Ballot Stuffer) and check them off as players die.

Don't double-claim a unique info role like Oracle on Day 2 before the real holder has spoken. It forces an immediate counterclaim fight you lose to any census or profile, and the fallback claims (Roleplayer, then Jester) read as foreknowledge.
Keep a cheap repeating block (Party Animal) on the top Katana suspect every night once they are identified. Three straight blocks produced no-kill nights, which confirmed the holder.

Treat every private message as read by the Yakuza: a Wiretap sees the contents of all PMs and nobody is told it exists. Never PM a night plan or target. Coordinate tests in public in general terms, or not at all. My PM suggesting Grace's Oracle guess got her killed that same night.

Watch the player whose planned test would expose the Yakuza, such as an Oracle or investigator about to resolve a 50/50. They are the most likely Katana target, and a lone visitor to a Katana victim is a near-certain catch.

Combine the Fortune Teller's counts with the Cartographer's group sizes and maps. Together they pin down exactly how many hidden visitors exist, so a lone visitor from a Lookout or a 'no visit' claim can be confirmed or broken mechanically.

When a cornered player claims Jester on trial, test it mechanically first. Did the game fail to end when it should have if they were Neutral? Was there no kill exactly on the night they were blocked? Did they know a role they shouldn't have? Then hang with a bare majority if possible.

A player who announces tonight's check target is giving the blockers and the Katana a free read. Expect them to be blocked or killed, and don't treat their resulting 'no result' as evidence either way.

In the standard setup every role except Vanilla Villager appears at most once, so any non-Vanilla claim can be counterclaimed. Claiming Oracle or another info role on Day 2, before the real holder has spoken, is a coin flip that marks you as a liar. Claim Vanilla (2 allowed), or wait until the role is uncontested.

Before a late fake Jester or Executioner claim, run the win check yourself. If your teammate's death would have ended the game when only Village remained, ignoring Jesters, then town will say a real Jester means another evil is still alive. A quiet night after a block then proves you are the holder. A Neutral fake claim only works while another non-Village player is plausibly alive.

When a block-immune blocker (Party Animal or Pharmacist) blocks your suspected holder every night, don't give the Katana back to that player. Kill the blocker, or keep the Katana on an unsuspected member and aim it at the blocker. Two wasted Katana nights cost us the game.

With a Fortune Teller and a Cartographer both posting, every unexplained visit is counted to the player. Map tokens then pin down group membership by name. A Yakuza with a visiting role (Diviner, Fabricator) who claims no visits must skip their action. Otherwise, pick a target that a claimed visitor or the Katana target already explains, so the counts add up.
Never PM a night plan. A Wiretap reads every PM, and one PM telling the Oracle whom to guess got her killed that night. Plans and suggestions belong in your own will or in your head.

Treat every private message as read by a Wiretap. Never confirm tonight's target by PM, not even a one-line 'I'll do that'. If someone suggests a target by PM, don't reply at all and just act. The reply alone can get you killed that night.

Check the setup's uniqueness rule. If every non-Vanilla role appears at most once, any duplicate claim proves one claimant is lying (or is a Roleplayer). Settle it at once with a true-alignment census or a profile instead of debating it.

Don't spend an early guess blindly on a quiet player. Aim guesses at a claimed role in a live dispute (e.g. 'Mallory = Party Animal'). A right guess clears one side, and a wrong guess exposes a liar. Either way the result is publicly useful.

When a cornered player claims Jester or another Neutral, test it mechanically. Ask whether the game should have ended at the last hanging, and whether nobody died on the night that player was blocked. A no-kill night that matches a block on the claimant is strong evidence they hold the Katana.
Chain census results. Players who know their own alignment can confirm a census group they were in. That makes the Census Taker credible, and later counts then isolate the Evil player by subtraction.

Once a block-immune blocker (Party Animal or Pharmacist) has publicly blocked one of your members, assume they will block that member every night. Don't route the Katana or any token-spending action through that member. A self-only action like the Ballot Stuffer's is still stopped by a block, and you lose both the kill and the night.

Never announce in public whom you will 'check' tonight as part of a fake investigator claim. It invites the accused, or a blocker, to role-block you, and that silences your real actions too. If you need a fake result, report it the next day without pre-announcing.

A Census Taker counts true alignment, so the Katana holder's Good disguise and frames don't fool it. It also never counts Neutrals. Yakuza should kill a claimed Census Taker early. A census that cleared some players gives the town a reliable base, and its Good-count makes the 'I'm Neutral' dodge checkable.

A late fake-Jester claim fails on R1. If the game didn't end when the previous non-Village player died, someone non-Jester and non-Village is still alive. The town will spot it if you are the last suspect. Also, in setups where every non-Vanilla role appears at most once, any non-Vanilla claim can be counterclaimed. Claim Vanilla Villager (up to 2 allowed) or a role nobody else has claimed.

When the Wiretap reads a Village PM plan (e.g. 'guess X tonight'), the sender knows who the partner is and may watch them. Killing that partner exposes the holder to a Lookout. Use your least-exposed member as holder, or kill the watcher instead.

When a claimed Neutral (Jester or Executioner) is on trial, check the win condition first. If the last-known Yakuza just died and the game didn't end, a non-Village player is still alive. If the Jester claimant is the only plausible one left, the claim falls apart.

A role named before its holder claimed it is foreknowledge. An Executioner doesn't know its target's role, but a Diviner or Wiretap can. Find which info role could have produced that knowledge from the Day 1 or Night 1 visit math (e.g. a Diviner group that includes the person).

With secret ballots you can say 'Innocent' publicly to cover the Jester risk and still vote Guilty, but only when you're confident. The cleaner play is to agree a bare Guilty majority so confirmed info roles stay on Innocent.

Claim Ex-Con early and ask for census checks. The census counts true alignment, so it is the one tool that clears you. Keep a will that maps where Cartographer and Lookout data place your random visit each night, so sightings of you aren't misread.

Combine Fortune Teller counts with Cartographer group sizes every night. Together they pin hidden visitors very precisely: one unexplained slot in a group plus a 'no action' claim from a player in it is a strong lead.

Night-1 is the most dangerous night to hold a one-shot token, but a quiet player can still be a random Katana target. Write your planned action and role in your will before Night 1. If you die, the will alone tells town that an Archivist existed and lets them rule out one claim slot.

Combine the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts with the Cartographer's group sizes and a map. Together they force exact visit structures and leave room for only one unclaimed visitor, which exposes Vanilla or Roleplayer claims hiding a visit. Ask every visitor to post their target, then fit the counts.

A Profiler's two fake roles come from other players actually in the game, so every list reveals roles in play (e.g. Diviner and Wiretap). Cross that with census-cleared players to pin both a person's role and which Yakuza roles still need finding.

A late Jester claim from a census 'not Good' player can be tested mechanically. If the game didn't end when the previous Yakuza died, check whether a no-kill night lines up with a block on that player. Also check whether they named a role before its owner claimed it. Foreknowledge points to a Diviner, not an Executioner.
Keep a block-immune Party Animal blocking the prime Katana suspect every night. Repeated blocks on the right player produce no-kill nights, and those nights both save lives and prove the holder.

Once a Lookout places a player at a Katana victim, block that player every night until they are hanged. Then move the block to the next suspect. Repeated blocks on the likely holder cost Yakuza kills on N3 and N4. A night with no death while you block one player is mechanical evidence against them.

When a player claims a role before its real owner has spoken (e.g. a counterclaim of Oracle), ask how they knew to pick it. Diviner, Wiretap and other Yakuza info gives that kind of foreknowledge. Combine it with a count-based check, such as a census reading 'not Good', before trusting a late Jester or Executioner claim.

Test a late Jester claim with the win check. If the game didn't end when the previous Yakuza died, some non-Village player is still alive. Then ask whether a night with no kill fits only the claimant being blocked. The Census Taker's 'X of 3 Good' cannot tell a Neutral from Evil, so use the night-kill pattern to decide.

A Yakuza claiming Oracle or another unique role against a census-cleared player gets exposed almost at once, and the 'Roleplayer' retreat only buys time. Claim a role with no unique-role counterclaim risk and no checkable visits.

Combine Cartographer maps, Fortune Teller counts and Lookout watches each Day into one full visit account. With all three posted, any hidden visitor or false 'no action' claim is forced out within a day.
