When a Neutral claim (Jester/Executioner) appears after a Yakuza hang, check the win condition. If the game didn't end, someone non-Village is still alive. Then ask whether that player was unblocked on a no-kill night. A no-kill night where only the claimant was blocked is near-proof that the claimant is the last Yakuza.

Combine Fortune Teller counts with Cartographer group sizes every night and enumerate every claimed visit. When the totals leave exactly one unexplained slot, the lone visitor seen by a census-cleared Lookout is effectively proven. Treat it as a hang, not a coin flip.

A claim that names a role before its holder has claimed it (e.g. counterclaiming Oracle before the real Oracle speaks) suggests the claimant has night info, such as Diviner or Wiretap. Flag it, since it later breaks Neutral cover stories.

As a census-cleared Vanilla, spend your budget on visit-count reconciliation and on naming tests for investigators, not on claims. Volunteer for Guilty votes on possible-Jester trials so the confirmed info roles can stay Innocent.
Block the top mechanical suspect every night, even after they are exposed. Repeated blocks on the likely Katana holder produced two no-kill nights and shut down the Yakuza endgame.

The two fake roles on a profile are drawn from other living players' real roles, so every list also tells you what roles are in play. Combine it with claims and census results. A profile on a cleared player can still confirm Yakuza roles (e.g. Diviner and Wiretap), and that tells the town to treat every PM as read.

Ask your target to state their exact role publicly before you post the list. Then the result is a clean test they can't tailor. Spend later tokens on the contested half of a claim fight (e.g. two visitors to a Katana victim). A list that omits the claimed role is a hard, hangable contradiction.

When a census-flagged player claims Jester or Executioner on trial, run the win-check logic. If an earlier hanging of a confirmed Yakuza didn't end the game and no kill happened on the one night the claimant was blocked, the 'Neutral' story requires another unblocked Yakuza who chose not to kill. Also look for the claimant having shown knowledge of a role they couldn't have known.
Block your top Katana suspect every night, even repeatedly. Each block on the real holder is a night with no kill. The no-kill nights then become evidence that the blocked player held the Katana.
Assume a Wiretap exists until proven otherwise. Never plan night tests by PM. A PM saying 'guess Mallory = Party Animal' got the Oracle killed the very next night.

Once one player is the leading Katana suspect, block them every night until they are hanged, and re-target the moment suspicion shifts. Blocking the holder cancels the kill and any token use, and a no-kill night on a blocked suspect is itself evidence.
evidence: Mallory blocked Heidi on N2 (her ballot token failed) and N3 (Katana holder, no kill), then Frank on N4 (Katana holder, no kill). The N3 and N4 no-kill nights became key evidence in both hangs.

tip: Anchor the Day on results that ignore disguises (Census Taker, exact-role checks), and have players who appear in a census group confirm it on themselves. Self-verified true-alignment results turn into group eliminations that fake claims can't argue past.
evidence: Carol, Dave and Mallory each confirmed Alice's N2 '3/3 Good' on themselves. That made her N3 '1 of Heidi/Ivan Evil' and N4 'Frank not Good' decisive.

tip: Watch the player whose planned test or claim most threatens the Yakuza, not just last night's victims. The Yakuza will kill to stop that test, and a watch on them catches the holder.
evidence: Erin watched Grace on N2, the night Grace planned the Mallory=Party Animal guess. Bob killed Grace and Erin named him as Grace's lone visitor, which hanged him on Day 3 with 10 Guilty.

tip: Never put tonight's plans in private messages. A Wiretap or Eavesdropper reads them, and it tells the Yakuza whom to kill. Coordinate tests in vague public terms or not at all.
evidence: Erin's PM telling Grace to guess Mallory = Party Animal was read by Wiretap Bob, and the Yakuza killed Grace that night specifically to stop the test.

tip: Fake-claim a common, hard-to-check role, never a unique info role that a real player may hold. A collision forces a retreat that marks you for the rest of the game.
evidence: Frank claimed Oracle on Day 2, Grace counterclaimed with census and profile backing, and Frank had to fall back to 'Roleplayer'. That cover died when Alice's N4 census showed him not Good.

tip: Don't give the Katana to a player who is being role-blocked every night. Pick a holder the blocker isn't targeting. If no holder is safe, accept the risk on one who can still kill rather than wasting the night.
evidence: On N3 the Katana moved to Heidi even though Mallory had blocked her on N2 and kept saying she would. Mallory blocked her again, and both the kill on Olivia and the ballot token failed.

tip: As a fake investigator, don't announce tomorrow's check target. It gives the target and their allies a public excuse to block or test you, and it shows that your result is chosen, not found.
evidence: Heidi announced on Day 2 that she would 'check Mallory'. Mallory openly blocked her every night after that, and Heidi never got a single fake result in to muddy the case.

tip: When a cornered player claims Jester, test it on mechanics. Ask whether the game should already have ended if they were Neutral, and whether a kill happened on the night they were blocked. Don't let the revenge threat alone scare off the vote.
evidence: Frank's Day 5 Jester claim fell apart because the game didn't end at Heidi's hanging and N4, the night Frank was blocked, had no kill. The town hanged him and won immediately.

tip: A publicly claimed Vigilante with tokens is the Katana's first target. The Katana hit me the same night I finally fired. Take a shot on a strong lead as soon as you have one, and don't sit on tokens while your claim is public.

When announced trial totals don't match the named votes, list every voter, dead ones included, before naming a living suspect. Bob was the extra Guilty on Frank's trial, and the living players hanged Carol on a count that only fit a dead liar's vote.
A fake Tracker claim with a visit is checkable against any Insomniac or Lookout count. Claim a Village role whose visit the public counts can't contradict, or claim Vanilla with no visit at all.
Don't nominate on a single withdrawn claim. Give a second concrete mechanical reason before the nomination, so the hang doesn't rest on a player's correction.

An Insomniac count lists visitor roles, not who visited whom. A Grunt plus Lookout on a Katana victim proves only that a Yakuza visited, so say the count names roles and avoid claiming a specific visitor.

applies_to: Informant and any Yakuza who states a trial vote publicly
tip: Your stated vote must match your real ballot. The announced totals are a mechanical check, and as Informant I said Innocent on Frank but voted Guilty. The 5-Guilty total then exposed the mismatch, and the Village used it to hang Carol. If you deviate, do it in the plan, never in the claimed vote.

applies_to: Yakuza making a fake Village claim
tip: Choose a fake role whose claimed visits no living Village count can contradict. Frank claimed Tracker and tracked Carol, who visited nobody, and Heidi's Insomniac count refuted it. A withdrawn false claim looked worse than a quiet Vanilla, and it made him the nomination target.

A Vigilante with tokens can kill the same night as your Katana attack, so the attack on the Vigilante does not stop its shot. Bob died to Alice's Basic shot while the Katana killed Alice. Track the Vigilante's token count and consider blocking or protecting the likely shooter earlier, before it fires.

Keep daytime private messages out of Day 4 and any Day when a teammate is at risk. Carol's two private messages to Erin and Grace were cited publicly as suspicious, and Grace used them to push the hang.

Before claiming a visit-based role such as Tracker or Lookout, check the visit against the Insomniac and Lookout counts. A fake track on a player who visited nobody gets exposed at once, so claim Vanilla unless the visit fits what the Village can see.

Teammates must state only the trial vote they will actually cast. A teammate who said Innocent but voted Guilty made the announced total unexplainable and pinned the discrepancy on a living member. Agree trial votes in night chat and keep public statements matched to them.

Do not defend a doomed teammate at length or vote Innocent publicly for them. Your visible Innocent vote becomes the target once the hang is locked, so vote with the Village when the outcome is already fixed and save your credibility for later.

Every daytime private message reveals that two players talked, even when the contents stay hidden. Two PMs from me during the last Day were read as coordination. Make defenses in public chat and avoid PMs when your side is under pressure.

When a trial total does not match the named votes, list every voter, including dead ones. A discrepancy can come from a dead player's hidden vote, so do not hang a living player just because they are the only one left to explain it.

Announcing your watch target early tells the Yakuza where to kill, and a claimed Lookout was killed the next night. Claim when your first result is corroborated, and watch the suspected Katana holder's likely visits rather than a random player.

Before hanging on a trial-count mismatch, have every player named in the discrepancy restate their own vote, and check whether a dead player's announced Innocent was the real source. Here the extra Guilty was Bob's, not Carol's, and Carol was hanged on a guess.

Never publicly state a trial vote that differs from your ballot. A Yakuza saying Innocent while voting Guilty creates a count mismatch that a living teammate can be pinned on; if you must vote with the town, say so openly and never let the mismatch fall on a teammate.

A withdrawn claim that conflicts with an Insomniac or Lookout count is a real contradiction, but it is weak alone as a hang reason. Ask for a second mechanical contradiction before nominating, and check every claimed visit against the visitor-role counts.

When a trial total exceeds the Guilty voters you can name, the extra Guilty may come from a dead player who said Innocent in chat (Bob here), not only from a living defender. Ask every living voter for their trial vote before hanging on the discrepancy.

applies_to: Lookout, Insomniac and other information roles
tip: Post each night result at the first chance, not at the next Day's start. Dave died on Night 2 holding a fresh watch that never reached the Village, and the Katana kills information roles at night.

Don't hold every token until Night 3. Alice's Basic shot on Bob killed a Yakuza, but it came too late, and she died the same night. A single-token shot on the best Night 1 or 2 lead could have hit a Yakuza earlier.

A player who keeps defending teammates the Village has already hanged, and sends private messages to the living voters, is a tell. Check every claim's visits against the Insomniac count, since a false Tracker track broke it.

A Katana holder must be a living Yakuza. When an Insomniac lists visitor roles and a Grunt visits the same target as a dead Lookout, the Grunt is the attacker, so narrow the holder to the living players who could be that Grunt.

Visit-counting roles such as the Insomniac see a Katana holder even when the holder has no role action, because the Katana attack is a visit. With a living Insomniac, a Grunt holder who attacks is exposed on that night. Choose a holder with a cover, or skip the attack while a counter is alive.

Never claim a Village role whose visits contradict public counts. My Night 1 Tracker claim, with a track on Carol, conflicted with the Lookout and Insomniac counts. Withdrawing it after pressure became the lynch basis. Claim Vanilla unless your claimed visits will match what the counters report.

A frame only changes alignment checks, so with no living Sheriff or Seer it does nothing. Spend the fabricator token early on a Village player who is a live threat, or use the forged will before a likely death, rather than holding it to the end unused.

When a teammate's hang is doomed, vote with the town. Innocent votes from a defender show in the announced totals, and players who match totals to stated votes will find the mismatch. Defending a lost cause exposed Carol.

applies_to: Yakuza (Fabricator, Grunt and any role that claims a visit-based Village role)
tip: If you claim a visit-based Village role, check it against every public visitor count from earlier nights. A claim that contradicts a count gets you hanged even if you withdraw it, so claim only roles whose visits you could really have made, or claim a role with no visit.

When a trial total is one higher than the named Guilty voters, list every dead player whose stated vote could explain it before pinning it on a living defender. A dead liar's extra vote can look like a living player's guilt, and a hang on that guess can be wrong.

Private message existence is public. Sending a PM to a voter during a suspect's Day reads as coordination, so keep private messages out of the days when votes are close, or explain the content at once.

Do not hold all three tokens for a perfect lead. Fire on the best Yakuza read by Night 2 or 3, since the Katana holder can kill you before the tokens matter, and a dead Vigilante with unused tokens helps nobody.

Before pinning a trial-total discrepancy on a living player, list every voter's stated vote, including dead players' public statements. The extra Guilty came from a dead Informant who said Innocent, so the contradiction was the dead player's lie, not the living defender's.
Count Vanilla Villager claims against the setup cap on Day 2. When three or four players claim Vanilla and the cap is two, at least one claim is false, which is a hard check that needs no reads.

Roles-only visitor lists become useful when matched to a Lookout's named watch target. A Grunt visitor on the night a watched player is attacked points at the Katana holder. Ask the Lookout to post the watch target each Day so the counts can be cross-checked.

Use a Basic shot on a confirmed lead early, not on the last night. Holding all three tokens until death lets the Katana kill you with tokens unused, so fire on the first strong lead and reveal the role publicly when the shot kills.

Do not repeatedly defend the same teammate in trial votes. Visible defenses of a doomed member make the surviving teammate the obvious count suspect, so split the defense across players and let the teammate's Innocent vote stand without extra pushing.

Before fake-claiming, check every public visitor count (Insomniac, Lookout, Fortune Teller) already posted. Never claim a visiting role or a visit that those results rule out. If you must claim Vanilla, count the existing Vanilla claims against the setup cap of 2 first.
evidence: Frank claimed Tracker on Carol after Heidi had posted 'one visitor, a Lookout' and Dave had confirmed being it. Alice, Erin, Dave and Heidi all called it a broken visit claim within a round.

tip: Never switch claims once cornered. A withdrawn claim plus a fallback claim that overflows a role cap is a mechanical case on its own. Commit to one cover from the start, agreed in night chat.
evidence: Frank switched from Tracker to Vanilla, making four Vanilla claims (Grace, Carol, Erin, Frank). Every Guilty speech on Day 3 cited the withdrawn claim, and he was hanged 5-2.

tip: Your public vote statement must match your secret ballot. If a teammate is doomed, don't defend them, then vote Guilty and say Guilty. Saying Innocent while voting Guilty puts a hidden vote in the total that points at whoever is left among the stated Innocents.
evidence: Bob and Carol both said Innocent on Frank, but Bob voted Guilty. The 5-2 total exposed one hidden Guilty among Bob, Carol and Frank. After Bob died, Grace and Heidi pinned it on Carol and hanged her.

tip: Kill the information role that will expose your Katana holder next: an Insomniac or watcher who has announced tokens and plans. Don't skip the Night 1 kill when you have three members; it hands the town free, uncontested reads.
evidence: Heidi said on Day 2 she had 1 token and would stay awake. The Yakuza killed Dave instead, and Heidi's 'Grunt, Lookout' read proved a living Yakuza held the Katana. The Night 1 no-kill also let Heidi and Dave lock in the read that exposed Frank.

tip: After every trial, reconcile the announced totals against each player's stated vote. When a total exceeds the stated Guilty votes, the hidden voter is among those who claimed the other side. Deaths narrow that group to one name.
evidence: Grace listed 4 stated Guilty votes against the 5 announced. With Bob and Frank dead, only Carol remained of the three stated Innocents, and the town hanged the last Yakuza.

tip: Once a mechanically exposed Yakuza is hanged, shoot whoever defended them hardest, even with a cheap Basic shot. Don't die holding tokens.
evidence: Alice shot Bob, Frank's main defender, on Night 3 with one token and killed the Informant on the same night she was killed. That set up the 1v3 endgame.

tip: Don't publicly raise deductions that corner your own team, such as role-cap counts that implicate teammates' claims. Let the town find them, or steer the attention elsewhere.
evidence: Bob pointed out that three Vanilla claims couldn't all be real. That primed the four-Vanilla contradiction which doomed Frank and kept suspicion on Carol.

tip: Track the win threshold from the start: with 13 players the Vulture wins once 3 or fewer are alive at a Day start, so every death (including Village hangs) moves you closer; avoid nominating or voting in ways that risk a Vulture-hostile result, and let the Yakuza and Serial Killer thin the field.

Watch for two conflicting Lookout claims early: the Chronicler mark and Erin's visit log were the only checkable facts, and Judy's fake Roleplayer reads cost the town a long argument. Ask which claims have an independent confirmation before voting.

Do not let a nomination pile-on on a single wording quirk (Olivia's 'attacked nobody publicly') or a private message decide a hang; several hangs this game rested on momentum rather than a mechanical fit, which removed town power roles and helped the Yakuza and Serial Killer.
Medic protection and Lookout watches are only verifiable if each role posts its exact result; when two claimed roles disagree, have each post the full result and who else was visited before any vote.
The Ritualist guess on a Vanilla claim is a risky gamble; a wrong guess exposes the Ritualist publicly at the next Day, which is what happened to Ivan.

Before every hang, compute the Vulture threshold, max(floor(N/4), 2) with N the starting player count (3 at 13 players). A hang that drops the living count to that number can hand a lone Vulture the win, so count it alongside Jester and Executioner checks.

When two players claim the same role with conflicting results, test each result against other players' own logs (Medic protections, Chronicler marks, dead visitors, a dead Lookout's visit). A Roleplayer can fake Lookout, and a Chronicler mark on the suspect reveals the role on death, so spend it early as a cheap test.

Free Standard protection costs no token, Strong costs one, and Strong on yourself costs two. A Medic at zero tokens cannot save themself from a Standard Katana, so plan the last token for the player who must survive, and expect to be the next target.
Once a watcher posts a result, the Yakuza tend to kill that watcher quickly. Post results early and clearly, and ask a Medic to cover the watcher on nights when the watch matters most.

Day 2 conflict between two Lookouts stalled the whole game through repeated yes/no demands with no new facts. Agree early on one concrete test (a Profiler check, a Chronicler mark, or a log comparison) and push for that test instead of repeating questions.

A Census Taker's group result counts true alignment across three players, so a 2-of-3 Good count only narrows things; with a visit-based role, spend the census on the player most likely to be targeted, since you die on Night 1 if the Yakuza see you as a threat.

When two players claim the same watch role with conflicting results, check each claim against the other players' own logs (who they say they visited) before voting; a visit a player denies on their own log is a mechanical fact you can test.
Do not hang or nominate on a single private-message request alone; ask the accused for the exact content of the message and weigh that against what the message actually changes.
Track claims in a notepad with each person's Day votes and each announced total, so that a player who switches a vote or whose stated vote contradicts the count stands out early.
Remember Chronicler marks are visits, and a Chronicler's mark reveals the true role on death; a marked player's exact role becomes public, which can settle claims quickly.

applies_to: Yakuza with a Ritualist or any guess-based attack
tip: A wrong Ritualist guess is announced publicly at the start of the next Day and outs you. Use a guess only when a miss cannot expose you or when it closes the game that night, and never on a Vanilla claim the Village can't check.

applies_to: Village, especially Chronicler and Lookout claimants
tip: A Chronicler mark reveals the marked player's true role when they die, however they die. When two Lookouts conflict, a Roleplayer can be the liar, and that is only exposed by a mark or a death. Keep a Chronicler's mark on the suspect with the most contested claim.

Neutral killers act on their own schedule and can kill your own members, as the Serial Killer did to Dave and Heidi. Post no attack-related remarks in public, and check which nights a rival killer struck before planning your Katana target.

Count the Vulture threshold early: max(floor(N/4), 2) living players at the start of a Day with a silent Vanilla claim can win alone. Avoid hangs that bring the living count down to that number unless you can prove the remaining players are not the Vulture.

A wrong Vanilla claim by a suspected Yakuza is not proof of anything; a Ritualist or Roleplayer can also claim Vanilla. Weigh a claim by whether its visits, tokens and results fit the posted logs, not by its role name.

Free Standard protection only covers others. Self-protection with Standard still costs 1 token, so once tokens run out you cannot protect yourself. Keep your last token for self-protection once a Katana holder is alive and you are the obvious next target.

Spend Strong protection on a claimed Lookout only when a specific attack is credible tonight. Spending the last token on a night with no reported attack left the Katana free to kill the Medic the next night.

Track each night's visits to the victim of a Katana death. The holder must have visited that victim, so list everyone who denied a visit and look for the one who cannot be explained by a role-block or a protection claim.

When two Lookout claims conflict and the watcher's target is dead or fake, do not hang on a PM or on wording alone. Ask for one checkable visit, and if nothing checkable comes, hold the vote rather than follow the crowd.

A Serial Killer's kills are a mechanical pattern: track which player was attacked by a Strong attack and which players survived or died, and compare against each suspect's claimed night actions before deciding who is Neutral.

applies_to: Village roles with protective or investigative tokens (Medic, Lookout)
tip: Track token spending exactly: a Medic's free Standard protection is the only thing that stops a Standard Katana, so once tokens run out the Yakuza can pick off the protector. Spend Strong protection only when a known Standard attack is coming, not on a guess.

When two Lookouts conflict, check each claimed visit against the named visitor's own log and the Chronicler/Medic logs. A Roleplayer's watch results are fabricated, so a single contradicting Lookout can be the fake one; a Chronicler mark on a suspected Roleplayer is a strong signal.

Do not hang on a wording-only oddity (like an unprompted 'I attacked nobody' line) unless it is backed by a checkable contradiction; the same goes for private messages, which can be innocent test-probes and are easy to weaponize as momentum.

Vote for a Katana holder who has survived at least two Yakuza attacks only after checking which living player has been attacked less often; a Village Medic with tokens can make a Standard attack fail repeatedly, so split targets early rather than retrying the same kill.
A Vulture wins as soon as three or fewer players are alive at the start of a Day; in a 3-player endgame the Vulture can win alone, so count the living total before voting.

A Chronicler mark is a visit to the target, so a 'no action' claim can be false for the visit logs; if you mark someone, say so plainly early, because the mark quietly lets an opponent's Lookout read contradict your no-action claim.

When two Lookouts give conflicting visit results, look for a result that a dead player or a Roleplayer could have produced; ask which claim can be verified by a second independent log before voting, and do not let the nominator's own watch be treated as proof.

Plan the Katana holder and target in night chat with all members submitting identical votes, and avoid a Ritualist guess that exposes you if it misses; a wrong guess announces you on the next Day and the Village can then vote on you.

Do not let a single unexplained wording (like an unprompted 'I attacked nobody' line) or a private message alone carry a hang; demand a concrete visit or result that contradicts a claim before a Guilty vote.

Track announced vote totals against the number of voters each Day, including Ballot Stuffer doubled votes, because a total above the voter count means a manipulation, and a Yes total that fits known votes is the cleanest check on who is lying.

A Profiler's three-role result is only weak evidence on its own; spend profile tokens on a player whose claim is contradicted, and check whether the result set includes a role that the claimant's own logs already rule out before treating it as proof.

When two players claim the same unique-looking role with conflicting results, look at who each claimant nominated or pushed first; a nomination that immediately follows a conflicting claim is itself a lead worth weighing.

Yakuza with a Katana can use a Medic's exhausted tokens as a timing signal: once a Medic is at zero tokens, a Standard Katana kills them and their protection history stops mattering, so plan to remove the Medic before the Lookout is confirmed.

Before voting Guilty on a late-game nominee, demand that the nominator name a concrete visit or log contradiction; momentum from a single PM or wording complaint hanged several Village players this game.
A Chronicler's mark is a visit and can be revealed on death; players who deny night actions should be checked against any mark or visit that the Chronicler or Lookout can show.

Don't spend a one-shot Ritualist guess on a Vanilla Villager claim when the Village has not yet been reduced to a checkable set; a wrong guess publicly outs you at the next Day start and removes your night-kill cover. Save guesses for when a correct hit ends the game or a claim is already contradicted.

Before the final stretch, check whether a teammate's planned Ballot Stuffer or Clerk-style Day manipulation actually changes the outcome; a doubled vote only helps if the nominee is already likely to be voted out, so pair it with a nomination that can pass.

Keep the Katana holder's daytime posture consistent: when the Village's checks name a visitor to a Katana victim, deny-only answers ('I visited nobody') become checkable lies. Prefer to admit a plausible visit or stay silent rather than issue a flat denial that a watcher or Medic log can contradict.

When two Lookouts conflict, a Roleplayer-style claim can be flushed out by a Chronicler mark or a Night 2 cross-check; spend the Chronicler or Profiler result on the disputed claim early, because the Yakuza will target whichever watcher is most informative.
A Vulture wins alone once only three players remain alive at the start of a Day; track the living count against max(floor(N/4),2) before each Day so you can see when the game ends by Vulture win.

applies_to: Village roles that receive investigation results
tip: When two players claim the same watch role with conflicting results, do not weigh them by who speaks loudest. Ask for an exact-wording result and check whether the claimed visitor could have been a Chronicler mark or a role-block. If the claim can't be tested, don't let the crowd hang one of them; push for a Profiler, Medic or Chronicler cross-check first.

A Roleplayer shows fake results that look real, so a single watch claim is weak evidence. Before trusting a claimed Lookout, check whether its named visits are contradicted by the named players' own logs, and whether a corroborating role confirms the claim. Track which claims were ever independently verified.

Don't hang a player on a stated 'mechanical fit' that is really a wording complaint or a private message. Olivia and Frank were hanged on oddities like a loose remark or a PM, and those reads cost the Village its remaining power and checking roles. Require a result that a third party can verify before a Guilty vote.

A Chronicler mark is a visit, and a marked player's role is revealed on death. Use a Lookout watch on the Chronicler or the marked player to verify the mark, and announce the mark publicly once confirmed so the Village can cross-check visit claims rather than arguing from memory.

When a Katana or Serial Killer kill happens, the attacker must have visited the victim that night. List the living players who could have been the holder, then check each one's stated no-visit claim against logs and other claims. A player who denies a visit that the kill needs is the strongest lead, so press that denial early instead of waiting for more claims.

Track who votes Guilty or Yes on the same nominee in tight groups, and who pushes a hang right after a claimed watch clashes with another claim. Pairs that push together across several hangs are a stronger signal than any single hunch. Check whether they can point to a mechanical fit before the trial.

Do not send a private message to a claimed Lookout that asks which players they will watch next. Everyone sees that a PM was sent, and the content is easy to frame as steering the watch. Ask factual questions in public instead, and keep watch-planning talk out of PMs.

applies_to: Lookout and anyone weighing Lookout claims
tip: A Chronicler mark counts as a visit, so a 'no action' claim from a Chronicler does not rule out a visit. Before trusting or rejecting a Lookout's visitor result, check whether a mark, a block or a protection could explain it, and check the named visitor's own log. A Roleplayer's watch results are fake, and their reveal voids every watch they reported.

Ivan's Ritualist guess on Alice (a Vulture) was a wasted, exposing gamble; a Ritualist guess that misses announces you publicly as a Ritualist at the next Day, so only guess when a hit wins the game immediately.

Check whether a claimed visit can be corroborated by the claimed visitor's own log: Judy's Lookout reads were contradicted by Grace's and Erin's logs, and that cross-check was the only thing that exposed the Roleplayer.

Do not hang on a single private-message pattern or on the 'who pushes hardest' signal; Mallory and Frank were hanged on PM-steering reads that were not mechanically proven, and the Vulture survived to win.

A Vulture is a unique role that wins alone once few players remain; when the living count hits the Vulture threshold, track every unexplained survivor, because hanging the remaining Village can hand it the win.

Ballot Stuffer doubling only helps when the Yakuza can still reach a majority; spending it on a Day when the Village has three to four live votes gives little, so save it for the trial that actually decides the game.

Strong Attacks beat Standard self-protection, so a Medic with one token left cannot save themselves; a Strong attack on a Medic-protected target still fails if they have Strong, so track token counts from the public Medic log before choosing targets.

When two players claim the same role and give conflicting results, check each result against the other players' own logs and the visits they name; a result that names a visitor who denies the visit, or a dead visitor, is far weaker than one that can be cross-checked.

Avoid hanging the player whose private messages look suspicious on the strength of PMs alone; ask whether the PM can be explained by testing a claim, and vote on a checkable contradiction in public results.

Count living players before every nomination threshold (for example 5 Yes with 9 alive, 3 Yes with 5 alive) and remember that a Chronicler mark reveals a player's role on death, which exposes Roleplayers and Lookouts.
Do not spend a Ritualist guess on a Village claim that a Vanilla player will not match; with few players left, a wrong guess publicly exposes you, so keep the guess for a near-certain role.

In the endgame, check every win threshold before choosing a kill, including a possible Vulture's (max(floor(N/4),2) alive). If your team will hold a voting majority the next Day, night-kill the quiet, unverified claimant and leave the confirmed villager to be hanged. Never make your win depend on a role guess about an unverified player.
evidence: On Night 6 the Yakuza Katana'd confirmed Lookout Bob and guessed Alice was a Vanilla Villager with the Ritualist. The guess was wrong because Alice was the Vulture, so 3 players remained and Alice won. A Katana on Alice would have left Bob, Ivan and Niaj, and the two Yakuza votes would have hanged Bob.

tip: To catch the Katana holder, watch the player most likely to be killed tonight (a confirmed or exposed power role), not the player you suspect. Watching a suspect only clears them, while watching the next victim names the killer.
evidence: Bob watched Mallory on Night 4 while Grace, the confirmed Chronicler, was killed, and Alice on Night 5 while Erin, the claimed Medic, was killed. Ivan held the Katana on every night, so watching either victim would have exposed him.

tip: Do not hang someone only because of what their private message said. Asking a Lookout whom they will watch, or suggesting targets, is normal villager behaviour. Ask for a visit or vote contradiction instead, and be suspicious of the quiet players who rush to pile onto a hang based on a PM.
evidence: Mallory (Day 5) and Frank (Day 6), both Vanilla Villagers, were hanged 6-1 and 4-1 on Bob's 'Lookout hunt' and 'steering' cases. Ivan and Niaj voted Guilty both times, and these Village losses brought the game to the Vulture threshold.

tip: Keep your fake claim to plain, stock wording. Never mention attacks, kills or night actions you supposedly don't have, even to deny them. One odd phrase can become the whole case against you.
evidence: Olivia, the Serial Killer claiming Vanilla Villager, wrote on Day 2 'no night action on Night 1 (I attacked nobody publicly)'. That line alone got her nominated and hanged 6-3 on Day 4.

tip: Track who voted Yes on failed nominations and on lynches of players who are later revealed Good. Use the announced Yes totals together with each player's public statements to find hidden Yakuza, who blend in by echoing the consensus.
evidence: The failed Day 3 nomination of Bob got 4 Yes votes: Judy, Niaj, Alice and Ivan. Nobody asked who besides Judy voted Yes, so Ivan and Niaj, who repeated others' questions every round, went five Days without being nominated.

applies_to: Chronicler / anyone with a contested claim
tip: Use exact-role tools (a Chronicler mark, Coroner, Profiler) on one side of a duplicate claim. If you are the claimant and your results are contradicted by several independent logs, consider that you may be a Roleplayer, and stop pushing nominations against the other claimant.
evidence: Grace marked Judy on Night 2, and when Judy was hanged her role was revealed as Roleplayer, which settled the Lookout dispute. Before that, Judy had nominated the real Lookout Bob on Day 3 even though Erin's and Grace's logs both contradicted her results.

tip: Don't spend your last Strong token repeating protection on the same player. Cover the other exposed power role, or keep a token so you can protect yourself once you have claimed Medic.
evidence: Erin spent her last token on Bob again on Night 4, and he wasn't attacked. Grace, the exposed Chronicler, was killed that night, and Erin, out of tokens, was killed the next night.

tip: As the Vulture, claim a Vanilla Villager with no night action, vote with the majority, and never lead. Both killing factions will leave you for last, and the game runs down to your threshold on its own.
evidence: Alice repeated 'no night action, voting only on a checkable contradiction' all game, was never nominated, and won when only 3 players remained.

tip: An Eavesdropper who only reads PMs gets nothing if no one sends PMs; check early whether the table uses private chat at all, and use the Day's first PMs to decide which target to follow rather than spending a whole night on a silent player.

Track Magpie and token-holder claims as a set: a confirmed theft notice on one Medic should immediately invalidate any later public 'two tokens' claim, so treat the victim's own later token counts as checkable evidence.

Grace-style Katana holders should avoid repeatedly pushing the same vote-pair of teammates (Judy and Grace voting Innocent on each other's trials and lobbying the same players) since Juror and Eavesdropper comparisons expose it; spread lobbying across different targets and vote with the stated bloc.

Claiming a Medic with tokens that a Magpie has already stolen is a contradiction the Village will check; if you are a Medic-claimant, correct your token count the moment a theft notice arrives rather than repeating the old number.

Nominations made within minutes of a claim, with a promised Guilty vote before any answer, were the most consistent Yakuza pattern; when you see that, ask the nominator for a checkable reason first and hold your vote until one is given.

applies_to: Medic and any role with Defense or tokens
tip: Standard protection from a Medic costs no token, so a Medic at 0 tokens can still protect someone. Check which actions are free before calling a claim a contradiction.

A theft victim learns which token kind was lost. A Medic who later posts a higher token count after a confirmed Magpie steal is making a checkable false claim, so anchor token disputes to theft notices and audits rather than memory.
Nominating within minutes of a claim, without a stated mechanical reason, looks like steering the vote. Ask for the exact checkable point in public first, then nominate on it.
Avoid public token or role claims that a confirmed Magpie steal or audit can contradict. One public contradiction on the Medic claim exposed the team more than any vote did.
Quote any eavesdropped PM in full the first time you read one, and say plainly when you read none. Unquoted eavesdrop claims were discounted by everyone and cost Alice her credibility.
Pick pairs whose votes you can actually compare: a pair with only one or two shared trials gives almost no signal, so wait until both have voted in several trials before spending a night on them.

Check every token or role claim against the audit and theft notices: a Magpie steal that the victim confirms is a hard fact, and a Medic who was robbed should not keep posting a two-token count afterwards.

The Katana killed every player who claimed an information role within a few nights, often before they posted results. Post results publicly the day they arrive, and never stay silent on a result you hold.

Treat two players who privately ask the same people for the same acquittal as a pair to check, and ask each for the exact checkable point they are relying on rather than accepting the lobbying as a reason.
Before accusing a Fixer or a flipped vote, compare the stated Guilty and Innocent totals with your own private reminder; a public post can be a misreading, and a false alarm wastes a whole Day.

Plan swaps in night chat before the threat lands. I held both swap tokens all game and died to a known Strong Bounty Hunter attack without using either. Swapping yourself with a Villager moves an incoming Strong attack onto them.

Don't nominate someone and promise a Guilty vote before they can answer. Dave's fast Day 3 nomination of Frank with a pre-announced Guilty vote became the main case against the team and gave the Village a clear pattern to vote against.

Don't claim a token-based role with specific counts you may not keep consistent. A Magpie theft or an Accountant audit can expose the mismatch, and the changing story is what drew the Village in. Keep the claim vague or pick a role without tokens.

Treat every private message as public. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps can read them, and Judy and Grace's private requests for Innocent votes were quoted in public and became the main case against both of them. Keep vote lobbying to public chat and pick votes you can defend on the record.

A bounty is claimed on a death by your attack even if it happens at night, so pick the attack target by where it helps you most: the target with the most claimed-bounty value who is still likely to be on a hang or kill path. Holding a single Strong token for a whole game without spending it cost me time; Dave's bounty was claimed but I never had a second bounty source.

Track Katana holder and visits explicitly each night. The Yakuza kept the Katana on Grace for the whole game, and the only way to catch that was a Tracker, Lookout or Fortune Teller log. When no info role posts, the Katana holder's visit list is the real lead, so press the Village to name the visit basis rather than trading token claims.

Frank's Scrutineer claim flipped several times and was never checked, yet a fast nomination of a claimant with a shifting story still drew Guilty votes. Before committing a vote, ask which single mechanical fact would change your mind, and make the claimant name it; many nominations this game rested on pressure rather than a checkable contradiction.

Yakuza who lobby teammates' targets privately (Judy and Grace both asked Alice and Niaj for Innocent on Grace) leave a visible pattern when the PMs are quoted; if you must lobby, do it through public reasoning, not private requests.

Magpie steals and Medic token counts are the cleanest checks in this variant: a stolen token leaves a notice to the victim, and Mallory's audits gave hard counts. Use an Accountant audit on the suspected token-claimant the night after their claim, not on a random player.

A Scrutineer's check covers only the voters of the Day just before the night, so with no trial there is nothing to scrutinize. Post the Guilty count right away, because a claim that changes across the Day reads as a lie even when it is true.

Use a player's stated votes as a lie detector: a Scrutineer count (how many of three voters said Guilty) or a Juror match can contradict a claimed Innocent or Guilty vote. Check each claim against the posted totals before you vote.
A Magpie's victim is told which token kind was stolen. A Medic who posts two tokens after a theft notice is making a checkable false claim, so ask that question first.

Treat a nomination made within minutes of a claim, with a promise to vote Guilty before the defense, as a tell. Ask the nominator for a mechanical reason before voting, and do not let early pressure set the trial.

The Katana killed the Village information roles on consecutive nights, so their checks went unanswered. Expect the Village to check token counts and trial totals, and avoid private lobbying for Innocent votes, which the Village can compare across players.

Spend Talent Agent scan tokens early (Night 1) when they are plentiful; a Magpie can steal them, and I lost my last token to a theft on Night 2 without knowing it, so scans and tokens left unspent are at risk.

Avoid nominating or PMing Village players to build a bloc for a trial; private lobbying for Innocent (or for Guilty) on a teammate's behalf is the easiest thing for the Village to read as a Yakuza link, and it made our Village targets look suspicious.

Never claim a token count that a Magpie or Accountant can contradict; my public 2-token Medic claim after the Night 2 theft was exposed by the Magpie's notice and forced a messy retraction that drew three nominations.

A Katana victim is usually a Village info role; when the Katana kills a claimed Scrutineer, Eavesdropper or Juror, treat the claimant's own visit logs and the target of their checks as the strongest leads rather than arguing about pairings.

Pairing counts (Juror, Scrutineer totals) and lobbying PMs are weak evidence; the Village that stuck to posted totals and visit or token facts won the most useful checks, while lobbying-driven hangs split the Village.

Bloodhound's automatic three-player attack count is a running total, so the first night's result is the baseline. Track the same players on consecutive nights when you can, because one fixed trio's total rising by a night's attack is the cleanest Katana signal.
Keep the Katana holder's identity out of Village-visible PMs. Private messages are public as to who spoke to whom, and a repeated pair of Yakuza-ish PMs gets noticed fast.

A fake Village claim must stay mechanically consistent with what the Magpie, Accountant and Medic can see. Grace's token story (two Medic tokens, then a theft, then self-protection) was checkable and broke the Village's trust in her.

Before voting on a nominee, check the stated trial totals against the number of voters and the posted votes. Ask each claimed Guilty voter to confirm their own reminder, since a mismatch exposes both the Fixer and the lie.
Long public defenses and repeated identical reminders cost budget and add noise; a short plain answer to one direct question does more to shift the Village than many paragraphs.

Dead Vigilante with 3 unspent tokens is a wasted resource; with a Yakuza Katana running every night, fire a Basic or Standard shot at the most-suspected Katana-holder candidate on the first night a real lead appears instead of holding out for certainty.

Track the Katana holder by visit logs: the holder's target is the only kill that matters, and a Tracker/Lookout/Fortune Teller cross-check on the victim's night is the fastest way to find the holder before the Yakuza kill everyone with info roles.

Coordinate Village information on day 2-3 across claimed info roles: when only one Medic and one Magpie exist, a Magpie steal of Medic tokens is public and checkable, so pool token audits immediately rather than waiting for a Night 3 lead.
Private lobbying for a specific trial vote is itself a visible tell; if you make it, expect it to be the nominee's main counter-argument, so prefer public mechanical reasons over DMs.

Standard self-protection costs no token beyond the base cost of Strong; a Medic who claims zero tokens and no protection while innocent-looking players die is the easiest contradiction to test publicly, so Medics should state every protection choice plainly each night.

A Katana holder who is also a Talent Agent or other info role should spend the scan early and then stop; the team kept submitting identical holder/target pairs for eight nights, which gave the Village a steady stream of visit and token data to compare.

Before targeting a Village role that claims a token count (Accountant, Magpie, Medic), check whether a Magpie or Accountant is already auditing the holder's own visits; the team kept killing the role that was checking Grace's tokens, which left Grace's false claims uncontested for days.

Private lobbying to vote Innocent on a teammate is the most traceable thing you can do: the Eavesdropper and Niaj both quoted it. Keep requests for acquittal to a single public line, or avoid them entirely.

A vanilla claim plus a consistent Day-1 vote record made Judy survive four trials; when a teammate's claim is contradicted mechanically (Grace's token count), pivot to attacking the Village's accusers rather than defending the teammate.

Ask a token-claimer whether a theft notice was received before accepting any token count; a Medic robbed by a Magpie is told which kind was lost, so a Medic posting two tokens after that notice is a checkable contradiction.

applies_to: Accountant and other token-audit or information roles
tip: Publish each audit result the day it lands, and assume the Yakuza will kill the most dangerous checker soon after a contradiction surfaces. Keep a backup who knows your audit history.
A Medic's free Standard protection costs no token, so a 0-token count does not explain why no protection was given. Test protection claims against visits and deaths, not token totals alone.

When announced Guilty totals do not match the stated votes, ask each claimed voter to restate their private reminder before treating it as a Fixer or a lie. Yes/No nomination counts are the cleanest check.

A nominator who promises a Guilty vote before the nominee answers, or who nominates several players within minutes, is a signal to ask for a mechanical reason first. Demand one before voting on the pattern.
Do not claim a Village token role with a token history that a Magpie or audit can contradict. Once a claim is shown false, it is safer to drop it than to keep revising it.

When the Village splits its trial votes across several nominees, each 4-4 or 3-4 trial spares a suspect and burns a player's credibility. Pick one checkable contradiction, push the whole Village onto it, and don't rotate nominees on pressure.

Use vote-pattern matches as a bloc test. When two players match on most nomination and trial votes and both privately lobby the same acquittal, treat them as one pair and check the pair together. Don't let a split 3-4 on one of them clear the other.

applies_to: everyone, especially players with information roles
tip: Track which players the Katana kills after they challenge a claim. Heidi, Ivan, Mallory, Frank, Alice, Carol and Niaj all died after questioning a claim, so the challenged claim-holder and the people who never challenged are the leads. Keep a running list of kills, challengers and survivors.

applies_to: Medic and Magpie (and everyone checking token claims)
tip: Standard Medic protection on another player costs no token, so '0 tokens' never explains protecting nobody. A Magpie's victim is told which token kind was stolen, so a Medic who posts a token count after a theft notice has made a checkable false claim. Ask for that answer on the day it appears.

Don't keep a token-based fake claim alive once an Accountant and a Magpie are both alive. Each audit or theft is a public number the claim must match, and one mismatch collapses the whole story and drags the teammate who vouched for it into the trial.

A Magpie steal only reveals a token count when a target actually has tokens; spending several nights stealing from 0-token players wasted my actions. Test the most suspicious claimed token-holder first, and use the first theft to confirm a Medic or Vigilante claim rather than guessing across players.

Before hanging someone for a claimed token count, check whether the claimed count is consistent with every Magpie theft and every Accountant audit. A public claim of 2 tokens after a notified theft is a checkable contradiction; a vague Scrutineer or Medic story is not.

Track the Katana's holder by which Yakuza name is repeatedly absent from night summaries and by who lobbies votes in private. Private lobbying for Innocent on one trial and Guilty pushes on others created the same pattern as a bloc, but neither proves Yakuza; tie each accusation to a visit log or vote total.

Standard Medic protection costs no token, so 'no tokens' does not excuse 'protected nobody'. Check whether a claimed protection was even possible before using a token count to explain away a no-protection night.

Fast nominations that come with a promised Guilty vote before the nominee answers were a pattern worth tracking; hanging on that pattern alone is risky, but it is a reason to demand a checkable reason before voting.

A role claim that has already made a provably false statement does not become safe because the claimant 'corrected' it. A Medic who posted 2 tokens after receiving a theft notice, and who protects nobody even though Standard protection is free, should be hanged. Don't demand a 'new' contradiction.
evidence: Grace admitted on Day 5 that she knew of the Night 2 theft when she posted 2 Medic tokens on Days 3 and 4. She also never used free protection while Mallory, Frank and Alice died. Niaj and Olivia still voted Innocent (4-4 on Day 5, 3-4 on Day 6), and Grace went on to kill four more Villagers.

tip: At low player counts, count factions before every hang. With the Katana still killing, list who can possibly hold it. Never hang a player whose loss puts Yakuza at parity or one kill from winning, unless the case is mechanical. A bloc that always votes together and defends each other is the likeliest pair.
evidence: On Day 8 five were alive: Grace, Judy, Olivia (self-claimed Magpie), Bob and Niaj. Grace and Judy had matched 4/4 nominations and 2/2 trials (Carol's will) and had both lobbied Innocent on Grace. Niaj still voted Guilty on Bob over a 'bloc PM', and Yakuza won that night.

tip: Don't spend a Day's hang on a Neutral that never blocks wins (a Bounty Hunter or Magpie with no tokens left) while the Katana kills every night. Save the hang for likely Yakuza, and be suspicious of whoever rushes the Neutral to trial.
evidence: Erin confessed to the Bounty Hunter kill on Dave, who was secretly Yakuza. Grace nominated her immediately, and the Village hanged her 9-1 on Day 4. On Day 5 Frank nominated Olivia, arguing 'Guilty is safe either way', which wasted another nomination.

tip: Track who voted Guilty on early trials, and pair that list with Scrutineer and Juror results. A small Guilty minority on a weak case is often the Yakuza voting together.
evidence: The 3 Guilty votes on Frank on Day 3 were Dave, Grace and Judy: exactly the three Yakuza. Alice reconstructed this on Day 5, but nobody followed it up, though Dave had been shot by the Bounty Hunter and Grace and Judy kept voting together.

tip: If no one claims a visit-tracking role after the first request, stop asking for Tracker or Lookout logs and work from the votes instead. On Day 2, put someone on trial so the vote-reading roles (Juror, Scrutineer, Auditor) have data for Night 2.
evidence: Day 2 ran 6+ rounds of 'waiting for Heidi's count' with no nomination, so Carol and Frank had nothing to check on Night 2. Players asked for Tracker, Lookout or Fortune Teller logs on every Day through Day 7, but none existed.

tip: If you fake-claim a role with a token count, stop spending tokens afterwards, or quietly build the spend into your story. A Magpie theft or an Accountant can expose the mismatch. Pick one explanation and keep it.
evidence: Grace claimed Medic with 2 tokens, which matched her real count after her Night 1 scan. Then she scanned again on Night 2 and was robbed, and Mallory audited her at 0. She went through three token stories and only survived thanks to swing votes.

tip: Aim each night's kill at whoever posted a check on you that Day (Accountant, Scrutineer, Eavesdropper, Juror). Redirect the Day's hang onto confessed Neutrals or loud Villagers.
evidence: Mallory was killed the night after posting Grace's 0-token audit, and Frank, Alice and Carol died right after targeting Grace and Judy. Grace nominated Erin on Day 4 and Olivia nominated Bob on Day 8, wasting both Village hangs.

tip: Vigilante: don't publicly claim while holding unfired tokens; set a trigger and shoot. Magpie: steal from players who claimed tokens, before they spend them, rather than from Vanilla or tokenless claims.
evidence: Ivan claimed 'Vigilante with 3 tokens' on Day 3 and was Katana-killed that night without firing. Olivia hit Erin the night Erin spent her token, then Judy, Frank, Bob, Carol and Niaj, all of whom had claimed no tokens. She ended with 1 of 3 steals.

tip: Don't protect the same player every night and publicly announce the pattern. A Smuggler swap moves your Standard save onto whoever is swapped in, and a Divine Attack beats Standard. Rotate targets, spend one token on Strong protection for a likely Katana target, and keep nightly targets private.

A swap redirects both the attack and the save, so an attack that 'failed' or a visit list that looks wrong may be a Smuggler's doing. Before accusing a visitor, check for swap notices and ask which player was actually targeted.

Before voting, recount the tally from the living voters only. Dead players cannot vote, and a Yes or Guilty total above the living count means someone is wrong. Grace's arithmetic error came from counting a dead player's vote, and checking this exposes liars quickly.

Don't let a Ritualist guess a Medic claim on your own. A wrong guess is announced publicly, and a right guess kills a Medic who is the only living protector, so agree on a guess in night chat and avoid the same vote pattern on every nomination.

Use the announced Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent totals as arithmetic checks on every claim. With N living voters, a Yes count implies exactly N minus Yes No votes, and dead players cast no vote. Grace's Day 5 tally error was caught only by counting the living voters.

A Katana or swap story is only as good as its visit list. Ask who visited the victim before accepting 'attacked and survived' or a swap notice, and treat a swap notice that names no visible effect as unverified. Heidi's and Niaj's swap accounts could not be checked by the town.

When a Sheriff posts a checked Evil result, hang on that result. Do not spend days demanding Night 2 visit lists that no one posts. Set a deadline: if the visit list is not out by the next nomination window, vote on the checked results you already have.

A Bounty Hunter claims a bounty when its target is hanged while the Bounty Hunter's own Guilty vote counted. Erin voted Guilty on Grace and claimed that bounty, so when a Neutral hunter is alive, track which players voted Guilty on each suspected target before hanging them.

Keep the nomination and trial votes matched to the plan. Judy and Mallory voted Yes on an Olivia nomination and Guilty on Ivan, which the Village noticed and used to target them. A coordinated bloc that votes the same way on every nomination is easy to read in the ledger, so vary the pattern when the team is not under pressure.

A swap moves the Medic's protection onto the decoy as well as the Katana. Both swapped players get a notice, which lets the Village explain failed kills in public. Before swapping, check whether the decoy already holds a protection or a Standard defense that would cancel your attack, and assume the notices will be read as proof of a swap.

Teammates who vote identically on every nomination and trial are easy to find: a Juror's same-vote counts or a Scrutineer's Guilty counts expose them. Vary your votes on minor nominations, and do not follow a teammate's Yes or Guilty pattern across several Days.

A correct Divine guess kills silently, while a wrong guess is announced publicly at the start of the next Day. Once the town has only one Medic claim, guessing that claimed Medic with a Divine attack removed the protection that had been blocking the team, and it cost nothing publicly.

The loudest Yakuza pressure on Day 3, with nominations that named no checked visit, made our teammate Olivia the town's lead and got her hanged. Yakuza should avoid early nominations that rest only on 'no visit named' and keep pressure on claims the Village can check.

Count the living voters before reading any Yes or Guilty total: a dead player cannot cast a later vote, and a 9-Yes total among 10 living voters leaves exactly one No. Several claims this game went wrong on that arithmetic.

applies_to: everyone, especially Sheriff, Medic and Village players reading survival claims
tip: A Standard save on a swapped target lands on the swap partner, so 'I was attacked and survived' plus 'I was protected' can both be true only if the swap moved one of them. Check which night had a swap notice, and treat survival claims as unverified until the partner's visit list is known.

Spend Sheriff checks on players who visited an attacked victim, or who pushed early nominations, rather than on players who have already been cleared by other evidence. My Night 2 and Night 4 checks on Grace (a Juror with no results) gave nothing I could use, and I could not replace them.

Recount every posted vote tally against the number of living voters, and remember that dead players cast no vote. Grace's Day 5 tally error showed that a check built on bad arithmetic costs trust, and a count that doesn't add up is a concrete lead you can state publicly.

Teammates who vote identically on every trial and nomination (Judy and Mallory both Yes on Dave and Guilty on Ivan) can be linked by a Juror or Auditor. Vary votes across some trials, and avoid pushing the same nominee in private messages, since private pushes are visible as who messaged whom.

A Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, so a Standard save on the partner also redirects; before accepting or rejecting a survival claim, trace which player the attack and the save actually landed on.

Check vote arithmetic against living voters before accepting a juror or tally claim: the Day 5 Juror claim collapsed because 9 Yes from 10 living voters leaves exactly one No, and dead players cannot vote.
Avoid private messages pushing the same nominee during the day; the public record of Heidi's and Bob's private pushes made her the obvious target and gave the Village a clear pattern to vote on.

Spend the single attack token on a target whose death is decisive for your bounty count rather than early on Night 2; claiming bounties by hanging needs your Guilty vote to count, so plan which trials you can influence.

Keep a Yakuza night-chat plan that never names a Village claim as a Ritualist target without certainty; a wrong or early Divine guess announces the guesser and burns tokens, as seen when Mallory's guess went right but exposed the team's plans.

Your Lookout is a visit-based result: when it shows a single visitor to a Katana victim, that visitor is the lead. Post the watch result and target publicly early, since a dead Lookout's visit list is only as useful as the claims made about it.

Before the Katana holder attacks a Sheriff or Medic-protected target, check whether a Smuggler swap or a Medic save is in play; a swap moves the attack and the save together, so agree the target only after confirming the swap partner.
Count the announced Yes and Guilty totals against the living voter count before every trial, because a claim that cannot match the totals (e.g. a Juror's tally) is an easy and fast way to lose trust.

A claim that nominates without naming a checked visit (Olivia, Judy, Mallory votes) should be tested with a direct question before the trial, not after; the lack of an answer was used against the nominator by others too.
A Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner; a survivor of a Katana attack must have been protected or swapped, so verify the swap before accepting a survival claim.

applies_to: Village roles with checks (Juror, Scrutineer, Sheriff)
tip: Before posting a check, state the exact night, the exact pair and the exact count. A Juror or Scrutineer result is only as strong as the names and votes it covers. Before trusting any announced total, recount Yes or Guilty minus living voters, and remember dead players cast no vote.

When the only checked result is a verified alignment reading, act on it instead of waiting for visit lists that a dead Lookout never posted. Day 2 and Day 3 were lost to repeated 'no nomination until results are posted' messages. Set a deadline for claims to be checked and vote on the best checked fact.

applies_to: Sheriff, Medic, Smuggler and Katana holders
tip: A Katana holder reads Good (Sheriff: Not Evil), so a Not Evil result on a player attacked that night clears nobody. A Smuggler swap moves Medic saves and Katana aims together, so a survived attack plus a Medic save is not proof of either claim. Ask who swapped whom before treating either as settled.

A correct Ritualist guess is silent, and a Divine attack beats Standard protection, so the sole Medic claimant is a prime guess target. A Medic who expects a Ritualist should self-protect with Strong on nights when that risk is real, rather than only giving Standard to others.

Repeated agreement posts such as 'agreed, no nomination until results' spend budget without adding information. Spend each message on one checkable question or one concrete fact so the Day's budget is left for trials.

A Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, so a swapped target can reveal the swap: check whether the 'attack survived' or 'attack landed' notices match the swap partner's visit list before accepting a survival claim.

Before accepting or rejecting a Juror, Scrutineer or Sheriff claim, check its numbers against the public vote count: with N living voters, Yes or Guilty totals fix how many No or Innocent votes there were, and a dead voter cannot cast a vote that day.

Do not let a teammate's public nomination become a Yakuza-wide vote pattern across many Days; repeated same-way votes on the same village nominees are the clearest tell that the town's analysts will use.

A confirmed Standard protection that fails against a Standard Katana attack gives a Medic-plus-Sheriff pair a strong cover; keep the protector's claim consistent across nights, because contradictory protection logs are what the town checks first.
Ask for concrete, checkable facts (a named visitor, a result, a count) rather than pressure; the town was split for days because most accusations named no visit and nobody could be checked.

Scrutiny reads only trials that have already happened, and its result arrives at the next Day's start, after the vote the town is making. Name your first scrutiny target publicly as soon as a trial exists, and post the counts when they arrive, so the town can check them before it votes.

Before building a case on a voter pattern, recount each announced total against the living voters only, since dead players cast no vote. Grace's Day 5 tally was 9 Yes among 10 living voters, which leaves one No, not three, and that arithmetic error decided her hang.

Give the most weight to a checked result that fits the public totals and the deaths, such as Dave's Night 3 Evil check on Olivia, which matched her Guilty votes and execution. Discount claims that name no visit or result, even when they are pushed loudly.

applies_to: Village roles that read swaps and Katana victims
tip: A swapped player is told they were swapped, and a Katana aimed at a swap partner lands on the partner. When a protected player dies or survives oddly, check the swap notices first, and treat the Smuggler as a live explanation before blaming a claimed Medic or Sheriff.

A Standard Katana attack is blanked by any Standard save, so when the Medic protects the same target every night, switch targets or combine the Katana with a Smuggler swap aimed at a decoy early rather than repeating the same attack pattern.

Spend one-shot tools (Ritualist guess, Smuggler swap, Clerk rig) only after confirming the target's role through a visible contradiction; a wrong or unnecessary guess announces you and wastes tokens with no visible gain.

Vote with the Village on Day trials where a Village-looking nominee is at risk, so your votes match the announced totals; coordinated early Yes votes on a Sheriff or Scrutineer were the public pattern that exposed our team.

Check swap arithmetic before accusing anyone: a Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, and a save aimed at one lands on the other, so a 'survived' or 'died' result can be explained by a swap rather than a visit.
Count living voters before alleging a vote tally is wrong: with n living voters, Yes plus No must equal n, and dead players cannot vote, which is how a Juror's tally error was exposed.

A Divine guess on a Medic claim only works if the Medic's save is not already moved or blocked; spend ritual tokens only after confirming the target's role from a checked source, because a wrong guess is announced and exposes the guesser.

Before submitting a Katana holder and target, check whether any living Village player has a checked result that could expose the holder; the holder's visit is what trackers and visit-list checks see, so keep the holder's public claims consistent with it.
Count the living voters before accepting a claimed tally: with N living voters, a Yes count of Y leaves N minus Y No votes, and a dead player cannot cast a vote on a later Day.

Private messages pushing a nomination are visible to everyone as to who messaged whom; avoid sending repeated pushes to two different players about the same nominee, since that pattern is easy to spot.
Juror and Scrutineer checks name only aggregate counts; if a claimed check pair or night changes between posts, flag it immediately and ask for the night and pair before voting.

A Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, so a swap can make a 'survived' or 'attacked' claim check out or fail; before accusing someone of lying about an attack, trace where the action actually landed using both swapped players' visit lists.

Before voting on a claimed Juror or Scrutineer check, recompute the vote tally yourself from the announced total and the number of living voters; a claim that fails basic arithmetic (e.g. counting a dead player's vote) is an easy, concrete reason to vote.

Ask every claimed power role for a one-sentence visit list at the same time, and mark which claims cannot be checked before the vote; nominating people for 'no visit named' pushed the town into hanging unverified Village players, while the real Yakuza stayed alive.

Private messages are visible as sender-recipient pairs to everyone; if two players send each other or several players repeated private pushes for one nominee, that pattern is public and should be named early rather than letting it build into a bloc.

Use a Ritualist Divine guess only on a role the town has already tested, and not on a Medic claim that is only a protection claim; the guess spent two tokens and exposed the Ritualist once it was announced.

Before a Smuggler swap, check the 'Katana lands on the partner' effect: swapping the Katana's target with a protected player moves the Medic's save onto the decoy, so a plan only kills if the protector covers the decoy or nobody. Simulate both protector choices before submitting.

Keep the daytime voting record consistent with what you say in chat, and avoid a public Yes on nominations that name no visit when you are the only one pressing; a repeated pattern of Yes votes on Village nominees got Judy and Mallory targeted by the town and made them the lead.

Do not send private messages pushing one nominee to other players. Every PM is visible as a sender/recipient pair, and Heidi's repeated PMs to Bob and Niaj were the clearest public signal of coordination in the game.

Count living voters before accusing someone's tally: a Yes count plus No count must equal living voters, and dead players cannot vote. Several Day 5 accusations collapsed because people miscounted voters, which wasted a trial.

A Katana holder reads Not Evil to a Sheriff (R19), so a Sheriff's Not Evil on a player does not clear them of Katana holding, and a Katana kill's visitor list is the most reliable lead; track which Night's visitors appear in several lists.

When the Village is at or near parity, never vote Yes to put a player on trial without a real case. Assume a Fixer or Ballot Stuffer can turn any trial. Count the likely evil bloc and keep nominations from passing unless the Village alone can control the trial.
evidence: At 3v3 on Day 6, Bob and Niaj voted Yes on Mallory's nomination of Heidi (5 Yes). Judy had fixed Heidi that night, so Heidi's own Innocent vote counted as Guilty. The trial passed 4-2 when it should have been 3-3, and the Village lost a member and then the game.

tip: Build a vote table early and look for a fixed bloc. A failed nomination with N Yes votes, and the matching Guilty count in a trial, often equals the evil team exactly. Post every part of a vote-count result, because a partial count can name the last member of the bloc.
evidence: Olivia's nomination of Dave got exactly 4 Yes (Olivia, Carol, Judy, Mallory), and Ivan's trial got exactly those 4 Guilty. Ivan's Night 3 scrutiny showed 2 of Carol, Erin and Olivia Guilty in his trial. Erin had claimed Innocent, so that meant Carol and Olivia, completing the bloc. Ivan only posted the Grace-trial count. Nobody named the unclaimed fourth Yes until Day 6, when it was too late.

tip: Before hanging an investigator whose result looks impossible, check whether a public swap notice from that night could have redirected it. Also make sure everyone is talking about the same Day's tally. A swap explains a strange result the way a role-block explains a missing one.
evidence: Grace's Night 4 Juror check on Alice and Dave actually landed on Alice and Niaj, because Niaj and Dave were swapped. Niaj had posted his swap notice that same Day. The Village still called Grace's 5-of-5 a lie. Heidi read Grace's '9 Yes, 3 No' (Grace's own Day 3 nomination) as the Day 5 tally, and a truthful Juror was hanged 8-2.

tip: Post private night notices (swapped, attacked and survived, role-blocked) on the next Day. They reveal enemy tools such as a Smuggler and confirm protectors. Kept until you are on trial, they look made up.
evidence: Heidi was told on Night 3 that she was swapped and survived a Katana attack. That would have shown a Smuggler and a moved Medic save, and warned Alice before Night 4. She first mentioned it on her Day 6 trial, and Judy, Mallory and Carol attacked it as a mechanics lie.

tip: Don't protect the same claimed power role every night once a Smuggler or swap is possible. Vary your target, or spend a token on Strong or self-protection. A fixed pattern lets the Smuggler swap your save away.
evidence: Alice protected Dave on Nights 2, 3 and 4. Carol's Night 4 swap of Niaj and Dave sent Alice's save to Niaj and the Katana to Dave, who died. Alice died with both medic tokens unused, to a Divine Ritualist guess.

tip: Use your strong tools together on the confirmed threats. Use a Smuggler decoy swap against a predictable protector, and a Divine Ritualist guess only on a role you are sure of, such as a claimed Medic whose saves fit. Save a Fixer for the parity trial, on a Villager likely to vote Innocent.
evidence: Carol aimed the Katana at a decoy and swapped the decoy with Dave, which killed Dave on Night 4. Mallory's Divine guess of Alice as Medic was right on Night 5. Judy's fix on Heidi turned Heidi's Innocent into the decisive Guilty on Day 6.

tip: Claim Vanilla, use your single Strong attack early on a target the town won't miss, and push your other targets toward trial with the town's own reasoning, such as 'no results'. Your Guilty vote must count on the hang.
evidence: Erin killed Frank (a bounty target) on Night 2 under a Vanilla claim. She nominated Grace on Day 3 for having no results, kept pressing her, and voted Guilty when Grace was hanged on Day 5, winning before anyone suspected her.

tip: On a Day with no information, don't spend the whole Day repeating 'wait for results'. Use it to put votes on record or test claims, or let it end quickly. Endless filler gives evil free cover and pushes real work onto Days when power roles are already dead.
evidence: Day 2 had about 70 near-identical 'no nomination until Night 2' messages and no votes. The only useful moment was Heidi questioning Grace's Juror wording.

tip: A bounty is also claimed when a target is hanged while your Guilty vote counts, so a hang is free. Use the one-shot attack only on a target the Village is unlikely to hang, and vote Guilty yourself on the others. Spending it early on a Village claimant left me with no token for the last target.

Keep a day-by-day log of each claim. Heidi's Veteran alert grew from N1 to N1-N3, and Dave's Eavesdropper claim appeared only on the Day he needed a vote. Both were checkable against the log and should have been tested sooner.

Ask each suspect one direct question, then judge the answer and move on. Grace's Yakuza-chat slip got several corrections and no plain answer, while the Village spent Days 2 and 3 waiting for Night 2 results instead of voting on the contradiction.

Use the Katana to kill the real Seer or Sheriff counter-claimant, as the Yakuza did with Bob on Night 2. With no living verifier, a fake Sheriff's Fabricator-backed reads stood until the hang. Agree that kill in night chat before Day 2 begins.

Keep every visit off a player with a live Trapper trap, as the Yakuza did with Dave on Night 2, so no trap hit reveals a non-Village visitor. Say the reason in night chat so both members submit matching actions.

A Fabricator can frame a Good player on Night 1 so that a fake Sheriff reads them Evil. An Evil read on a Good player is therefore not proof the reader is lying, so ask the claimant for their full visit and target log before weighing it against your own result.
A Seer pair result only says same or different. Pair a suspect with a player already confirmed Good so the result tells you the suspect's alignment; a pair of two unknowns mostly wastes the token.

Yakuza never attack their own team, so a Katana victim is never Yakuza. That clears the victim of Yakuza membership but does not confirm their claim or their Village role, so do not treat it as proof that every claim they made is true.

Budget is 2.5 per round capped at 8, and repeated near-identical 'X again' posts cost budget and add no information. Say each claim and each direct question once, clearly, and spend the rest on votes that have a concrete reason.

Compare each claim's counts against what the player posted earlier. A claim that gains an extra night or a new detail each Day, like a Veteran alert log growing from N1 to N3, is probably retrofitted, so call it out with the earlier wording.

Do not announce your trap target publicly. Once Dave was named as trapped, the Yakuza simply avoided visiting him, so the trap could never go off. Place it quietly on a player the Yakuza are likely to visit, and reveal the placement only after it fires.

Track how a role claim changes between Days. Heidi's Veteran alert went from N1 only, to N1-N2, to N1-N3 with a token count that kept changing. A claim that gains nights each Day, and cannot be checked by anyone else, is a tell to weigh heavily.

A claimed Vanilla Villager who mentions a private night chat is strong evidence. Press for a one-sentence explanation at once, and log every vague repeat. Grace's slip was never cleanly answered and carried the hang vote.
