Day 2 was spent on many near-identical posts saying not nominating yet and demanding the same Night 2 targets. That burned budget without new information. Either nominate to force mechanics, or post only new facts or questions.

Before a Guilty vote, name one concrete mechanical fit, such as a Katana victim being non-Yakuza or a result that conflicts with a visit. Frank, Heidi and Dave's Erin trial vote succeeded because each named a specific mechanical reason.

Before committing to a claim or vote built on private messages, check the ledger's per-day PM counts. If no PMs have been sent, an Eavesdropper's read is empty, so say so and lean on visit logs and vote totals instead.

When two Sheriff or Seer claims conflict, check which claimant's Evil or Good read could come from a Fabricator frame, and whether the accused was visited by a framing-capable role that night. An Evil read on a real Seer is then a lead, not proof of a lie.
Never let a claimed Vanilla Villager mention night chat or private night notes, even as a correction. That single slip was the clearest tell on the board and it was never explained convincingly.

Escalating claims are the tell. A Veteran who adds a night to the alert log each Day, or a Vanilla who restates a role-free name, invites checks. State a claim once, plainly, with its full history, and keep it stable.

Name one concrete mechanical reason before each Guilty vote, such as 'Yakuza don't attack their own, so the Katana victim was Good'. Votes that were justified this way were easy to follow and to defend.

A Katana kill on a Village claimant tells the Village that the victim is Good, so every kill should be checked against which claim it helps expose. If a counterclaimant is killed mid-dispute, the other side's claim gets stronger, so pick targets that don't settle the fight for the Village.

Never mention night chat, Yakuza chat or any private team detail in public, even as a correction. Grace's Night 1 Yakuza chat slip was never explained in one sentence and became the main case for hanging her.

A frame on a real Village player is only safe if your claimed role's result cannot be tested by a kill or a Seer pair. My Sheriff Evil read on Bob was undone when the Katana killed him, which proved the read false. Frame players whose survival or death won't expose the claim, or claim a role whose results you can keep consistent.

Spend the puppet token on a Day before a likely hang or death, not at the end. Grace held the puppet token unused through two Days and was executed with it still unspent, so the Yakuza gained nothing from it.

A claim that grows a night each Day, like Heidi's Veteran alert count, is a tell that the claimant is improvising. Check every claim for stability across Days and ask for the exact repeated fact before voting Guilty.

When two players claim exclusive roles (Sheriff vs Seer), ask each for a complete list of every night target and result early on, and vote on who dodges that list; repeated re-asks with no answer were the clearest signal this game.

Check claims against what a role can actually produce: a Veteran who 'goes on alert' with no visitors and a claim that grows a night each Day is a fabricated timeline, so track each claim's history across Days in your notepad.

Do not let a single unexplained slip (like a Vanilla Villager mentioning a night chat) become the whole case; it carries weight only when the accused has given a direct explanation that you can test, so push for a one-sentence answer and then judge the answer.

A Katana victim is not proven Good: the Yakuza choose targets from among non-Yakuza players, so 'Yakuza don't kill their own' is only half the logic; the attacker chooses victims for strategic reasons too, so use visit or vote logs instead of the kill alone.
With few living players, a single trial vote decides the game, so tally every announced total against the number of voters and your own stated vote before the next nomination.
Spend a one-shot puppet on the Village's strongest accuser the day before a likely hang instead of hoarding it. I died with my puppet token unused.
Kill a Seer claimant on the first night their claim threatens a teammate. A Seer's pair check can name two Yakuza, and Bob's Night 2 pair tested Erin and Grace.
If a line slips (for example mentioning night chat as a Vanilla Villager), fix it in one plain sentence at once and never invent a second reason later. Village voters tally how the wording changed.
Claims that grow by a night each Day (Veteran alert N1, then N1-N2, then N1-N3) are a visible tell. Keep a claim frozen and identical each time it is repeated.

When a Sheriff reads Evil on a player who later dies to the Katana, first ask who visited that player and whether a Fabricator framed them, before treating the Sheriff as Good or the victim as Yakuza-cleared.

A Katana kill proves only that the victim was not a Yakuza teammate, since Yakuza don't target their own. It does not prove Good, because Neutrals can die to the Katana too. Don't treat a Katana death as an alignment verdict.

When a Sheriff or Seer claim can't be checked, weigh the two claims by which one produces a concrete mechanical contradiction, not by who asked more questions. Repeated demands for a Night target that was never going to be posted cost the Village days.

Before voting Guilty, write down one specific mechanical reason (a visit, a result, a vote total or a contradiction) and post it. Votes that rest only on a slip or on tone were the ones that looked weakest in hindsight.

An alert with no visitors gives no information and an alert is not a visit, so it can't be read by Trackers or Lookouts. Spend alert tokens on a specific threat, such as a visible Katana or Bounty Hunter lead, not on a fixed schedule; three empty alerts left the Veteran with nothing to show.

A Fabricator frame on a player who is later checked by a Sheriff looks like a lie to everyone if the Yakuza claim it on the wrong player. Keep a frame on a player who has no contradicting public claim, and back the frame with a Katana kill timed to hide it.

Never mention faction-only mechanics (Yakuza chat, the Katana, teammates) in public, even as a figure of speech. If you slip, give one plain, consistent explanation at once and never revise it. Shifting stories turn one slip into a three-Day case.
evidence: Grace opened Day 2 with 'no night info beyond the Night 1 Yakuza chat I can't share'. She then offered a 'correction', then 'private night notes', then 'scratch notes'. Every Village player quoted the slip until she was hanged on Day 4.

tip: If you fake-claim an investigative result calling someone Evil, do not then kill that player with the Katana. A Katana death tells the town the victim was not Yakuza, which exposes your read as false. Kill someone else, or hang them instead.
evidence: Erin claimed Sheriff with an Evil read on Bob. On Night 2 the Yakuza killed Bob with the Katana. On Day 3 Dave, Frank, Heidi and Alice all argued 'Yakuza don't kill their own, so Erin's read is false', and Erin was hanged 5-1.

tip: Frame or forge the player the Katana is attacking that night. A forged will on the Katana victim can plant a fake result and erase their real one. A frame on someone nobody checks does nothing.
evidence: On Night 2 Erin framed Carol, whom nobody investigated. Meanwhile the Katana killed Bob, who had just spent his Seer token on Erin and Grace. Forging Bob's will could have accused someone else; instead Erin's forge token went unused.

tip: Do not publicly announce where your trap or protection sits. Evil players will simply avoid that player, and you waste the ability. Reveal it only after it triggers, or when it decides a vote.
evidence: Carol announced 'trap on Dave, armed Night 2' several times on Day 2. In Night 2 chat Erin wrote 'I will not visit Dave, because Carol's trap on Dave is live'. The trap never fired.

tip: Before each night, put your planned target in your last will. If you are killed that night, the town at least knows whom you were testing. Also remember that a Katana holder reads Good, so a 'different' Seer pair still means at least one of them is likely not Good.
evidence: Bob spent his Seer token on Erin and Grace and got 'NOT the same'. He was killed the same night. His will said only 'no confirmed information', so the town never learned he had targeted the two actual Yakuza.

tip: When a teammate is doomed, don't publicly defend them and then secretly vote Guilty. The public defence is remembered, and the totals show your stated Innocent never happened. Either stay quiet or openly join the town.
evidence: On Day 3 Grace publicly said she was 'voting Innocent', then voted Guilty, giving a 5-1 total. On Day 4 Heidi and Frank both cited 'she voted Innocent on Erin without a mechanical reason' as part of the case to hang her.

tip: Use Katana kills as alignment evidence: the Yakuza almost never kill a teammate. If a self-verifying player confirms a dead claimant's result, that claimant's counter-claimant is likely lying.
evidence: Dave knew he was Good, which confirmed Bob's Night 1 pair (Heidi and Dave, same alignment). Combined with Bob's Katana death, this gave the town a clean mechanical case against Erin on Day 3.

applies_to: Yakuza (Puppeteer and other one-shot token holders)
tip: Spend one-shot tokens before you are doomed. A puppet used on a trusted Villager the night after a slip could have muddied the case, or framed someone else as the suspicious one.
evidence: Grace kept her puppet token through Nights 1-3 'for later' and was hanged on Day 4 with it unspent.

applies_to: Village information roles (Census Taker, Coroner, Sheriff, Seer and similar)
tip: Publicly posting a result or role claim early makes you the obvious Katana target the next night. In this game, the Yakuza's Night 2 proposal cited my census result as the reason to kill me. If you claim an information role, post the result in full immediately, as I did, so the Village keeps it even if you die, and expect the kill. Also consider whether a second, consistent check on the same name next night would give the Village something to cross-check.

applies_to: Village, especially players who hold a protective role
tip: Check every claimed Medic's protections against the actual attack map each night. A real Medic protects the likely Katana target, which is usually a publicly claimed information role. Bob's claimed protections went to an unattacked Dave on Nights 2 and 3, while the claimed Census Taker and Coroner were killed unprotected. A pattern of protecting nobody who gets attacked is a strong red flag, and the Village should ask for the protection target directly.

Count the living before you plan a trial. With 4 alive, 3 Yes votes are needed, and with 5 alive, 3 Guilty votes are needed. Two Yakuza can block every nomination. Once the Village is down to a Yakuza pair plus one or two Good players, it can't force a hang without a third vote, so the Village needs confirmed evidence before the head count shrinks.

A Ritualist guess succeeds most often on a player who has claimed Vanilla and has not been challenged, as Dave did. A correct guess removes a Good player for one token, but a wrong guess exposes the Ritualist publicly the next Day. Plan the guess only when the target's claim is already unchallenged, and keep the Fixer for a trial that actually needs flipping.

applies_to: Yakuza with one-shot tokens (Fixer, Ritualist, Clerk, Puppeteer)
tip: Before spending a one-shot token on a Day effect, check the same night's kill list. My Fixer token went on Dave, who the Ritualist killed that same night, so it did nothing. Spend it on a player who will still be alive to vote, or hold it until you know who survives.

Track the living-count majority math. With 2 Yakuza and 2 Good alive, a nomination needs 3 Yes out of 4, so Good cannot hang anyone and the Yakuza are safe as long as they keep the count at that point. Plan kills so the parity you reach is one Good voters cannot break, rather than killing the last Good voter too early.

applies_to: Yakuza with a fake protective claim (Medic)
tip: A fake Medic whose nightly protections never cover the Katana's victims becomes the attack line by Day 3: my Medic protected an unattacked teammate-friendly player while Alice and Grace died unprotected, and three Good players used that gap. Either claim a role with no checkable nightly output, or protect a plausible victim so the claim is consistent with the kill pattern.

A Ritualist guess on a player who keeps publicly claiming an unrevealed role (Dave claimed Vanilla four times) was right and removed a Good voice for one token. Guess when a claim is repeated and unchallenged, and keep the token when the claimant has a live info role that could be checked.

Killing a player who publicly claims an info role can make Good treat that death as proof the role was real, since Good reasons that the Yakuza never kill their own team. Use that: a Katana kill on a claimed Census Taker or Coroner strengthens their claim, so kill info roles only when their results would hurt you before the Day they post.

applies_to: Village information roles (Sheriff, Seer, Coroner, Census Taker, Bloodhound, Tracker, Lookout)
tip: The Yakuza kill whoever threatens them, so a claimed information role that is Katana-killed the night after posting or examining is probably genuine. Cross-check every protector claim against the kill list: a Medic who protects an unattacked player on the nights when claimed info roles die is the strongest Yakuza tell this game.

Do not wait for a perfect read. Here the Village waited from Day 2 to Day 4 for a Coroner result, and with 4-5 alive a trial needs 3 Yes, so the Yakuza removed one Village player per night while nominations failed 1 Yes and 2 Yes three times. Agree on a deadline and a threshold early, and vote on the best available read by Day 3 even if it is imperfect.

Post each night's target, role and exact result publicly in your first speech after it happens, and do it before anyone else can make the claim their own. Carol's Bloodhound result and Alice's census were held or contested, and the Village argued over whether Alice was a real Census Taker for days. A night result announced early is hard to call a single unverified claim.

The Bloodhound's attack count is cumulative, so track it. Record each of the three names' counts every night; a player whose count rises after a Katana kill is the holder. Pre-write your planned target and any results in the will, since a result that arrives on the night you die is only reachable through the will.

A fake protector claim survives only while nobody checks its target against the kills. Keep the Medic claim's targets plausible (protect the claimed info role on nights they are likely to be hit), and never let a clearly unattacked target be the only one protected while info roles die unprotected.

Every private message shows publicly as sender-to-recipient (R4), so a private nomination pact is visible the moment it is sent. Frank's PMs to Dave ('let's nominate Erin together') were public. Coordinate in public or not at all.

applies_to: Village info roles (Census Taker, Coroner, Sheriff, Seer and similar)
tip: The Yakuza killed each publicly claimed info role within one night of its first result (Alice on N2, Grace on N3). Post every result the next morning in the same message as your claim, not on a later scheduled Day. Grace held her Alice result until a planned Day 4 post and died with it, so the Village never got that check.

A trial needs a majority of living players, and the Yakuza only need to survive each Day. With 5 alive, Village had 3 Good votes on Day 3 but split on Frank, and the 2-2 Day 4 nominations then failed. Two-versus-two is a Yakuza win. Don't wait for a read that the Yakuza can kill first. Nominate the strongest mechanical contradiction while the majority still exists.

Check each Medic claim against the attack list every night. A real Medic protects the publicly claimed info role that is likely to be hit. Bob's Medic 'protected' Dave on N2 when nobody was attacked, and protected nobody on the nights Alice and Grace died. Matching token counts (2 Medic tokens, same as a Ritualist's) proves nothing.

A Ritualist guess of Vanilla Villager is the cheapest Standard kill, because Vanilla has Defense None and most Village are Vanilla. Don't spend a Fixer token on a target the same night a Katana or Ritualist hit lands on them: Erin's Fixer on Dave was wasted when Dave died that night.

applies_to: Yakuza with a Fixer, Clerk, Puppeteer or other one-shot token
tip: Before spending a one-shot token, check whether a teammate's kill or block this same night already removes the target. On Night 4 I spent my Fixer token on Dave while Bob's Ritualist guess also targeted Dave. The flip was wasted because Dave died that night. Agree in night chat which of you spends which token, and drop any token whose only use depends on the target surviving.

applies_to: Yakuza posing as a protective claim (Medic, or any claim with night protections)
tip: A fake Medic is structurally exposed. The Yakuza choose the Katana victim, so the Village can compare who was protected with who died. Bob's claim protected an unattacked player on Nights 2 and 3 while the claimed info roles died unprotected. Choose protection targets that are plausible Katana victims, or prefer a claim with no checkable night outcomes, such as Vanilla.

applies_to: Yakuza posing as a Village role
tip: Give one role wording from the first speech and repeat it exactly. My early 'no night action' phrasing, later changed to 'Vanilla Villager', gave Frank a line of attack for three Days. A simple claim with no night action is safe only if it is stated identically every time.

Count the nomination threshold before a Day. At 4 alive, 3 Yes votes are needed, so a 2-2 split with a Yakuza on each side stops every trial. Keep the Village split on a census claim that cannot be checked, and do not push a trial that needs a Village vote you cannot get.
Submit the agreed holder and target every night and keep daytime plans out of private messages. This worked perfectly: no mismatched submissions, and no daytime PMs about team plans.

applies_to: Village, especially players without a night role
tip: Judge each claimed Medic by whether their protections line up with actual Katana attacks. A Medic who protects an unattacked player while a publicly claimed info role dies unprotected, night after night, is the strongest tell available. Check this before weighing any other read.

Do not wait for a perfect read when you already have a credible one. The Yakuza kill one claimed info role per night, so every Day of waiting for a Coroner or Census Taker result to be posted costs you a source. Nominate once the evidence points one way, and say in advance what result would change your vote.

A Ritualist guess on a player who has openly claimed Vanilla Villager is a cheap, high-value kill. If it is wrong, you only lose one token and a cover. If it is right, the Village loses a player and has no way to check the attack. Use it when the Village has no reliable way to verify the target.

A Vanilla Villager claim that the Village can't disprove is a strong cover. Erin's unchallenged Vanilla claim survived all game while the Village argued about it, so pick a Village role whose claim has no checkable result.

Repeated accusations and 'I'm not nominating' loops spend budget without adding information. Each public message should add one new mechanical fact or one concrete question. My budget fell to about 1 by Day 4 from repeating the same census argument.

applies_to: Coroner, Census Taker, and any claimed information role
tip: Post results the moment they arrive and never pre-announce tonight's examination target. I wrote 'tonight I examine Alice' on Day 3, and the Yakuza's night plan explicitly cited my Alice read as the threat before killing me. A public claim already makes you a Katana target, so the announcement adds nothing but a clearer kill order.

Check every Medic claim against the attack record each night. Bob's claimed protections went to Dave twice, and Dave was never attacked, while the publicly claimed information roles Alice and Grace died unprotected. A real Medic covers a claimed info role when the Katana is likely to hit one, so a Medic who protects only unattacked players is a strong lead. Make them name the target publicly the day after and compare it to who died.

Do not stall for three Days waiting on one read. Every night without a trial is a free Katana kill for the Yakuza, and the Village lost Carol, Alice, Grace, Dave and Frank this way. Even with partial information, get one nomination and trial through each Day, and aim it at the claim with the worst mechanical gap, not at the loudest accuser.

Once the living count reaches 4 with 2 Yakuza, a 2-2 split can never produce a majority, so the Yakuza win by simply surviving and killing one Village player per night. Village must force a hang while the count is still odd or with a Yakuza-vs-Village majority available; waiting for 3 Yes at 4 alive is a losing plan.

A public Vanilla claim is a free Ritualist guess. Dave's 'Vanilla Villager' post let Bob spend one token for a correct Standard kill, and nobody on Village had a Medic who covered him. Also, a Medic claim with protections on unattacked players survived three Days because nobody demanded the target in the moment, and a 'no night action' wobble followed by a clean Vanilla claim cost Erin nothing.

Count down to the point where you can't win any more. If the Yakuza can block every nomination after one more night kill (e.g. 2 Yakuza at 4 alive, where 3 Yes are needed), the Day before that is your last chance. Hang your best suspect then, even on a 50/50, and don't wait for a result that only arrives after the next night.
evidence: On Day 3, with 5 alive, Frank's nomination of Erin got only 1 Yes. Dave and Grace held out for Grace's Day 4 read. Grace died on N3, and on Day 4 every nomination failed 2-2. With Frank, Dave and Grace voting Guilty, a trial on Erin would have hanged her 3-2.

tip: Treat a Katana victim as near-certainly non-Yakuza, and remember that a Roleplayer is only ever told one of Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle or Accountant. A dead Census Taker or Coroner who was Katana-killed doesn't need confirming. Act on their result at once.
evidence: Grace spent both Coroner tokens on Katana victims (Carol, then Alice). The Village delayed a whole Day to 'verify' Alice's census, even though Alice couldn't have been a Roleplayer and had been killed by the Katana.

tip: Don't publicly promise that tomorrow's result will decide the game. It tells the Yakuza exactly whom to kill tonight. If a result truly matters, say who you're examining in your will, not in chat, and push for the vote today.
evidence: Grace said repeatedly that her Day 4 read of Alice would settle the census. The Yakuza night chat picked Grace on N3 specifically to remove that check.

tip: Save Ritualist tokens until a public claim makes the guess nearly certain, especially a Vanilla Villager claim. An endgame guess combined with the Katana gives a two-kill night that can end the game at once.
evidence: Bob held both tokens until N4, then guessed that Dave, who had openly claimed Vanilla, was a Vanilla Villager. Together with the Katana kill on Frank, that killed both remaining Villagers and won the game.

tip: Fix a likely Innocent voter the night before the first Day with a contested trial. One flipped vote decides a close trial, and a token held back may never matter.
evidence: Erin used no Fixer token before Day 3. Frank's trial failed 2 Guilty to 3 Innocent, so fixing Dave or Grace would have hanged a Villager. The token she finally spent on N4 was wasted because Dave died that night.

tip: Have a full role claim ready before Day 2 and give it in your first message. A vague 'no night action' invites several rounds of pressure, and other players start citing it as evidence.
evidence: Erin opened with 'no night action' and only said 'Vanilla Villager' after Dave, Alice, Frank and Grace pressed her. Frank built his whole case on that wobble, and only the Village's caution saved her.

tip: When one suspect is narrowed to two names, look at who keeps shielding the more likely one and voting with them. A fake protector claim whose 'protections' never cover the claimed info roles is a strong second-Yakuza lead.
evidence: Bob claimed Medic, but he protected the never-attacked Dave on N2 and nobody on N3, while Alice and Grace died. He said 'let's not pile on Erin' and was the only player besides Erin to vote Guilty on Frank. Dave noticed all of this but never turned it into a vote.

tip: Center your census on a player who is already under suspicion or who sits in a known holder group. Then post the group and count right away. Several overlapping groups (N1 Frank/Grace/Niaj, N3 Bob/Grace/Ivan) cross-constrain each other, so once one member is confirmed Good, by an Oracle hit or by an Evil-0 count, elimination often leaves one name.

When an FT shows visitors equal to the number of claimed visitors, the Katana holder is hiding behind a claimed visit. List the claimed visitors whose visit landed on the victim, or who could have, and treat a mid-game claim switch (Vanilla to Medic) by anyone in that list as a near-confession.

A Diviner gets the same neighbor-group plus one-role results a Surveyor gets. A Surveyor claim whose hits come true doesn't clear anyone. Look for an independent alignment source (census, Oracle) instead.

Avoid a Vanilla claim on Day 2 if you may later need to explain a visit. Switching to a power role once a map puts you in the holder group got Bob hanged. Pick a visiting cover role at the start and stick with it.

Once the mechanical evidence converges on one player, nominate early in the day and give a clear 'if the Katana kills again, X is next' fallback. It keeps the town unified, and Yakuza teammates can't hide their Innocent votes in the totals.

applies_to: Yakuza with no night visit (Wiretap, Grunt, Informant, Clerk...)
tip: Your Day 2 cover claim must still work on a night you hold the Katana. Claiming Vanilla rules out any visit, so the first time you hold, the Cartographer or FT will show an edge you can't explain and you'll have to switch claims, which gets you hanged. Either claim a role with an optional visit from Day 2 (Medic, Tracker) or leave the Katana with a teammate who already has a visit cover.

When an FT and a Cartographer are both alive, the safest holder is one whose claimed visit lands on the victim, so the Katana adds no new edge or visitor. Moving the Katana to a no-visit player adds a visitor the counts will expose. Kill the Cartographer before they can map the victim's group, because one map shrinks the holder pool to 4 or 5 names.

Any fresh or changed claim will be Oracle-guessed that same night. If you have to make a new claim, kill the Oracle that night (or that night's likely tester) instead of a lower-value target. A single WRONG on a fresh claim was enough to hang me.

Rank kill targets by who produces alignment or group results against your team: Census Taker > Cartographer > Lookout. Here a living Census Taker gave three results that each pinned one non-Good player in a small group, and those drove two of our three hangings.
If nobody sends PMs (none were sent all game here), the Wiretap is effectively a Grunt. Don't count on PM intel. Spend your effort on a robust visit cover and on vote steering instead.

Combine your two counts with the Cartographer's sizes and the claimed visits, then post the full visited and visitor lists. When the visitor count equals the number of claimed visitors, the Katana holder must be hiding behind one of those claimed visits. Say this outright, because it shrinks the suspect pool to the claimed visitors.

A role-claim switch, such as Vanilla to Medic, that comes right after a map or group result puts the player in the holder group is a strong Evil tell. Pair it with any exact-role check that wasn't free (an Oracle guess, a profile) and push the hang the next Day.
Oracle results that only confirm roles already claimed in public prove nothing. Ask the Oracle to guess unclaimed or disputed roles instead. A non-free WRONG on a claim is close to decisive.

A Diviner gets exactly Surveyor-style results, so correct neighbor-group hits never clear a Surveyor claim. Weigh census and profile decoys more heavily. A profile decoy that is held by another living player, like Diviner here, points to a hidden role.

State your vote and your next suspect in one short line each trial. Keeping consistent public tie-break lines (for example "the archive breaks the tie") lets the town hang quickly before the Katana gets extra nights.

Spend map tokens on the player most likely to be killed (the strongest confirmed info role). If they die, the map names everyone linked to the Katana visit, which cuts the holder down to a handful of players. Post it the next morning and cross it with the Fortune Teller's counts; together they show which claimed visits must hide the Katana visit.

When the visit graph shows no room for an extra visitor, the holder is hiding the Katana visit behind a claimed visit to the victim. Treat every claimed visit to the victim as a suspect, and give the most weight to claims made last, after the graph was already public.

A Profiler's decoys are informative. One of them is the role of another living player. If a profile on a confirmed player lists an Evil role such as Diviner, that role is alive, so look for a claim whose results it could fake (for example, Surveyor-style neighbor groups).

Don't claim Vanilla early if a map or count might later place you in a visit group. Being forced to switch to a visiting role afterward (Vanilla to Medic) is nearly an auto-hang, and a single Oracle guess can expose it. Pick a cover with a plausible visit from Day 2.

Compare each player's stated nomination vote with the announced Yes count. A suspect who admits a lone No on a well-supported nomination stands out, and the clean Yes/No totals make that admission checkable.

applies_to: Lookout, Tracker and other visiting investigators
tip: Before each night, put your planned target in your last will (for example 'N2: watching Carol'). The will stays private until you die. The result of the night you die never reaches your will, but the target still gives the town an edge it can place in the visit graph. A will that only says 'target picked at night' wastes the whole night if you die.

When the Fortune Teller or Cartographer graph narrows the holder down to you and one other claimer, use your private certainty that you didn't visit the victim. Claim your watch and its exact result before the graph is public, then argue that the other person claimed last and picked a visit that conveniently explains the kill. Claim order counted for more than anything else in deciding a 50/50.

Each night, line up the Fortune Teller's visited and visitor counts with the Cartographer's group sizes. If there's no spare visitor slot, the Katana holder is hiding behind a claimed visit to the victim, so every claimer who visited the victim is a suspect. Account for the Ex-Con's random visit as a floating edge.

Don't claim Vanilla on Day 2 and then upgrade to a power role once a map catches you. An Oracle or Profiler can test the new claim cheaply, and the switch alone sinks your credibility. Pick a cover on Day 2 that already explains any future Katana visit.

If your Day 2 result decided a hang, assume you're the Night 2 kill. Watch the player most likely to be targeted or most likely to be lying, rather than someone whose visitors add little. Get the will's target line in before night.

Once a census, group or profile result has narrowed suspicion to a small set that includes a teammate, kill that investigator next, ahead of a generic watcher. Alice's N1 census (1 non-Good among 3) was what hanged the Diviner, and she lived all game while we killed the Lookout.

A Surveyor fake-claim matches a Diviner's results exactly, so informed town players see through it. Any Profiler decoy or Oracle check that mentions Diviner exposes it. If you use it, also put a plausible Neutral or another suspect in front of the town early. Don't rely on 'my hits came true before the claims' as proof, because a Diviner gets the same hits.

Pick one fake claim on Day 2 and keep it. Claiming Vanilla and then switching to a power role (Medic) after a map puts you in the holder group is almost always fatal, especially with an Oracle around who can test the new claim directly.

With a Fortune Teller and a Cartographer both active, the holder's Katana visit always shows up. Kill the Cartographer or Fortune Teller early, before they can map the victim's group, or move the Katana to a player whose claimed visit is to someone other than the victim.

Claiming a check on the Katana victim (Heidi's 'Sheriff checked Mallory') turns your teammate's holder visit into a 50/50 against a Lookout who claimed first, and an Archivist list then breaks the tie. Use a cover visit that doesn't land on the victim.

Your best guess is a suspect's claimed role, especially a power-role claim made after a map or count put them in a suspect group. A WRONG result breaks the claim outright, and nobody can call it copied the way they can a guess on an already-claimed Vanilla.

Blind Vanilla guesses on unclaimed players tell you little: WRONG only means 'not Vanilla', and RIGHT on an already-claimed Vanilla looks free to others. Use early guesses to confirm one player whose Good status unlocks another result, such as a member of a census group.

A Yakuza Diviner gets the same neighbor-group results as a Surveyor, so correct survey hits don't clear a Surveyor claim. Combine a census count with one confirmed-Good member and the remaining name is the suspect.

Cartographer maps plus FT counts can narrow the Katana holder to people with claimed visits on the victim's group. When a 'no-visit' claimer ends up in that group, any role-claim switch to explain the edge (Vanilla to Medic) is a strong tell.
If you hold a result back until others claim, say so in one line and post it within the same round. Waiting longer turns you into the census suspect, and others start threatening nominations.

Decide who holds the Katana from the cover claims, not at random. The holder's attack is a visit that the Fortune Teller's counts, the Cartographer's groups and Lookouts all pick up. So the holder should be a teammate whose claimed role visits, and ideally one who can say their claimed visit went to the victim. A teammate with no visits of their own (Ballot Stuffer, Wiretap, Grunt) holding the Katana on N1 while planning a no-visit claim is the easiest Yakuza to catch.

Post your fake claim early on Day 2, before the Fortune Teller's counts and the Cartographer's groups are pieced together in public. If you claim last, with a story that exactly fills the one gap left in the graph, it reads as made up to fit, and the town hangs you on any tiebreak (here, an Archivist list).

Kill the Census Taker first, ahead of the Fortune Teller and Cartographer. Its count uses true alignment: the Katana's Good disguise doesn't fool it, frames don't change it, and the Ex-Con counts as Good. Each night it narrows the non-Good players to a group of 3, and those groups decided two of the three Yakuza hangs this game.

Pick a claim on Day 2 that you can keep all game. Claiming Vanilla and later switching to a power role (e.g. Medic) once a map catches you is fatal. An Oracle can test the new claim directly, and the switch counts as evidence on its own. If you need a visit later, claim a visiting role from the start.

When a Fortune Teller and a Cartographer both post every night, work out the full visit graph (visitors, visited, group sizes) against every claim. The Katana holder almost always has to hide behind one claimed visit, which shrinks the suspects to 2-4 players a night. Combine that with true-alignment results (Census) to settle it.

When a Katana kill comes on top of a claimed visit to the same victim (a 'Sheriff check' on the victim, a census centered on them), check it against the FT visited/visitor counts and the Cartographer groups. If the counts leave no room for a separate holder, the holder is hiding behind one of those claimed visits. Line up who claimed a visit to the victim, and lean toward whoever claimed it last, after the numbers were public.

A late claim switch (Vanilla to Medic right after a map put the player in the holder group) together with one Oracle/Profiler result that couldn't have been copied is enough to hang. Weigh an investigator's free results (ones that repeat public claims) as zero, and its non-free ones heavily.

applies_to: Ex-Con / any Good player with unverifiable visits
tip: As Ex-Con, claim early and plainly, and put in your will that census counts you as Good. Late-game Yakuza will pin unexplained visits on your random visit. Answer with mechanical checks (the census counts true alignment, so an Ex-Con counts as Good) and don't just deny it.

Use Archivist lists with probabilities. If one claimed role shows on the list and the other doesn't, the odds are roughly 10:1 for the listed one being real. That is a fair tiebreak when the visit math has narrowed it to two players and waiting a night costs a kill.

When the visit graph narrows the holder to two players, nominate early with a clear tiebreak rather than accepting a 'test overnight' delay. Every night of delay is another Katana kill, and the accused gains nothing they couldn't fake.

Post the whole archive list on Day 2 and use it as a tiebreaker between rival claims. A claimed role that shows on the list is roughly 5-10x more likely to be real than one that doesn't, because a fake only shows by chance. Remember that roles in the game can also turn up as fakes, and that a listed role (e.g. Medic) becomes a ready-made fake claim for the Yakuza. So treat a newly claimed role that is on your list with suspicion too, not as confirmation.

When the Katana victim's visit group is mapped (Cartographer) and the FT counts leave no unexplained visitor, the holder is hiding behind a claimed visit to the victim, or behind a no-visit claimer who suddenly reveals a visiting role. Anyone in the holder group who changes from a no-action claim to a visiting role should go to the top of the list.

Spend Oracle guesses on a contested or recently changed claim (e.g. 'X = the role X just claimed'). A WRONG on a claimed role is near-proof of a lie, and it is the only kind of result nobody can say you copied. Guesses that confirm an uncontested claim are free for a fake to invent, so they build little trust.

Overlap census groups across nights. Two 'Good 2/3' results that share one player, together with independently confirmed Good players, can pin down the non-Good player. Remember that the Ex-Con counts as Good and a Neutral is never counted, so leave room for a Neutral before you hang on a census alone.

A Diviner posing as a Surveyor gets matching results, but sharp players will point out that a Diviner gets the same groups, and a Profiler's decoy can name Diviner. Kill or discredit the Census Taker and the Profiler early, before their results can cross-check your cover.

applies_to: Party Animal and any visiting role
tip: Put your Night 1 target in your will before Night 1. You can't edit the will at night, and the first Katana kill often lands on N1. A will that says 'N1: TBD' wastes the block log. Also name a fallback: 'If I die N1, whoever I blocked was told they were role-blocked.'

When Fortune Teller counts and Cartographer sizes are posted, rebuild the whole visit graph from the claims. The Katana holder almost always hides the attack behind a claimed visit to the victim, such as a 'check' or 'census' that lands on the person who died. A claimed visit to the Katana victim is the first thing to examine. Lookout, Sheriff, Census and Profile claims made after the numbers were public deserve the most scrutiny.

Use Oracle guesses and profiles to test claims that are contested or that changed. An Oracle guessing a claimed role and getting WRONG nearly proves a lie. Guessing a role someone already claimed as Vanilla gives no new information to anyone else. Profiler decoys follow fixed rules: one decoy is another living player's role and one is a role not in the game. Combine that with the archive list.

If you might hold the Katana later, don't claim Vanilla on Day 2. A no-visit claim leaves nothing to hide the Katana visit behind once a Cartographer maps you. Switching to Medic or another role afterwards was spotted at once, and an Oracle guess confirmed it. Pick a claim with a visit early and stick to it.

Pair the census with confirmed-Good anchors. Once an Oracle confirms one member of a census group, the 'one of three is non-Good' result narrows to two. Cross-checking census groups from different nights pinned down Frank and then Bob.

Combine the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts with the Cartographer's group sizes and one map. Every claimed visit has to fit both. Once they do, the Katana holder must be someone whose claimed visit lands on the victim, or someone with no visit claim who is linked into the victim's group. Each night this narrows the holder to 2-4 names. Ask every visitor in the group to post their target before anyone argues.

Treat a mid-game role switch as a strong tell, especially one made right after a map or count puts the player in the holder group (for example 'I was Vanilla, actually I'm Medic'). Spend the next exact-role check (Oracle, Profiler) on the switcher's new claim. A wrong result plus the switch is enough to hang.

A Profiler result's decoys are informative. One decoy is the role of another living player, so a non-Good decoy such as Diviner or Ritualist means that role may be alive. Compare it with any claim whose results look the same as that Evil role's (a Surveyor claim vs a Diviner). That is how a fake Surveyor gets caught.

As a Vanilla you can personally confirm any check made on you. Say so plainly to back that investigator, but also point out that a result copied from an already-public claim doesn't clear the investigator. Use your census and other overlaps to cross off names out loud, so confirmed info roles can see the eliminations.

Pick a fake claim on Day 2 that already covers any visit you might need later. A no-visit claim like Vanilla gives you nowhere to go once a map puts you in the victim's group, and switching claims then is fatal. If you might hold the Katana, claim a protector or visiting role from the start.

Look at every decoy in a profile, not just the true role. One decoy is the role of another living player, so if a profile lists a role nobody has claimed (for example Diviner while someone claims Surveyor), that role is held by a living player. Say so publicly right away. Also check whether the not-in-game decoy rules out a claimed role. That is how a confirmed Lookout result also exposed the Yakuza Diviner.

Combine the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts with the Cartographer's group sizes every night. When the visitor count equals the number of claimed visitors, the Katana holder must be hiding the attack behind one of those claimed visits, usually a visit that 'happened' to land on the victim. That narrows the holder to 2-4 players, and other results can then split them.

Guessing a suspect's claimed role is the cheapest lie test there is. A WRONG result on a recent or switched claim (for example Vanilla to Medic) is close to decisive. A RIGHT result on a claim that was already public proves little to everyone else, so spend guesses on claims that are contested or haven't been checked.

Don't pick a fake claim whose results look exactly like an Evil role's. Surveyor results are identical to the Diviner's, so once a Diviner showed up anywhere (a profile, an archive), the cover fell apart. Also, never claim Vanilla and then switch to a power role once you're in a suspect group. Pick your claim on Day 2 and keep it.

Profile players whose claims would sort out the most others, such as one player of a census pair or someone linked to the holder. A profile can confirm two claims at once: here Alice's Census Taker plus Judy's Archivist decoy, with Ritualist not in the game. Keep your last token for a contested claim late in the game.

When a Fortune Teller, Cartographer or Lookout might be in play, the holder's Katana visit needs a cover visit to the same target. Give the Katana to a teammate whose role visits, and point that role's action at the victim, so the kill adds no extra visitor or group link. If the holder claims no night action, one Fortune Teller count plus each visitor posting their target exposes them on Day 2.
evidence: Heidi held the Katana under a planned Insomniac cover that involves no visit. Carol's 6/6 count and Dave's group sizes left one unexplained visitor. Heidi was pushed into claiming 'Sheriff checked Mallory' after everyone else had claimed, which narrowed the holder to Erin or Heidi, and she was hanged.

tip: Solve the visit graph in public on Day 2. Every visitor posts their target, the Fortune Teller posts both counts, the Cartographer posts group sizes, and anyone role-blocked says so. After that, only one or two people can be hiding the Katana visit behind a claimed action. Then spend a Cartographer map on the most likely next Katana victim, so the holder's group is named the next morning.
evidence: On Day 2, Olivia's graph matched 4/3/2/1/1/1/1 and 6/6 exactly, leaving Erin or Heidi. Dave mapped Erin on Night 2, and she was killed that night. The map named the group Alice, Bob, Carol, Ivan and Olivia, which contained Bob, the holder.

tip: Before you fake-claim, check every public result that lists roles (archive, profiles, Surveyor or Diviner hits). Pick a role that fits that evidence, or at least isn't made unlikely by it. Claim early and in turn: a claim made after the visit math is public reads as fitted to it.
evidence: Lookout appeared on Judy's archive list and Sheriff did not. Judy and Ivan both pointed out that this made Erin's Lookout claim far more likely than Heidi's Sheriff claim, and that broke the tie. Heidi claimed last, and Dave and Erin both used that against her.

tip: Chain census results with confirmations. Once a census narrows a group to 'one non-Good among three', clear the others with any confirmed result: an Oracle hit on a claimed Vanilla, or a later census on overlapping players. The last name left is the target. Also note that a Profiler's decoys include the role of another living player, so a decoy like Diviner tells you that role is alive.
evidence: The three results above isolated Frank. Olivia's profile listing Diviner as a decoy matched Frank's fake Surveyor results, since a Diviner gets the same kind of result.

tip: Never switch claims once cornered. A switched claim is easy to test: an Oracle simply guesses the new role, and a WRONG result is decisive. If you hid as Vanilla, keep that claim and explain your graph edge some other way, or let a teammate absorb it.
evidence: Bob claimed Vanilla on Day 2. On Day 3, after Dave's map put him in the holder group, he switched to Medic. Grace guessed 'Bob = Medic' on Night 3 and got WRONG, and Bob was hanged 7–1 the next day.

tip: Kill the roles that keep producing information before the ones that are already spent. Census Takers, Fortune Tellers and Cartographers produce new evidence every night. A Lookout who has already posted their watch is worth less, and many players will visit them, which can make the victim's group a trap for the holder.
evidence: Yakuza killed Erin on Night 2, even though Bob had said 'we'll take Alice out soon'. Alice survived to Day 4. Her three census results convicted both Frank and Bob, and Carol's counts confirmed each graph.

tip: Keep discussion fully public and avoid private messages. A Wiretap or Eavesdropper then learns nothing, and every claim stays on the record where it can be cross-checked.
evidence: Nobody sent a private message all game, so Bob's Wiretap role, which was the Yakuza's planned source of information, gave them nothing to act on.

tip: Spend the doubled ballot the night before a close trial, not while holding it for a later one. I died on Day 3 with both tokens unused, so my extra vote never mattered.
Never name a Yakuza-only role in public, even as a slip. Alice's Smuggler slip, for a role never revealed, gave the Sheriff a hang on a concrete tell. A correction afterwards does not undo it.

Check every trial total against the nominees' votes, counting a Guilty self-vote and any doubled ballot. A 3-of-5 total with only two stated Guilty voters exposes a miscount or a lie, and it can split a town when raised late.

After a Katana attack fails on a Sheriff, switch the next target to the Medic who protected them. Our Day 2 kill on Grace failed to a Standard protect, and the team needed two more nights to kill the Medic and then the Sheriff.

Ask each Sheriff for a second check on an uncleared player before any hang. Grace's Night 1 Evil read on Carol led to the first hang, and her Not Evil reads were then used to clear players the Katana still needed to explain.

Private messages are visible as sender-recipient pairs to everyone, so a PM offering a trade or plan to a Village player is public evidence. Keep all Yakuza coordination in the night chat, and never send a daytime PM that offers a deal.

A living Medic with Standard protection blocks a Standard Katana, so kill the Medic first. Once the Medic is dead, the protected Sheriff falls the following night. Repeating the same target into a known protector wastes the night.
Never name a Yakuza-only role, even as a slip. A dead player's exact role is hidden, so naming it is a mechanical tell that the Village can use to hang you, as Alice's Smuggler slip did.

A Katana holder reads Good, so a Not Evil result only clears a player who is not the holder. Do not treat Not Evil as a clearance while a living Katana holder is unexplained; use visits and the kill pattern instead.

Before accusing someone of a vote-count mismatch, add the accused's own vote, since self-votes count and defaults count as No. Dave's Erin miscount led to two nominations and a hang on a wrong premise.
Long public defenses and repeated 'vote on evidence' speeches are expensive later in the game; keep trial speeches short and put the concrete reason in the first sentence.

Tally every trial and nomination total against the posted votes early; a miscount (like the 3-of-5 Erin total) can get a player nominated and hanged, so check counts before voting on anyone's stated vote.
Never give a slip-of-the-tongue role name that is Yakuza-only (like naming Smuggler for a dead player); a public error of that kind became the nomination reason and got a teammate hanged.
Avoid private messages to teammates or others during the Day about the team's votes or plans; they are visible as a pattern and can be used as a lead to hang you.
Before voting on a nominee, ask which role's visits or results actually fit the death pattern; a Katana kill needs a visit, so demand each living player's visit answer plainly on the Day it matters.

When a trial total doesn't match your expectation, count the nominee's own vote before accusing anyone. Erin's 3-of-5 Guilty included her own Guilty vote, which I had wrongly assumed was Innocent. Recount each total against the living voters and each player's stated vote before calling a miscount.

A Katana holder reads Good to Sheriff checks, so a Not Evil on a living player does not clear them of being the holder. Only visit logic does: a Katana kill proves a visit to the victim by the holder that night. List who could have visited each attacked player before treating any Not Evil as a clearance.

Treat a single Sheriff read as the strongest hard information but not a verdict. Ask for a second independent check and also check which trial pushes came early and from whom. Here the Village hanged three Village players on weak pushes while the one credible Sheriff was killed at night, so the Village lost its best information source.

Never name a unique Yakuza-only role for a dead player without a source. Alice's Smuggler slip, offered as a typo, gave Village a concrete mechanical lead to nominate her, and the slip explanation did not hold.

A Not Evil result does not clear a player who could be the Katana holder, because holders read Good. Before trusting a Not Evil, list who could have visited the Katana victim that night, since a Katana kill needs an unexplained visitor.

If the Katana is alive and you have protected the same target twice, the holder can simply kill you. Vary your target and spend a token on Standard self-protection once you claim, since a Standard self-protection blocks the Katana.

Recount announced trial totals against the votes people have stated before nominating someone on a claimed vote. A miscount on Erin's 3-of-5 trial led to two nominations (Frank, then Bob) built on it.

Never name an exact unique or Yakuza-only role for a dead player without a source. Alice's Smuggler slip was read as a tell, and her Evil explanation did not cover the exact role, which got her hanged.

Before any hang, require the accuser to say what the nomination rests on. Carol, Alice and Erin were each hanged on one unverified read or a bare no-action answer, and the Village ended up hanging its own players.

When a trial total doesn't add up to the nominations and visible votes, check every voter's stated vote against the count before anyone is hanged. Frank's Erin miscount nearly got a Village player nominated, and the total was simply right once Grace's Innocent was counted.

Avoid flip-flopping Yes-then-Innocent on the same player without a new hard fact, since it reads as Yakuza cover and gets you nominated. Explain each switch in public with the specific information that caused it.

Don't pile onto a nominee for a single slip or bare answer. Alice's 'Smuggler' slip was a Yakuza-only role, but the hang was driven by Grace's nominations; check which claim is actually verifiable before voting.

Protecting the same Sheriff who is repeatedly attacked on consecutive nights is predictable to the Katana. Vary protection targets or self-protect, since Grace died to the Katana the night after the Medic was already dead.

A Sheriff's Not Evil read on a player doesn't clear them against a Katana holder, who reads Good. Weigh Sheriff results together with which players were attacked and who visited them, not as standalone clearances.
Post each investigation result at the first dawn, not later. The Yakuza targeted me on Night 2 after my Carol read, so holding results back gave them time to act and made the claim look retrofitted.

A Not Evil result on a living player does not clear a Katana holder, who reads Good. When a Katana victim dies, list the living players who could have visited them, then spend checks on the players who remain unexplained rather than on people already cleared by a visit.

Track which players pushed the earliest nominations and which players defended or voted with them. Pairs that defend each other across several trials, or that get defended after a slip, are the strongest Yakuza signal available without a result.

Keep a written log of every nomination tally and trial tally. When a claimed vote does not match the announced count, check the count against the Yes/No totals before accusing anyone, because a Ballot Stuffer or a miscount can make an honest player look guilty.

A Medic who protects a publicly claimed Sheriff every night becomes an obvious target. Consider self-protecting on the night after the Sheriff is first attacked, since the Yakuza killed the only protector the next night.

Once you claim Medic and protect a Sheriff-like claimant, expect the Katana to come for you. Spend a token on self-protection on nights when your protected player is threatened, instead of repeating the same Standard protect on them; I protected Grace on N2 and N3 with the same pattern, the Katana killed me on N3, and I died with two tokens unused.

A Not Evil result does not clear a player while a Yakuza Katana holder reads Good. Before treating a clearance as settled, ask which visit could have hit the night's victim and whether the holder could be that player.

If a player names an exact role that was never revealed, such as a unique Yakuza-only role for a dead player, treat it as knowledge a teammate would have. A 'slip' explanation does not cancel that; check it against what the death reveals actually showed.

Keep a ledger of each trial's Guilty count and check it against the named Guilty voters. A count that doesn't match the names is the cheapest hard check on who is lying, and Dave's miscount on Erin's trial almost sent Frank to the gallows.

Require a concrete visit or a second independent source before each nomination, not just before each hang. Nominations that chained one after another (Dave, then Alice, then Erin, then Frank) were driven by single reads and pushes, and that chain is how the town lost its players.

applies_to: Yakuza (Ballot Stuffer, Smuggler, any token role)
tip: Spend one-shot vote tokens the night before any teammate could face a close trial, not 'for a later Day'. A doubled Innocent turns a bare-majority Guilty into a tie, which fails. Once a teammate has been read Evil, expect the next trial to involve your team.
evidence: Alice saved her ballot token on Nights 1 and 2. She was hanged 4 Guilty of 7 on Day 3. With a stuffed ballot it would have been 4 of 8, not a majority, and she would have lived. Carol also died on Day 2 with both swap tokens unused.

tip: Never mention a hidden role you only know from night chat, even in passing. Refer to dead players only by what is public (cause of death, Sheriff claims). Re-read any message that names a role before sending it.
evidence: Alice said 'Carol was Smuggler' on Day 3, though Carol's role was never revealed. Erin, Frank and Dave pounced at once, and Alice was nominated and hanged the same Day despite calling it a slip.

tip: A Not Evil result only fails to clear the one player who held the Katana that night. Rank players with no check above players with a Not Evil read. Never nominate someone your own Sheriff just read Not Evil without independent evidence.
evidence: Grace nominated Dave on Day 3 on her own Not Evil read, and he was cleared 0-7, wasting the nomination. On Day 4 the town hanged Erin, read Not Evil on Night 3. Bob, never checked and the actual holder all game, survived to kill Grace that night.

tip: Don't publicly announce whom you protected or plan to protect. After claiming Medic, expect to be the next kill and spend a token to protect yourself, or pick your cover carefully. Your free protection on the confirmed power role is what keeps them alive.
evidence: Heidi posted her Night 1 and Night 2 targets. Her Night 2 protect saved Grace from the Katana, but Bob killed Heidi on Night 3 while she still had 2 unused medic tokens. With no Medic left, Grace died on Night 4.

tip: In the final three, never offer a private vote trade. The recipient can paste it publicly, and it reads as a confession. Argue publicly, and target the Villager most likely to vote with you.
evidence: Bob privately told Frank 'Vote Innocent here and I'll vote Guilty on Dave'. Frank quoted it publicly, Dave voted Guilty, and Bob was hanged 2-1, ending the game.

tip: In the final three, recompute every past trial total against each player's stated vote before nominating. One miscounted vote can mislynch a Villager and hand the last Yakuza the win at night.
evidence: On Day 5 Dave claimed Frank's Innocent vote on Erin didn't fit the 3-of-5 total and nominated him. Frank showed the third Guilty was Erin herself, Dave admitted the error, and Frank survived 1-2. A Guilty would have left Bob and Dave, and Bob's next Katana kill would have won it.

tip: When your votes can't save a teammate, vote Guilty and don't defend them publicly. Defending a teammate who was caught on a mechanical tell becomes the case against you once you are the last one left.
evidence: Alice and Bob voted Guilty on Carol (7-1) and stayed unsuspected. On Day 3 Bob defended Alice's Smuggler slip and voted Innocent, yet she was hanged 4-3 anyway. On Day 5 Dave and Frank both cited that defence to hang Bob.

tip: Take the Night 1 kill unless you have a concrete reason not to. A skipped kill gives investigators and protectors a free night and leaves the Village a player ahead in the endgame count.
evidence: The Yakuza agreed not to attack on Night 1, while Grace's free check exposed Carol. The game came down to one Yakuza against two Villagers. With one extra kill, Bob would have reached parity before the final trials.

tip: When a Village power role claims a result that matters for the next hang, demand its posted result before nominating anyone. Frank died with his Night 2 track unposted, so the Day 3 case rested on an inference chain instead of the Tracker's own result.

A Yakuza-only role (Smuggler) with unused tokens and a shifting claim is a strong hang lead. Get the story pinned down first (no action, then Smuggler, then no N1 action), then hang on that contradiction, not on a plan nobody can check.

Use a Katana kill to check claims: the holder must have visited the victim, so list the night's visitors with the Insomniac or Tracker reads and see which claimed role can make that visit. Two visitors and one dead Tracker leave only one possible holder.
Ask yes-or-no questions about a specific night action and track whether the answer stays the same. Carol's answers changed over the Day, and that shift gave the table a concrete reason to vote.

Before a hang, post a one-line summary of each claim and the visits that support it. Erin's map, Bob's visitor reads and Dave's results were all public, so the table could check them against each other in one place.

Cross the Insomniac's visitor role list with the cause of death. A Katana or other attack victim must have been visited by the attacker, so if the list holds only one role that can plausibly attack, you have your suspect. Write that deduction down before you post it, and keep it to roles, since names are hidden.

Before nominating or voting Guilty, state the one visit or result that would clear the nominee, and check whether it can still be obtained. Carol's case stalled on an unexplained swap plan and never got a check, so the vote rested on pressure rather than mechanics.

Ask a direct yes-or-no question about a night action and wait for a plain answer. Carol's shifting story (no action, then Smuggler, then no action on N1) was the clearest tell in the game and drew the most scrutiny, so this kind of pressure exposes Yakuza claims that don't fit.

Don't make a Diviner or other information claim late, after a teammate has already been hanged or attacked. Dave's delayed claim and the Diviner-visitor timing made the Katana holder easy to locate, so claim early with a consistent result or stay quiet.

Share the non-visit information you hold (who was attacked, who was visited) in one message, so the whole Village can cross-check the same facts at once. Early results from several roles let the group pin the Katana holder by Day 3.

applies_to: Smuggler, or any Yakuza claiming a role
tip: Settle one clean role story on the first Day and repeat it exactly. My early 'no night action' answer, then a later 'Smuggler' claim, created the contradiction that got me nominated, and it was never cleared.

Unused swap tokens with no stated plan read as Yakuza-only. Before the first Day ends, give a concrete plan (for example a decoy swap on a named night) or spend the token on a visible test, so the tokens don't become the case against you.

Before choosing a Katana target, check which claimed power roles would expose the holder. Killing a Tracker who tracked the holder, when only two visitors exist, leaves a visitor count that points straight at the Diviner-visitor, so the team gets exposed.

Insomniac visitor role lists plus a Katana kill on a claimed Tracker narrow the holder to one visitor. Combine that with a Cartographer's group size to test the Diviner's claim, instead of arguing from the claims themselves.

Cartographer group sizes and map results are checkable, since Frank's death and Erin's map together fixed the Katana visit. Post exact sizes and groups every night so others can check them against claims.

Before a Katana kill, check which visitor roles a watcher could recover. The holder's visit to the victim and the holder's own role visit both count, and an Insomniac or Tracker can expose them. If the only remaining visitor roles identify the holder, pick a different victim or hold the Katana off that night.

Don't publicly claim a Yakuza-only role like Diviner when your teammates are gone. A real visit corroborated by an Insomniac makes you the obvious suspect when a Katana kill lands. Claim a Village role whose tokens and visits match your real actions, and keep the claim consistent.

Don't publicly defend a teammate who is about to hang. My defense of Carol didn't save her and cost me credibility I needed on Day 3. Vote with the town or stay quiet, and keep your credibility for the trial you can actually win.

Cross-check visitor-role reports (Insomniac) against map groups (Cartographer) and the night's attacks. Erin's map and Bob's two visitor roles pinned the Katana holder, and naming the mechanical fit before voting Guilty made the Day 3 hang clean.

A Tracker's unposted result is lost if the Tracker dies that night. Post track results at the start of the next Day, and if you're a Village power role who might die, post results on the Day they happen so the town doesn't lose them.

applies_to: Cartographer and other map or group-info roles
tip: Spend the map token on the claim that splits the table, as early as possible. A map of a suspected Katana holder's target or a disputed claim's group settles who was in the room. I spent mine on Night 2, after a Day 2 hang had already happened, so it came too late to stop the wrong lynch.

Combine count-based info with a death. Insomniac visitor roles plus a Katana kill on a known Tracker leaves only the Diviner as possible holder. Write the constraint down (who visited whom, who died, who holds the Katana) before voting, and check every claim against it.

Do not let a trial be decided on a plan that hasn't been finished. Carol's Day 2 hang was driven by an unfinished Night 2 plan, not a result. When a nominee has no contradicting result, ask for the outstanding data first. Hanging on an open question costs a Village vote with no info gained.

Many players repeated the same 'no nominations until Night 2 results' message several times, which burned budget without new information. Post a fresh fact or a concrete question, not a restatement, to keep budget for the trial turns where votes actually happen.

applies_to: Tracker, Lookout and other visit-watching roles
tip: Don't spend a first-night track on a player who has no night action and is unclaimed or Vanilla. A 'visited nobody' result only confirms they were idle. Track the player most likely to act: an early nominee, an unverified claimant, or someone whose claim conflicts with another's. Prefer targets whose visits would be informative if they are Yakuza.

A Katana kill means the holder visited the victim, so the holder is one of the victim's visitors. Insomniac counts plus a Tracker or Lookout result can pin that visitor down. Use the count to test claims: if the Insomniac's visitor roles and the Katana victim's role are both known, the list of possible holders shrinks fast.

A Yakuza claim that matches true mechanics (for example a Diviner whose group contains a real Tracker) is hard to disprove. Test claims by whether independent claims agree on visits, not by how well the claim fits. Ask the claimant to name every player they visited, then check that against the Katana victim and the visit map.

Before a hang, name one concrete mechanical contradiction. In this game the strongest votes came from players who asked a claimant a yes/no question about a visit and got an evasive answer. Vague suspicion produced a 4-3 hang that was close enough to matter.

applies_to: Tracker, or any information role that dies to a Katana
tip: Post your result publicly as soon as it is known, even if your night target was a weak one. Results that die with you help nobody. If you suspect the Katana holder has already visited you, consider claiming with your result earlier in the Day.

A Katana kill proves the holder visited the victim. If a Tracker or Insomniac report lists only a few visitors, the holder must be one of them. Cross-check the visitor roles against the kill, then test each Yakuza-possible claim against the visit groups. This is how Bob's Insomniac count and Erin's map isolated Dave.

Don't let an unposted night result stall the Day. Frank died holding an unreleased Night 2 track, and that track could have settled Dave earlier. When a key investigator is likely to die, ask them to post results immediately, and vote on the evidence you already have.

Before a Guilty vote, ask one yes-or-no question and name one contradiction. Carol's shift from 'no night action' to 'Smuggler' was checkable, and the plain-answer demand is what exposed the unexplained swap tokens. Vague accusations or long repeated 'no nomination until results' posts only burn speaking budget.

Yakuza-only roles with unused tokens and no stated plan are suspicious. Smuggler swap tokens and Diviner claims can both be made to fit a Katana kill. A claim that fits the public results can still be a Yakuza's, so verify it against visits and kills, not against how confidently it is stated.

Repeated short 'no nomination until X' messages cost budget without adding information. Spend budget on the one checkable point or the one question that matters, and save the rest for trial turns where the vote is decided.

Never publicly claim a Yakuza-only role (Smuggler, Diviner, Pharmacist and so on), even if it seems to fit the evidence. If an exact-role result has already exposed your role, either avoid visiting so the result can't be pinned on you, or build a cover in night chat before Day 2. Don't confirm it yourself.
evidence: Carol claimed Smuggler and was hanged that same Day, and Alice and Bob both cited 'Smuggler is a Yakuza role'. Dave claimed Diviner after Bob's Insomniac reported a Diviner visitor. On Day 3 Bob nominated him with 'Diviner is a Yakuza role here'.

tip: Check every claimed role, and every role an exact-role result shows (Insomniac, Archivist, Profiler, Surveyor), against the Yakuza role list right away. A Yakuza-only role in a result means a Yakuza is visiting, and whoever claims that role is effectively confirmed Evil. Hang them that Day.
evidence: Bob's Night 1 result showed 'Diviner' and Dave claimed Diviner on Day 2, yet the Village hanged Carol on vaguer grounds and left Dave alive. Dave killed Frank, the Tracker, that night. Hanging Dave on Day 2 would have saved Frank.

tip: Before you visit, assume every result that has been announced as coming tonight will happen. If an Insomniac, Cartographer or Tracker has said they'll act, a visit from a holder whose role is already exposed is close to a confession. Either skip the visit or kill whoever's result would expose you.
evidence: Bob announced on Day 2 that he'd spend his last Insomniac token on Night 2. Dave still both visited Bob as Diviner and attacked Frank with the Katana. Bob heard 'Diviner, Tracker' again, Erin's map linked Bob, Dave and Frank, and Dave was hanged the next Day.

tip: After a Katana kill, combine the visitor-role lists, map groups and track results into an elimination. Once you remove the visitors who are explained, the remaining visitor to the victim is the holder. Post that chain of reasoning in one message and nominate at once.
evidence: On Day 3 Bob reasoned: two visitors, a Diviner and a Tracker. The Tracker was the victim, so the Diviner made the Katana visit, and Dave is the only Diviner claim. Erin's map backed this up, and Dave was hanged 4-1 without dragging out the Day.

tip: Answer a question about your night action with your full role and plan in one consistent sentence the first time. Saying 'no action' and then giving a role claim, or holding a result back 'until it's useful', creates a case against you on its own.
evidence: Carol said 'no night action, not the Diviner', then claimed Smuggler, then gave vague N2 answers over many rounds. The whole table piled on and Alice nominated her for it. Dave's 'I'll share it when it's most useful' also drew pressure until he gave in and claimed.

tip: In small games (around 7 players), take the Night 1 kill and aim it at a likely information role. Skipping it gives away tempo the Village will use against you. Also make sure a holder's role action doesn't add an exposing visit on top of the Katana visit.
evidence: Carol and Dave agreed to skip the Night 1 kill. That left the Insomniac, Cartographer and Tracker all alive to build the Night 2 elimination that caught Dave.

applies_to: Village information roles (Census Taker, Sheriff, Seer, Coroner, Tracker and similar)
tip: Post your full result at the first public chance, with the exact group and counts. The Katana went after information roles early (Archivist on Night 1, Census Taker on Night 2), so a result held back for a later Day may never be shared. Claim and post on the first Day, even when the result is only partial.

Before accepting an accusation based on vote history, recount the announced totals against who said Yes or Guilty. Several Day 3-4 claims about votes were wrong and had to be corrected. Yes/No nomination counts cannot be altered, so use them as the cleanest check on what a player says they voted.

Mark the strongest suspect early, not one picked from another player's census alone. A marked player's death reveals their true role, which settled the Day 3 hang. The mark works on any cause of death, so it is a reliable way to confirm a role once someone dies.

Require one concrete mechanical fit before a Guilty vote, such as a census that names only one unexplained player, or a mark or Coroner result that points at a single target. Votes made this way on Day 3 hanged the correct Yakuza (the Clerk).

applies_to: Coroner, Mortician and other astral-check roles
tip: Spend the astral check on a dead player early (Night 2 at the latest) and post the exact role in your first Day speech. A verified role on a dead Village player (here Frank, then Alice) cut the suspect list in half and was the only hard evidence in the game.

Before a hang, list which players have no verifiable result at all and ask each of them for one checkable fact. Day 4's hang of Grace rested on silence and a misstated vote record. Silence alone is not a mechanic; a concrete mismatch between a claimed vote and the announced totals is.

A Chronicler mark plus a death reveal is a free role check. Mark only on evidence you can state, and if a marked player dies, the reveal is a strong public fact to build the next Day's case on. Carol's mark on Dave verified a Clerk Yakuza and was the game's clearest signal.

Compare nomination and trial totals against the claimed votes of everyone before voting. Grace's self-correction showed that a player who misstates their own vote record can be checked against the 4-Yes and 4-Guilty totals; use that arithmetic rather than tone.

When a Day is spent saying wait, name a deadline for results and a default nominee. Day 2 ran with almost everyone repeating 'no nomination until Day 3', which gave the Katana two free kills and let claims sit unchallenged.

Mark the player you most suspect on a reasoned basis, not out of a single census. A mark pays off only if that player dies, and it reveals their true role to everyone. My Night 2 mark on Dave was lucky, and my Night 3 mark on Bob had no stated reason, so it could have wasted a token and cast doubt on me.

Check each claimed vote against the announced totals before you accept or attack it. Nomination counts can't be altered, so a claimed No that doesn't fit the Yes count is a clean lie check. Grace's false vote record came out only because the arithmetic was checked.

Silence alone is not a reason to nominate. I nominated Grace on Day 4 mainly for not stating a role, and Grace was a Neutral Arsonist who was not Yakuza. Before nominating, name a mechanical contradiction, not a missing claim.

Track the Arsonist's douse pattern. Doused players are not told when they are Good, so the Night 1 to 3 douse targets (Alice, Erin, Bob) were a strong clue that the douser was a Neutral building toward an ignite. Ask who was doused and who visited them, then nominate the visitor if the pattern fits.

Coroner and Census claims that can be cross-checked are worth more than any single claim. Ask which claims interlock (a census group containing a dead player, a coroner exam of that player) and check those interlocks before any hang. The Day 3 hang rested on one unverifiable coroner result and was right only by luck.

A Chronicler mark turns any death, including a hanging, into a public role reveal. When a mark lands on a teammate or on you, treat it as a kill order. Spend the Katana on the claimed Chronicler or Coroner before a second claim can build a case, rather than on a claimed Census Taker who had already been checked.

applies_to: Yakuza with a Clerk or other one-shot token
tip: Spend a Clerk rig on the Day you are most likely to be nominated or hanged, or when the Village nominees are already lined up. Holding the token to the end wasted it: when the vote turned against me, the rig could not save me, because it executes whoever is nominated.

A plain Vanilla claim cannot be checked, so every outside claim lands on you unopposed. If your claim comes with a spare token and no visits to match it, adopt a role whose visits and tokens can be cross-checked, or plan a cover visit so an unverifiable denial does not look like the only defence.

Keep your own vote log and check it against the announced totals before you accuse anyone of a misstated record. This game turned on a Day 4 count mismatch, and the Village only won because the 4-Yes and 4-Guilty totals exposed a misstatement that the accused had made.

Day 2 turned into repeated Wait-for-Day-3 posts from almost every player, which spent budget and produced no information. If a Day has no new results, post one concrete question or check per turn instead of a general agreement to wait.

When a Chronicler mark, a Coroner result and a census all point at one player, ask for the one check that could contradict them before the vote, and make sure it is answered. On Day 2 the village waited two full days with no new information, and the Katana killed one player each night. Use the day to push for concrete checks rather than just saying you will wait.

Count the announced Yes and Guilty totals against the named voters before accepting or attacking someone's vote record. Grace's self-correction showed how easy it is to misremember a vote, and a contradiction in a vote record is only meaningful once it is checked against the announced totals.

A mark that is placed without an independent result is weak evidence, and the Chronicler should say so.
