Carol's Night 2 mark on Dave came from Alice's census alone, so it confirmed nothing until Dave died and the reveal settled it. It is still worth marking a strong suspect, because the reveal on death converts the mark into a verified role.

Track which players were doused by the Arsonist and which were visited by Katana attacks. A Neutral killer can look like a passive Village player, and the Arsonist's doused players are never told, so the only public clue is repeated night visits to players who survive. Note these visit patterns early so a Neutral can be hunted before the final two.

With a single Yakuza and a Neutral among seven players, the Katana attacks and the Clerk's reveal can identify the Yakuza quickly. A Vanilla should press for a Night result from the Coroner, Census Taker or Chronicler as soon as one is claimed, instead of joining the wait.

applies_to: Village roles that might die early (e.g. Archivist, any power role with no result yet)
tip: Your will is the only channel that survives your death, so write your role claim, any Night 1 info, and your suspicion of who attacked you into it before Night 1. A generic will like 'weigh every claim' gives the town nothing. Frank died on Night 1 with no role information reaching anyone.

Check each player's stated vote against the announced totals before trusting any vote-record argument. The Day 4 Grace dispute was resolved only because the Yes and Guilty counts fit one version of her votes. Do this arithmetic every trial, and treat a mismatch as a lead to question, not as proof.

A single unverifiable claim (a Coroner read, a Chronicler mark, or a census result) should not drive a hang alone. Look for a second source or a death-reveal that tests it. Carol's Chronicler mark on Dave was confirmed only when Dave died and his Clerk role was revealed, which is the kind of independent check the town needed before voting.

With 6 other living players, the Archivist sees 3 roles of which only 3 are real and 3 are fake, so one read is weak. Use it to corroborate a claim you already have, not as a standalone check. Spend the token when it can confirm or refute a specific claim, not on a whim.

When a claim is made on Day 2 and the town is told to wait for a result, make sure the claimant has a way to be checked against a second source. Here, the Day 3 nomination rested on Bob's Coroner read and Carol's mark, and only the Clerk reveal on Dave's death tested either of them.

Before posting any vote or correction, write your exact nomination and trial votes in your notepad and check them against the announced totals. I misstated my Day 3 votes (said No/Innocent when I had voted Yes/Guilty), and the correction cost me credibility when the table was already split. A self-inflicted mismatch looks like a lie even when it is an honest error.

Silence is a liability. Being quiet for two Days with no role or result got me nominated 'for silence' on Day 4. Post a short, concrete status each Day (role or no role, what you did, what you're watching) so nobody can build a case from your absence.

Build a Yakuza read from mechanics, not volume. The Day 3 hang was right because Bob's Coroner result on Frank and Alice's census both pointed at Dave, and Carol's Chronicler mark on Dave came back as a Clerk. Checking which claims share a common mechanical source is what separated true from false here.

Douses persist across nights until an ignite, but a doused player who dies no longer counts toward the 3 living doused needed. Count only living doused players, and plan ignite timing around deaths. Dousing Village players who are being watched by Coroner, Chronicler or Census Taker risks drawing attention, so keep the douse pattern quiet and don't announce it.

A Neutral who is only dousing or waiting to ignite should choose one clear public story early (for example Vanilla with no night action), and keep it. My silence plus changing vote records made me the hang target when Yakuza were already losing.

Don't Katana-kill someone who shares a group result (census, survey, Diviner group) with you. Katana victims are assumed Good, so each one you kill from the group narrows the suspects toward you. Kill outside the group, or kill the investigator who can confirm the remaining names.
evidence: Alice's Night 1 census put Bob, Dave and Frank at 2 of 3 Good, and Dave had Katana'd Frank that same night. From Day 2 on, everyone reasoned 'Frank was Katana'd, so it's Bob or Dave.' Once Bob claimed to be Good, Dave was the obvious suspect.

tip: When a player has publicly promised the next night's confirming result, kill that player, not the one whose result is already public. A dead Coroner can't confirm the body that convicts you.
evidence: On Night 2 Dave killed Alice, whose Night 1 result was already known. Bob, who had announced he would examine Frank, lived and posted 'Frank was an Archivist' on Day 3. That locked the census onto Dave, and Dave was hanged that Day.

tip: Spend Day-only tokens such as a Clerk rig before you become the nominee. Rig a Day when you can push a nomination onto a Villager, and have a claim ready that explains the group results against you, not a bare 'Vanilla, no action.'
evidence: Dave held the Clerk token through Day 2, when nobody was nominated and he could have rigged and pushed a nomination of Bob. He died on Day 3 with the token unused. His defence was only 'three unverifiable claims,' and it lost 4 to 1.

tip: Once you are the only player without a claim, or the Yakuza are gone and you're the obvious last suspect, ignite with whatever living players are doused that night. A late ignite is better than being hanged with your douses unused.
evidence: On Night 3 Bob and Erin were doused, 4 players were alive, and Grace was the only one who hadn't claimed. She doused again instead of igniting. She was nominated and hanged on Day 4 without killing anyone.

tip: Claim a plausible role early, and if you state your votes, make them match the announced totals. Nomination totals are public and can't be changed, so a stated vote that contradicts them is an easy catch, and changing your story afterwards confirms the lie.
evidence: Grace said 'no claim' through Days 2 to 4 and drew a silence nomination. In her defence she claimed No on Dave's nomination, but it passed 4 Yes of 5 with only Dave voting No. Carol and Erin pointed this out, and Grace's correction did not save her.

tip: Combine group-count results with the assumption that Katana victims were Good, then use a body exam or a reveal to confirm. When elimination leaves one name and a second source agrees, nominate right away, and say what the mechanical fit is.
evidence: Erin nominated Dave on Day 3 using Alice's census, Frank's Archivist result and the fact that Katana victims are usually Good. The hang revealed a Clerk.

tip: Mark the most likely next hang or the most suspicious unclaimed player, so the death reveal confirms the Village's read. Don't spend a token on a player who is already well confirmed.
evidence: Carol's Night 2 mark on Dave revealed the Clerk on his hanging and confirmed both Alice's and Bob's claims. Her last token, on Night 3, went on Bob, who was already consistent. A mark on the unclaimed Grace would have revealed the Arsonist when she was hanged.

tip: If a public group result plus a Katana kill already narrows things to one unexplained name on Day 2, weigh hanging that night's suspect then. Waiting a night for confirmation usually costs a power role.
evidence: On Day 2 Bob argued it was Dave once Frank was assumed Good, but the Village spent all 8 rounds repeating 'wait for Day 3.' Dave used that night to kill Alice, and her Night 2 census (which would have exposed Grace too) was lost.

tip: Never publicly claim a Yakuza-only role such as Ritualist, even when pressed to explain yourself. Once it was public, Bob's push turned it into a 4-1 Guilty vote and I was hanged on Day 3, which left Carol to carry the team alone.

Plan Katana targets in night chat so that the most dangerous information role dies early. Killing the Scrutineer on Night 2 removed the only check on the trial voters, and the Village never recovered it.

Keep your public Yes and Innocent votes internally consistent. My Yes on Dave's nomination and Innocent at Frank's trial were both fine taken alone, but they handed the Village a clean read on my behaviour that they used against me.

When two players claim the same role, demand a checkable result, then test it against public tallies. Grace and Bob caught Dave's Juror result contradicting the public trial record, which is the strongest verification move in this game.

With two players left, a nomination needs both votes. A lone Vanilla cannot force a hang, so the Village should act before the Yakuza reach parity. Spend the earlier Days on checkable questions rather than on claim-versus-claim disputes that stalled the Village through Day 2 and Day 3.

When two players claim the same information role, check each claimed result against the public trial and nomination records yourself before judging either. Here Dave reported 'Frank and Alice: no shared votes' even though both had voted Innocent at Frank's trial. That made Dave look provably false, but Dave was a real Juror. Treat a moderator-style result that conflicts with the public record as a question to raise, not as proof of a lie, and don't hang on one line.

Don't let Day 2 stall into 'post your result at dawn' loops. Repeating 'no nomination from me yet' for a full Day lost time, and the stall rule then forced hangs on thin evidence. Commit early to one nomination backed by a concrete reason, and keep the team to a trial per Day.

With two players alive, a nomination needs two Yes votes, so one Yakuza voting No can freeze the Village forever while the Katana keeps killing. Avoid reaching a last-two standoff with a Yakuza alive. Hang the most suspicious player while three or more are alive, so the remaining votes can still carry a trial.

Never claim a Yakuza-only role (Ritualist) publicly, even to deflect. Alice's public Ritualist claim gave the Village a clear, uncontested lead and got her hanged on Day 3. If a role claim is needed, pick a Village role whose tokens and visits match your real actions.

A forced trial is a strong tool early, when a claim is clearly Evil. Use it on a public Evil-role claimant in the first Day when it can change the vote count, and post the reason in plain words. Keep one token for the Day when the Village is most likely to stall.

Never publicly claim a Yakuza-only role such as Ritualist. Villagers almost never advertise an Evil role, so the claim draws the first trial and gets the teammate hanged. Stay silent, or claim a Village role whose visits and tokens match yours.

Do not defend a teammate on trial with a visible Innocent vote when the team can't save them. Other players read the Innocent totals and the public defense as proof. Vote with the town and save the defense for a case you can win.

Katana kills on Village roles that threaten you (Scrutineer, Juror, Sheriff) are worth it, and killing a power role early removes the Village's only checks. Keep the holder and target agreement in night chat every night, since one missing vote cancels the kill.

When two players claim the same role and give conflicting pair results, check each result against the public trial and nomination tallies first. A result that contradicts the public record is provably false, and that settles it without a hang. Do not hang either claimant on claim-vs-claim alone.

Before a Guilty vote, name one mechanical fit against the nominee, such as a result that contradicts a public record. Grace's Dave argument did this, and it made the hang defensible. Hanging on who pushed the nomination wastes votes that the Village needs for later checks.

Before hanging anyone on a checkable result, reconcile it against the public trial and nomination record. Dave's Night 2 line 'Frank and Alice have no shared votes yet' contradicted the Day 2 record, where both voted Innocent, and the Village hanged him on it. If a result seems impossible, check it against the ledger and say so publicly before voting on it, rather than treating it as proof either way.

When two players both claim the same role, don't trust either claim. Compare each claimant's checkable results with the others' (e.g. a shared pair both of them report) and with the public record. Frank's result on Dave and Alice matched the record exactly, which was the strongest evidence in the game, but it was not weighed against Dave's conflicting line.

Don't open a nomination on a claim-versus-claim dispute with no mechanical evidence behind it. Day 2 went to a 6-Yes nomination of a Juror with nothing checkable, and the Village lost the Day, the Juror, and later the Scrutineer's and Juror's information. Wait for a result that can be tested, and nominate only then.
Never publicly claim a Yakuza-only role such as Ritualist. Alice's public Ritualist claim gave the Village a clean reason to push and hang her, even though she had made no guesses to test.

Repeating 'no nomination from me yet' with no new information costs budget every round and rises in price later. Spend the budget on one concrete question or check per Day, which gives the other players something to answer.

applies_to: Village power roles (Scrutineer, Sheriff, Seer, Juror and similar)
tip: Name your role in your first public speech, with what it reads and when. Dodging the question for two Day-2 turns made the table read me as a dodge, and the Yakuza then targeted me on Night 2. A reader who is hidden or vague is a Katana target.

applies_to: Village power roles that read trials
tip: If your role needs a trial to produce a result, push for a nomination early (Day 2) instead of waiting for someone else to nominate. Day 2 went by with no trial, so my Scrutineer read never got going before I died.

Check a conflicting claim against public records before anything else. Dave's Night 2 pair result said two players had 'no shared votes', but the public Day 2 trial tally showed they had both voted Innocent. That single contradiction exposed a liar, so verify each checkable claim against what is already public.

applies_to: Village players facing two same-role claims
tip: When two players claim the same role and one result contradicts public records, treat the contradicted claim as false. Don't hang anyone on who pushed the nomination. Trial votes that match the public record are the cleanest signal.
Trial totals can exceed the voter count because of a Ballot Stuffer. Track the announced totals against the voter count each day, and don't read a surplus as an error.

When two players claim the same role and their checkable results conflict, a contradiction only proves one report is wrong. Get a second independent check (public vote totals, a second night's result) before a hang. I hanged a genuine Juror on one conflicting line, and both Jurors turned out to be real.

If you hold a checkable role and have no result on Day 2, do not just promise one at dawn. Repeated 'I'll post it later' reads as a dodge and became the basis for my nomination. Post your full log as soon as you have it, or a test you can run on Night 1 so you have something to show by Day 2.

The Katana kills information roles early (Scrutineer on Night 2, Juror on Night 3). Put every result into your will the same night and post it at the first chance on the next Day, so the village keeps the information even if you die before speaking.

Count the endgame before each hang. With 2 alive, a nomination needs both votes, so a Good player cannot remove a Yakuza alone. Prioritize hanging the strongest Yakuza read while 4 or more are alive, and never spend a hang on a weak read at 4 or fewer.

A trial total above the voter count (4 Guilty of 5 votes with 4 voters on Day 4) means a Ballot Stuffer. Use that as a lead: who has ballot tokens and who pushed the trial. I noticed the anomaly but did not follow it up.

applies_to: Village roles that check votes (Juror, Scrutineer, Auditor)
tip: Before calling a checkable result false, reread the exact rule. The Juror's count excludes any vote on the nomination or trial of either tested player. So 'no shared votes yet' can be true even when both players voted the same way on the other's trial. I convicted a Good Juror on a contradiction I had misread.
A public mechanical contradiction is only a lead until you have checked the rules and the exact trial record. Ask the claimant to show the rule that makes their result wrong before you vote on it.
Do not let Day 2 drift with no nominations. Three days of stalling forced rushed hangs with no evidence. Put a low-cost nomination up early so trial voting records exist for the checks to read.

At 2 living players a nomination needs 2 Yes, so the nominee's own No blocks any hang. A Vanilla in a 2-player endgame cannot force an execution. The Village has to hang the Yakuza while there are 3 or 4 players alive.
Name your role and post your results on the first chance. Erin's dodge over two Days made a Good Scrutineer look Evil and gave the Yakuza a reason to target her at night.

Only unique roles (Smuggler, Vulture) are limited to one copy. Two players claiming the same ordinary role is not a contradiction. Both can be real, so judge each claim by its own results, not by 'only one can be real.'
evidence: Frank and Dave were both real Jurors. All of Day 2, and the case for hanging Dave on Day 4, rested on the false premise that one of them had to be lying.

tip: Before calling a result 'provably false,' reread the role text for exclusions and edge cases. Juror results leave out votes in the trial of either tested player, and Scrutineer and Census groups add random players. Work out the expected result yourself before using it as a mechanical fit.
evidence: Dave's 'Frank and Alice: no shared votes yet' was correct because the only trial had been Frank's, which the Juror excludes. Grace, Bob and Carol all called it a lie, and the real Juror was hanged.

tip: Never name your real Yakuza role, in chat or in the claim ledger. Have a Village fake claim ready before Day 2, ideally a role with no checkable results, such as Vanilla Villager.
evidence: Alice's Day 2 ledger entry read 'Ritualist (Evil).' Bob prosecuted her on Night 2, and she was hanged 4-2 on Day 3 with nothing else against her.

tip: Once a player is hanged as near-certain Yakuza, go straight to whoever publicly argued or voted Innocent for them. When few players are left and a mislynch loses the game, put that lead on trial before a disputed claim.
evidence: Carol announced Innocent on Alice, and the totals showed 2 Innocent votes. Bob raised it on Day 4, but nobody nominated Carol. Dave was hanged instead, and two nights later the game was lost.

tip: A prosecution forces a trial, and an execution ends the Day. Use it only on your strongest, double-checked lead, especially when few players are left. A wrong prosecution can use up the Village's last chance to hang the real Yakuza.
evidence: Bob's Night 2 prosecution of Alice won a hang. His Night 3 prosecution of Dave, based on a misread result, filled Day 4 at 4 alive with a mislynch.

tip: When the Village has settled on a wrong target, join the Guilty vote and, if you can, add your doubled ballot. Spend vote-changing tokens on the night before the trial you expect. Kill the confirmed information roles each night while the Village argues.
evidence: Carol stuffed her ballot on Night 3, voted Guilty on Dave (4 Guilty of 5), and killed Erin and Frank, the two reliable sources of results.

tip: On Day 2, with no result yet, either say nothing about your role or claim it plainly once. Half-hinting ('my role reads past trials') brings both pressure and a Katana target.
evidence: Erin hinted, was hounded until she named Scrutineer, and was the Night 2 Katana target. The Yakuza chat said explicitly that her claim was the reason.

tip: Count the endgame. At 4 alive with 1 Yakuza, a mislynch leads to 3 alive, then 2, and a nomination needs a majority. A lone Villager facing the last Yakuza can never get a trial, so the Village has to solve it while 4 are alive.
evidence: On Day 5 Grace nominated Carol four times and got 1 Yes each time. That could never reach the 2 needed, so the game was already over.

tip: Place the trap on a claimed investigator or info role that a Serial Killer or Katana holder must visit to kill, not on a Yakuza member who will simply avoid visiting. Frank and Niaj were both killed by visits, and a trap on either would have hit the Serial Killer on that night. My trap on Heidi never went off because the Yakuza never visited her.

A trap moved onto someone is armed only from the next night, so moving it onto a player who dies that night (Ivan, on Night 5) wastes the move. Before moving, prefer a player likely to survive the coming night, or keep the trap where a killer would have to visit.

When a player pushes a trial and then says "hang me" after a claim that cannot exist in this game, treat it as a Jester pattern. A Guilty majority hands the Jester the win, and the Jester's revenge then kills a random Guilty voter (Dave died this way). Keep Guilty votes to a bare majority and make sure power roles are Innocent, or demand a checkable answer before the vote.

Check whether a claimed role exists in this game's role list before weighing its results. A Yakuza-only role claimed by a Good player is a lie, but a true Yakuza may claim it too. A Diviner claim plus the Vigilante draw from the same group is a consistency check, not proof.

Post a checkable night result early and trade it for a matching result from another role, rather than waiting for a second pair. The town spent Days 2 and 3 waiting for Frank's Night 2 pair, and the Yakuza used that time to remove the Seer and the Tracker.

Treat a player who asks to be hanged, or who pushes a trial on a thin read and then claims an impossible role, as a possible Jester. A Jester wins by being hanged, so a Guilty vote may hand them the win. Demand a mechanical reason before voting Guilty on such a player, and vote Innocent if none is given.

Check every claimed role against the rules' faction lists before trusting it. Heidi's Diviner claim was a Yakuza-only role, which Good players cannot hold, and the Village took until Day 5 to act on it.

Read the cause of every death. A Serial Killer attack proves a Neutral killer is alive, and a profile or pair that names the same player as the only non-Good candidate is a strong lead. This is how Erin's Serial Killer identity was reached.

Juror vote-agreement counts are low information when the sample is 0 of 1 or 1 of 2. Spend checks on pairs with many votes, such as players who voted in the same several trials, or on the nominator and nominee of a fresh nomination, so the count can separate Yakuza from Village.

Fire the shot on the first night you have a concrete lead, not after several nights of waiting. Olivia held three tokens until Night 5 and only then shot a Yakuza, so the Village lost the chance to remove an informer earlier.

Spend exact-role checks on the first dead claimant whose result conflicts with another claim, on the very next night. I held my Coroner tokens for two nights while the Frank/Erin/Carol pair stalled the town; the exam that cleared Frank came on Night 3, one Day too late. An Astral Visit is also invisible to the Trapper, so it is a safe check.

The Yakuza killed every claimant who posted a result each night (Frank, Niaj, Carol, Ivan). Publish results early and in full, but don't stake the whole town on one claimant's word. Ask for a second independent check before a nomination, and keep your next-night action on the most threatening unverified claim.

Vanilla Villager and Grunt are never in the setup, so any Vanilla claim is false. Treat it, together with a thin trial push and a 'hang me' plea, as a strong Jester signal. Before hanging a suspected Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority: revenge kills a random Guilty voter, and Dave died that way.

Diviner is listed as a Yakuza role in these rules, so a Good player cannot hold it. Check the faction of a claimed role against the rules before weighing the claim. Also, two attackers (Katana plus a Serial Killer) can both hit one target, so a single surviving attack proves little about how many killers there are.
A hanged Jester wins but the game does not end. The Village must still win afterward, so hanging a suspected Jester is not a win by itself. Track which side still has living members.

Voting Guilty on a suspected Jester can cost you: the Jester's revenge kills a random living Guilty voter. Dave, a Yakuza Katana holder, was killed this way and the Katana passed. Before a Yakuza votes on a possible Jester hang, weigh that risk against the vote count.

Do not publicly claim a Yakuza-only role (such as Diviner) as cover. The town can check it against the role lists, and Heidi was hanged on that claim. Pick a Village role whose token count and visits fit your real actions.
Keep coordination in night chat. A visible daytime PM cluster between two Yakuza (Judy and Heidi on Days 4 and 5) became the town's main lead and got them both hanged or exposed.

applies_to: Neutral killers (Serial Killer, Arsonist) and anyone facing a trial with no claim
tip: Silence plus 'I won't invent a role' reads as guilt. When you're on trial, give a concrete, checkable answer (a role you can defend, or a specific night result) rather than only attacking the accuser's timing. Attacking the accuser's timing did not move the town.

State every nomination and trial vote out loud when asked, even ones that look harmless. A jury-style role deduced my unstated Day 2 Yes from the vote pattern, and an unexplained mismatch became the town's case against me.

A nominee who says 'hang me' after a claim that cannot exist in this setup is a strong Jester tell. Don't let the 'wants the hang' signal get drowned by a pattern-based push. A Jester hang gives that player the win, so check whether they want it before voting Guilty.

Don't hang on one random Seer pair from a dead player. Frank's pair named me, but it was a single unverifiable check, and the town hanged me on it. Require a second independent check or a verified night result before a Guilty vote.

Kill the Seer and the highest-information Good role early. Killing Frank on Night 2 removed the pair that threatened me, and the Tracker kill on Night 3 removed the role that could see visits. Use the cause of each death to show the town that a killer is alive.

Spend a one-shot token on the first night it can change a vote, not on the night you feel safest. Frank held his last Seer token through Day 2 under town pressure and died on Night 2, so the held token did nothing for the town. Dead players' tokens are lost, and the death risk is highest for claimed info roles.

Check every claimed role against the faction sections in the rules. Diviner is listed under Yakuza, so a Good Diviner claim is false by construction. Heidi's claim was caught this way, and the same check works for Pharmacist, Ritualist, Puppeteer, Fabricator, Clerk, Smuggler, Ballot Stuffer, Fixer, Talent Agent and Informant.

A nominee who says 'hang me' after an impossible claim is a Jester signal, but the hang is only worth it if the Jester is the real threat. Mallory's hang gave the Jester a win while the Village still had to finish the Yakuza. Ask whether a hang removes a Yakuza or Serial Killer before spending it on a self-nominated suspect.

applies_to: Coroner, Vigilante, Trapper and other one-shot roles
tip: Start using one-shot roles on the Night when the information or the threat matters, not later. Carol held 3 Coroner tokens until Night 3 and was killed the next night. Olivia held 3 shots until Night 5, when the Yakuza had already taken most of the Village's confirmed info roles. Trappers who move a trap away from a dead holder lose a night of coverage.

Before submitting a Katana attack, check whether the target's death is the one that might trigger a revenge or Divine kill (Jester revenge killed Dave the holder). Kill the info role that can read your visits, but also keep the holder alive or the Katana moves to a player you have not coordinated with.

applies_to: Village investigators and anyone weighing a single investigative pair
tip: A lone Seer pair becomes credible once a second source confirms the Seer was real (here a Coroner exam of the dead Seer). Ask for that confirmation before hanging on a pair, and check the pair against later deaths: Erin's pair result led to the correct Serial Killer read.

A Jester who keeps pushing to be hanged is a real risk: a Guilty vote gives them the win. Before a trial, ask the nominee directly what role they hold and why they want the hang, and prefer a checkable mechanical reason over a 'hang me' bluff.

applies_to: Village roles that can see deaths (Coroner, Vigilante, Cardinal)
tip: Read every death's cause. Two Serial Killer kills with no Katana source meant a Neutral killer was alive well after the Yakuza's obvious targets, so the Village should track that killer's presence explicitly.

Private-message clusters between two living players are visible to everyone. Heidi and Judy's Day 4 and Day 5 PMs became the town's main lead, so Yakuza should coordinate in night chat and keep daytime PMs to a minimum.

Holding shots until Day 5 let a Yakuza Informant survive several Days, and it was the Vigilante's own claimed Yakuza-only suspicion that delayed the action. Fire at the first solid lead, since dying with unused shots is the usual failure.

applies_to: Yakuza, especially any Evil-only role (Diviner, Puppeteer, Fabricator and similar)
tip: Never publicly claim a role the rules list as Yakuza-only. Once a Good player is seen claiming an impossible role, the town treats it as proof. Pick a Village claim that fits your real visits, agree it in night chat on Night 1, and only claim under pressure if that claim holds up.

Do not exchange daytime private messages with a teammate. The moderator reveals that a PM was sent and who sent it to whom, so a cluster of PMs between two players becomes the town's lead. Keep all Yakuza coordination in the night chat and keep day talk to public chat.

A confirmed Seer, Coroner or other role does not confirm what that role's result said. Check the specific result itself (the pair, the group, the visit) against deaths and other results before a hang. Hanging on one pair from a confirmed-dead investigator is a thin case even when it happens to be right.

Read every cause of death. When two victims on consecutive nights share a cause with a Serial Killer, that proves a Neutral killer is alive, and a hang that is followed by no kill on the next night is evidence about who was removed. Use this to rank hang targets.

A group result names a role with only 60% odds for the player you chose. Use it as a consistency check against public claims rather than as proof. Yakuza Diviners should also avoid groups that include a teammate, since that draw can reflect a teammate's role and muddy your own checks.

applies_to: Profiler and other one-shot info roles
tip: Spend info tokens early on the player whose role decides a live vote, not on whoever is nominated last. A three-role profile only narrows the field, so pair it with a second source (a Juror, a Coroner or a Tracker result) before it decides a hang. Posting a profile publicly also made me the Katana target the next night, so either claim it with a plan to be protected or hold it until it matters.

Use the rules as a filter on claims. A claimed role that is Yakuza-only (Diviner, Wiretap, Informant) can't be held by a Good player, and a kill cause tells you whether a Serial Killer or Katana is still alive. Check every claim against the role list before you vote on the person.

A player who self-nominates, pushes a trial on a thin read, and then says 'hang me' may be a Jester. Ask for a real role before the vote, and keep Guilty votes to a bare majority when a Jester is possible, because the Jester's win and revenge both come from a hang. Do not let a nomination push carry the vote alone.

Ask every claimant for exact nights, targets and results early, and tie each claim to a checkable public event (a death, a trap report, a visit). Late asks for 'checkable nights' just repeated the same questions for several Days and did not change the vote.

A Jester hang ends the game for the rest of the Village only when the Jester wins outright. Before you hang a suspected Jester, check whether the Jester's win is the outcome you want, since it was not the same as a Yakuza hang here.

Do not trade daytime private messages with a teammate. Every PM sender and recipient is public, so a Day 4 and Day 5 PM cluster between Heidi and me was flagged by three players as the town's lead. Move all coordination to the night chat.

Never let a teammate publicly claim a role that is Yakuza-only in this rules set (such as Diviner). The Village can reject that claim outright, and it got Heidi hanged. Agree on a cover claim in night chat that the Village cannot disprove.

Use the Diviner or other group checks to find an unclaimed Vigilante or Killing role early, then kill it before it shoots the Katana holder. Olivia's group sat in our Diviner results for two nights, but we kept killing Village information roles instead, and her Basic shot killed me the night I held the Katana.

When a player pushes for their own hang ('hang me') with a thin or impossible claim, check whether they are a Jester before you vote Guilty. A Jester's win is locked in by the hang, and its revenge kills a random Guilty voter, which can be one of your own. Our Yakuza Puppeteer Dave died that way.

The Informant sees every trial vote, so track which living players vote with which known Good players, and use that to pick the Katana target. Share only what cannot be traced back to the Informant, and do not announce a vote-reading source in night chat, where the Yakuza can be wrong about who knows what.

Before accepting or making a role claim, check the setup's exclusion list (here Vanilla Villager and Grunt are never in the game). A claim of an impossible role is a near-certain lie or a sign of a Jester, and it cost me credibility on Day 2 that a plain 'I have no night action, name no role' would not have.

Check each claimed role against the rules' faction lists. Heidi's Diviner claim was a Yakuza-only role; the town flagged it on Day 5, which is a clean mechanical test that doesn't rely on who pushed hardest.

Pair the Katana with a Serial Killer or other attack on the same night to kill info roles (Seer, Tracker, Coroner). The Yakuza killed Frank, Niaj and Carol this way, which removed nearly all the town's investigative results before they could be cross-checked.

When a Jester is possible, keep the Guilty total to a bare majority and vote Innocent with power roles, since a hanged Jester's revenge kills a random Guilty voter. On Day 3 the 8-4 vote let the revenge kill Dave, a Village player, and it was avoidable.

A Jester wins fastest by self-nominating once the town is already split and has a pattern to point at. The pattern alone (a thin push plus a fake claim plus 'hang me') got eight Guilty votes, so a Jester should give a plausible real role rather than an impossible one.

applies_to: Tracker, Lookout, Seer and other info roles
tip: Post each night result publicly on the next Day, as soon as it comes in. My Night 3 result (Erin visited Niaj, the night of the Serial Killer attack on me) was never shared, and it died with me in my will. A held-back result is worth nothing if you die before the Day.

When a kill is made by a Serial Killer or Katana, check which player visited the victim that night. A tracked or watched visit to a victim is stronger evidence than any claim, so match visits against deaths before trusting anyone's pair or profile.

A player who pushes a trial on a thin read, claims an impossible role and then says 'hang me' may be a Jester who wants the hang. Ask the accused for a real role before voting Guilty, and remember that a hanged Jester wins immediately, so a mass Guilty vote on a suspected Jester gives them the game.

Check the role list for impossible claims. The Diviner is Yakuza-only in these rules, so a Diviner claim from a Good player is a lie or a Yakuza claim. Catch such claims early, because a Yakuza who defends one may be hiding in the open.
Before a hang, ask what the reveal settles. A Coroner examining a dead Seer proves the role but not what the Seer's pair saw, so do not treat a confirmed role as a confirmed result when voting.

Fire your first shot on the first credible Yakuza lead (a PM cluster with a claimant, a defended Yakuza-only claim, an unexplained visit), not after several Days of waiting. I held all three tokens through Nights 1-4 while the Katana killed Carol and Ivan, and only shot on Night 5, when Judy was the last Yakuza. An earlier shot might have removed the Katana holder before two more deaths.

Check which side a claimed role belongs to in the rules before trusting it. Heidi's Diviner claim was a Yakuza-only role, and the Village used that to hang her. Any Good player claiming a Yakuza-only or Neutral-only role is a strong lead.

Ask a suspected Jester directly whether they are one, and watch how they answer. Mallory's fake Vanilla claim, the push on Frank's trial and the 'hang me' line matched a Jester, and the hang was correct, though it gave the Jester a win. Before voting, check whether a Jester win is acceptable for your side, and keep Guilty votes to a bare majority when power roles are alive.

Make Day 2 productive. Almost every Village player posted the same 'no nomination until more results' line for two Days, which gave the Yakuza time and let one Jester drive the only trial. Agree early on a concrete checking order (who posts a result, who gets tested first) so the town is not stalled for a whole Day.
Repeating 'no nomination from me, still waiting' costs budget and adds no information. Spend budget on specific questions and checkable results, which are what actually moved the votes this game.

Never name your real role if it's Yakuza-only, even in passing (for example 'as Diviner I get no visit notices'). Choose a Village cover role on Night 1 that fits your real visits, and if you must say something about yourself, describe it in terms that cover role allows.
evidence: Heidi said 'I get no visit notices as Diviner' on Day 2. On Day 5 Ivan pointed out that Diviner is Yakuza-only, and she was nominated and hanged 5-2 within one round.

tip: Check every role claim against the rules as soon as it's made: is it a Yakuza-only role, or a role this setup never uses (Vanilla Villager)? Either one breaks the claim at once and should be called out that Day, not three Days later.
evidence: Ivan caught Mallory's Vanilla claim the morning after she made it, but nobody noticed Heidi's Diviner slip from Day 2 to Day 5. During that time two more Villagers died to the Katana (Niaj, Carol).

tip: If someone self-nominates after a role claim that can't exist, treat them as a likely Jester. Hanging them is fine (Jesters never block your win), but keep the Guilty count near a bare majority and keep your proven information roles on Innocent, because revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
evidence: Mallory nominated herself after an impossible Vanilla claim, and Ivan's profile listed Jester. The trial went 8 Guilty to 4 Innocent, and Ivan and Niaj both voted Guilty. The revenge hit Dave (Yakuza) only by luck.

tip: Combine results by elimination. A three-role profile becomes an alignment read once claims you trust rule out the Good option, and a Coroner exam that confirms a dead investigator's role makes that investigator's posted results trustworthy.
evidence: Erin's profile was Juror/SK/Wiretap and Bob had claimed Juror, so Erin was non-Good. Carol's exam showed Frank was a real Seer, which backed his Erin/Carol pair. Together they got the Serial Killer hanged 6-3. Judy's profile (Cardinal/Cartographer/Informant) next to Grace's Cardinal claim set up Olivia's later shot on Judy.

tip: Once a Neutral killer has shown up, or is likely, don't spend the Katana on the single most obvious investigator, because the killer will probably hit them too. Aim at the second-biggest threat, and use your Night 1 kill and one-shot tokens (puppet) instead of saving them.
evidence: The Katana and the Serial Killer both attacked Frank on Night 2 and Niaj on Night 3, so the Yakuza got no extra kills. They also skipped the Night 1 attack, and Dave died still holding his puppet token.

tip: Do all planning in night chat and send no Day private messages to teammates. Once a teammate is doomed, don't defend them or vote Innocent unless your votes can actually save them, because a Juror or the town's lists of stated votes will tie you to them.
evidence: Judy and Heidi messaged each other privately on Days 4 and 5, and Ivan, Olivia, Grace and Bob all asked what the messages were about. Judy publicly defended Heidi and voted Innocent in a 5-2 hang, and Olivia shot her that night because of it.

tip: Fire a Basic shot as soon as there's a reasonable lead, such as an impossible role claim or a defender of one. Don't wait for proof, because unused shots are lost if you die.
evidence: Olivia held all 3 tokens from Night 1 to Night 4 even though Heidi had been publicly claiming Diviner since Day 2. Her first shot, a Basic on Judy on Night 5, won the game. An earlier shot on Heidi might have saved Carol or Niaj.

tip: Don't announce that you'll use a token tonight or whom you plan to test. Do put tonight's planned target in your will, so the town can work out the result if you die.
evidence: On Day 2 Frank announced he would use his last token that night and test Mallory's 'pattern'. Both the Katana and the Serial Killer killed him that night. His will left out his Mallory/Alice check, so the town only learned the pair from Niaj's tracking, and never learned the result.

applies_to: Eavesdropper (and any role that reads a later Day)
tip: Pick an Eavesdropper target who will be alive and PMing the next Day. Both of my targets died that night (Carol, then Bob), so I got zero reads for two nights. Prefer a living, active player whose private chat matters, and check whether the target is likely to die before you spend the night on them.

When the only check on a claim is a dead player's result (here, a dead Fortune Teller's visit counts), treat the claim as unverified and ask for a living cross-check on Day 2. The town spent Days 2 to 4 arguing over one count that nobody could re-run.

A player who repeatedly self-nominates with no role or result is a Jester-pattern suspect, but a hanged Jester wins outright. Keep the nomination Yes-vote count below the threshold and vote Innocent until there is a mechanical reason. Two failed self-nominations cost the town nothing and kept the Jester alive, and no Village player was hanged on behavior.

Many of my Day 2 to 4 posts were 'no nomination from me yet' with no new information. They cost budget and changed nothing. Spend budget on one concrete question that a named player must answer, or on a vote with a stated reason.

Ivan's private messages to Heidi, Dave and Frank became the town's main lead, and Ivan was hanged on them. Coordinate in night chat instead of daytime PMs, and do not leave a visible PM cluster around a teammate.

applies_to: Medic, and any protector or visitor
tip: Visiting a player who may be on Veteran alert is lethal: an alert hits every visitor with a Strong Attack, which beats a Standard protection. Protecting a possible Veteran with Standard defense got me killed on Night 2. Before visiting an unknown player, ask whether they have alert tokens left. If they might, use Strong (1 token) on yourself or a claimed target, or skip the visit.

applies_to: Village investigators (Fortune Teller, Eavesdropper, Tracker, Lookout)
tip: Count-based results such as 2 visited and 3 visitors only settle identities when someone names each visitor. The town spent all of Day 2 arguing over one Night 1 count that was never resolved. Request one named, checkable detail per claim, and vote only on results that can be cross-checked against another source.

A player who self-nominates repeatedly and privately asks others for Guilty votes is either a Jester or a Yakuza pushing a hang. Before voting, ask whether a hanged Jester would win. Test the player with a direct question rather than hanging on behavior, and do not let the nominee's pleas set the timing. Refusing to nominate while the case stalls also lets the Yakuza run the clock.

Many of this game's messages were 'no nomination from me' filler that repeated the same request. Spend budget on one specific, checkable request per round and on a real defense at trial, and keep enough budget to speak during the trial itself.

The Katana holder dies if they visit a player who goes on alert with a Veteran, because the alert's Strong Attack hits every visitor. Before a Night 1 Katana attack on a random player, consider that the target might be a Veteran. Carol's Night 1 Katana visit to Erin got the holder killed, which ended Carol's plan immediately. Ask whether the target has alert-capable tokens, or whether the Katana holder can use a target that is less likely to be a Veteran.

Spend the puppet token on the first night you can, because dying on Night 1 wastes it. A puppet placed on Night 1 can set a false claim for Day 2, while a token you never use is worth nothing. Even if the puppet only lasts one Day, it can change the town's read at the start of the game.

A Veteran's kill claim is hard to verify, since the dead role is hidden. The best check is whether the claim matches every death across nights. Erin's account of one visitor, killed by alert each night, matched every death, and the town was right to treat it as the working line. Check each claim against the public death sequence and cause of death instead of asking for a second source.

Stop count arguments after one pass and move to a vote. Fortune Teller counts and visitor disputes took all of Day 2 without a nomination, and Alice's and Bob's Carol visits were never resolved. Set a rule, such as a nomination once each player has spoken once, and vote on the best supported read even if it is not fully proven.

A player who nominates themself repeatedly and asks to be voted Guilty is a Jester or a Yakuza pushing a wasted hang. Do not decide on the nominee's wording alone. Ask for a concrete check. If there is none, vote Innocent on the self-nomination and watch whether the same player keeps pushing votes in private, since that behavior was the clearest signal this game.

Repeated self-nominations plus PMs asking others for a Guilty vote read as a Jester tell and made the town wary, so they stalled rather than hanging me. Instead, make a reasoned, checkable case against a living suspect so the town votes you up on its own logic, and keep your push subtle.

When a key claim (Veteran, Fortune Teller) depends on a result that was promised but never posted in full, or on a now-dead player's counts, treat it as unverified for the vote and say so. Demand a specific, testable result early, on Day 2, rather than letting it sit until the claimant's Night 3 or 4 post.

When several players repeatedly ask for a checkable point and get only behaviour in reply, the group stalls. Name one concrete question per day and vote on the answer, so the Day doesn't run out of time with no execution.

Long, repeated public messages that restate the same point used budget without moving votes. Keep public posts short and spend the budget on nominations or trial defenses when a vote actually depends on them.

An alert with no visitors gives you no information, and the claim is only your word. If you are Veteran, post the visitor count and results publicly each night, because a bare 'no visitors' or 'killed X' is easy for the town to doubt.

When a Day gets stuck on a count-based claim that can't be resolved (for example, visitor counts from a dead Fortune Teller), stop waiting for it. Ask each claimant for a different, checkable result, and set a deadline for the nomination. This game lost about three Days to one unresolvable count puzzle.

Alert on every night the Katana or a known killer is active, and post the exact outcome at once: who visited, and whether the shot hit. A Veteran's alert kill is the only real proof of a Yakuza, and it is strongest when posted in the first speech. Keep the Armed shot for a confirmed lead, since it was never used here.

A self-nomination that asks for a Guilty vote, with no role and no night result, is a Jester tell, but a hanged Jester wins outright. Treat such a player as a suspect to test, not as a Yakuza to hang, and check whether anyone is pushing their trial.

Verify a late reveal before you vote on it. Ivan quoted a private message only when on trial, and the Village hanged him on that basis; hanging a suspect because of a delayed answer, rather than a checked fact, cost the Village its only Yakuza-tracking lead.
Keep public posts short and specific. Several players repeated the same unverified claim across many messages, which spent speaking budget and gave no new information.

Hand your tokens out early to a claimed role that is running out, such as a Veteran's alert token or a Medic's token, rather than hoarding them. I kept both tokens unused for three nights while the Veteran spent her last alert tokens, and an earlier handoff could have protected a key player.

Do not let a hang rest on a claim that only a dead player could have checked. Erin's Veteran account leaned on Grace's Night 1 counts, and once Grace died nobody could recheck it. Prefer claims that a living player can confirm, and note which claims are now uncheckable.

When a player repeatedly nominates themself and asks to be voted up, treat it as a possible Jester push and do not vote them up on behaviour alone. Hanging a Jester wins for them outright, so demand a mechanical reason first.

Stop repeating the same unverified argument in public every turn. Many messages this game restated the same unchecked claims and questions, which spends budget without moving votes. Post a new fact, a vote, or a specific question instead.

Private-message clusters are visible to everyone (who messaged whom), and they drew suspicion on Heidi, Ivan and Dave. If you need to coordinate, keep it brief and be ready to summarise the content publicly, because the town will ask.

applies_to: Fortune Teller and any information role
tip: Post every night's result publicly at the start of the next Day, not 'after tonight'. My Night 2 counts were never posted and died with me, while my will only held Night 1. Keep the newest result in the will too, since it is the only thing that survives your death.

Don't let the Day stall on 'wait for the next Night result'. Days 2 and 3 produced no nominations and gave the Yakuza two more free kills. Set a concrete rule: once a claim survives a check, nominate it, and say what result would change your vote.

Repeated self-nominations that ask for your own hanging are a Jester or Executioner tell. Check whether that player's target just died, since a target dying by other means turns an Executioner into a Jester. Don't hang them on behaviour alone, but don't defend them either.

Prioritise killing a Fortune Teller or other count-based role once its counts start fitting the claims. Its counts are what exposed the lies, and killing it removes the only check on the Veteran story for the rest of the game.

Keep a notepad of each claimant's exact statements. Alice's Day 2 'visited Carol' and Day 3 'eavesdropped Carol' described the same action, and the contradiction only surfaced later. Cross-check every claim against every earlier claim by the same player.

applies_to: Neutral killers with a win that needs several kills or hangs (Bounty Hunter, Executioner, Jester)
tip: Count your remaining paths to the win on Night 1. A Bounty Hunter with one token and three targets needs two claims, so one token plus hanging a target with your Guilty vote is the realistic route. Spend the token only when it claims a bounty you need, and plan which target you can get hanged before the Village starts voting.

applies_to: everyone, especially Village players checking visit counts
tip: Write out the visit arithmetic yourself before arguing it. An alert is not a visit (R6), the Katana holder's visit counts, and a self-visit counts once. Several players on Day 2 added a phantom visitor and argued a false contradiction for a full day. Post the set of visitors and visited players explicitly, with names, so others can check it in one read.

Reward claims that can be tested later, and be wary of ones that can only be re-checked through a dead player's information. Erin's whole line rested on Grace's Night 1 counts, and Grace was dead by the time it mattered. Ask every claimant for a result the Village can verify on the next night, and note who promised a result and never posted it.

A player who repeatedly self-nominates and asks for a Guilty vote can be a Jester or Executioner, but a hanged Jester wins outright. Before pushing a hang on a self-nominee, check whether the hang helps them. Repeated refusals to hang them can stall the Village for days, so decide early on a checkable test and set a deadline for it.

Private-message pushes are visible as a pattern (who messaged whom, how often), and the town fixated on them. If you're pushing a vote in PMs, expect to be asked about it publicly. Prepare a clean, quotable answer in advance, because late quotes read as evasion and got Ivan hanged.

Don't send the Katana at a player who could be an alert Veteran on Night 1. Carol's Standard attack on Erin let the Veteran's alert kill the holder, and the Yakuza lost their holder and a night of tempo. Before choosing a target, rule out Veteran or other alert-style defences, or pick a target whose claim you can see is weak.

Keep teammate coordination in the night chat. Daytime PMs between a Yakuza and a Village player (or between two Village players about one trial) were visible to everyone as a cluster, and the town used that cluster to nominate me. If you must talk during the Day, keep it to public messages or keep it short.

When two claims disagree about a visit count, ask for a result only one of the claimants could fake (a specific target, a specific night, a specific outcome) rather than re-deriving the count. The Village spent most of Day 2 on arithmetic over Grace's counts, and the claims that pinned a concrete result (Erin's alert kills) were the ones that held up.

Repeated self-nominations with no role or result are a Jester-style push, and a hanged Jester wins outright. Refusing to hang on behaviour alone worked well here, and a hanging should wait for a mechanical reason. Don't rely on a single claimant's word, though. Both sides were stuck on unverifiable claims for most of the game, so a request for a dated, checkable result should come early.

Many turns this game were filler like 'no nomination from me yet' repeated by most players. Each one costs budget and adds nothing to the vote. Spend the budget on a single concrete request or result, and keep the rest short.

Never protect or visit a player who has claimed Veteran and may still have alert tokens. They protect themselves, and an alert kills every visitor, friend or foe. Put your protection on another likely target instead.
evidence: Erin claimed Veteran on Day 2 and said she had 2 alert tokens left. On Night 2 Bob gave her Standard Defense, she alerted, and her Strong attack killed Bob. The Village lost its Medic for nothing.

tip: Once you have claimed Veteran, tell the Village each Day not to visit you while you have alerts left. You can say this without saying which night you will alert. It keeps your alerts from killing your own protectors and investigators.
evidence: On Night 3 Erin announced her last alert and nobody visited her. On Night 2 she gave no warning, and her own Medic, Bob, died on her alert.

tip: Before calling a visit-count contradiction, list the visitors and the visited separately and apply R6 exactly. A Veteran's alert, Astral actions and passive results are not visits, and one player visited several times counts once.
evidence: Ivan, Heidi, Dave and at first Grace counted Erin's alert as a visit. They insisted that Alice or Bob was lying about visiting Carol, and Day 2 passed with no nomination until Bob corrected the count.

tip: Use Katana kills on Village players who can vote you out. Neutrals that never block your win, such as a Bounty Hunter, Jester or Executioner, cost you nothing alive and can even vote with you. Killing them wastes a night.
evidence: On Night 3 Ivan killed Heidi, a Bounty Hunter who had voted Guilty alongside him on Dave. That left Alice, Erin and Frank, three Village votes, against him, and they hanged him 3-2 on Day 4. Killing Alice or Frank would have left Erin and one other Village voter against Ivan and Dave, a 2-2 split that is not a majority, so no hang could pass.

tip: Have a believable Village cover claim ready, and answer PM-content questions at once with a plausible summary. Refusing a role claim and stalling on 'what did your PMs say' leads to a nomination.
evidence: Over Days 3 and 4, Ivan was asked many times to quote Heidi's PM and delayed until Alice nominated him for it. At trial he gave 'no role claim'. That was the only case the Village needed.

tip: Refuse to hang a player who keeps asking to be hanged, especially through self-nominations and PM pushes. Treat whoever keeps backing that push as a suspect.
evidence: Dave (Jester) self-nominated four times. Alice, Erin and Frank voted No or Innocent every time, so Dave never won and no Jester revenge happened. The Village then turned on Ivan, who had backed Dave's hanging, and he was the last Yakuza.

tip: As a Jester, never ask outright to be hanged. Repeated self-nominations and 'vote me Guilty' PMs are the best-known Jester tell. Act quietly suspicious instead, for example with a shaky claim or an odd vote, so the Village hangs you on what looks like evidence.
evidence: Dave's self-nominations drew at most 4 Yes, then 2, 2 and 2, and his only trial failed 3-3. Every Village player publicly named the 'Jester pattern'.

tip: Keep daytime PMs to a minimum. Everyone sees who messages whom, and a visible PM chain with a pushy player becomes the town's lead against you.
evidence: The visible PMs between Heidi and Ivan, plus Dave's PMs to Ivan, became the main topic of Days 3 and 4. Alice and Erin used that link to justify nominating and hanging Ivan.

tip: Don't publicly announce your protection target. Once Carol's protection was public, the Yakuza's Pharmacist blocked me on consecutive nights and Carol died to the Katana. A block result tells you a blocker is alive, so switch to a less obvious target or hold the protection until you know who the blocker is.

Self-protection doesn't beat a role-block. Spending tokens on yourself only helps if no Pharmacist or Party Animal is alive to block you. Plan for blocks: keep a second likely target in mind and don't assume the claimed target is safe.

A player who nominates themselves and says 'test me' without a second check may be a Jester. A Jester hanged during a Day wins, so before voting Guilty on a self-nominee, ask whether hanging them is what they want.

Track pairs of players whose votes always match, including on nominations. Frank and Grace voted identically on every trial and nomination, and both posted Vanilla Villager claims with no results. A pair like that is a lead to test, not a reassurance.

If the nominee could be a Jester, remember that its revenge kills a random Guilty voter. When every living player votes Guilty, the revenge can hit a power role, so vote Innocent on weak evidence even if you think the nominee is Evil.

If the Sheriff reads you Evil, that is a Jester win path: nominate yourself while the Village still treats the Evil read as their only hard fact, and make them vote Guilty on you. Stay in the trial and don't spend tokens to prove a claim you can't win on.

A Yakuza Pharmacist who blocks the Medic every night can strip all protection while a Katana kills. Medics who see a 'role-blocked' result should self-protect at Strong and move to a less predictable ward, and Trackers should treat a visit-less target as a possible blocker before trusting that absence.

Don't resolve a claim conflict by shooting one claimant. Heidi and Dave both claimed Sniper; the Day shots killed one claimant, left the other alive, and removed the only Sniper-side checks. Vote or test the claim instead, because a Day shot can't be undone.

Repeating the same block-then-attack pattern (block the Medic, then Katana the Sheriff or Tracker) worked because each night's target was the one whose protection or results threatened the team. Keep it, but vary which Village role you block so the pattern doesn't become readable.

A hang with only 2 Guilty of 3 votes passed, and a 4-3 Innocent result on Day 2 let the Yakuza keep the Katana. When the Village is down to two or three players, decide early which claim will be tested, because each hanged claimant shrinks the Village's information.

Before hanging on an investigator's Evil read, check whether the target claimed a role that reads Evil by design (Jester, Executioner). Bob claimed Seer, and my Evil read on him (a Jester) was accurate, but the town hanged on it and the Jester won. Ask 'could this claimant be a Jester?' before a hang that depends on one Evil read.

A self-nomination after a claim is a Jester signal. Bob nominated himself twice while his claim was untested. Treat repeated self-nominations as a reason to test the claim another way, not as a reason to hang on the nominee's behalf.

Two players claiming the same role (both Sniper) is a conflict that a Day shot cannot resolve. The real Sniper shot the other claimant on Day 2, which removed a real Village power role and left the town with a contradicting will. Test conflicting claims with a vote or a result, not a shot.

A Pharmacist block on the Medic cancels protection, and the Yakuza used it twice on the same Medic. Protect the Sheriff through a second source, or self-protect early, rather than relying on one Medic's protection each night.

Public results posted at dawn are what let the town catch Yakuza. Carol's N1 and N2 results were posted and corroborated by Erin's track, but the team could not use them fast enough before the Katana killed both. Post results the same Day they are learned, and have a second investigator confirm them early.

A Day shot on a player whose role claim conflicts with yours is not a test. Two real Snipers can exist, and a Sniper's claim can only be checked by your own role knowledge. Shooting a claimant kills a real Village player when the other claim was true, so spend the token on a mechanical read (a Sheriff or Tracker result that conflicts with the target), not on a claim clash.

Track which claimant's protections or results get blocked each night. When a Medic is role-blocked on the same target that later dies to the Katana, the blocker is a living Yakuza candidate. Note which other players were on the same nominations and votes, since the Pharmacist and Katana holder voted together and pushed the same hangs.

Do not hang on a dead player's will. Heidi's will named me as Yakuza and was false, yet two players pushed a hang on it, and that bloc later decided a 1v1 endgame. When two players push the same nominee on an unverified will, ask each to name a mechanical reason before voting.

A player who self-nominates twice and refuses to spend their last token to prove a claim may be a Jester trying to get hanged, since a hanged Jester wins. Before hanging a self-nominator, check whether their hang helps them, and keep Guilty votes to a bare majority if a Jester win is possible.

Plan the Katana holder and the blocker in night chat, but don't let the town see a repeated pattern (the same Medic blocked every night, the same target hit). Spread the blocks and vary the targets so a Medic or Tracker cannot map the pattern.

applies_to: Tracker, Sheriff, Lookout, and any investigator
tip: Post a night result publicly the moment you learn it, and don't promise it 'at dawn'. I announced I would post my Night 2 track at dawn, which signalled that I was acting and that the result was pending. The Katana killed me that night, so the result never reached the town and the Yakuza had already read my claim. Update your will with each night's result too.

Don't protect the same claimed investigator every night. Repeating the same target made the Yakuza's blocking easy to plan, and a Pharmacist block on the Medic left the Katana unstopped two nights running. Vary the target, or spend a token on self-protection once you're a claimed Medic.

An Evil read on a player who self-nominates while claiming an unverifiable role is ambiguous. A Jester or Executioner reads Evil to the Sheriff, so a Jester hang wins the game for them. Before hanging on an Evil read, ask whether the target would benefit from being hanged, and whether anyone else could be the Jester.

Two players claiming the same role (here Sniper) is a conflict to test with mechanical evidence, not a reason to hang. A shot by one claimant on the other killed a Village player, and the will that accused the shooter was never checked against anything. Require a result or a visit that the claim explains before voting.

Planning the Katana kill and the block in night chat worked, but the Tracker's claim was public and its N2 target was predictable. Before killing a Tracker, check whether their visit could expose the Katana holder's visit. Avoid repeating the same plan pattern (Katana plus Pharmacist block on the Medic) on consecutive nights.

applies_to: Yakuza with a Pharmacist or other blocker
tip: Before blocking a Medic, confirm where their protection is going that night. On Night 2 our block on Alice was wasted because she protected Carol, not the Katana target Erin. Our plan assumed a protection that wasn't there. Ask the blocker to confirm the Medic's declared or likely target in night chat, or block only after the Medic's target is known.

Village claim conflicts (two Sniper claimants, a will naming a claimant as Yakuza) are cover. Push the town toward the contradicting claimant and let its own votes do the work. Nominating a Village claimant who has shot another claimant was persuasive, and the town hanged Dave on that basis.

Kill the investigators whose posted results would narrow the team, in order of threat. Erin (Tracker) died Night 2 and Carol (Sheriff, who had just posted Bob as EVIL) died Night 3. Both kills were the right priority and kept the town from building a clean case.

Do not let claimants settle a dispute with a shot or a will alone. Dave's Standard shot on Heidi removed one Sniper claimant, but the town was left with two unverifiable claims and a hang on a will. Require a mechanical result before any hang, and check that the Village can still win the parity count after each hang.

With 2-3 players alive, a Village hang of a Village claimant can hand the Yakuza a one-on-one win. Count the remaining Yakuza before voting, and hang only someone whose alignment is proven, not someone whose claim is only disputed.

applies_to: Yakuza with a Pharmacist or other blocker
tip: Before a Katana attack, block the most likely protector (the Medic) in the same night. Blocking Alice on Nights 2 and 3 let the Katana kill Erin and then Carol through a Standard protection that was otherwise active. Confirm the block target and Katana target in night chat before submitting.

A self-nominating claimant who pushes for a vote and then reads Evil on a claimed Village role may be the Jester. Hanging a Jester wins them the game and their revenge kills a random Guilty voter, which can remove a Village power role. Plan around that: Yakuza can let a Jester hang and then count on the revenge.

Kill the investigator whose already-posted result is least useful to you, but kill the Tracker or Sheriff whose next night result could still expose you. Erin (Tracker, who could confirm the Katana visit) and Carol (Sheriff, with a posted Evil read) were killed in order of threat.

Once the living count reaches two versus one Village player, a successful hang on that player ends the game for the Yakuza. Count the parity state before pushing a vote, because each hang or kill is decisive at that point.

Public Sniper claims that conflict (two Snipers) were handled by a shot that killed one claimant. Log every Day shot and its timing, because a shot that kills a player before round end cancels the other shot and its tokens return.

A Day shot resolves at the end of the round, so if you are shot during that round you die before your own queued shot fires and its tokens are lost. Firing back in retaliation does nothing. If you are about to be shot, your tokens are only useful if you can fire them on a turn that resolves before the enemy shot, or if you get out of the shot's way first.

applies_to: Sniper and any role with a one-shot kill
tip: Publicly counterclaiming a role that another player also claims invites a shot from the real holder. Two Sniper claims made Dave shoot me on Day 2. If the claim is contested, test it with a vote or a mechanical read rather than your ability.

A Jester reads Evil to the Sheriff. An Evil read on a self-nominating claimant who pushes for their own trial is a Jester signature, and hanging them can hand the Jester a win. Before hanging, check whether the claimant wants to be hanged and whether the hang gives a neutral player the win.

Count the endgame before each hang. With 3 alive, 2 Yes votes nominate and 2 Guilty votes hang. Hanging a Village player that leaves one Yakuza against one Village player lets the Katana holder win the next night, so the hang must be backed by a mechanical read.

Blocking the Medic's ward on the night you attack worked well here: the night-chat plan and the Pharmacist block stopped each protection. Keep submitting the agreed plan exactly, and confirm the block is on the Medic before the attack.

applies_to: everyone, especially Village holders of duplicate-able roles (Sniper, Vigilante, Medic)
tip: When someone claims your own role, remember that roles can repeat in hand-picked setups. Don't kill the counter-claimant on the spot. Ask for a Sheriff check or test them at a vote. Only shoot when another result breaks their claim.
evidence: Dave said himself that 'one of us is lying or there are two Snipers', then shot Heidi with a Standard shot on Day 2. Heidi was a real Village Sniper, so the town lost a shooter and gained nothing.

tip: Don't hold your last shot for proof that may never come. Once the player count is shrinking, spend it on your best unchecked suspect, such as whoever pushed a hang on a cleared player. Do this before the Yakuza can reach voting parity. Also, when you are shot, don't fire back at a player the Sheriff has cleared.
evidence: Dave held his last token 'for a clear Evil read' from Day 2 to Day 4. Frank and Grace had nominated him and voted Guilty on him despite Carol's Not Evil read. He was hanged by exactly those two with the token unused. Heidi's 3-token counter-shot went at that same cleared player.

tip: A claimant who reads Evil, nominates themselves and won't prove their claim is most likely a Jester. While the Katana is still killing, don't spend the day's hang on them. If you do hang, keep the Guilty votes to a bare majority and have the power roles vote Innocent, because the revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
evidence: Day 3: Bob had nominated himself twice and Carol's check read him Evil. Carol even said he might be a Jester. All 6 voted Guilty anyway, so the hang went to a Jester and the revenge killed Alice, the Medic. Day 4 opened with 3 players alive, two of them Yakuza.

tip: Once a player has a corroborated Not Evil result, look at whoever pushed to hang them and investigate those players next. Re-checking a player who is already cleared wastes a night.
evidence: Frank nominated Dave on Day 2, and Frank and Grace both said they were voting Guilty against Carol's corroborated Not Evil read. Carol checked Bob, then Dave again on Night 3, and never checked Frank or Grace. Both were Yakuza.

tip: Change who you protect, and use your tokens: a Strong protection or protecting yourself. A Medic who protects the same obvious claimant every night is easy for a role-blocker to predict, and it lets them kill your ward.
evidence: Alice protected Carol three nights in a row. Grace blocked Alice on Night 2 and Night 3, and Carol died on Night 3. Alice died that same night still holding 2 medic tokens.

tip: Before you kill a protected investigator, block the claimed Medic. Agree the holder, target and block in night chat and submit exactly that plan. Kill the info roles whose results can still narrow down your team, such as a Tracker who could see the Katana visit.
evidence: Frank and Grace agreed every plan word for word in night chat. Grace blocked Alice while Frank killed Erin (Tracker) on Night 2 and Carol (Sheriff) on Night 3. Both kills succeeded, and no Village investigator ever looked at them.

tip: Let a likely Jester or a chaotic claimant soak up the town's hangs, and back hangs on Village players when it costs you little. Quiet Vanilla claims with no visits leave nothing to contradict. Track the vote math so you know when you have the majority.
evidence: Frank and Grace claimed Vanilla Villager, voted with the town to hang the Jester, then used their 2-of-3 majority on Day 4 to hang Dave. They won without either of them ever being investigated.

tip: Count toward parity every Day. With 2 Yakuza among 6 players, one wasted hang plus a night kill can hand them the game. Before agreeing to a hang, ask whether it removes a Katana holder.
evidence: At 6 alive on Day 3, hanging the Jester, then the Katana kill on Carol and the revenge on Alice that night, left 3 players: Dave and both Yakuza. The game was decided before Day 4's vote.

applies_to: Village investigators (Cartographer, Sheriff, Seer, Tracker, Lookout)
tip: Publish your mechanical result the moment it exists, with night, target and exact output. Don't defer it to 'the start of Day N'. A deferred result lets a duplicate claimant copy your numbers unchallenged, and it gives the Yakuza a free night to remove you before the result is ever read.

applies_to: Village players facing a duplicate claim
tip: When someone copies a unique-sounding claim with identical numbers, don't both wait for the next night's test. Ask the copier for a concrete check that only the real holder could pass, and push for the nominee's mechanical contradiction instead of PM timing. Five PMs with a dead Yakuza was a lead, but the group sat on it for a full Day.

Don't let a Day pass with no nomination when a stall clock is running. Day 2 was spent saying 'wait for sizes' from every seat, and by Day 5 the Village had to choose between a weak hang and losing to R14. Set a concrete decision point (e.g., 'nominate on Day 3 if no mechanical result') and keep to it.

applies_to: Medic and anyone relying on Standard protection
tip: Standard Defense does not stop Strong attacks. Arsonist ignites and Serial Killers hit Strong, so a Medic who protects Standard on a likely Arsonist target has protected nothing. Use Strong protection on any player who may be doused or threatened by a Strong attacker, and keep one token for that.

Don't hang on wording or timing alone. Two nominations this game (Frank over three changed answers, Heidi over watch targets posted after the nomination) were based on inconsistency, not a mechanical contradiction. Each cost a Village player or a wasted Day. Require one checkable result or one clear contradiction before voting Guilty, and state that rule publicly so others can hold you to it.

Don't claim a role that another living or dead player has already claimed with identical mechanical outputs. Copying Alice's Cartographer sizes exactly made my claim testable and it was immediately counterclaimed. Pick a role whose results can't be cross-checked against a public claim, or make the claim only after the real holder is dead and their results can't be contested.

Keep daytime teammate contact out of private chats. Five Day 2 PMs with my Katana-holding teammate were public as a count and became the town's main lead for the whole game. Do all coordination in night chat, and never let a teammate's daytime messages line up with yours.

Before a Katana attack on a Village claimant, remember that an Avenger trait makes a lone attacker die with the target. Carol's fatal Standard attack on Alice killed Carol through Avenger, which left the Yakuza with one player. Prefer a test (a frame, a Basic attack, or a delay) on a claimant whose death would cost the attacker.

Spend one-shot tokens (such as the Fabricator frame) while the holder is still alive and the frame can change a vote or a read. I died on Day 3 with my token unused, so the planned frame never happened.

Standard protection does not stop an Arsonist's Strong ignite, and Arsonist kills are Strong. Against a suspected Arsonist or any Strong attacker, protect with Strong (2 tokens) or yourself-protection, not Standard. Grace's Standard protection on Ivan was beaten by a Strong ignite.

Hidden Village traits can kill the attacker. Carol's fatal Katana hit on Alice set off Alice's Avenger trait, so the Katana holder died the same night. Before a Katana kill on a Village player with no known traits, weigh the chance that the attacker dies too, and prefer a holder whose loss you can absorb. Remember the Katana passes to a living Yakuza, so keep a second Yakuza ready.

Keep all planning in night chat. The count of private messages between two teammates was public, and Bob and Carol's five Day 2 PMs became the Village's main lead and helped convict Bob's cover story. Day chat should only carry claims that match your night actions.

Standard protection does not stop a Strong attack. Ivan died to an Arsonist ignite despite Standard protection. When an Arsonist or Serial Killer may be alive, protect with Strong (one token) on the likeliest target, and never assume a Standard shield covers a Strong threat.

Changing your wording of a night result (Frank's three versions of Night 3) gives opponents a nomination hook even when the underlying fact is harmless. Give one plain answer once and stick to it, and state a role or trait early, before anyone else's timing questions start.

When the stall clock is running and no mechanical lead exists, a nominee whose public behavior contradicts the facts (Heidi's watch targets posted only after the nomination) can be the right hang, but it is still a guess. Confirm with a checkable event if one is available, and post each trial's stated votes against the announced totals before the next nomination.

Standard protection does not stop a Strong attack. Arsonist ignites and other Strong attackers kill a Standard-protected player. When an Arsonist or Strong killer is alive, protect with Strong (2 tokens for self, or Strong on a key target), and don't publish the same protection target every night.

Don't vote Guilty on wording changes, PM volume or a nomination's timing alone. Two of my Day votes rested on that kind of evidence.
