While you're alive, post your own checkable evidence (the full result details, what you know of other players' votes) before a day shot or nomination lands on you. Once the shot is fired, the town reads your will as a Yakuza's dying spin.

If the game doesn't end after a death, a Yakuza isn't necessarily still alive. Any Neutral that blocks wins (Vulture, Serial Killer, Arsonist) keeps the game going too. Before you hang someone because 'they're the only one left', count possible Yakuza deaths: a Vigilante kill on someone who also held the Katana may have wiped out the team. Also consider a quiet 'Vanilla' who might be a Neutral.

Two players claiming the same non-unique role (Auditor, Sheriff, etc.) is not a contradiction. If two Auditors both pick an obvious target like the nominator, matching results are expected, not copied. Don't shoot or hang over a bare duplicate claim or a late claim unless there's a mechanical break.

When an exact-role checker's WRONG result clashes with a claimant whom other evidence backs up (they were attacked, and a Notorious hit landed on the right player), suspect that the checker is a Roleplayer before calling them Yakuza. Roleplayer results are fake but plausible, and Vanilla guesses often come back 'correct'.

Audit the players whose votes broke from the crowd, such as a No on a nomination that passed or a hidden Innocent. Don't audit the obvious nominator: another Auditor will probably pick them too, and the overlap makes you both look like copycats.

When a Vulture is possible, keep the endgame head count in mind: it wins at max(floor(N/4),2) players alive. A 'Vanilla' who keeps asking where protections or traps are and pushes leads without results may be a Neutral. Hanging them is still correct, because they block the Village win.

If the game doesn't end after a death, a Yakuza isn't necessarily still alive. A win-blocking Neutral (Vulture, Serial Killer, Arsonist) also keeps the game going. Before you kill the next 'last Yakuza', count which deaths could already account for every Yakuza. A Vigilante or Trapper kill on a known attacker usually does.

Don't spend a kill shot on a duplicate claim of a role that can repeat (e.g. two Auditors) just because one claim was late and its results can't be checked. Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique. Wait for something mechanical, or let the town hang someone by vote, which costs no Village shot.

In a 13-player game, the Vulture wins once 3 or fewer players are alive at the start of a Day. A Vanilla claimant who keeps pushing hangs and nominations late in the game, and isn't Yakuza by the mechanics, may be a Vulture. Hang them before the count drops, not after.

An exact-role checker whose result contradicts a claim confirmed by mechanics (a Seer whose pair matched a Notorious claim, a Katana survivor) may be a Roleplayer, not a liar. A Roleplayer's 'CORRECT' Vanilla guesses are easy lucky hits. Weigh this before you hang them, but be aware their results are noise either way.

Seer pair plus Katana holder: if a Yakuza held the Katana that night, they read Good. So 'Yakuza holder vs X = DIFFERENT' means X is not Good. Teams rarely move the Katana early, so this inference was right here.

If you're the last Yakuza and a claimed Vigilante (or any killer with tokens) is alive and suspects you, swap yourself with a harmless villager that night. Their shot lands on the villager, and your Katana attack on a third player isn't moved. Worrying that 'swapped players are told, so people learn a Smuggler exists' doesn't matter when your death ends the game. Swaps still unused when you die are wasted.

Once you're the last Yakuza, or close to it, vote with the town majority on every nomination, even when a mis-hang of a villager is coming. Auditors can expose a No vote, and a No for a player whose results vouched for you makes you the next target. Voting with the town costs nothing.

When a villager's result accidentally vouches for you (e.g. a Roleplayer 'Oracle' guessing you correctly) and that villager comes under fire, don't defend them or lean on the vouch. Distance yourself early. If they hang as a 'liar', anyone they cleared is the next suspect.

An investigator who gives hints on Day 2 ('nothing actionable yet') is the player a Trapper or Medic most likely protected on Night 1. Hit an unhinted target instead, or have the Smuggler swap the hinted target with a decoy so a trap doesn't hit your holder.

An exact-role 'CORRECT' about a living player who denies the role, or a 'WRONG' about a proven role, often marks a Roleplayer, not a liar. Before hanging someone over a clash in exact-role claims, ask which of the two could be a Roleplayer.

An exact-role checker whose result contradicts a role that has independent mechanical support (e.g. a Seer whose pair matches a Notorious claim, or who survived a Katana attack) may be a Roleplayer, not Yakuza. Roleplayer results can also be fake 'CORRECT' results, so a claimed match counts for nothing. Anyone who publicly confirms a fake 'CORRECT' read on themselves is suspect: here a Yakuza Smuggler confirmed an Oracle's 'Vanilla' read on himself.

A second claim of a non-unique role (Auditor, Vanilla, etc.) is not evidence of a lie, even if it comes late and its results copy public information. Before acting, look for a result that would break the claim: a Seer pair, the claimant's will, a token count.

With the Seer, take a DIFFERENT pair that includes the likely Katana holder as pointing at the other player: the holder reads Good, so the partner reads Evil. Judy/Niaj DIFFERENT on N1 correctly caught Niaj. Say in public which reading you assume, and why the holder probably didn't move.

If the game doesn't end after the last suspected Yakuza dies (a Vigilante kill, a hang), count the possible Neutrals that block wins (a Vulture, Serial Killer, Arsonist). Late Vanilla claimers who push hard for hangs are prime suspects. Here the Vulture claimed Vanilla.
On Days 1-2, use exactly the same filler words as everyone else. Saying 'nothing actionable' when everyone else said 'nothing mechanical' got me flagged as an investigator and drew the Katana on N2.

applies_to: Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle, Accountant (any role a Roleplayer can be told it is)
tip: If your result contradicts a claim that game mechanics already back up (for example the claimant survived a Katana attack that a trap death confirms), first suspect that you are the Roleplayer. Post the result with that caveat. Don't build an accusation on it or bet your life on it.

When a player confirms another player's result about them ('yes, I'm Vanilla, his guess was right'), that proves nothing. Yakuza will happily confirm a wrong Vanilla guess because it vouches for them. Count a result as verified only if someone other than its target can check it.

Don't guess Vanilla Villager on unclaimed players. It tells you little and it's easy to fake. Spend guesses testing exact claims that decide a vote, and before going public, run a second test on a claim the town already trusts. That shows whether your own results are real.

A trait claim like Notorious, made right after an Evil read comes out, isn't a lie just because of the timing. Ask whether a fake result would happen to land on that exact player. If a pair matches the claim, that's strong evidence the checker is real.

Once a Village claim gets damaged, putting a teammate on its side (Dave confirming my Oracle result) ties the two together. When the town turned on me, the Vigilante shot Dave for backing me. Stay neutral on disputes between town claims.

Counts are cumulative, so treat them as equations. Subtract attacks you can prove (a trap death proves its victim attacked that night, a Katana kill proves the holder attacked) and write out every possible split. Spend tokens on the one player who stays ambiguous after that, and put all the readings in your will so the town can finish the deduction after you die.

Don't say 'I have a private result that agrees' without posting it. It marks you as an info role for the Katana, and it gives the accused an easy line ('nobody has seen it'). Either post the full result once it decides a vote, or stay completely silent.

When two info claims clash and one claimant is mechanically Good (for example, the Katana attacked them), consider that the other may be a Roleplayer before hanging them. A Roleplayer's fake results can still come back 'CORRECT', especially on Vanilla guesses. Hanging the Roleplayer costs a Village life. Discount their results instead.

A late duplicate claim of a non-unique role (for example, a second Auditor) is weak evidence on its own. Before shooting, look for a mechanical break, like a result that contradicts known facts. If there isn't one, prefer the player with no checkable claim at all.

At low player counts, a quiet 'Vanilla, never attacked' claimer may be a Vulture: it wins alone once at most max(floor(N/4),2) players are alive (3 in a 13-player game). Hang such a claimer before the count gets that low, even if the Yakuza case against them is shaky.

applies_to: Notorious players (any Village role with the trait)
tip: When an alignment check reads you Evil, claim your role, the trait and your exact token count straight away, and point out how unlikely it is that a fake result would land on the one Notorious player. Townspeople found this convincing, because a real Yakuza would have taken the easier way out and called the result fake.

Once you have claimed, expect the Katana that same night. Fire on that night, not later. A 1-token Basic shot is enough to kill a Yakuza who has no protection, so save your Standard and Strong tokens for Neutrals with Defense.

Don't trust an exact-role "CORRECT" result about a player who already claimed publicly, and remember the investigator may be a Roleplayer. The person such a result 'clears' is still a suspect, especially if they voted No to protect that investigator. In this game the 'confirmed Vanilla' was the Smuggler.

If a claimed investigator contradicts a result that has been confirmed, consider the Roleplayer explanation before hanging them. Throw out all of their results, which may have falsely cleared Yakuza, and look at whoever their 'clears' protected. Don't spend a hang on them. (Frank was a Roleplayer and was mis-hanged.)

Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claim of a non-unique role made late (like a second Auditor) is not evidence by itself. Don't fire a day shot at someone just for a duplicate claim or for repeating a result that was posted publicly.

On Day 1, say one short, bland message and stop. Don't sound like a sharp vote-tracker or analyst. The Yakuza pick their N1 Katana target from whoever sounds most dangerous, and a Jester killed at night can never win.

Your Basic Defense doesn't stop the Standard Katana. Don't count on surviving night kills. Start looking mildly suspicious early, for example with a vague role answer or an odd vote, so the town aims its suspicion at you and the Yakuza see no reason to spend their kill on you.

Spend your one-shot tokens (swap, rig, puppet) while they can still change the outcome. A rig on the Day a teammate is about to hang, or a swap on a known trap or protection target, is worth more than saving it. Teams that hoard tokens 'for a better moment' often lose every holder with nothing used.

After a Katana attack fails and someone dies to a Trapper the same night, the dead player held the Katana. With the rule that the holder reads Good, a Seer pair from an earlier night involving that holder becomes strong evidence against the other player in the pair.
A lone No on a popular nomination stands out, because Auditors and vote claims expose it. If you can't stop a nomination, vote the way the room votes on both the nomination and the trial.

Before a Katana attack on a likely investigator, assume a Trapper, Veteran or Medic may be on them. The trap's Strong counterattack kills the holder and leaves a 'killed by Trapper' cause that exposes them. Either hit a quieter target, or use a Smuggler swap so the attack lands on a decoy.

Write your will for the ways the holder can die at night: by Trapper, Veteran or Enforcer. A plain 'Vanilla, no action' will plus a Trapper death is a proven lie, and it hands town your teammates through Seer pairs. A will claiming the Armed trait or a Vigilante shot on the Katana target at least leaves room for doubt.

Use one-shot team tokens in the first two nights or Days. Our team lost with all of them unused: 2 swaps, 1 puppet and 1 rig. A Day 3 rig would have executed whoever town nominated (a villager, if the push went that way). A puppet could have posted a fake result to break the Seer's case.

The holder reads Good, so every random Seer pair that includes a non-holder teammate reads as a mismatch against the holder. If the holder is later exposed, that pair convicts the teammate. Rotate the Katana, or plan a counter-story for a teammate who has a 'DIFFERENT' pair with the holder.

Votes get audited. Dave's 'No' on Frank's nomination, followed by a Guilty vote, plus his defense of Frank, drew the Vigilante's shot. Once a teammate is exposed or doomed, vote with the majority on every ballot, not just the trial vote.

If the game goes on after you believe every Yakuza is dead, the blocker may be a Neutral (e.g. a Vulture claiming Vanilla), not a hidden Yakuza. Count the confirmed Yakuza deaths first. A Vulture wins at a low headcount (max(floor(N/4),2)), so hang the last unexplained claimant before the count falls that far.

If an investigator's result contradicts a player the facts already back up (attacked by the Katana, backed by a Notorious claim), the investigator may be a Roleplayer rather than Yakuza. Treat their results as noise, and hang them only when no better lead exists, because they are still Village.

On Night 1, put your trap on the player who sounded like an investigator on Day 1 and leave it there. A trap stays armed for nights and turns the Katana holder's attack into a kill. Then claim in one line once the trap death makes the claim check out.

applies_to: Village with day or night kills (Sniper, Vigilante)
tip: Don't fire on a late duplicate claim of a non-unique role (Auditor, Medic) on its own. Duplicates are legal, and a copied-looking result may simply be the same audit. Fire on a voting slip or a mechanical contradiction instead, like a switch from No on the nomination to Guilty in the trial plus vouching for a doubtful investigator.

Before you attack a player who hinted at an info role (or opened the game sounding like one), assume a Trapper or Medic may be on them already. A trap set on Night 1 is armed from Night 2. Either send the Katana through a non-critical holder, or use a Smuggler swap so the attack lands on someone else while the protection stays put. An attack into a trap costs you the holder, plus a free 'killed by Trapper' clue that exposes them.

A random Seer pair or Census check that lands on two Yakuza reads DIFFERENT when one of them holds the Katana. Once the holder dies, anyone paired with them is badly exposed. Moving the Katana now and then, and keeping your claims apart from the holder's, limits how much one dead holder can reveal about the rest of you.

Don't have all your members claim Vanilla Villager. One Vanilla among you is fine. The others should claim roles they can't be caught on, such as a duplicate-allowed passive investigator with plausible empty results, or a token role that matches your real token count. Three Vanillas, one of them a dead liar, made every later Vanilla claim look suspicious.

A one-shot token held 'for the perfect moment' usually dies with its holder. Our team finished the game with an unused rig, an unused puppet and 2 unused swaps. Pick the first realistic use and commit. For example, rig a Day when town is already leaning on a villager, or swap the night you attack the strongest info role.

Once you are trying to blend in, don't cast a visibly off-consensus vote to protect a fake-claimant or a lead that helps you. Dave's lone 'No' on Frank's nomination showed up in an Auditor result and got him shot by a Vigilante that night. Vote with the majority and only argue with words.

The Vulture blocks the Village win. Once the Yakuza are gone, the game keeps going and the town hunts the last outsider, which is you. Keep Yakuza alive as long as you can: they kill at night and soak up suspicion. Vote Innocent on likely Yakuza when your vote won't stand out, and push the town toward mis-hanging villagers instead.

Track your dead-role reports. A Yakuza-only role in a report, like Clerk, Smuggler or Puppeteer, is true about half the time, but it is strong evidence. Together with the causes of death, it tells you how many Yakuza are probably left. When the reports point to the last Yakuza being dead, expect to be the next target, and switch to a defense that doesn't rely on the Yakuza killing tonight.

applies_to: Neutral or Yakuza with a fake claim
tip: Never ask publicly where a protector or trap is. Only a killer needs that, and the town will quote it straight back as the case against you.

A Vanilla claim is weak once a cumulative investigation, like the Bloodhound's attack counts, leaves you as one of the possible readings. Late in the game Vanilla claimants get pressed hard. Choose a cover that has plausible, uncheckable results from early on, or one that matches a role you know is already dead.

Don't nominate people yourself. Being the nominator of a mis-hang, as I was with Frank, gets written into wills and becomes a lead against you. Let villagers drive the hangs you want and just vote with the majority.
On Night 1, put your trap or protection on whoever sounds most like an investigator, because that is where the Yakuza aim next. A trap is armed from Night 2, so set it early.
evidence: Mallory trapped Erin on Night 1. On Night 2 the Yakuza attacked Erin because of her 'nothing actionable' wording, and the trap killed Judy, the Katana holder. Judy's trap death, together with her fake Vanilla will, was the foundation of every later conviction.

tip: Before attacking someone you only guess is an investigator, think about traps and protection. Let the least valuable or most exposed member hold the Katana for risky attacks, or have the Smuggler cover the attack. Use one-shot tokens (puppet, rig, swaps) while they can still change a Day. Tokens held 'for later' usually die with their owner.
evidence: Judy attacked Erin on a wording hint and died to the trap with her puppet token unused. Niaj was hanged with his rig unused, and Dave died with both swap tokens unused. The Yakuza never used a single special token all game.

tip: Don't stand out from the town's vote, even on a nomination, and especially not to protect someone whose result 'confirmed' you. Auditors and Vigilantes treat a lone No as a lead.
evidence: Dave stayed hidden through Day 3 by voting Yes and Guilty on his teammate Niaj. On Day 4 he voted No on Frank's nomination, the only No besides Frank's own. Bob audited it, and Heidi named that No in her will as a reason she shot Dave on Night 4.

tip: If an exact-role claim with no checkable results contradicts an investigator whose results fit together, think Roleplayer before you call it a lie. Often the right move is to ignore those results rather than spend a hang on a Village player.
evidence: Frank (a Roleplayer who thought he was the Oracle) posted a fake 'Erin = Seer WRONG'. Dave even raised the Roleplayer possibility, but the town hanged Frank 8-1 anyway, a Village mis-hang on Day 4.

tip: When the game doesn't end, work out who could be blocking the win. If a Vigilante shot a suspect the same night the Katana fired, the Yakuza may all be dead, and the blocker may be a Neutral claiming Vanilla. Don't spend a shot on a bare claim clash before you check this.
evidence: On Night 4 Heidi shot Dave and Dave's Katana killed Heidi, so the Katana holder could have been Dave. On Day 5 Bob said 'at least one Yakuza is still alive', and Carol shot Alice, a real Auditor, because Bob also claimed Auditor. The only non-Village player left was Olivia, the Vulture.

tip: Several players can have the same role, and two Auditors who check the same player get the same result. A matching result supports the second claim; it doesn't prove a copy. Judge a duplicate claimant by alignment evidence and how well their story fits.
evidence: Alice claimed Auditor late, and her Carol audit matched Bob's. Erin's Night 4 pair read Alice Not Evil. Carol shot her anyway, and Alice was an honest Village Auditor.

tip: Write the trait in your will early. When an alignment check reads you Evil, claim the trait right away and explain why the result is true. It backs up the real investigator and exposes anyone whose claim conflicts with theirs.
evidence: Heidi's Notorious claim turned Erin's Heidi/Grace DIFFERENT result into proof that Erin was the real Seer. Her Katana death on Night 4 confirmed she was Village.

tip: Hinting 'I have a private result' marks you for the Katana without helping the town. Post the result in full once it bears on a vote, and keep the reasoning in your will.
evidence: On Day 3 Grace said she had a private result but didn't post it. The Yakuza killed her on Night 3. Her detailed will (Readings A/B/C) then drove the Day 5 case against Olivia.

tip: Each Profiler list includes one role that another living player has. If the same Evil role shows up in two lists on different targets, assume it is in play. Hunt for it right away by checking the players who pushed hardest. Don't use the overlap to cast doubt on the Profiler.

Spend your guesses on suspects, not on clearing a player who already looks Good. After one wrong guess on someone, move on. Pair the role most likely to be in play (for example, an Evil role that keeps showing up as filler) with the strongest pushers who have role claims nobody can check.

Two players claiming the same non-unique role (for example, two Auditors) can both be telling the truth. Before anyone hangs or shoots, check both of them (profile, audit, guess). Calling a quick counterclaim 'proof of a pair' can get two real villagers killed.

Don't hang a claimed investigator just because the story 'fits' if their results are consistent with each other and can still be tested (Accountant, Coroner, a profile still pending). Wait for a mechanical break, and vote Innocent if you have to. Claims that only repeat publicly stated votes (Juror, Scrutineer) cost a Yakuza nothing to fake. Treat them as unverified.

Once few players are left, check every passive claim against public visits from wills. A Scout or Fortune Teller result can be broken by a dead player's posted audit target. Post these checks early, not only at the final trial.

If someone claims your non-unique role, assume first that there are two of you. Say 'I'm also X, could be two' and offer checkable results, such as the exact audit that night. Don't vote to hang them. A blind counterclaim plus a Guilty vote makes you the town's top suspect, and it can get you killed by a Good killer.

Reading a Profiler list: one filler always comes from another living player's role. When a Yakuza role turns up in two separate lists, that role is very likely in play. Hunt whoever is holding it instead of hanging the Profiler for 'posting lists after claims'. Asking the target to claim first is how a Profiler is supposed to play.

Check each claimed passive result (Scout groups, Fortune Teller counts) against the visits other players have stated publicly, every night. One broken claim, such as two Scout names that a known audit puts in the same visit group, is mechanical proof. Use it before the Yakuza reach half the votes, not in the final 3.

Keep your will to facts: role, targets, exact results and votes. A speculative accusation in a will, such as naming the confirmed Katana target and her protector as Yakuza, misleads the town after you die. It also makes your other claims look fake.

Don't keep re-testing the claimant you already cleared. Guess the recurring Yakuza role, such as a Ballot Stuffer that shows up in several Profiler lists, on the players who pushed with the losing side, and do it early.

Don't leave your trap on the most obvious target, such as a confirmed Katana survivor, for several nights. The Yakuza can reason about where a trap probably is: they skip that player and kill the Trapper instead. Move the trap now and then to a less obvious likely target, such as a claimed investigator who hasn't been attacked yet.

applies_to: Cursed (any Village player with a death-triggered penalty)
tip: If your death also kills a random Good player, avoid drawing the Katana. Don't soft-claim a protective or power role when nobody needs it. Each night kill on you costs the Village two players. Stay as unclaimed and low-profile as you can until the endgame.

In a Profiler list, one role is always 'in play' and one is 'not in play'. If two players both claim the Good role in the list (roles can repeat), the Evil role beside it is probably the in-play filler, so a Yakuza with that role is alive. A role that shows up in two different lists (Ballot Stuffer here) is almost certainly in play. Read such a list as a lead on that Yakuza role, not as proof that the Profiler is fake.

Every Day, check each passive claimed result (Scout names, Fortune Teller counts) against the visits that are public. A Scout who names two players from the same visit group, or a Fortune Teller whose counts can't be reached, has a broken claim. Do this check early. A fake that isn't caught until 3 players are left can't be hanged anymore.

Be careful about building 'they're a pair' stories (fake Profiler plus planted counterclaimer) when there's no data. In this game I made that kind of argument on D2, and it later helped get a real Profiler hanged. Before you argue someone is a fake, ask what their result would look like if they were honest.

If a role shows up in profiles of two different targets, it is almost certainly the 'in play' filler, so someone alive has it. Hunt that role (here, Ballot Stuffer) rather than treating the target as the suspect.

If someone claims a role before a Profiler, Surveyor or Diviner posts a result on them, and the claim matches one of the listed roles, it is probably true. A fake claim lands in the list only if it happens to hit the single 'in play' filler. Treat it as confirmation, not as a case to hang them.

Don't nominate on a list of several possible roles, and don't call the people who push back 'teammates'. A failed push followed by an attack on a confirmed-Good player brands you as fake. Post the result, call it a test, and save the nomination for a mechanical break.

Never fire a one-shot kill at one side of a duplicate-role claim. Roles repeat (only Smuggler and Vulture are unique), so two real Auditors is plausible, and killing a real one wastes the shot and muddies every later read.

Late in the game, test every passive claim (Scout, Fortune Teller, Juror, Scrutineer) against the visits that are now public in wills. Scout names must come from three different visit groups, and Fortune Teller counts must match the claimed visitors. Do this before the Yakuza reach half the votes, not on the last Day.

Don't spend a one-shot kill on one side of a duplicate-claim clash. Roles repeat, and a Profiler's 'in play' filler can be a second copy of the true role. In this game there really were two Auditors. A better target is someone who held a stated Guilty vote after hard evidence turned the case. Here every Yakuza did that.

A Profiler list always holds one role that some living player really has. If the same Evil role, such as Ballot Stuffer, shows up as filler in lists on different targets, treat that role as almost certainly in play. Hunt whoever's claim is unverifiable. Don't drop the role because the lists are inconvenient.

If a Profiler's list contains a role that was later confirmed as its target's true role, the list is very likely real. Hanging that Profiler for 'tailored lists' throws away your best exact-role source. Verify before you hang an investigator whose output keeps checking out.

Keep guesses out of your last will, or label them clearly as weak. A dead player's will naming a 'next lead' carries outsized weight, and Yakuza will quote it to hang that person. Write facts and results, with confidence levels.

Every Day, check each passive 'results' claim (Scout groups, Fortune Teller counts) against the visits already made public: audits, Katana deaths, released attacks. Fake passive results usually break within a night or two, but someone has to do the arithmetic before the endgame.

When a Profiler posts two lists and the same non-Good role shows up in both (here Ballot Stuffer, next to Auditor/Informant and then Auditor/Mortician), that role is almost certainly the 'in play' filler, so someone alive really has it. Hunt that role instead of calling the Profiler fake. Two people claiming the same non-unique role (two Auditors) fits these lists perfectly.

In the endgame, count parity before every hang. At 5 alive with 2 Yakuza likely left, hanging a Neutral killer (even a real Arsonist) loses: the Katana kills that night and the 2 Yakuza control the vote at 3 alive. If a Neutral killer is also alive, it threatens the Yakuza too, so today's rope has to go on a Yakuza suspect.

Check every passive visit-pattern claim (Scout, Cartographer, Fortune Teller) against all the visits known for that night, on the day it is posted, not only when cornered. A Scout listing two players from the same visit group, or an FT count that needs a visitor nobody claims, is mechanical proof. Audit and Katana targets from wills give you free known edges.

Claims whose 'results' only repeat votes people already stated (Juror, Scrutineer) cost an Informant or any Yakuza nothing to fake. Treat them as unclaimed, and weigh D2 Guilty pushers who hold such claims as top suspects.

Once you publicly claim Veteran, the Yakuza simply stop visiting you, so later alerts almost never kill anyone. Either stay hidden and alert on nights you're likely targeted (after you've drawn attention, or when a visitor-checker might hit you), or claim only once your tokens are nearly gone, using the claim as a shield rather than a trap.

applies_to: Yakuza / anyone faking a visit-based passive role (Scout, Cartographer, Fortune Teller)
tip: Before you post a fake visit-group or visit-count result, check it against every public will and claim for that night. One audit or other known visit between two names you list as being in 'different groups' is a mechanical contradiction. For a fake Scout, it's safest to name players nobody has claimed to visit or be visited by.

Before you attack the obvious target (a confirmed or previously attacked investigator), ask where a Trapper or protector would most likely be guarding. Often it's better to kill the protector or Trapper first: they can't easily cover themselves, and their death opens up the real target the next night.

Don't kill the player whose will is about to say 'hang [your teammate]'. Some players argue frame, but the published will usually becomes the town's consensus lead. Kill someone neutral to your team, and let the accuser look paranoid while he's alive.

Use Count on threat roles (Veteran, Coroner, Accountant, Trapper) early. The exact number tells you which visits are risky and which covers or results can be checked. Count is more useful than Scan once you need to plan kills.

Keep at least one doubled-vote token for the endgame. At 3 or 4 alive, a doubled Guilty turns 2 Yakuza into a guaranteed trial majority, so the town's last mechanical case doesn't matter. Spend it the night before the Day when you expect to reach parity.

Don't kill the player whose public suspicion or will names your teammate. Ivan's death made 'hang Niaj' the last thing everyone read, and Niaj hanged the next Day. Kill someone neutral to your team, or the investigator whose next result could expose you.

applies_to: Yakuza with visit-based fake claims (Scout, Fortune Teller, Lookout)
tip: Before posting a fake visit-based result, check it against every visit made public that Day, including new wills. Grace's fake Scout result named Mallory and Heidi as separate groups, but Mallory's will showed she had audited Heidi. Frank caught it at once. When in doubt, post a result that can't clash with a public visit.

Work out where a known Trapper's trap probably sits: the confirmed earlier Katana target is the obvious spot. Attack the protector instead, since a Trapper can't trap themself. Carol's trap was really on Alice, so switching the kill to Carol saved our Katana holder.

Hold your tokens while an over-count would prove a Ballot Stuffer exists, especially if a result names your role. Spend one the night before the endgame Day so your doubled trial vote decides the final hang (at 3 alive, you plus a teammate make 3 of 4 counted votes). Remember the nomination vote is not doubled.

A Profiler's in-play filler means another living player really has that role. If two blind claims of the same role both turn out real, the not-Good filler (here Ballot Stuffer) is a live lead. Don't throw out the Profiler's lists just because they were posted after the claims.

Your target might be Yakuza, and if you push them early and alone, you become the Katana's obvious next kill. You only win if you are alive at the hang. Plant doubts about your target in other players' words, and don't be the only named accuser.

Don't nominate your target until you can count a likely majority. A failed nomination (mine got 4 Yes) gives you nothing, labels you the accuser and gives the target's team a reason to kill you. Wait for a result or claim from someone else that you can ride.

A Profiler's list always includes one role that is really in play. If the same Yakuza role shows up in two lists for different players (Ballot Stuffer here), that role is very likely held by someone alive. Two real Auditors is entirely possible. Don't hang the Profiler for listing a role that 'can't be checked'.

Passive claims that report numbers or groups (Fortune Teller, Scout) can be broken. Count the visits posted publicly and in wills. Scout names must come from different visit groups, so a known audit between two named players breaks the claim. Do this check every Day, not just in the endgame.

Kill the player whose will is about to point at your teammate only if the town will read that kill as a frame. Otherwise the will gets published and the teammate hangs (Niaj died the Day after Ivan's will said 'Hang Niaj').

Work through a Profiler list once the target's true role is pinned down. If you know which entry is true, then one of the other two is a role another living player really has. If the same non-Good role shows up in two different Profiler lists, or also in an Archivist list, treat it as almost certainly in play and look for whoever could be holding it. Don't write it off as a fake's 'untestable filler'.

Two people claiming the same non-unique role (two Auditors, say) can both be telling the truth. Before anyone hangs or shoots one of them, test both with an Oracle, Accountant or Profiler. Firing a killing role at the 'fake' counterclaimer on a coin flip can take out a real villager.

When an investigator asks the target to claim before posting a result, that is normal good practice, not a sign of a fake. Don't hang the only exact-role investigator over a 'pattern' or 'it fits' story. Ask for a mechanical test (Accountant token count, Oracle guess, Coroner) and keep them alive until it comes back.

Endgame parity: at 5 or 4 alive, count how many Yakuza could still be alive. If hanging a Neutral killer lets the Katana bring the Yakuza to half the votes that night, you lose anyway. In that case hang your best Yakuza suspect, even if the Neutral killer case is stronger.

Check passive visit-group claims (Scout, Fortune Teller, Cartographer) against every visit that's public, every night, as soon as they're posted. An audit or profile that links two named players breaks a Scout claim that puts them in different groups. Catching this on Day 4 or 5 instead of Day 6 decides the game.

applies_to: everyone (especially a player whose true role shows up in a Profiler/Diviner result)
tip: If an investigator's result names your true role, treat that investigator as very likely real. A fake can't reliably list your role. Defend them; don't help hang them. A blind counterclaim of your role is often a second real copy of it, since only Smuggler and Vulture are unique. Ask for a profile of the counterclaimer and treat 'two real copies' as a live case. Don't call them fake.

In Profiler lists, one filler is drawn from roles really held by other living players. If the same non-Good role turns up as filler in two different lists, it is very likely in play. Once Oracle guesses rule it out for the profiled players, hunt it among the others, starting with players whose claims (Juror, Scrutineer, passive roles) can't be checked.

If everyone states their votes truthfully, auditing stated trial votes tells you nothing. Audit votes that were never stated: secret Yes/No votes on failed nominations, or players who gave vague or changed vote statements. Also check vote-based claims (Juror, Scrutineer counts) against your audits so a fake result breaks.

Test every passive info claim (Scout, Fortune Teller, Cartographer) against all known visits each night as soon as it is posted. A Scout who names two players linked by a known visit (an audit, a Katana kill) is lying. Do this check yourself on the day of the claim, before the endgame, while you still have votes to act on it.

Don't hang a claimed exact-role investigator on 'the pattern fits a fake' when their results are internally consistent and a mechanical test (Accountant, Coroner, next profile) is coming. Losing a real investigator and a day was the swing that cost this game. Hang the vote-only claimers first.

Don't Katana the one player whose will names your teammate. The will becomes the first thing everyone reads that morning, and 'they were silenced' beats 'it's a frame'. Ivan's kill got Niaj hanged the next Day. Kill an investigator or a quiet player instead, and let a lone accuser's case fade.

Avoid fake vote-based results (Scrutineer, Juror) that only restate public votes. Town calls them free Informant cover. Pick a cover that can produce new, checkable-looking information, or a passive role with nothing to report.

applies_to: Yakuza (fake Scout, Fortune Teller or Cartographer claims)
tip: Before posting a fake visit-structure result, check it against every visit made public in claims and wills, especially the newest will. Grace's N5 Scout names put Mallory and Heidi in separate groups, but Mallory's will said she audited Heidi. Frank caught it at once.

An accused player's best trial defense is a concrete arithmetic break in another claim, like Fortune Teller numbers against public visits. It may not save you, but it seeds the next hanging. Niaj's attack on Olivia's numbers led to the Arsonist being hanged the next Day.

Diviner-ing your own Katana holder gives them Strong Defense, which survives a Veteran alert or a Trapper hit. Use it on nights when the target is unclaimed and a Veteran or Trapper is known to be in play. It costs only one night of information.

applies_to: Neutral killers and Yakuza faking a passive information role
tip: Don't fake a numeric passive role like Fortune Teller, Cartographer or Scout unless you rebuild every night's numbers from all public claims. Once claims and wills come out, others can count the visitors (my N1 '4 visiting' was below the 5 claimed visitors, and my N4 count was beaten the same way). Pick a cover with no result others can test, such as an Astral role that hasn't acted yet, or post ranges instead of exact counts.

Don't douse players who have already survived an attack or who are obvious protection targets (the N1 Katana survivor, claimed investigators). A trap or charm is probably on them and will stop your ignite. Douse quiet players nobody is guarding instead.

Watch who the Yakuza are likely to kill next (players hunting a suspect, players who just claimed). A douse on someone the Katana kills first is wasted. If a doused player is under Yakuza pressure, ignite that night rather than waiting for a third douse.

With 5 or fewer alive and the Yakuza still strong, the remaining villagers are your only votes. Build the case against the Yakuza early, ideally a mechanical break in their claims, before you're nominated. Defending yourself in round 1 of your own trial rarely turns enough votes.

A Profiler list that includes the Auditor someone claimed blind, alongside a second blind Auditor claim, can simply mean there are two real Auditors. Duplicate roles happen. Before hanging the investigator, test the cheap explanation (two Auditors, so the in-play filler is real and a Yakuza role is alive).

When a Profiler (or any list-style check) is run on two different players and the same non-Good role turns up as filler both times, treat it as strong evidence that the role is really in play. Then question everyone whose claim could be hiding that role. Don't assume the investigator built the lists around claims they had already seen: the moderator generates the results, and asking the target to claim first is correct practice.
evidence: Ballot Stuffer appeared in both of Dave's lists (on Mallory and on Bob). The town hanged Dave 10-1 for 'posting after claims' and never looked closely at Heidi, the actual Ballot Stuffer, who sat behind an untestable Juror claim.

tip: Two players claiming the same non-unique role can both be honest. Before you hang one side of a claim clash, work out the case where both claims are true. If a third result already fits that case (a Profiler list containing the claimed role, or an Oracle miss), test further instead of hanging.
evidence: Bob and Mallory were both real Auditors. The clash got Bob killed by Erin's release, nearly hanged Mallory, and led to the hanging of Dave, whose lists fit two Auditors exactly.

applies_to: Kitsune, Vigilante and other Village killers
tip: Don't fire a stored or limited attack on someone whose only evidence against them is a claim clash. Hold it until there is a mechanical lead, or until you are about to die with it unused.
evidence: Erin released the swallowed Katana attack on Bob, her 'best lead (fake counter-Auditor)', and killed a real Auditor. Bob's death also made it look like the Yakuza had killed one of their own.

tip: In the endgame, count what each possible hang leaves behind. With both Yakuza and a Neutral killer alive at 5-6 players, the Katana kills every night, while an Arsonist with no douses left needs several nights to kill again. Hang your best Yakuza suspect first. Be wary when a suspected Yakuza leads a quick round-1 push onto the Neutral.
evidence: On D5 Grace nominated Olivia in round 1 and the town hanged her. Olivia had already ignited, so she had no douses left. Two Yakuza stayed alive against two villagers, the Katana killed Mallory, and the Yakuza won the D6 vote.

applies_to: Yakuza and Neutrals faking visit-based roles
tip: Before posting made-up results for a visit-based role (Fortune Teller, Scout, Cartographer), check them against every claimed visit and every published will, including the one that came out that morning. Only a few honest numbers or names are possible, and a single impossible one exposes you.
evidence: Olivia's FT claim of 4 visitors on N1 was impossible: Carol, Erin, Grace, Dave and Niaj had all visited, and her N2 and N4 numbers were also questioned. Grace's N5 Scout names put Mallory and Heidi in different groups, even though Mallory's will said she had audited Heidi.

tip: Use your team's info and protection roles to make the Katana safe. Count the dangerous roles (Veteran, Coroner), shield the holder on risky nights, and don't attack the obvious trap or protect target. Hit the protector instead.
evidence: Grace used Talent Agent Counts to learn there was 1 Veteran and no Coroner. Niaj Divined Grace for Strong Defense on N3. On N4 Heidi switched the kill from Alice, who had Carol's trap on her, to Carol herself, and that kill also set off Carol's curse on Alice.

tip: Vote-based passive covers (Juror, Scrutineer) are hard to break because their results only repeat votes people already stated. Agree on them on Night 1, write them into your wills early, and keep your votes matching what you say publicly.
evidence: Heidi's Juror cover was never broken, even though she was Alice's last Oracle target. Niaj's Scrutineer cover held until Ivan's lead and the town's frustration got him hanged on a lean, not a mechanical result.

tip: Base each guess on the strongest role lead you have, and aim it at untestable claimers. Don't keep re-guessing on players whose claims have already been checked.
evidence: Alice spent N3 guessing Mallory, who was already heavily supported as the real Auditor. On N4 she guessed Heidi = Informant when Ballot Stuffer, the filler that appeared twice, was the better guess. That guess would have been right and would have been published in her will.

tip: Don't shoot a player because they announced a self-protection plan. Announced protection is only a claim. If the target's role is a claimed Medic who was role-blocked earlier, the block may still apply, and a Basic shot can kill a real Good player. Shoot only when the target's Defense is known or the kill is likely to hit a Yakuza.

Check each claimed role against the Katana timeline before accepting it. A Standard protection on a Standard Katana target should have stopped the attack, so a claim that fails this math is either a lie or a block. Ask whether the block is confirmed by a second source before you use it to clear or convict.

When a trial total does not match the public Guilty statements, ask each voter to post their reminder once and record who flipped. Flips and retractions made after a nomination are strong signals, but make sure the flip is not the thing being used to frame someone.

Using a Yakuza-only role claim (Grunt, Clerk, Wiretap, etc.) even as a bluff is effectively a confession. Retracting it after nomination does not undo the damage, and the Village will hang you on it. Never make such a claim unless you can recover from it.

A player who repeatedly self-nominates with no data and asks to be hanged is a strong Jester candidate. Keeping them alive is safer than hanging them, since a hanged Jester wins outright. Only hang a repeat self-nominator if the vote is clearly needed and the counts are checked.

Before you post your vote publicly, re-read your private reminder. I announced Guilty while my reminder said Innocent. That one mistake made the count look broken and gave opponents a lever against me for the rest of the game.

applies_to: Lookout, Tracker, Sheriff and other investigators
tip: Post a result when it can change a live vote, not as soon as you have it. My Night 2 watch was posted on Day 3, and I was killed the following night, so the information reached the village only as my death approached. If you are going to be a claimed info role, get the result out in the same turn you learn it.

A self-nomination with no data is a weak Jester tell, not proof. Erin's three self-noms and the trial push turned out to be a Jester hunting a hang. Spend the vote on a check you can actually run, such as a result that clears or convicts someone, not on who is loudest.

If you have a claim that matters, tell the village a checkable result in your first or second public message, not a hidden promise to post at dawn. Dave's Sheriff result on Erin (Evil) never came out, because he died before dawn, and the village never heard the one hard fact it needed.

Heavy public pushes that cite a teammate's retracted claim, such as Frank's Grunt post, cost the Yakuza more than they gained. The team kept winning the hang votes by coordinating in private and then voting in a bloc, and that was harder to read than an open, consistent story.

Frame only a player that a live investigator (Sheriff, Seer, Lookout or similar) will actually check or watch that night. My Night 2 frame on Bob reached nobody: Dave checked Erin, and Bob's watch never mattered, so the token and the tell were wasted.
Keep private PMs with a teammate to a minimum during the Day. Carol-to-Alice messages were visible to everyone, and they became the main lead for the village against the pair who pushed Heidi.
Don't let a teammate's public Yakuza-only role claim stand. Frank's 'Grunt (Yakuza)' post was retracted too late; it got him nominated and hanged, and the village treated the retraction as weak.

Check each claim against the dead's last wills and the public announcements, then ask the claimant to restate. Several Day 3-4 cycles were lost to self-nominations of Erin and to unverifiable Medic/Lookout claims that could not be checked after the claimant died.

When an announced trial total does not match the public votes, ask each voter to restate their own vote before anyone is pushed. Bob's public Guilty-to-Innocent flip and the 3-3 split created a mess that cost the village a clean hang.

applies_to: Investigators (Sheriff, Lookout, Tracker, Seer and similar)
tip: If you claim a role, expect to be the Katana's next target. I claimed Sheriff on Day 2 and was killed that same night, before my Night 2 result could be posted. Claim only when the claim is needed to win a vote, or when a Medic is likely to protect you. Once the claim is out, your results are the most valuable thing you have, so get them out early.

Results from the night you die never reach your will, and I did not record my Night 2 result in it. Write each result into your will as soon as it arrives, using the exact wording, rather than promising to post it later.

Repeated self-nominations with no data, followed by pleas to be hanged as a test, fit a Jester. Leaving that player alive was reasonable, but the village still needs a checkable lead. Pair the pattern with a concrete check (a result, a vote record, or a Night 3 watch) before the next vote, so the Yakuza cannot use the stalemate.

Before announcing your own trial vote, compare the Guilty count you expect with the count announced. When totals fail to match, ask each voter to restate their reminder, not to argue from memory. Several players in this game publicly stated Guilty votes that did not match a 3-3 tally, and that cost the village a full day.

A Yakuza-only role claim, even one retracted after a nomination, reads as a confession. Frank's retraction did not undo the claim. Do not make such claims as bluffs, and do not drive a trial you could be exposed by.

Before accusing a Medic or any protector, do the defense math: a Standard protection stops a Standard attack, because an attack kills only if its level is strictly higher than Defense. Heidi's 'Standard on Bob didn't stop Katana' claim was checkable and was read as a lie without anyone testing the rule.

Never publicly announce a trial vote you didn't cast, and correct any flip immediately with the reason. The Day 3 public Guilty-to-Innocent flip and the 4-Guilty-said vs 3-announced mismatch made the village spend a whole day on the vote count instead of on the Yakuza.

Never publicly claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a slip or a bluff. Frank's 'Grunt (Yakuza)' post got him nominated, and the retraction after the nomination did not undo it. Retract only with a plausible innocent explanation before anyone can build a case on it.

Repeated self-nominations with no data got only 1 to 3 Yes votes and were read as a push to be hanged. Instead, make one specific, checkable accusation that others can act on (e.g., a claimed role whose result contradicts a stated death), and vote Guilty on the target with the strongest stated reason. A Jester needs a Guilty majority, so the case must be made to others, not announced to yourself.

Private daytime messages between two players who then push the same nomination were read immediately as a coordinated pair (Alice and Carol on Heidi, Erin on Heidi). Pushes that are coordinated should rest on different stated reasons, and any day PMs should be kept minimal or explained in public.
Don't post a claim of a Yakuza-only role, even as a joke or a probe. Retracting it after you are nominated doesn't undo the signal, and it becomes the whole case against you.
Keep private coordination in night chat only. Daytime PMs between teammates are visible to everyone (the ledger shows them), and a visible pair that pushes the same target invites scrutiny.

Repeated self-nominations with no data are a strong Jester tell. Either vote Yes on that player once the pattern is clear, or stop treating their repeated pushes as evidence. Letting the pattern run for four Days wasted several rounds.

Many turns were 'no nomination from me, still waiting' filler. That spends budget that later rounds need for reads and trial defenses. Post only when you have a new fact, a vote, or a question aimed at a specific player.

A Medic who claims a self-protect against a visible Vigilante shot is exposed if the Vigilante is real. Before claiming a protection that failed, post a concrete result, and consider protecting a likely Katana target rather than yourself.

applies_to: Tracker, Sheriff, Lookout and other info roles
tip: Post your first useful result on the first Day you survive, even a single 'nobody visited' result. Night-1 kills hit info roles before they speak, and a result held in a will never reaches the village.

Never publicly claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a joke or cover story. The Grunt claim turned the village's vote onto the claimant. If a cover story is needed, pick a Village role that fits your visits and keep it consistent.

When a Medic or other protector's record conflicts with a Katana or Vigilante death, check for a role-block or a Drowsy trait before calling a liar. Ask who could have blocked them, and check the self-protect math (Standard does not stop a Basic or a Standard-level attack you did not expect).

Do not spend a one-shot kill on a bare claim, especially a claimed protector. A self-protect or block can fail, and the kill removes a Good player with no information gained. Wait for a corroborated lead or a clash the village can verify.

Correct any public vote statement immediately and say exactly what your reminder shows. A public Guilty that became Innocent (or the reverse) left the village arguing over the count for two days, and it was used to justify a nomination.

Don't announce a self-protect plan in public chat. Heidi said she would self-protect on Night 4, and the Vigilante shot her anyway, because a blocked protector is a predictable kill target. Post the protection result at dawn and keep the plan private.

Repeated role-blocks on a role with a night action (Medic, Sheriff, Tracker) don't prove a Yakuza blocker. A Drowsy-trait player, or a Party Animal or Pharmacist, can produce the same pattern. Before treating blocks as evidence, check whether the claimant's other results line up, and ask who was blocked or protected and whether the results match the Katana timeline.

A repeated self-nomination with no data (Erin used four) gives the Jester nothing to lose and gives the Yakuza a free pressure point. Ask for one checkable reason before voting, and don't let a self-nomination stand in for evidence.

When a public trial tally doesn't match the Guilty statements, first ask each voter to restate their reminder. Public flips (Bob's Guilty to Innocent) are cheap talk, so weigh the reminder over the announcement.

Private pairs that push the same nomination (Alice and Carol on Heidi) are a strong lead. Ask them to explain the private discussion in public before the vote, and don't let a pair's shared reasoning count as two independent votes.

Once a Yakuza is hanged or confesses, the players who defended them or voted Innocent become your top suspects. List them out loud the next morning. In a small endgame this is often the only mechanical lead you have, so don't let it get lost in arguments over who coordinated with whom.
evidence: Frank's trial went 4 Guilty to 2 Innocent, and Carol had just argued publicly for Innocent. With Frank, Grace, Dave and Bob dead, the only Innocent vote not cast by Frank himself had to be Carol's. On Day 4 nobody raised this, and Alice and Heidi spent the day suspecting each other.

tip: Never put your real Yakuza role into a public claim or the claim ledger, even by accident. If you have no cover, claim a plain Village role or none at all. Agree on a cover in night chat before Day 2.
evidence: On Day 3 Frank posted the claim 'Grunt (Yakuza)'. Heidi, Alice and Bob each called it a confession, Bob nominated him at once, and he was hanged 4-2. That cost the Yakuza half their team.

tip: Use your shots while the Village still has numbers to spare. In a lock endgame, don't shoot a player whose claim fits the deaths, and especially not a protector. Aim at the mechanical lead (a defender of a hanged Yakuza), or hold your fire and push a hang on that lead.
evidence: Alice took no action on N1-N3. On N4 she fired a Basic shot to 'test' Heidi's self-protection claim. Drowsy had blocked Heidi, so the shot killed the real Medic. Carol killed Alice the same night, and the Village lost with Alice's tokens unused.

tip: Post a result once it matters, but don't spend the day promising tomorrow's result, and don't announce who you will protect tonight. Promised results make you the next Katana target. An announced self-protection tells the Yakuza to attack someone else, and other players may 'test' it with a shot.
evidence: Dave and Bob repeated 'I'll post my N2 result at dawn' all through Day 2, and the Katana killed them on N2 and N3. Heidi announced she would protect herself on N4. Carol switched her attack to Alice, and Alice shot Heidi to test the claim.

tip: Count the players left each morning. With 4 alive (1 Yakuza, 1 Neutral that never blocks wins, 2 Village), one wrong night ends the game. Hang your best lead that Day rather than waiting for night results that may never arrive.
evidence: Day 4 ended with no hang after Heidi's Innocent trial and several self-nominations by Erin. The night that followed ended the game: the Katana killed Alice and her own shot killed Heidi.

tip: When you're the last Yakuza, try to turn the remaining Villagers against each other. Pick a target, push it with an ally through private messages, then back off before your own vote gives you away. Let the Villagers' night actions do your work.
evidence: Carol messaged Alice privately to agree on suspecting Heidi, nominated Heidi, then voted Innocent once Heidi's Medic claim held up. The damage stayed: Alice's last will and her N4 shot both targeted Heidi.

tip: Don't ask to be hanged outright or keep nominating yourself. Most players read that as Jester right away and vote No. Act like a cagey suspect instead: dodge questions, make shaky accusations, or hint at a role, so that Villagers want you hanged for their own reasons.
evidence: Erin nominated herself seven times. By mid-Day 2, Bob, Alice and Carol were calling her a Jester. Her one real chance came on Day 3, when Frank nominated her, and it failed at 3-3. After that she never got more than 2 Yes votes.

applies_to: Everyone, especially players reporting visit results
tip: Treat a reported visit as positive evidence of one destination, not evidence that the visitor went nowhere else. A player can make multiple visits in a night, including an extra Sleepwalker visit; a Lookout watching one target does not give an exhaustive list of everyone’s destinations.

applies_to: Village investigators and anyone assessing their results
tip: Keep different kinds of evidence separate. A Sheriff’s Not Evil result and a Tracker’s no-visit result can both be true for a Yakuza Katana holder who did not attack: the holder appears Good to alignment checks, and holding the Katana without attacking is not a visit.

Report exactly what your alert told you—how many visited and whether your attack succeeded—and label any identification of the victim as an inference from the announced death. Precise wording makes it harder for opponents to portray a deduction as a result your role could not provide.
Keep teammate planning in night chat. Daytime private-message contents are hidden, but the sender-recipient ledger is public and can draw scrutiny to a teammate connection.

When the town repeatedly asks a plain yes/no question about a checkable fact (did you hold the Katana on N1?), answer it once, directly, with a line that matches what the public record shows. Repeated non-answers read as guilt and were the main reason the town voted me out 5-1.

Every daytime private message between Yakuza is logged publicly as an event (sender, recipient, count). Bob's daily PMs to Grace were called out on Day 1 and became the town's main lead. Coordinate in night chat, and keep daytime PMs to a minimum or none.

Before calling a role claim a lie because its visit logic doesn't fit public data, check for hidden random-visit sources such as the Sleepwalker trait (R24). Alice's Veteran claim was true, and Grace's hidden Sleepwalker visit explained the second visitor. A 'gotcha' built on the visible visit record is weak when a hidden mechanic can explain it.

A Katana holder's visit is visible to any Tracker, and a Veteran alert kills any visitor, including random Sleepwalker visits from teammates. Before striking a claimed Tracker or a Veteran-claimer, consider whether the strike exposes the holder's visit or a teammate's trait visit, and prefer targets where the reveal costs least.
Separate a role’s chosen visit from any automatic trait visit. A player may visit more than one destination in a night, so a result showing one visit does not establish that it was their only visit.

Keep different kinds of results in their own lanes: an alignment check and a visit check neither corroborate nor contradict each other. A Tracker’s “did not visit” result also does not establish whether someone held or used the Katana.

Share results when they can inform a vote, but avoid naming your power role or next target before you need to. A public Tracker claim can make you the obvious target for Yakuza who fear being tracked.

At trial, ask what each speaker actually knows firsthand. A claim that a particular player caused an event may be a deduction from separate announcements, not something their role directly identified; challenge the inference without treating missing public evidence as proof of a lie.

applies_to: Lookouts and anyone interpreting visit reports
tip: A watch tells you who visited the watched player, not where else those visitors went or everything they did. Allow for multiple actions and automatic visits such as Sleepwalker before treating two visit reports as contradictory.

Before publicly claiming a role, ask whether the result is useful enough to justify revealing that role to the opposing faction. A weak result can expose you without changing anyone's vote; share the exact result when it bears on a decision.

applies_to: Yakuza and other teammates with private night chat
tip: Keep strategic teammate communication in the private chat intended for it. Even when message contents are private, daytime messages publicly reveal who is contacting whom and can invite scrutiny.

Separate a refusal to answer from mechanical proof. Ask a narrow, answerable question and weigh the response alongside results; if the day is ending without stronger evidence, make an explicit decision about the best available lead rather than letting suspicion become certainty by repetition.

State exactly what an alignment result does and does not establish. A Not Evil result is not a clear: account for exceptions such as a Katana holder appearing Good, and seek independent evidence before treating the target as safe or suspicious.

Before publicly claiming a power role, weigh the value of coordinating against the risk of becoming a block or kill target. Share results when they can meaningfully guide a decision, and avoid announcing future targets.
A result showing who visited one target does not show where those visitors did not go. Consider multiple visits and automatic visits like Sleepwalking before calling two claims contradictory.

applies_to: Village players when evidence is limited
tip: Treat evasiveness as a reason to investigate or ask a direct question, not as mechanical proof. If a trial is the best available lead, make the case honestly as a behavioral read and test competing explanations before voting.

Before calling a visit claim a lie, check hidden traits. A Sleepwalker visits a random player each night and nobody is told. Grace's Sleepwalker visit on Alice explained Alice's Veteran kill, and the town wrongly treated it as impossible. Ask whether any living or dead player could have had such a trait before voting Guilty on a 'the visits don't fit' argument.

When an argument against a claimant depends on a public visit log, list the hidden sources that could add a visit: Sleepwalker, Katana holder, Yakuza Spare Blade, Enforcer, Sleepwalker-style random visits. If one of them fits, the argument is weak. A teammate pushing this line hard is a Yakuza signal.

Two investigators checking the same target on Night 1 is a split, not a contradiction. Don't spend days on it. Ask for the second night's target and exact result in the same message, and nominate on whichever contradiction comes back first, rather than on silence from the suspect.

applies_to: Jester or any Neutral seeking a hanging
tip: A bare self-nomination with no data gets only one Yes and fails. To get hanged, you need a visible lead that a majority wants to act on, such as pointing at a claim with a checkable contradiction. Prepare that case before Day 2 instead of relying on a test nomination.

Protect the Veteran or Tracker claim that your Katana can expose. Carol was killed as a Tracker, and the Veteran's remaining claim was then argued against by the Yakuza's own 'visit logic' framing. Pushing 'publicly fake visit logic' against a real Village claimant has to be coordinated with the Pharmacist's and Grunt's stories, or it reads as a targeted vote.

When a town member asks a direct yes/no about your Katana or holder status, give a flat answer, even a lie. Repeated non-answers ('no claim, I won't vote on claims') read as guilt and became the lynch case, with 5 Guilty votes. A plain denial is cheaper than silence.

applies_to: Yakuza with Sleepwalker or other random-visit traits
tip: A random Sleepwalker visit can land on a Veteran on alert and kill you, and it can also create visits you can't explain. Before attacking or blocking on a night you have a random visit, consider that the random target may be an alert Veteran, and count that risk in the plan.

Don't use daytime private messages between teammates. Two Day PMs (Bob to Grace, then Bob to Frank and Heidi) were noticed at once and became the trial's main lead. Keep all coordination in night chat, as the older tip says.

When a claim needs a visit the public record doesn't show (for example a Veteran kill by a visitor who visited nobody else publicly), first ask whether a hidden random-visit trait such as Sleepwalker explains it. Ask the claimant or the suspected teammate directly before voting on the visit logic alone.

Hidden traits can add visits nobody can see. Alice's Veteran claim looked impossible from public visits, but Grace had a Sleepwalker trait that visited a random player each night. Before doubting a visit-based claim, ask whether a hidden Sleepwalker, Armed or similar trait could explain the extra visit, and don't let a Yakuza's 'the visits don't fit' argument decide your vote for you.

A Not Evil result on a player who may hold the Katana proves nothing, because the holder reads Good that night. Treat a Sheriff's Not Evil on a suspect as weak until you know whether that suspect was the Katana holder. Yakuza-holder checks matter more when they are repeated over several nights.

When a player repeatedly refuses a direct yes/no question (here, 'did you hold the Katana?') while pushing the table toward other people's claims, count that as a real signal. Ask once with a clear deadline and then vote on it, rather than accepting non-answers for three days.

Post your results early and exactly, with target and outcome. A Tracker who checks a Yakuza holder and then dies to the Katana gives the town a strong clue, but only if that result is public before the death; holding results back let the Yakuza frame the discussion around 'who claims what'.

On Days 2-3 the town spent a full day repeating 'no nomination, post your results' without making progress. Agree on a concrete vote trigger early, such as a named suspect plus a named test, so that the Yakuza don't get free days to sow doubt about the true Veteran.

Plan an answer to the obvious yes/no questions (such as 'Did you hold the Katana?') before Day 2. Then answer briefly and consistently. Dodging the same direct question for a whole Day becomes the case against you, even if no result says you are Evil.
evidence: Bob was asked about eight times on Day 2 whether he held the Katana and replied each time with 'no claim, I want data.' On Day 3, Erin nominated him because of that refusal, and Alice, Dave, Erin and Heidi all named it in their Guilty reasoning.

tip: Never send daytime private messages to a teammate. Everyone can see that a message was sent, and on early days it is often the only event, so it decides who the investigators check that night. Keep all plans for night chat.
evidence: Bob sent Grace a private message on Day 1, and Carol pointed it out publicly. That night Carol tracked Bob, Erin checked Bob and Dave watched Grace. On Day 3, Heidi and Alice asked Bob to explain the private messages.

tip: Don't skip the Night 1 kill in a small game. Each night without a kill gives every investigator a free result and takes nothing from the Village. Kill a vocal player or the person driving suspicion toward your team.
evidence: The Yakuza agreed on 'no kill, no block' on Night 1. Carol, who had pressed Bob and Grace on Day 1, survived to claim Tracker. All three investigators got a free look at the Yakuza pair.

tip: Combine a block report with the Lookout's list of visitors. If a player says they were role-blocked and the Lookout saw only one visitor whose action is unexplained, that visitor is very likely the blocker. A blocker is most often the Yakuza Pharmacist, so their daytime private-message partner becomes the top suspect.
evidence: On Night 2, Erin was role-blocked and Dave saw only Carol (claimed Tracker) and Grace visit her. So Grace was the blocker, which tied Bob to the Yakuza through his private messages to her. No one stated this chain. Bob was hanged on behavior alone.

tip: A player can visit more than one person in a night: their own action plus a Sleepwalker visit or a Katana attack. Before calling a claim impossible because 'X only visited Y,' check whether a second visit could explain it.
evidence: In his trial, Bob argued that Alice's Veteran kill of Grace contradicted Dave's report that Grace visited Erin. Dave, Erin and Heidi answered that a second visit, for example from a Sleepwalker, explains it, and this was in fact what happened. His defense collapsed and the vote was 5-1.

tip: Use alerts on the early nights, before you claim, when visits are spread around randomly. After an alert kill, claim Veteran the next Day so the town reads the dead visitor correctly.
evidence: Alice alerted on Nights 1 and 2 without claiming. Grace's Sleepwalker visit ran into the Night 2 alert, killing one of the two Yakuza. Alice claimed right away on Day 3, which explained the death and kept the town's attention on Bob.

tip: A self-nomination with no data is the most recognizable Jester move, and it almost never gets a majority. Instead, create mild suspicion through small factual errors or odd votes that make you look like a Yakuza, and push for a nomination only when the town is short of leads.
evidence: Frank nominated himself on Day 2 and got only his own Yes vote. Alice publicly called it 'bait, possibly a Jester play,' and the town stopped considering him.

tip: Hold back a power-role claim until your result can actually decide a vote. A Day 2 claim of a result that decides nothing mostly makes you the night's kill target.
evidence: On Day 2, Carol claimed Tracker with an inconclusive result about Bob, and the Yakuza killed her that night because she was 'the bigger threat.' Erin also claimed (Sheriff) and was the target of Grace's block.

tip: Stay unclaimed and save alerts for the late game, when few Yakuza are left and the usual town targets are protected or already used up. That is when the Katana starts going after quiet unclaimed players, and an alert then is most likely to kill the holder. Alert on consecutive nights once the Yakuza are down to one or two players.

A 'CORRECT' exact-role result whose role turns out wrong doesn't need a swap story. A Roleplayer's random results can still land on Yakuza by chance, especially when the Yakuza make up a large share of the table. Before you build on a swap explanation, check that someone actually reported being swapped.

Chronicler marks on suspects make a hang check itself, because the role is revealed even on a Day death. Hanging marked suspects early is cheap and high-value. A Chronicler should mark whoever is most likely to come up for a vote next, and say so after the mark is placed.

Claiming a role that matches your tokens isn't enough. Hold one-shot tokens like a Puppeteer's only while they can still change a vote. With two Yakuza left, spend them early, or you lose them to the next death.

Silent investigators can quietly agree with a loud claimant. If a public 'Oracle' call is backed by quiet Guilty votes and no counterclaim, the table is often right. Kindred and Faultline results that show who votes with whom are worth recording in your will.

Spend marks on the first nights, on whoever is most likely to be hanged next: the target of a contested claim or the player pushing No. A Day hang can't be cleaned, so a marked player's hang always reveals their true role. Announce the mark before the vote. It turns a hang the town would argue over into a test that checks itself, and it exposes the accused's false claim.

A Yakuza flip that doesn't match the exact role an Oracle called is still a strong sign the Oracle chose well, but don't explain it with a swap unless someone reported being swapped. Roleplayer results are random, yet their choice of targets still shows real reasoning. Judge a claimed checker by the flips their targets give, not by the results they report.

When every trial ends with exactly 1 Innocent, that vote is almost certainly the accused's own, so the surviving Yakuza are voting Guilty on their teammates. Vote totals won't find them. Look at the night evidence and at who argued against the nomination (Dave's No push) before the flip.

Your trial votes always count as Guilty, so you can never be the Innocent in a total. Write the trait in your will and keep it in mind before you state a vote. If you say 'Innocent' and the totals show none, you look like a liar unless you've disclosed it.

Late in the game, with few Yakuza left and the Medic already guarding the loud checker, go on alert. Once the obvious targets are covered, the Katana tends to turn to unclaimed players, and one alert can kill the last holder and end the game.

Once a Chronicler publicly says they marked you, your hang tests itself, and the town will hang you whatever cover you claim. Don't spend your last turns arguing. Leave a will that misleads, plant doubt that points at real villagers, and tell your teammates in night chat beforehand to vote Guilty and stay quiet.

Teammates must never argue No or ask to 'test it tonight' for an accused Yakuza before the vote. The table logs that push, and it becomes the next nomination, Bloodhound token and Chronicler mark. Switching to Guilty later doesn't erase it.

Kill a Chronicler who has claimed, or anyone who can reveal flips, before they spend their remaining marks. One extra mark can turn the next hang into a confirmed Yakuza flip. If a protector saved them once, hit them with a Ritualist's Divine guess rather than the Katana.

A Roleplayer's 'CORRECT' results are random, but its targets still come from real reads. When a claimed checker keeps landing on players who flip Yakuza, their read is working even if the exact role named is wrong. Yakuza shouldn't count on a 'Roleplayer' label to make the town ignore that player. Kill them or the protector guarding them.

In the endgame, don't send the Katana at a quiet, unclaimed player who survived without a claim. That profile fits a Veteran on alert. A Veteran kills the visiting holder and can end the game for you. Pick a claimed role whose night actions you can account for.

Once you become the day's main suspect, use a self-swap that night. You might be the Smuggler who argued against a hang, or a player people say they will check. Chronicler marks, Bloodhound tracks, Oracle guesses and Katana-free checks aimed at you all land on the player you swap with. Being told you were swapped is a small price. Dying with 2 unused swap tokens because you feared revealing that a Smuggler exists is the worst outcome.

When a teammate faces a hang that will reveal their role (a Chronicler mark, a confirmed exact-role result), don't argue No before the nomination. The lone dissenter becomes the next mark, track and hang. Vote Yes and Guilty with the table from the start, and change your vote only if the totals show you could actually win.

Don't send the Katana at the player who just made the day's biggest public play (a Chronicler whose mark flipped someone, an Oracle steering the hangs). The Medic guards exactly them, and two Standard Katana attacks in a row bounced off one ward. Hit an unclaimed mid-value player instead, or pair the attack with a swap or Divine kill. Late in the game, a quiet unclaimed player who has survived may be a Veteran, so hitting them can kill your last holder.

A Roleplayer-Oracle's 'CORRECT' is random and true only by chance. It still names whoever the Roleplayer chose to target, and a sensible Roleplayer picks real suspects. Several hits on Yakuza mean his targeting reads are good, not that his results are real. Yakuza should attack his reasoning and his choice of targets, not only the mechanics of his results.

A public role claim from a key investigator (e.g. a Bloodhound with a narrowing result) is a free, untraceable Divine kill with 2 ritual tokens. It goes through Medic protection and is an Astral Visit, so nobody sees it. Spend it on the claim that most threatens the team as soon as it's made.

Until a Ritualist is ruled out, share your result without naming your exact role, e.g. 'I have an attack-count result', or post it in your will. A public exact-role claim lets a Ritualist make a 2-token Divine guess, and no Medic or trap can stop that.

Use your scent token to split an earlier trio instead of chasing a vote lead. If the trio A+B+C showed 1 attack, tracking B tells you whether the attack belongs to B or to A/C. Don't assume the flipped Yakuza in the trio was the attacker: the Katana holder may be a different teammate.
