tip: Fake counts posted after everyone else has claimed get called 'copying the board'. Worse, they tie you to whichever teammate they back. Don't make your numbers support a teammate's fake result word for word. Leave them a little loose (for example, one unexplained visitor) so that if you're exposed, the town can't simply flip everything you backed.

Before a night when you might die, rewrite your will so it doesn't push the same Villager your teammate is about to push. The town reads a proven Yakuza's will in reverse. An accusation in my will cleared Grace and convicted Niaj. A neutral will, or even one that mildly doubts your teammate, is safer.

Exact-role surveys of overlapping groups add up fast. If one player sits in two Yakuza-role groups and also claims a role that is a common Yakuza cover (Party Animal for a Pharmacist), they're almost certainly the one. As Yakuza, kill the Surveyor-type before their second token, or block the likely protector the same night you attack.

An investigator whose 'confirmations' only ever repeat claims that were already public adds nothing. Judge them by the results that brought new information. If every new result points at a Village-claimer, that is a strong Yakuza tell (a fake Tracker or Lookout).

Once a Yakuza is mechanically confirmed (an Enforcer death, a dead holder), go back over whom their claims and will backed and whom they pushed. A dead Yakuza's fake counts backing a living player's story, while their will points at someone else, usually marks the backed player as their teammate.

Ask whether a claimed 'catch' fits rational play. If a Tracker announces their target for tonight and then 'catches' that player visiting, the target would have had to blunder. A framer-Tracker who needs a mislynch has every reason to invent that result.

Survey a seat that overlaps your earlier groups so the groups narrow each other down: Bob/Dave/Erin, then Dave/Erin/Grace, pinned down two Yakuza roles. Post the group and the role together so others can cross-check them against claims.

A Pharmacist's visit would block the player it visits, so any 'X visited me' or 'X visited my target' claim against a suspected Pharmacist has to fit the block mechanics. Check each accusation against the accused role's actual effect.

Give an investigator's 'confirmation' no weight if it only repeats a claim that was already public (e.g. a track posted after the target had claimed). Count only the results that added something new. If every new result a Tracker or Fortune Teller gives points at a Village claimer, treat them as the likely fake.

applies_to: Village with an uncheckable or vote-based role (Auditor, Juror, Scrutineer)
tip: If an exact-role result puts you in a Yakuza group, give the town something it can check before night falls. Say whose votes you will audit and what result would clear or condemn them, or ask a Profiler, Surveyor or Oracle to check you. A passive-looking claim in a Wiretap group, set against a fake Fortune Teller whose numbers fit every claim, gets you shot.

Don't shoot to settle a 50/50 between two uncheckable claims when one more night of results would settle it. Here the audit or Enforcer result was due the next morning. A fake Fortune Teller who posts numbers after everyone else has claimed can always make them fit, so 'his numbers fit everything' doesn't clear him.

Write your pending target and how to read each possible outcome into your will before night results come in. A dead player's will can still catch a fake Tracker: here 'audited Bob' set against 'Dave visited no one' was the break that won the endgame.

Use the hidden PM early, on the Day you land in a suspicious group. Send your role and planned target to the player you trust most, for example the Surveyor whose survey named you. That gives one confirmed person a reason to vouch for you, which a Wiretap or watcher can't connect back to you.

On a night when your block clearly mattered (a Kitsune release or a protector failed), claim that block with a town reason. Don't claim you stayed home. A proven blocker who says 'no block' exactly when a block happened becomes the obvious unclaimed visitor, and the story can't be checked in your favour.

A Scout names only three players from different groups, not every group. Don't build a 'therefore X' elimination from it. When a suspect pushes this kind of false deduction, town counts it as a mark against them, and it cost me my trial.

A Surveyor's or other exact-role checker's next token is a bigger threat than a protector who is holding a release. If your Katana on the checker gets swallowed, try again on the checker (or block them). Killing the protector instead lets the checker's last token expose a Yakuza-only role in a known neighbour group.

Fake results have to fit the dead's last wills as well as live claims. A 'visited no one' track that contradicts a dead Auditor's will, or a fake FT count that leaves that visit out, becomes the town's endgame proof. Never fake a result that only makes sense if the target blundered right after an announced check.

An Enforcer who keeps adding the same player as a second visit will likely visit them again. Don't move the Katana to a player the Enforcer has visited every night just because an earlier visit 'cleared' them. Kill or block the Enforcer first, or hand the Katana to someone the Enforcer hasn't been visiting.

Fire your one Strong attack on Night 1 at the target least likely to be hanged (a quiet, organized player). Your token dies with you, and the Night 1 chaos hides the kill. After that, every remaining bounty needs a hang with your Guilty vote, so always vote Yes and Guilty on a target's trial, and don't push them early in a way that looks like you have a stake.

applies_to: Neutrals who visit (Bounty Hunter, Serial Killer, etc.)
tip: Before you claim 'no visits', check the passive visit-group readers (Scout, Cartographer, Fortune Teller). A Scout result can put you in your victim's group. A blocked visit makes no link, so your victim being blocked can clear you by luck. Keep the claim vague ('passive, nothing to report') and let others explain the deaths for you.

Rate an investigator by whether their results ever added new information. A fake Tracker or Fortune Teller only 'confirms' claims that are already public. The first time they give a fresh result that clashes with a will or a Village claim, that's the break. Carol's timing argument won the final 1-vs-1 hang.

Role-blocked visits (including hidden Drowsy blocks) create no visit and no link. When a Scout or Cartographer group result clashes with a claim, ask first whether the claimant was blocked. Then ask why they posted their chosen action as fact after they had already been told about the block. Posting it that way is the real tell.

Don't publicly announce whom your fake Tracker will track the next night. It gives the target a strong defense: 'why would I visit on the exact night I knew I'd be tracked?' Invent the result quietly, or pick a target nobody expected you to check.

A Scout result names only three players who were each in a different group. It does not list every group, so 'X isn't in group A or B, so X must be in group C' is a false deduction. When someone pushes that inference, treat it as a red flag.

Check when an investigator's results were posted. If every 'confirmation' only repeats a claim that was already public, and the results that add new information all point at Village-claimers, you are probably looking at a fake investigator.

After a player is proven Yakuza (for example, killed by an Enforcer), go back over their claimed counts and their will. Whichever claim their fake numbers supported is probably a teammate's, and whoever their will pushed is probably Village.

applies_to: Village with an Astral or uncheckable role
tip: If a Tracker announces they will track you, welcome it and stay home. Then, if they report a visit, it is their word against yours, and you can argue that a guilty player would simply have stayed home. Keep your results in your will each night, so they read as consistent over time.

A fake Tracker who only echoes claims that are already public builds little credit. A planted 'visit' on the final night also looks suspicious when that player knew the track was coming. Make sure the frame fits a reason the target would plausibly visit.

applies_to: Neutral roles faking a Village role (Executioner, Jester, Disguised players)
tip: Don't make up night visits. Scout, Cartographer, Fortune Teller and Tracker results quietly test every claimed visit, and one wrong group result counts as a mechanical break. If you fake a role that visits, say you stayed home or held your action that night. Only claim a visit if a known visit already links you to that player.

If you claim a night action, decide on your full story, block included, before you post it. Posting what you chose as if it happened, then adding 'I was blocked' once someone breaks it, then trying a second fix, reads as three stories. The town hangs that even when the last version is possible (Drowsy).

Never post a claim or result that helps clear your target. If a survey group holds both you and your target, use the shared result to cast doubt on the target, for example by counter-claiming or leaving the role open. Don't hand them a clean claim. Once your target is confirmed town, hanging them is almost impossible, so start pressure on Day 2 before they claim.

Check when an investigator's 'confirmations' were posted. A Tracker whose results only repeat claims that were already public, and whose only new results contradict Village claimers (a will, an Astral claim), is likely a fake Tracker framing people. Carol caught the Fabricator this way at 4 alive.

A Scout result says those named players are in different visit groups. It does NOT mean everyone unnamed is in one big group. Even so, any claimed visit between two named players is a hard break, so cross-check every claimed visit against posted Scout draws.

Don't spend a one-shot kill to settle 'passive claim A vs passive claim B' when one of them has a result already pending. An Auditor, Juror or similar will report next morning, so wait one night and shoot whoever that result breaks. A claimant whose numbers fit every public claim, posted after all of them were out, has proven nothing: a fake can copy the board.

An investigator 'confirmation' that only repeats a claim already made in public is worth nothing. Sort the investigator's results by when they were posted. The informative ones are those that added new facts, and if every new fact points at Village-claimers, the investigator is likely Yakuza.

Visit-group results break visit claims hard. Any visit links two players, and so does a blocker's visit or a Smuggler's swap, so 'A and B in different groups' rules out A visiting B even through a block or a swap. Only a blockless block (Drowsy) or an Astral action explains it. Post the break at once and name the escape routes before the claimant picks one.

Test an accusation against the accused's suspected role. If X is said to be the Pharmacist and the accuser claims X visited him, the visit would have blocked him and he would have no result. Check the mechanics of each accusation, not only who has been cleared.
Once a player is proven Yakuza, re-read their past counts, their pushes and their will. Whoever their fake numbers backed is likely a teammate, and whoever their will pushes is likely Village.

Once your charm swallows an attack, don't announce that you're holding it or say whom you'll release it on. While you hold it you can't charm yourself, so you become the easiest high-value Katana target. A Pharmacist holder can block you and kill you with one visit, so the release never fires. Stay quiet, or release it on the very next night.

Results posted after everyone else has claimed (FT counts, tracks that only repeat an existing claim) are worthless as corroboration, however neatly they 'fit every claim'. Give weight only to results that were committed before the claims they check, or that add new information.

When two players both claim passive or unverifiable roles and one is a Yakuza info role, the one whose results fit too perfectly is not cleared. An Auditor or Juror who says 'my role works once we vote' is a natural real-Village claim. Wait one night for an audit or juror result before shooting or releasing on them.

Hidden one-shot killers often pick the same target on the same read. Two kills on one Village player waste both. If you're going to fire on a lead, agree publicly on who the strongest lead is, and keep your own target only in your will.

Write your intended night action and how to read the outcome in your will (e.g. 'released on X; if X doesn't show this cause, I was blocked'). My will proved I had been blocked N3, which pointed the town at the Pharmacist and got Erin hanged.

Don't visit the obvious likely victim. Five players piled onto Ivan on N1. An Enforcer only fires on a visitor who attacked, so pick a likely killer: the quiet player with a block-immune claim, or a later visitor to a Katana victim. With 2+ tokens, spend 1 to cover two suspects. Alice's two-target N4 visit killed the Katana holder that way.

On Day 1, sounding like the organizer ('I'll keep a ledger', speaking twice) gets you role-blocked or killed on Night 1. The Yakuza named exactly that as their reason to block Mallory. Speak once, briefly, and save the organizing for Day 2.

Weigh each investigator claim by the new information it added. A 'Tracker' or 'Fortune Teller' whose results only repeat claims that were already public, and who contradicts only Village-claimers, is a likely fake. Carol's timing check exposed Niaj this way at 4 alive.

Once a player is revealed as Yakuza, reread their posts and will. Whatever claims their numbers backed and whoever their will pushed are probably the reverse of the truth. Bob's fake counts backed Niaj, and his will pushed Grace, which pointed at Niaj.

Don't spend a one-shot kill on a 50/50 read between two claimants when a check is coming the next day. Ivan shot Village Dave on a hunch. An audit result or an exact-role check would have settled Bob vs Dave for free.

applies_to: Yakuza with a fake investigator claim (e.g. Fabricator posing as Tracker)
tip: Never post a fake result that contradicts a dead player's will (e.g. 'X visited no one' when X's will says they audited someone). The dead can't argue back, but the town later counts it as a clash against you. Match the will or pick a target nobody else reports on.

If every 'confirmation' you post comes after the matching claim is already public, and your only new results accuse Village-claimers, sharp players will spot it. Post at least one result early that couldn't have been copied from the board, and don't announce your next target if you plan to fake a hit on it: 'a guilty player would just stay home that night' is an easy rebuttal.

A teammate's fake claim that backs yours (fake Fortune Teller counts supporting your fake track) becomes evidence against you once that teammate is exposed. Keep the covers independent, and plan in night chat for what each of you says if the other flips.

Before moving the Katana, list who each living Enforcer or Veteran visited on earlier nights. Enforcers keep revisiting the same suspects. Don't give the Katana to someone the Enforcer has visited twice already, and if a holder is in doubt, keep it with the player she's least likely to visit.

With no Sheriff or Seer showing, framing does nothing. Save the forge for the night you attack a player who writes detailed wills: a forged will from the victim that names your chosen scapegoat is the strongest misdirection you have. Dying with the token unused wastes it.

On Day 1, don't give advice that only a visit-based role would think of, such as 'keep your visit info ready.' The Yakuza read it as a Tracker or Lookout hint and sent the first Katana at you. Generic lines about votes and PMs are safer.

Check when a claimed Tracker or Lookout posts each result. If every 'confirmation' comes after the claim it confirms was already public, and the only new information it ever adds contradicts a Village claim or will, the claimant is probably a fake (for example a Fabricator using a Tracker cover).

Once a Yakuza dies, re-read their earlier fake data (numbers, counts, wills). Whichever living claimant it backed, and whoever it pushed against, tells you a lot: a fake count that backs one player over another's will points at a teammate.

applies_to: Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle, Accountant claimants
tip: You may secretly be a Roleplayer whose results are random. Before you push a hang on your own result, check it against other claims (for example, a 'visit' by someone credibly claiming a passive role). If it clashes with several consistent claims, suspect your own result.

When you fake an investigator's result, a contradiction against a dead player's will gets checked closely late in the game. Prefer a fake result that matches the will, or one that can't be checked, especially at 4 or fewer alive, where one exposed clash decides the game.

Judge an investigator by what their results added. If a track or watch only repeats something already public, it confirms nothing. Only results that brought new information count, and if all the new ones point at Village-claimers who can't answer back (dead, or holding an uncheckable claim), suspect the investigator.
evidence: On D5 Carol showed that Niaj's N1 and N2 'confirmations' were posted after Ivan's and Carol's own claims. His only new results were 'Dave visited no one', which contradicted Dave's will, and 'Grace visited me', which contradicted her claim. That flipped the final vote to Niaj, the last Yakuza.

tip: Don't fire a one-shot kill on a coin flip between two uncheckable claims. Wait for a break in the target's own claim, or for a result that splits the pair. A wrong kill costs the town a voter and an investigator.
evidence: On N3 Ivan shot Dave, a real Auditor, because Bob's FT numbers 'fit every claim'. Those numbers were made up by Bob after the claims were posted. Judy planned to release on Dave on the same reasoning. Dave's audit of Bob died with him.

tip: Before choosing a Katana holder, check which players a two-target Enforcer (or a Veteran or trap) has been visiting. A player an Enforcer 'cleared' is often the one they test again. Give the Katana to a teammate they haven't touched, or skip the kill that night.
evidence: Alice visited Bob on N2 (blocked), N3 and N4. The Yakuza moved the Katana to Bob on N4, reasoning that Alice had cleared him. Her Enforcer attack killed Bob while the Katana killed her, which left Niaj alone.

tip: Fake results must fit every visit that a living or dead Villager can claim, wills included. Don't contradict a will that names a visit (e.g. 'audited Bob') unless nobody else can confirm the visit. Agreeing with it costs little. A clash with a dead Villager's will stays on record and a teammate's matching fake count ties the two of you together.
evidence: Niaj claimed 'Dave visited no one' even though Dave's will said he audited Bob. Bob's N3 count of 5 visitors left Dave's audit visit out in order to back Niaj. On D5, Grace, Ivan and Carol used that clash to expose Niaj.

tip: If you blocked and attacked the same player in one visit, claim the block and give a reason that sounds like town. Saying 'I stayed home' leaves an unexplained visitor to the victim. Don't push a deduction that doesn't follow; the town will catch it and count it against you.
evidence: Erin claimed 'no block' on N3. Bob's count then left one unclaimed visitor to Judy, and her 'Ivan's groups prove Grace is the holder' argument was refuted at once. Ivan, Niaj and Alice all named that false deduction as a reason to hang her.

applies_to: Neutrals and anyone faking a visiting role
tip: Visit-graph roles (Scout, Fortune Teller, Cartographer) can disprove any visit you make up. Claim a role that doesn't visit, or claim visits that can't be checked. If your story says you were blocked, say so when you first claim, not after you've been caught.
evidence: Heidi (Executioner) claimed a Trapper move to Carol. Ivan's Scout result put them in different groups. She then gave two more explanations (a Pharmacist block, then Drowsy) and was hanged 10-1 without ever pushing her target, Judy.

tip: Kitsune: after a swallow, report it but don't announce whom you will release on. Release soon, because you can't charm while you hold the attack and you become the obvious next target. Yakuza: once a Kitsune says she holds a release, kill and block her on the same visit.
evidence: Judy announced she was holding the Katana attack 'for the confirmed Yakuza'. On N3 Erin blocked and killed her in one visit, so the attack was lost.

tip: At low counts, ask whether the accused had a reason to do what they're accused of. If the accuser announced a track in advance, a guilty target would simply stay home, so a 'caught visiting' result against that target is more likely a frame.
evidence: On D4 Niaj announced 'N4: will track Grace' and then claimed she visited him. Carol argued that a Yakuza Grace would have stayed home and been cleared for free. This persuaded Ivan to vote Guilty on Niaj, and the vote won the game.

applies_to: Neutral non-killers (Vulture, Magpie) and anyone faking an info role
tip: Don't fake a role whose results are exact numbers that can be checked against everyone's visit claims (Fortune Teller, Cartographer). Unknown visitors such as a paid second Enforcer visit, a Magpie or a Sleepwalker will break a made-up count. Pick a cover with no checkable output, or one whose results you could only get from that role (tokenless, Astral, or results nobody else can check).

Give your full claim the first time you're asked for visits. Saying 'passive role, will say more later' drew the questions that forced a claim later, and every later change of claim (FT, then Roleplayer, then true role) made the town's case stronger. Claiming three roles is an automatic hang.

The town will hang a Neutral who blocks wins at any player count, so arguing 'hang me later' fails once you're on trial. Win by staying invisible. Spend little, never be the odd claim out, and don't post numbers that can be checked. If you must come out early, offer your daily death reports as useful info before you're cornered, not after.

Before trusting or faking a visit count, list every visitor you can't see: a Magpie stealing, Enforcer second visits, Trackers or Auditors who said they'd act that night. An 'impossible' count is more often a hidden visitor or a liar than a Roleplayer.

When two players claim the same role, don't let a trial total that doesn't fit the stated votes slide. One hidden Guilty vote (a Fixer) decided the Niaj hang. If the town had treated '4 Guilty vs 3 stated' as a Fixer warning before voting, it might have hung the right Auditor.

A visit with no attack only shows that the target didn't attack that night. It doesn't clear their alignment. Say it exactly that way when you post it ('X didn't attack N2'), not 'X is cleared'. Otherwise the town counts it as a clear, and the Yakuza will hand the Katana to the player you just 'cleared'.

Once you've claimed, the Yakuza expect you to visit whoever looks most suspicious, and they move the Katana away from that player. Your free visit has the best chance on a quiet player you haven't checked yet, or on someone you earlier showed didn't attack. Don't spend it on the loud suspect the whole town is watching.

Check each fake 'passive info' claim against what the public already knew when it was posted. A count that exactly matches what someone could have worked out at that moment, and is wrong only where hidden information comes in (paid extra visits, a Magpie), is a fabrication, not Roleplayer randomness.

If two people claim the same role and both have only reported results the public could already work out, a non-claimer's role-specific trait can break the tie. Ask who could be Bonded or Disguised. Weigh behaviour (who set up a test the fake couldn't pass) over 'my will has said so since Day 1', which nobody can check.

When you counter a fake result with your own paid action, post the exact token spend so an Accountant or Auditor can confirm it the next night. Then promise to spend nothing that night so the count stays clean. That makes the clash something anyone can check.

In hand-picked setups, roles can repeat. Two players claiming the same role may both be telling the truth. Don't treat a counterclaim as proof that one of them is lying. Ask both for results they could not have pieced together from public info, and keep the hang for a real break. Here both Auditors were Village, and the town hanged one of them.

To spot a fake investigator claim, ask whether each posted result is exactly what someone could have worked out from public facts at the moment it was posted. Real results often include surprises the public didn't know about. A run of results that only match what could already be inferred points to a fake. Results posted only after the matching public fact appeared (like a Juror number given after the votes were public) are a strong tell.

A visit-group read that clears someone as the Katana holder on a given night only clears them of holding it that night. The Yakuza move the Katana to dodge Enforcers and Scouts. Don't treat 'not the holder N3/N4' as 'not Yakuza'. The player such reads cleared here was a Fixer.

Naming your trap target publicly scares the Katana away from that player, but it also tells the Yakuza that you can't trap yourself, so you become a free, no-risk target. If you claim, keep your current trap target quiet, or move it quietly and claim the old target as a decoy.

When a trial total shows more Guilty votes than players stated, suspect a Fixer before you suspect the Innocent voters. Ask who cast the decisive Guilty votes, and especially who pushed the hang hardest alongside a confirmed-bonded or counterclaimed player.

applies_to: Cartographer, Scout, Tracker, Lookout and other visit-info roles
tip: On Day 2, don't say you can 'check visit claims against what I have.' The Yakuza read it as visit info and killed me that night; their chat named that exact line as the reason. Say nothing beyond agreeing, and put the data in your will.

Before each night, write in your will how to read every possible result, since that night's result never reaches it if you die. My N2 map (Carol, Mallory and Olivia in one group, so the holder was in neither 3-group) died with me. A will line like 'if Mallory's group has 3, then the holder is in another group' would have kept the logic alive.

Spend map tokens early, on the likeliest Katana target or a player with a claimed visit. The group sizes alone don't name the holder. I wasted N1 with no map and died holding a token. A map on a likely target puts the holder's name in your result.

A visit-group or Enforcer result clears a player only of holding the Katana that night, not of being Yakuza. The Yakuza moved the Katana to players the town had 'cleared' (Ivan after Bob's N2 visit, and Frank's two Scout clears). Track the holder by night and suspect the cleared players too.

When a trial total has more Guilty votes than players stated, suspect a Fixer before hanging the accused. A real Auditor (Niaj) was hanged 4-2 because a fix flipped his own Innocent to Guilty. A total that's off by one can mean the accused's own vote was flipped.

On Night 1, don't leave the Katana with whoever led Day 1's talk. Enforcers, Trappers and Magpies tend to visit the player who spoke first or most. Give it to the quietest Yakuza, preferably one with no night action of their own, so an Enforcer visit is less likely to find the attacker.

applies_to: Yakuza faking an investigator (Juror, Auditor, etc.)
tip: When you fake a result, post the exact numbers on the first Day they could exist, and only numbers that the public record already supports at that moment. Calling a result 'nothing either way' and filling in the numbers later, after the votes are public, is a timing slip that a Sniper or Vigilante can act on.

At 4 or fewer alive, think about where tonight's kill leaves the count, not just who is the biggest threat. A Village player whose will promises to 'name the killer' may be an Avenger, and losing your holder can collapse your Bonded partner too. If a different kill target or no kill still keeps you at vote lock, take the safer line.

Fixing the defendant of the likeliest trial is a strong use of a token. Their own Innocent vote becomes Guilty, and the town suspects a Ballot Stuffer or a liar among the voters instead. Fix that player the night before the hang you need.

A Bonded heartbreak death or an Avenger death names the faction link outright. Read the wills of the dead on that basis: if A dies of heartbreak right after B dies to Avenger, B held the Katana, and A was only tied to B, not necessarily on B's team.

If you fake a role whose results can be worked out from public votes or visits (Juror, Auditor, Fortune Teller), state an exact result the first time it comes up. Don't call it 'nothing either way' and fill in numbers after the missing input goes public. Timing gaps like that are what a good Villager uses to shoot or hang you.

Treat a player who claims a vague 'day role, no night visits' as a likely Sniper and kill them before they get a reason to suspect you. A Sniper's day shot can't be blocked, and night protection doesn't stop it.

Fixing the player you expect to be on trial is a near-certain flip, because the accused nearly always votes Innocent and that vote counts Guilty. Expect the totals to exceed the stated Guilty votes, though. Have a story ready for why one stated Innocent counted Guilty, or win the hang with votes to spare.

Near the end, remember that a hidden Avenger kills whoever holds the Katana, and through a Bond that can take out two players. If you have only one Yakuza left and a choice of targets, avoid the Villager whose behaviour suggests they're happy to be killed at night, or swap the attack onto a decoy if you still have a Smuggler token.

A claimed Enforcer can't hurt a holder who doesn't attack, so move the Katana away from whoever he'll likely visit next. Moving it is free and can't be blocked, and Enforcers often check the most suspected players.

On Day 1, say one short agreeing line and stop. Speaking twice or setting rules for nominators makes you look like a vote leader, and the Yakuza often pick that player as their first Katana target. Your shot only matters if you survive to Day 3 or later.

Fire your token-based day shot as soon as there is a real mechanical lead, such as a role claim with a timing hole or a claim that clashes with a result. A Magpie can steal unused tokens overnight, and a night kill wipes out all of them.

When the trial total has more Guilty votes than stated Guilty voters, and someone who stated Innocent is the one on trial, consider a Fixer. The Yakuza fix the player they expect to vote Innocent so that his vote helps hang him. Count the stated votes before the trial vote, and if the numbers are tight, think about holding the nomination until the next Day.

applies_to: Village with Avenger or Bonded traits
tip: With Avenger, say in your will exactly how to read an 'Avenger' death. Bonded heartbreak deaths can then link a Yakuza to their bond partner. A single night kill can set off a chain of deaths that ends the game, so put the full logic in your will before every night.

Visit-group results (Scout, Cartographer) are strong mechanical clears, but Astral and tokenless claims such as Juror or Philanthropist add no visits. A Yakuza can hide behind them by making no visits. Check whether a claimed result could have been worked out from public votes and wills at the time it was posted.

To test a claimed vote-based result (Juror, Auditor, Scrutineer), check when it was posted against when the votes it relies on became public. A real result often reveals a vote before it was public. A fake one only shows up after every vote it needs has been stated, or stays vague until then.

applies_to: Village players with the Avenger trait
tip: Once you've done your main job, claim loudly and make yourself the obvious Katana target. With few Yakuza left, the night kill on you trades their holder for you, and the 'Avenger' cause of death publicly names the holder. Write that in your will so the town can read it.

If a trial total shows more Guilty votes than players stated, and it's late with few players, assume a Fixer or Ballot Stuffer before assuming a miscast. The player whose Innocent got flipped is likely the Village one in a counterclaim pair, and the players pushing hardest for that hang are the Yakuza leads.

A heartbreak death reveals a Bonded pair. While both are alive, notice a player who keeps defending someone and steering hangs away from them. Bonded partners protect each other whatever their faction, so that defense tells you about the bond, not about alignment.
Fire the day shot as soon as you have a mechanical break, before the hang vote, so the shot can land the same Day. A Magpie can steal unspent tokens at night, so holding them has a real cost.

If your bond partner isn't on your team, the Yakuza can't win while both of you are alive (the partner blocks the win), and if either of you dies, the other dies too. So the Yakuza can only win through a teammate who outlives you both, or if the partner is a Turncoat. Tell your team early, keep the teammate with the least exposure safe, and don't plan around you being the last Yakuza standing.

applies_to: Yakuza faking an info role (Juror, Auditor, Fortune Teller)
tip: Only post fake results you could have worked out from public information when you post them, and post them promptly with exact numbers. If you are vague ('tells us nothing') and the exact number only appears after the relevant vote goes public, a timing argument can catch you. Frank was shot for exactly that.

applies_to: Smuggler and other Yakuza with one-shot tokens
tip: Swap tokens you hoard can be stolen by a Magpie or lost when you die. Plan a concrete use for them, such as moving a teammate out of an expected check or Enforcer visit, or covering a risky kill, instead of saving them for an ideal moment that never comes.

Before a trial you expect, fix the swing player who is likely to vote Innocent. Their Innocent then counts as Guilty, and the totals look like a lying voter, not a manipulated count. In this game, fixing the accused himself turned a 3-3 into a 4-2 hang.

applies_to: Yakuza Katana holder in the endgame
tip: Hidden Avenger and Grudge-type traits mean a night kill can take the holder down with it. When you are the last Yakuza and the target is a lone confirmed Villager, weigh whether you can win by daytime voting or by killing a different target instead. The Katana kill that wins the night can still end your game.

applies_to: everyone, especially players in a duplicate role claim
tip: Roles can repeat, so knowing your own claim is true doesn't make the other claimant fake. If two people claim the same role and neither result breaks, don't nominate the other one. Look at the third parties pushing hardest for that hang; Yakuza love a Village-vs-Village clash.

If a trial total has more Guilty votes than anyone stated, the likeliest Fixer target is the accused or one of their defenders, since that is how Yakuza force a hang. A hidden Guilty vote is evidence that the hang was what the Yakuza wanted. Don't count it against the people who stated Innocent.

Your bonded partner is told your name and may be Yakuza. If they defend you persistently and push hangs away from you, that may be a Yakuza protecting their own life, not Village trust. Their accusations aren't a clean read, so weigh them on their own merits.

Check the timing of claimed results that can be worked out from public votes (Juror, Auditor, Scrutineer). If a player names a result only after the votes behind it became public, or describes it vaguely before then, treat them as a likely fake. In this game that caught a Yakuza Fixer posing as Juror.

Near vote lock, if two claimants can't be told apart mechanically, a failed trial is cheaper than a wrong hang. Back the player who set up a test a fake couldn't pass. Don't make the clash a coin flip settled by your own certainty about yourself.

applies_to: Scout, Cartographer, Enforcer and other visit-based roles
tip: A visit-group or Enforcer result only shows who did not hold the Katana that night. It does not show that the player isn't Yakuza. Here Frank and Ivan were both Yakuza, and both were 'cleared' this way because the team passed the Katana around. When you post the result, say 'not the holder on Nx', never 'cleared'. Push back hard when others use your read to vouch for someone.

If a trial has more Guilty votes than players who said Guilty, and the accused and their defenders all said Innocent, think Fixer first. A Yakuza Fixer usually reverses the vote of a defender or of the accused. That makes it more likely the accused is Village, and that whoever drove the hang is Yakuza.

When two players claim the same role, look at who keeps vouching for each side. Here the Yakuza steered every hang away from Judy because Ivan was Bonded to her, so she was defended without being Yakuza herself. Players who loudly back one claimant and also defend someone your reads only 'cleared' as holder are the best Yakuza leads.
A player who claims a token-counting role (Accountant) can be a Magpie inventing numbers. Back a token result with a second source before you hang anyone on it.

Avenger plus Bonded can end the game overnight. When a night-killed Avenger is announced, read the 'Avenger' and 'heartbreak' deaths together: the Avenger death names the holder, and the heartbreak death is their Bonded partner, who may not be Yakuza.

applies_to: everyone, especially players whose role is counterclaimed
tip: Roles can repeat (two Auditors were both real here). Before treating a counterclaimer as Yakuza, look for a hard break. A same-role counterclaim alone is weak. Nominating the counterclaimer without a mechanical reason makes you look like the fake, and later it gets you hanged.

applies_to: Auditor, Juror, Scrutineer and other vote-reading roles
tip: Vote-reading results can be faked from public statements. To make a result count, post it before the audited player states their votes, or audit someone who has promised to keep their votes secret. Results that only confirm votes already stated prove nothing about the reader.

applies_to: Village players on trial when Yakuza may have a Fixer
tip: If you're the likeliest trial target, the Fixer may already have flipped your own vote. You can't fix that, so don't count on a 'stated 3-3 tie' to save you. Before the vote, say that any extra Guilty proves a Fixer or Ballot Stuffer, and put that in your will so the town can act on it the next Day.

Watch timing: compare when a player's 'result' first appeared with when the information it depends on became public. Heidi caught a fake Juror because his number only surfaced after the votes it needed were public. Then she sniped him.

Deaths in the same night tie people together. An Avenger death names the Katana holder, and a heartbreak death that night shows who that holder was Bonded to. Bonded pairs can mix Village and Yakuza, so a heartbreak death says nothing about the dead player's own faction.

Claim Accountant. It visits one player a night and reports a token count, so it explains every Magpie visit. It also lets you publicly ask token-holders to name their token roles, so you learn whom to rob next. Your fake counts should fit the target's claimed role minus what they've spent, and whatever you stole should fit inside that.

Only visit players who have publicly claimed a token role or a day role that hasn't been named. Skip anyone who claims a tokenless passive role (Scout, Auditor, Juror): robbing one wastes a whole night. Yakuza covers that claim tokens (Philanthropist, Profiler, Medic) are especially good targets, since the Evil role underneath usually has tokens too.

If someone else publicly claims your disguise role first, drop it and use a different cover. An exact-role check reading you as a role that's already claimed sets up a clash you can't win. Pick a cover that fits your real visits instead.

Don't claim a passive role whose numbers others can check, like Fortune Teller. The results you make up will clash with later claims, and each claim change looks worse than the last. Pick a role with no checkable output, or one whose single visit is your real one.

When two players claim the same role and both pass every test built from public information, look at who pushes the hang and who controls the vote count. Here the pair who pushed hardest (the counterclaimer plus her Bonded partner) and a Fixer flipped the Village Auditor's vote and hanged him.

applies_to: Yakuza and Neutrals faking an investigator
tip: When you fake a role, pick one whose results nobody can check, or one with tokens that match yours. If you fake a result, post it with exact numbers as soon as you 'get' it, and only use what you could really have known at that moment. Count results like visit numbers and vote overlaps get broken by hidden actions. Results that stay vague and only come out after the facts go public look made up.
evidence: Alice's fake Fortune Teller counts were built from Dave's will. They broke on Bob's unseen paid second visit on N2, and she went through three claims before she was hanged. Frank called his Juror result 'nothing either way' on D4 and only gave '0 of 1' once Alice had posted her vote. Heidi caught the timing and sniped him.

tip: A clear that only shows someone didn't hold the Katana on a given night (Scout groups, Enforcer misses, Tracker/Lookout) clears them as holder that night, not as Village. The Yakuza move the Katana on purpose, often away from whoever is being watched. Never count such a player as confirmed Village.
evidence: Bob's N2 double visit 'cleared' Ivan, and Mallory's N3/N4 reads 'cleared' Frank. Both were Yakuza: Frank had moved the Katana to Ivan to dodge the Enforcer. Players then defended Frank and Ivan with those clears during the Day 5 hang of Niaj.

tip: Roles can repeat. When two players claim the same role and their results match each other and the public facts, the clash alone isn't a break. Look for a separate mechanical break before hanging either one, and don't take 'who claimed first' or 'who nominated whom' as proof.
evidence: Judy and Niaj were both real Auditors, and every audit they posted matched. Niaj was hanged on Day 5 on behavior alone (his D3 nomination of Judy), with the Yakuza pushing it.

tip: Use a fix the night before a close trial you can see coming, and put it on the player most likely to vote Innocent. Even the likely accused works, since a fix can make their own vote count Guilty. In a small game one reversed vote decides the trial, and fixed players are never told.
evidence: Frank fixed Niaj on N4 expecting a Judy trial. Instead Niaj himself went on trial, and his Innocent vote counted Guilty: 4-2 instead of a failing 3-3. That hanged a real Auditor.

tip: Early on, visit the player most likely to hold the Katana: the confident Day 1 organizer, or a quiet player trying to steer the game. Once the Yakuza know an Enforcer exists, expect the Katana to move. Spending a token on two visits can clear two players as holder, but only for that night.
evidence: Bob visited Erin, who had led Day 1, and killed the N1 holder. After Bob claimed, Frank moved the Katana to Ivan, the player Bob had cleared. Bob's free N3 visit then found nothing.

tip: Fire a day shot when a claim has a concrete break: a result that came out after the facts it depends on, or numbers that can't be true. Fire it before the Yakuza can kill you that night. Then say publicly that you shot, so the town can read the result.
evidence: Heidi worked out that Frank's Juror number only appeared after Alice posted her vote, and shot him on Day 5. Frank was a Yakuza and died, and Heidi was killed that night.

tip: Claim a tokenless role that explains your real visits (an Accountant visits one player a night). Make your fake results fit the claims already public, then steal from claimed token roles. Village: don't let an unconfirmed claimant's results carry a hang.
evidence: Olivia's fake counts (Erin 2, Mallory 0, Bob 2) fit every claim. They helped seal Alice's hang while Olivia stole from Erin, Ivan and Heidi, and she won on N4 without ever being suspected.

tip: Use your swaps and other one-time tokens while they can still change the game. A Magpie or your own death removes them for good. Late in the game, with few players left, kill a target you can't see behind (a possible Avenger or a trap) only when it ends the game or prevents a loss, and weigh what a sudden death of the holder would cost.
evidence: Ivan never used a swap: a Magpie stole one token and the other died with him. At 4 alive his Katana kill on Heidi set off her Avenger trait. He died, Judy died of heartbreak, and the game was lost.

tip: Spend the chosen-pair token pairing a suspect with a player already proven Good (for example by a curse, or by a death that only a Good player could cause). Same/Different then becomes an absolute alignment read. Because a chosen pair is a visit, a Lookout seeing you at either target also proves you aren't a Roleplayer, since a Roleplayer's actions aren't visits.

When reading Seer or Sheriff results, ask for trait reveals first. A Notorious or Turncoat player reads Evil, and the Katana holder reads Good, so either can flip the meaning of a Same/Different pair. Write down every reading the result allows before you build a case on it.

When a trial total diverges from stated votes, build the smallest model that fits it exactly. Count the Stuffer's double, admitted misclicks and at most one Fixer flip per Fixer token. Also allow for a Merciful player: someone whose vote keeps counting Innocent while they say Guilty may be Merciful rather than fixed. Then hang the pattern, starting with the player who has the least checkable claim.

In small endgames, combine visit-graph results. A Lookout's watch puts the watcher in the same group as the watched player, and Scout or Cartographer groups then show which players could have reached the Katana victim. Together these can prove who the holder is when no alignment check is left.

Once the Yakuza can block hangs with a stuffed or fixed vote, a day-kill (Sniper) or a single convincing hang matters more than spare trials. Don't run a third trial while a known fix is active; it just repeats the same tie.

Being told you were attacked and survived, with nothing else to back it, may be the hidden Paranoid trait (Village only, 1/4 chance each night). Don't publicly call it proof of a second Katana, Spare Blade or Stolen Blade. Report it as 'told I was attacked, cause unconfirmed' so you don't send the town after a ghost.

Don't claim Sniper until your first shot has gone off. Shots are anonymous, and that anonymity is your protection. Once a shot kills, a public claim marks you as the top Katana target that night. You still hold tokens that die with you, so either stay quiet after the kill or put your next target in your will.

A Basic shot (1 token) is usually enough, because most Yakuza have Defense None. The best moment to fire is right after a trial total proves a hidden block is protecting someone. Fire the same Day: the Day you reveal yourself may be your last.

A Remorseful player who survives a Guilty vote proves the hanged player wasn't Village. A curse death proves the victim was Good. Use these hard confirmations to sort out which visit claims are real, then work through visit groups (Lookout plus Scout) to find who held the Katana.

When a trial total comes back far below the stated Guilty count, write out every voter's stated vote and build a model that matches the total exactly. Then nominate within that model the same Day, while the Village still has the votes, before the Yakuza reach a vote lock.

A Divine (Katana Master) attack is still a visit by whoever holds the Katana. Once you know a Lookout exists, for example because she said so in a PM a teammate can read, kill her first or use your best-covered holder. Don't take the Katana yourself to hit the obvious watch target, like a newly claimed Sheriff. Save the Divine upgrade for a target you know is protected or trapped.

Stuffing proves a Ballot Stuffer exists, because there are more votes than voters. If teammates also secretly click Innocent after saying Guilty, the town's stated-vote tally shows how big the block is and points at whoever you lobbied. If a clean visit break has you doomed, let the hang go and keep your teammates hidden.

Before picking a cover, check whether other players' results could contradict it. A Trapper co-visitor, an Insomniac who heard roles and a Lookout together can leave you as the only unexplained visitor. Pick covers that explain a visit to whoever the Katana will hit, and don't let the holder be the one teammate whose cover is weakest.

An Innocent verdict doesn't make you safe. A Village Sniper can shoot you the same Day, so a suspect who survives a trial through vote manipulation can still die right away. Yakuza should count unclaimed day-killers before spending their credibility to save someone.

Use the Fixer on the player most likely to nominate or vote Guilty on the teammate who's in danger, and use it the night before that teammate is likely to be exposed. A fixed vote, a Merciful vote and a stuffed vote can together cover the gap with no visible lying, which is much safer than asking teammates to vote secretly.

If your Evil read claims Executioner or Jester, don't publicly claim Sheriff to push the hang. Those roles never block a Village win, so the hang gains little, and the claim gets you killed that night. A Katana Master can make a Divine attack that no Medic or trap stops. Keep the read in your will and keep checking.

Always put tonight's check target in your will (e.g. 'N2: checking Erin'). If you die that night, the result never reaches your will, but naming the target, along with why you suspect them, steers the town onto the right player.

When a player's vote counts Innocent although they said Guilty, and they blame a Fixer on a night when no Fixer had acted yet, suspect the Merciful trait on a Yakuza. Keep tracking that player across trials. A vote that keeps counting Innocent is a team that keeps protecting itself.

As soon as your trait shows someone's vote counted against what they said, post it publicly, or at least put it in your will. Named voters are the only thing that turns an anonymous total into a suspect.
If a Remorseful player votes Guilty and survives the hang, the hanged player was not Village. Use that confirmation to go after the people who openly voted Innocent in that trial.

applies_to: Yakuza (or anyone) with Merciful or Zealot
tip: Your trial vote always counts one way, and Faultline, Kindred, Auditor or Informant can see that. Publicly state the vote as it will count, and give a reason that fits your claim. Saying 'Guilty' while your vote counts Innocent creates a mismatch, and a Faultline will pin it on you by name. 'I was fixed' is a weak excuse after that.

A Lookout who has claimed and is posting sightings is the most dangerous player on the table. Every Katana kill puts the holder in her watch, and she can stack sightings night after night. Kill her before a Trapper or protector covers her. A Sheriff whose results are already in his will is worth less.

Don't save a teammate with hidden Innocents while publicly saying Guilty. A total like 4G/7I against 9 stated Guilty shows the town roughly how big your block is, and who got the doomed player's PMs. The saved teammate can still die another way (Sniper, next trial). Either commit to openly voting Innocent, or let them go.

Fix the town's loudest, surest Guilty voter on the night before you expect to be tried. One flipped vote turned two D4 trials into 3-3 ties. A fix on a random player 'just in case' is usually wasted. With 2 Yakuza left, 1 fix plus 2 Innocents ties a 6-player vote.

Before you claim a night result, check it against every visit-based role that could be live: Lookout, Scout or Cartographer groups, Tracker. Scout groups combined with a Lookout's watch can rule out alternative killers. 'Tracked the victim, they went nowhere' only works until the visit-group results trap you.

A trap only arms the night after you place it, so moving it each night to whoever just claimed is always a night late. Put it early on a likely future target, such as a strong investigator who hasn't claimed yet, and leave it there. Remember that Divine attacks (Katana Master, Ritualist) ignore traps completely.

Traps stay in place after you die. Name the trapped player in your will: a known armed trap makes the Yakuza avoid that player, so it protects a key villager (like a Lookout) for the rest of the game even if it never goes off.

Fixers like to target whoever nominates or pushes Guilty hardest. If you nominate, expect your next trial vote may be flipped, and say so in public. That way, an unexplained hidden Innocent in the total doesn't get blamed on another villager who told the truth.

Combine visit-group results (Scout or Cartographer) with a Lookout's watch. The watch links the Lookout to the target, so a group split can rule people in or out as the killer without anyone having to trust a bare claim. Ask for both in one line each and line them up.

If a Remorseful player votes Guilty on a hanged player and survives, that shows the hanged player wasn't Village. Use it to confirm a hang after the fact, and to point the next day's case at whoever openly voted Innocent on that player.

applies_to: Village info roles (especially vote-based ones like Auditor)
tip: On Day 1, keep any suggestion general. Don't propose anything that points to what your role does. My call for everyone to state their votes publicly was quoted in Yakuza chat as the reason to kill me N1, because it threatened their Ballot Stuffer and Fixer. If a procedural idea matters, let someone else raise it, or bury it among other ideas.

A Remorseful player who publicly votes Guilty and survives the hang has proved that the hanged player wasn't Village. A 'remorse' death proves the opposite. Treat this as a hard result and build on it: Judy's survival after Mallory's hang settled who had defended a non-Villager.

Put visit-group results (Scout or Cartographer) together with a Lookout's watch. The Lookout's own watch links them to the player they watch, so a group split that puts the Katana victim apart from certain players rules those players out as the holder. Late in the game this is a mechanical break, not a lean.

Don't mass-PM teammates during a trial asking them to vote Innocent. Everyone can see the PM pairs. Once the total comes back with too many Innocents, the town hangs the players you PM'd, so a doomed teammate's PM spree costs you a second member. Plan vote-saving only in night chat.

Votes-as-counted traits (Faultline, Kindred, Martyr) catch hidden Innocents. If you are Yakuza with Merciful, or you rely on a Fixer flip, expect a Faultline holder to report your vote counted Innocent. Have a consistent 'I was fixed' story ready from the start. Erin's D2 mismatch was the thread that eventually hanged her.

Check every heard role against the claims. A Yakuza-only role (Mortician, Fixer) proves the team is active, and a heard Village role that nobody claims, or a claimed role that would have to be among the visitors but conflicts with the list, is a break. Spend both tokens early, while there are many visitors and few covers, and post the lists once they back up or contradict a claim.

If Faultline, Kindred or an Auditor shows that a player who said Guilty counted Innocent, treat 'I must have been fixed' with suspicion. A Merciful Yakuza says exactly that. If the same player's votes keep counting Innocent across trials, or they vote Innocent openly later, that is a strong lead.

Your fixed reminder still shows the vote you cast, so you can never rule yourself out as the flipped voter. Yakuza Fixers like to target the loudest Guilty voter or nominator. When two trials in one Day tie by exactly one hidden Innocent, stop holding trials and bring the case back the next Day, after the fix has expired.

Combine visit-group results with Lookout sightings. A Scout or Cartographer result that puts the victim in a different group from a watched player clears everyone who would be linked through that watch. A Remorseful player who survives a Guilty vote on a hanged player proves that player was not Village.

Compare a large Innocent total with the stated votes right away (for example 4G/7I when 9 said Guilty) and model who the hidden Innocents are. The players a doomed suspect PMs during their own trial are the first place to look. That model won the vote lock race this game.

Saving a teammate with secret Innocents that you publicly deny is a trap. The total shows how many people lied, and everyone who was PM'd or who has an uncheckable claim becomes a suspect. Only hide Innocents if they actually win the trial and the teammate can't be killed by Day afterwards (a Sniper or a later trial). Otherwise vote Guilty for real.

Kill the Lookout or Tracker who watches the likely Katana victim before a Trapper's trap on them arms (it arms the night after it's placed). Every night they live, they publicly name the holder at the body. Sightings like that brought down three of our four players.

Before posting a fake result, check it against visits already made public. A Roleplayer's actions aren't visits, so a player a Lookout saw visiting is not a Roleplayer. 'Your claimed role is WRONG' then falls apart and exposes you. Choose fake results that no public sighting can contradict.

Claim traits that explain away evidence (Notorious, Sleepwalker) early and once, before the evidence shows up. Bringing them out at 3 alive, right after the result they explain, reads as invented and convinces nobody.

Merciful votes plus a Fixer token on the loudest Guilty voter can force tie trials at small counts. Our 3-3 trials on Day 4 came from exactly this, so plan the Fixer target in night chat around the next Day's count.

Watch the player most likely to be killed tonight: a confirmed power role who just claimed, or the town player who is driving the votes. In this game that caught the Katana holder three times (Carol at Dave, Erin at Bob, Ivan at Alice). Watching a suspect usually only shows their protectors.

Combine Lookout sightings with Scout or Cartographer visit groups. A watch links the Lookout to the watched player, so 'Judy and Heidi were in different groups' plus 'Judy watched Alice' rules Alice out as Heidi's visitor. Those exclusions can decide a hang when only two players visited the victim.

Don't confirm your role or result in a PM to the player you watched, even when the result looks harmless. If they're Yakuza, the whole team knows your role that night. Here the cover claims were changed to avoid clashing with mine, and I was put on the kill list. Ask your question in public, or wait until the result bears on a vote.

Once you've survived a Guilty vote on a hanged player, say so. It proves that player wasn't Village and can't be faked by anyone else. Before you vote, check your click against the vote you stated: a misclick produces a hidden Innocent you then have to explain while the vote math is being argued.

When a trial total has more votes than voters, or shows several hidden Innocents, list everyone who stated Guilty and test the smallest set of liars that fits the total. Carol's 4G/7I trial pointed to her team, which was later confirmed. Yakuza also defend a teammate by voting Innocent in the open and PMing other voters mid-trial.

When the whole table has said Guilty on your teammate, every hidden Innocent shows up in the total. Vote Guilty, or let only the Ballot Stuffer's double and the Merciful/fixed votes carry the save. If the save fails, the leftover gap tells town how many liars there are and who to hang next.

Clean every Katana kill while you have tokens, especially kills of claimed info roles. Their wills hold results and suspicions that point at your team. Saving tokens 'for a better target' tends to leave them unspent when you're hanged.

Pick a cover that gives a checkable-looking result every night (e.g. tokenless Tracker or Oracle results). 'Held my token' or 'no result' is read as having nothing to show, and it becomes the hang case. Also avoid common Village covers like Sheriff, which a real claimant can break.

Before choosing who holds the Katana, work through what a Lookout watch plus a Scout or Cartographer group result would show. Late in the game, with few players alive, one sighting plus a group count pins the holder. Pass the Katana to someone whose cover explains a visit to the target, or pick a target the Lookout is unlikely to watch.
Do all vote-swing requests in night chat. Daytime PMs from a doomed teammate to several players get read publicly as a list of teammates, and those players get hanged next.

Combine your group results with a Lookout's watch. The watcher and the watched player are always in one group, so if the Katana victim is in a different group from the watcher, the watched player didn't visit the victim. You also know your own visits, so late in the game, once a few players are cleared this way, the victim's group often has only one possible killer left.

applies_to: Village with Stolen Blade or Armed
tip: Use a one-shot attack on your top Yakuza suspect when a vote lock is coming, and post the result whatever happens. A failed Standard attack is a lead, but it isn't proof: the survival can come from hidden Narrow Escape, a Diviner shield or an unclaimed protector. Combine it with the target's visits before you hang on it.

When several trials in one Day come out with the same hidden-Innocent gap (for example two 3-3 results), suspect a Fixer or Merciful vote that lasts all Day. Stop nominating that Day, plan the hang for the next Day, when the fix is gone, and line up your strongest case first.
If a player who claims Remorseful votes Guilty and survives the hanging, the hanged player wasn't Village. Treat that as near-confirmed, and look at whoever openly voted Innocent on that player.

At 3 alive, ignore trait claims that first appear in a trial, like Notorious or Sleepwalker. Trust the Lookout sighting and visit-group result that agree with each other and with earlier corroborated results. The cornered Yakuza will build a model that fits everything only by adding hidden traits nobody can check.

If a Sheriff reads you Evil, don't claim Executioner. Town will say 'hanging a real Exec costs nothing, and it might be Yakuza' and hang you almost unanimously. Claim Jester instead: it also reads Evil, but hanging it sets off a Divine revenge on a Guilty voter. That gives the town a real cost to hanging you, and Remorseful or cautious voters will hold back.

Keep a low profile on Day 1 and early Day 2. Telling investigators not to post results, right after a Mortician kill, sounds like a Yakuza protecting the team, and it handed the Sheriff a reason to nominate me. Your win depends on staying alive until your target's trial, so don't start fights before you have to.

If you must give a fake target, pick someone the town already wants alive and trusts (I named the Sheriff). That keeps your real target unexposed. It only helps if you survive, though, so put survival first and treat the target claim as secondary.

An offer to be tested ('check me tonight, hang me tomorrow if I break') rarely saves you on a Day with no other lead. The town would rather take a sure hang than wait. Show them a concrete cost of hanging you, or give them a better lead today, not tomorrow.

Visit-group results (Scout or Cartographer) combined with a Lookout's watch can clear or convict players by graph logic. Write out who links to whom each night, because a lone unexplained link to the Katana victim is near-proof.

State your trial vote in public, including 'insurance' Innocents. Put any Faultline or Kindred vote information in your will right away. A known tally plus one trait result can expose a specific hidden Innocent.
evidence: On D2, Dave and Judy announced their Innocents, so the town expected 3 Innocents but the total showed 4. Dave's Faultline named Erin as an Innocent even though she said Guilty. He wrote it in his will before he died, and Erin stayed the town's top suspect until she was hanged.

tip: Once a teammate is caught by a corroborated visit, don't have the team secretly vote Innocent to save them, and never lobby teammates by Day private message. A large gap between the total and the stated votes reveals how many of you there are, and the message ledger shows who is involved.
evidence: Carol messaged Ivan, Mallory and Niaj (twice to Ivan and Mallory) asking for secret Innocents. The 4 Guilty, 7 Innocent result with 11 votes let Heidi and Alice count about 4 hidden allies. Bob sniped Carol anyway, and Mallory was hanged the same Day on the message link.

tip: Each night, watch the most likely Katana victim, such as a just-claimed investigator, the confirmed killer role, or the player whose innocence tomorrow's case depends on. A lone or corroborated visitor to a Katana victim nearly decides the game.
evidence: Judy's watches decided the game. She watched Dave on N2 and saw Carol, Bob on N3 and saw Erin and Alice, Alice on N4 and saw nobody (which cleared Alice of Heidi's death), and Alice on N5 and saw Ivan.

tip: Combine visit-group results with Lookout sightings. A watch is itself a visit, so the watcher and the watched player share a group. Use that to rule out visitors whose own claims can't be checked.
evidence: On N4, Niaj's Scout result put Heidi, Ivan and Judy in different groups, and Judy had watched Alice. So Alice could not have visited Heidi, which left Erin as the killer, and she was hanged on D5. On N5, Niaj's two-group result matched Judy seeing Ivan at Alice's.

tip: Pick covers that produce plausible, checkable-looking results every night. 'Held my token' or Oracle 'confirmations' of already-public claims look empty. A late invented result or a last-minute trait claim made at 3 alive rarely convinces anyone.
evidence: The town hanged Mallory mainly because she 'held her Profiler token N2' and had nothing checkable. Ivan's Oracle hits were only on public claims. His fake 'Alice = Seer, wrong' clashed with Judy's sighting, and his Notorious and Sleepwalker claims on D6 were brushed off.

tip: Expect Lookouts on just-claimed or confirmed power roles. If you must kill one, give the Katana to the player whose cover best explains the visit, and save once-per-game Divine attacks for when protection is actually likely. Use the Fixer on the loudest Guilty voter right before a trial you expect.
evidence: Carol's Katana Master kill on the outed Sheriff Dave was seen by Judy, which started the collapse. By contrast, Erin's N3 fix on Heidi caused both D4 trials to tie 3 to 3 and nearly let the Yakuza reach a vote lock.

tip: When a Fixer flip is known to be active for the Day and trials keep tying, stop nominating. The fix lasts all Day. Put the remaining votes on the best lead the next Day, before the Yakuza reach parity.
evidence: After two 3 to 3 trials on D4, Niaj, Alice and Judy refused a third trial. They hanged Erin on D5 with all three really clicking Guilty, one step before the 2-versus-2 lock the Yakuza had planned.

tip: Spend a chosen-pair or one-shot check by pairing someone already proven Good (for example by a curse or a lone-visit result) with your top suspect. Then the result reads directly as that suspect's alignment.
evidence: On N3, Alice paired Bob, who was later proven Good when his curse killed Frank, with Ivan and got DIFFERENT. That marked Ivan as not Good and led to his hanging on D6.

tip: Shooting a suspected Jester at night removes them with no revenge (revenge only follows a hanging), and your kill result confirms the role. A Basic shot works as a Defense test: if it kills, the target had no Defense, which rules out an SK, Jester or Arsonist. Aim it at the player whose case is weakest. An accuser whose evidence nobody else can check is often a better target than the person they accuse.

When a case against someone (e.g. 'tracked him onto two SK victims') comes from only one player, treat the source as just as suspect as the target. An SK can kill next to a Sleepwalker and then fake tracks to frame them. Ask for a second, independent result before acting on it.

If a known Fabricator is alive, an Evil read on a player who has just counterclaimed someone's role is exactly what a frame looks like. Duplicate investigator claims, such as two Scouts or two Sheriffs, can both be honest: one may be a real duplicate, or one may be a Roleplayer who believes the claim. Before hanging on a read like that, look for a second mechanical break.
An attack you survive with no explanation may be your own hidden Paranoid trait. Don't build cases on it, and don't present it as proof that a Shaky holder or a protector exists.

If your first Katana attack fails and no protector has claimed a save, assume a hidden Shaky holder and move the Katana to a teammate the next night. Two failures by the same holder almost always mean Shaky, not bad luck.

Never send a Standard Katana at a player who may be a Serial Killer, such as a Katana survivor or someone whose claimed results look suspiciously convenient. SK Standard Defense blocks it every time. Hit a confirmed, defenseless info role instead, or let the town hang the SK.

Claiming an info role and publicly promising tomorrow's target ("I'll track X tonight") makes you the obvious night kill for anyone whose story that result could break. That includes a Neutral killer running its own fake claim. Either claim later, or don't name your next target.

Frame a player who is already in a public role clash or counterclaim, on the night the Sheriff is likely to check them. An Evil read on top of a disputed claim gets a town player hanged nearly every time. It worked twice in a row this game.

Two Sheriff-claimants reading each other Evil, with a Fabricator known to exist, means a frame or a Roleplayer is likely. If one of them is Chronicler-marked, hang the marked one if you need to test the claim, rather than hanging blind.

In hand-picked setups, duplicate roles really happen (this game had two Scouts and a Sheriff/Roleplayer pair). If someone already claims your role, counterclaim calmly and offer your results for cross-checking. Don't push the other claimant as the killer: that costs you credibility and makes you the obvious target for a frame.

Distrust a single Tracker or Lookout whose results keep putting one player on the killer's victims. That is the easiest cover for a solo killer: kill next to a Sleepwalker or another frequent visitor, then 'track' them onto the body. Get a second source, or test the accused with a Basic shot, before hanging on those tracks.

Once a Fabricator is confirmed (Insomniac draw, etc.), a single Sheriff Evil read on an unconfirmed player isn't enough to hang. Fabricators frame counterclaimed or unconfirmable players on purpose. Ask for a re-check or a second result first, especially when the Sheriff's targets keep turning up 'Evil' among players who were arguing with him.

applies_to: passive info roles (Scout, Cartographer, Fortune Teller)
tip: Your results can't be confirmed, so build trust early by publishing every night's names plainly and connecting them to known visits and kills. Avoid speculative accusations. Your claim only holds up if your record stays clean and your reads stay modest, and that record is your only defense against a frame.

A private message from a likely Jester or Neutral is poison. Post its contents at once, as I did, but also say publicly that you reject their support. Opponents will still bring the PM up later as an association.

If you protected someone with Strong Defense and were told no attack was stopped, then nobody attacked them that night, whatever the attack level. Post this right away when someone claims they shot or attacked that player. It is one of the few hard breaks a protector can give, and it exposed a Jester's fake Vigilante shot.

Once Olivia's Insomniac draw showed a Fabricator exists, a lone Sheriff Evil read on a counterclaimed player is not a mechanical break. Here two Evil reads were frames: one hanged a framed Roleplayer, the other a framed real Scout. Before hanging on an Evil read alone, ask whether framing that player would help the Yakuza, and look for a second, independent source.

A Basic attack that kills proves the target had no Defense, so they can't be the Serial Killer (which has Standard Defense). The kill then clears them and makes whoever built the SK case against them the new suspect. One source repeatedly placing a player at the SK's victims is a classic SK frame.

If a suspect sends you a private deal or confession, post it word for word at once. It reads as believable, especially when your own claim is backed by your logs. They can say you made it up, but a quick and exact repost usually wins the table.

Duplicate claims of non-unique roles happen even in hand-picked setups: there were two real Scouts here. Don't treat 'hand-picked games rarely repeat roles' as evidence. Wait for results that can tell the claimants apart.

Once a Fabricator is confirmed (e.g. an Insomniac draw), treat a single Evil Sheriff read as a coin flip, especially on a counterclaimed or vocal player. The Yakuza frame exactly the players a Sheriff is likely to check next. Wait for a second, independent break before hanging on it.

A Chronicler's death reveal is an exact-role check, so a Disguised Yakuza shows up as their disguise (here a Ballot Stuffer showed as Party Animal). A Village role revealed on death doesn't prove Village. If someone's 'Not Evil' result on that player was really a Roleplayer's random result, both claims can look like they fit.

When one Tracker alone keeps putting a Sleepwalker or another player on each new kill victim, suspect the Tracker. A Neutral killer can make up tracks onto its own victims. A Tracker with no corroboration who keeps feeding the same case is a better SK lead than the target.
In hand-picked setups, duplicate roles (two Scouts, two Sheriff claims) really happen. Don't add 'two of the same role is unlikely' to a case; ask which claim has a mechanical break instead.
If the Katana fails on the same target twice, stop attacking them: they probably have innate Defense (SK) or protection. Switch to an unprotected investigator, or let town hang the survivor.

Don't use fake tracks or watches that put a living, Defense-less player on your own victims. One Basic Vigilante shot or a later night death disproves the frame, and the frame then points straight back at you as the only source. Frame dead players, or make claims that stay unconfirmable.

When a player publicly holds a cheap test that can clear your scapegoat (e.g. a Vigilante with a Basic shot, since a Basic kill proves the target had no Defense), kill that player first. That matters more than killing an investigator who can't read you as Evil anyway.

Never put a confession or deal in a private message. The recipient can quote it word for word, and every PM is publicly logged, so 'they made it up' is a weak defense. If you must PM, write only things you would be fine seeing quoted publicly.

A role that kills with a Basic attack and learns the role on a kill (Vigilante) works as a Defense test. If the shot kills, the target had no Standard Defense, so it wasn't an SK. That clears the target and shows whose claims had pointed at them falsely.

Surviving repeated Katana attacks is information the Yakuza hold. Don't publicly name the role behind a failed attack on you, and expect the Yakuza to steer town toward you if they survive. Killing the Katana holder early (as I did N2/N3) helps, because it also removes the players who know you have Defense.

If a Katana attack fails on a player who has no claimed protector, assume innate Defense (Serial Killer, Arsonist) before blaming a trait, and don't attack them again. Three of our Katana attacks went into the Serial Killer this game. Use frames and day votes to get the town to hang a suspected Defense holder, and spend the Katana on players who can actually die.

A claimed result that contradicts a fact you secretly know (for example a 'Not Evil' read on a teammate you know is Evil) doesn't prove the claimant is a lying killer. It often means a Roleplayer is reporting random results. Weigh the Roleplayer explanation before you plan around 'they must be the Serial Killer'.

Frame players who are already under suspicion: counterclaimed roles, or players in two-way clashes. In those spots an Evil read reads as confirmation, not as a possible frame. This game, frames on a counterclaimed Sheriff and a counterclaimed Scout got two Villagers hanged. Once you hold the Katana you read Good anyway, so keep your frames on others.

A fake visit-based role (Lookout or Tracker) whose 'results' back up the town's leading story makes you look like an investigator worth killing to a solo killer. If you need to survive, pick a quieter cover, or report results that don't make you central to the case.

When choosing a kill target, discount players who claim a role 'on cue' to confirm another player. A loud claimed Tracker who appears exactly when needed may be the Serial Killer hiding behind that claim. Prefer targets whose claims have been confirmed by others, such as protected investigators or confirmed Scouts.

applies_to: Village investigators (Sheriff, Tracker, Lookout, Seer, Fortune Teller, Oracle)
tip: You might be a Roleplayer and not know it. Before you build a case on your own result, check it against hard public facts. If an Insomniac drew your role among that night's visitors, but someone else claims the same role, remember a Roleplayer never visits. So that draw is evidence for the other claimant, not for you. A result that clashes with a claim backed from several sides is more likely random noise than a lie by the other player.

A Chronicler's death reveal is an exact-role check, so it shows a Disguised player's disguise. A revealed Village role on a marked body doesn't prove the player was Village. Weigh it like a Coroner result, not as proof of alignment.

When you give a vague night line to hide your role, never use wording that suggests a result type your claimed role can't get. For example, a Sheriff saying a result 'matched' a revealed role sounds like an exact-role check. Opponents will quote it back as a broken claim. Say 'nothing suspicious' or name the role outright.

applies_to: anyone in a mirrored counterclaim (two claimants reading each other Evil)
tip: Being the late claimant with the weaker backing almost always loses the mirror. Pushing for 'hang them, they're marked' after the table has lined up looks self-serving. Claim early, bring a test that doesn't depend on your own word, and if you lose the mirror, leave a will that helps the town whichever of you was real.
