A Night 1 guess with no claims to work from is close to wasted, especially on a common role like Sheriff. Guess Yakuza-only roles (Fabricator, Mortician, Pharmacist) on whoever spoke first or set the agenda, because a hit there is a real lead. Also keep your will current, because a Mortician clean or an early death hides any result that's still pending.

When a stated Guilty vote is counted as Innocent, check for Merciful (and Zealot) before blaming a Fixer. Those traits can belong to any player, including a Neutral, and the holder may keep quiet about it. In this game Olivia (the Arsonist) was Merciful, which explains every 'missing Guilty' gap, and the town lost days hunting a Fixer that didn't exist.

Use the structure of Profiler results. Of the two decoys, one is a role held by another living player and the other is a role no player has. Once the true role is known, the decoy that is in play proves the other decoy is absent, and that can break a claim. Heidi used this to prove that Frank's Eavesdropper claim was false.

Count vote locks early, including Turncoats. A claimed Medic who protects the same suspect every night and votes Innocent on them may be a Turncoat even if they really are Medic. Hidden Innocents (Merciful, Turncoat, Neutral) can lock the vote long before the Yakuza alone hold half. Once you're near the lock, hang the strongest mechanical lead immediately, while you still have the votes.

If the town publicly asks you to Enforce a suspect, the Katana holder just skips attacking that night (Frank did on N3). Pair the suspect with a different likely killer instead, such as an unclaimed or unverifiable player who might be a Neutral killer, rather than the person everyone named. Also remember that with two targets only one gets hit, and a Strong hit can still fail to Narrow Escape.

A claimed Medic who guards a census-flagged suspect night after night and keeps voting to save them may be a Turncoat. A Census Taker counts a Turncoat as Good, so the census never catches one. Hang or kill them anyway: their Innocent vote is what creates the vote lock.

Before you blame a missing Guilty on a Fixer, consider hidden Merciful or Zealot traits and plain lying. In this game the Day 2 gap was a Merciful Yakuza, and every later gap was a liar. There was no Fixer at all. Blaming a Fixer let the real Innocent voters hide.

Each Profiler list has one true role, one role that is in play and one that isn't. Cross-reference all the lists as soon as they're public. Once one list is confirmed, it can prove another claim is impossible (Arsonist in play meant no Eavesdropper). Heidi only worked this out on Day 6, after it was too late to use.

Count the vote lock using declared Merciful voters plus every player who keeps voting Innocent. Once a hang becomes impossible, put every night kill on the Innocent bloc. A Mayor with Merciful should never reveal, because the doubled vote would count as Innocent.

Before you post a cover claim, read what has already been claimed that Day. Don't take a role someone has just claimed (I claimed Medic right after Mallory did), and don't take a visit role that a real investigator may hold (Ivan's Lookout ran into Judy's). A double claim gets you checked or Enforced, and the real holder usually has a visit result that breaks you.

Once an Enforcer or a Lookout has claimed, give the Katana to the teammate whose claim draws the least suspicion, and be ready to skip the attack on a night when the holder is likely to be Enforced. A holder with a contested claim makes an attack, so a 2-target Enforce has a good chance of killing them. Frank survived N3 by not attacking.

applies_to: Yakuza (any fake protector or visitor claim)
tip: Your last will's claimed visit has to survive a Lookout or Tracker on your real target. Claiming I protected Grace while I really hit Bob was exposed by Judy's watch on Bob. Either claim a visit to the player you really visited, or claim a role that visits no one.

Count the guaranteed Innocent votes every Day: the accused's own, any Merciful player's, a Turncoat's or teammate's. Once those reach half of the living players, no trial can pass, and the game is settled at night. Neither side should waste nominations then. Plan the night kills around the lock, and keep the players whose votes hold it alive.

A Profiler's three-role list carries a deduction: besides the true role, one of the other two is in play and one isn't. Once one role on a list is shown to be in play by another source (here, an Arsonist kill), the remaining false role is known to be out of play, and that can break a claim. Heidi used this to show Frank's Eavesdropper claim was false.

A forged will is strongest when it fits the victim's own public claim and only adds doubt, such as 'don't hang X on my N1 result alone'. Never put results from that night in it, because wills are written before results arrive. Other players quoted my doubt-only forge for days and never questioned it.

Against a Profiler, a cover whose results can be checked (Tracker, Lookout) breaks within a day. If your profile list may include a tokenless information role with no visible output (Eavesdropper), that is the fallback that survives. A switch that lands on a role named in the profile list keeps you alive, while a switch to a role that isn't on the list gets you hanged.

Count the trial-vote lock, not just the nomination lock. A Village player with Merciful counts as a permanent Innocent, so you, any ally and the Merciful voter can block every hang. Keep that Merciful player alive while the lock is useful, and kill them only when your faction can then hang 2-of-3.

A 'Village' player who protects you night after night and votes Innocent on you is probably a Turncoat. Answer their PM and coordinate fully: they can lie in public, guard you, and give you the second vote in a 3-player endgame. Tell them their Remorseful trait can't hurt them on a Yakuza win.

A Standard Katana can't kill a Neutral with innate Standard Defense (Arsonist, SK, Werewolf). Don't waste kills on them. Kill the townsfolk around them and plan to hang the Neutral in the final 3. Get Strong protection from an ally against the ignite.

A Profiler result has a hidden constraint: of the two false roles, one belongs to another living player and one is held by nobody. So once one of the listed roles is proven in play (here, an Arsonist kill), any claim of the other false role is a lie. Check every profile list against every death and confirmed role, not only against the target's own claim.

Not every vote gap is a Fixer. A gap that repeats on every trial with the same size fits a hidden Merciful or Zealot voter who doesn't announce it, and the moderator may have hand-picked several such traits. Before blaming a Fixer and splitting the town, check whether one silent Merciful voter explains every total. Don't treat a supposed fix as proof that any one claimant is Yakuza.

Count the lock with fixed Innocents included: announced Merciful players, the accused, and anyone who keeps protecting or defending the main suspect. Once those reach half the votes, nothing can be hanged. So hang the first suspect with two independent mechanical breaks (census plus profile) on the spot. 'One more night of checks' is how the Yakuza survive to the lock.

A Village-role claimant who protects the top Yakuza suspect night after night, votes to save them, and backfills traits like Remorseful to fix their own math is probably a Turncoat. A Turncoat reads Good in a census and their exact-role check comes back clean, so only an alignment check (which shows them Evil) or their own behavior exposes them. Treat them as a Yakuza vote when counting the lock.

applies_to: Insomniac and other end-of-night info roles
tip: Your result arrives after your will is written, so dying that night loses it. Spend your first token on Night 1, and post the result right away (I did, and it helped hang a Fabricator). After you claim, expect to be killed, so use your will to name exactly what each possible result would mean.

A Merciful voter is a fixed Innocent on every trial. Once you announce it, every side can work out the vote lock: with N alive, the accused plus you plus one ally can block every hang. Before revealing a forced-vote trait, count how few hidden allies the defense would need. Expect the Yakuza to keep you alive until a 2-of-3 endgame and then kill you.

A Profiler list has a fixed structure: the true role, one decoy drawn from the other living players' roles, and one decoy no player has. Once the true role is confirmed, any death or claim that proves one decoy is in play proves the other is NOT. Cross-reference every profile list this way to break claims (for example, a false Eavesdropper claim).

When trial totals come up short of stated Guilty votes, don't jump to 'Fixer'. First count every player who could be lying: Neutrals such as an Arsonist, a Hitman or a Jester also hide Innocent votes, and so does a Turncoat. Settle on a Fixer only when no combination of liars fits. Several unrelated liars explained every gap in this game.

A claimed Village protector who guards a strongly suspected Yakuza night after night and votes to save them may be a Turncoat: a true Village role that census counts as Good. In vote-lock math, count them as a Yakuza vote even if a census or exact check clears their role.

If your trial vote is forced (Merciful/Zealot), don't reveal as Mayor, since it only doubles the forced vote. Your value is then mostly as a mechanical deducer and a nominator. Write your will early with the proofs, because you will likely be the Katana target once the lock math turns against the Yakuza.

Don't frame on Night 1 unless someone has hinted at being a Sheriff or Seer. With no alignment checker in the game a frame does nothing, but the visit still shows up for Lookouts, Trackers and Insomniacs. An Insomniac hearing 'Fabricator' and a Profiler list both nailed me. Staying home leaves no trail.

Pick a cover that a Profiler list or a visit result can't break on its own, and decide ahead of time what you'll say if a profile names your real role. If you fall back to the Good role on the list after you've been caught, it reads as a switch and gets you hanged. That's worse still when someone else already claims that role, as Bob did with Census Taker.

Stay quiet and unremarkable on Day 1. Don't speak first or set the agenda. I opened Day 1 and then got six visits/checks on Night 1 (Oracle, Census Taker, Enforcer, Profiler, Lookout, Arsonist). Players with nothing to go on seem to pick whoever stood out.

At small player counts, count the Innocent votes you can rely on: the accused, players who openly count Innocent (like a Merciful claimant) and suspected allies. Once those make half the votes, no trial can pass. Then you can stop defending yourself and let the night kills win the game, which is how Frank survived five trials.

When a Profiler's list for one player turns out right, apply its rule (one of the other two roles is in play, one isn't) to every list that player produced. Heidi showed this way that Eavesdropper wasn't in play, which broke Frank's claim. Do this deduction early, not in the endgame.

When trial totals come up short of the stated Guilty votes, don't jump to a Fixer. Neutral killers (Hitman, Arsonist) gain from failed trials and lie about their votes too. Count the plausible Neutrals among the stated Guilty voters before you build a Fixer theory. A Fixer theory you can't check can lead you to hang or block the wrong person.

Combine Profiler lists as soon as they come out. On each list, one of the two decoy roles is in play and the other isn't. When a role is confirmed in play (by a death cause, a win reveal or another list), you can rule out its partner decoy across all the lists. This broke a false Eavesdropper claim, but only on Day 6, when it was too late.

When a claimed tracking result contradicts a visit that two other results confirm (here, an Insomniac heard a Fabricator and a Profiler found the Fabricator), the tracker is the one breaking, even if a Lookout saw them visit. Seeing someone visit proves the visit, not the role. A Neutral killer can claim Tracker to cover a douse.

If a claimed Medic guards a known Yakuza every night and votes to save them, consider a Turncoat (a Village role whose holder wins with the Yakuza) as well as a hidden Yakuza. An exact-role check will show Medic, and a census counts them as Good. Only votes and behaviour expose them, so stop counting their vote as town.

Once the Yakuza plus their sympathizers can lock votes, stop spending nominations on test trials. Spend the Day agreeing on who uses night abilities on whom and on keeping the swing voters alive, because the endgame is decided at night and in the final 3-player vote.

Work out who the Yakuza are from public mechanical results (a census, a profile, claim switches), then tell one of them in a short PM that you are a Turncoat and offer concrete help. They aren't told about you, but an offer of votes and protection that you can back up gets trusted quickly and turns you into a hidden extra Yakuza.

applies_to: Turncoat with Remorseful (or Selfless/any death-penalty trait)
tip: A Turncoat wins with the Yakuza whether alive or dead, so Remorseful does not limit your Guilty votes. If you vote Guilty on a Villager and die of remorse, that still fits your win. Opponents may threaten you with remorse; ignore it.

Do the vote-lock math with always-Innocent voters included (Merciful, the accused's own vote). At 5 or 6 alive, one Merciful player plus two allied voters means no trial can pass. Keep that Merciful player alive while the lock helps you, then kill them right before the final 3 so a 2-of-3 hang becomes possible.

applies_to: Medic (or any protector) on an evil-aligned win
tip: Once an Arsonist has doused someone you need alive, put Strong protection on that player for the nights an ignite could come. Standard protection does not stop a Strong ignite. On Night 5, Strong protection saved the Katana holder.

In a vote-locked endgame, push suspicion at a Neutral killer whose claimed results contradict someone else's, like Olivia's 'Ivan visited no one'. Then the Neutral, not you, becomes the swing person to hang once the count reaches 3.

Use the fake slots to narrow a profile. One fake comes from the roles of other players alive at the start of that night. The other comes from roles nobody in the game has. So a role known to be in the game (heard by an Insomniac, say) whose only holder is already dead can't be either fake. Also, when two of your lists share the same two candidate roles, finding where one of them is in play rules out the other. Run this check the morning each result arrives. It would have proved Frank was the Fabricator on Day 3, not Day 6.

When trial totals come up short of what people said, assume first that people lied about their votes, not that a hidden Fixer flipped them. Neutrals, Hitmen and Turncoats all lie about their ballots. In this game there was no Fixer at all, and the Fixer theory let the real liars (Olivia the Arsonist, Alice the Hitman) shift blame and kept the town arguing in circles.

A Village claimant who keeps protecting a proven Yakuza and votes to save them may be a Turncoat. A Turncoat really holds a Village role, reads Good to a census and can't be ruled out by an exact-role check. Count them as a Yakuza vote for the vote lock, even if their role claim is real.

A 'Tracker' whose results only repeat visits that are already public, or that clash with a role known to visit, is probably a Neutral killer using the visit as cover. Their visits really happen, so a Lookout's confirmation doesn't clear them. Ask for a result that only a real Tracker could have known.

Once you know trial votes that always count Innocent (Merciful traits, the accused, a teammate) reach half, stop spending nominations on 'test' trials. They show little and tell night killers who the swing voters are. Spend the remaining Days making sure the right players survive the night instead.

Dousing a non-Good player tells them an Arsonist doused them. Once you douse a Yakuza, expect them to protect themselves (Strong Medic, Diviner) and hunt you. Douse Good players first, and ignite on the night you douse the Yakuza or the night right after, before they can arrange protection.

Count your live douses every night. Doused players who die to other causes (hangings, Katana) are wasted douses. Ignite as soon as 2 or more live threats are doused, and don't hold off for a bigger burn. Waiting until the endgame left me with too few kills and let a 2-player vote bloc form against me.

applies_to: Neutral killers with a fake investigator cover
tip: Make up results that can't be contradicted. 'X visited no one' gets broken by any visit-based result (Insomniac, Lookout, a role whose job is to visit). Name a visit target someone else has already confirmed, or report a harmless result that fits the claimed role of the person you supposedly checked.

A hidden Merciful or Zealot trait makes a gap in every trial total, and opponents will pin those gaps on you. Either claim the trait early, as Heidi did (she was trusted), or have a ready explanation like a Fixer flip. Remember that your own trial can never get your vote as Guilty, and at 3 players the other two decide alone.

Watch for a 2-player bloc that votes and protects together (a Yakuza plus a Turncoat or Medic). Kill the protector part of that bloc before the game gets down to 3 players. Otherwise they hang you 2-1, however good your arguments are.

When a trial total falls short of stated Guilty votes, list every cause before blaming a Fixer: someone lying about their vote, an undisclosed Merciful or Zealot, a Turncoat, or a Neutral who wants the game to drag on. A 'my reminder shows Guilty' claim proves nothing, because Merciful and Zealot reminders show how the vote counted. Don't spend nominations on 'tests' whose reading depends on everyone being honest.
evidence: Frank's Day 3 trial came out 3-5. The town explained the gap as a Fixer, but no Fixer was in the game. The missing votes were Alice (Hitman, lied after Frank's PM) and Olivia (hidden Merciful, said Guilty). Niaj's Day 4 and Day 5 'tests' then gave totals that Frank and Mallory turned against Olivia and Niaj.

tip: Count the vote lock using effective votes, not living players. Every Merciful voter, defender and suspected Turncoat is a fixed Innocent. If the lock is close, push the strongest mechanical case (census plus a broken claim) on the earliest Day you can, and press uncommitted players publicly before the vote. Don't let the trial go out on 'one more night of checks'.
evidence: On Day 3 Frank had a census hit, a broken Tracker claim and a switch to another claim, yet one PM to Alice plus Mallory's 'give him a night' cost the hang. From Day 4 on, Heidi's Merciful vote plus Frank and Mallory made every trial impossible, as Judy noted too late.

tip: Before igniting, check who the douses will kill and what the next day's vote count looks like. Douse the Yakuza and their protector, not the Village voters who are holding the vote lock against them. A solo killer needs the Village alive long enough to grind the Yakuza down.
evidence: Olivia's Night 5 ignite failed on Frank, who had Mallory's Strong protection, and killed Niaj, the most active anti-Frank voter. That left Frank, Mallory, Heidi and Olivia. Frank killed Heidi on Night 6, and Frank and Mallory hanged Olivia 2-1 on Day 7.

tip: If a trait makes your trial votes count one fixed way (Merciful or Zealot), say so publicly as Heidi did. Hiding it and claiming the opposite vote leaves a gap in every total that people will eventually pin on you.
evidence: Olivia (Merciful) said 'Guilty' on every Frank trial. Mallory and Frank used the missing Guilty in each total ('her third hidden Innocent') to make her the scapegoat, and that framed the final 2-1 hang.

tip: As a Turncoat, tell the Yakuza privately who you are (they aren't told). Then act as a reliable Innocent vote and protector for the Katana holder. Save Strong protection for the night a Neutral killer goes after them, and promise protection to others in public as cover.
evidence: Mallory's Day 4 PM to Frank created a vote lock. She protected Frank every night and put Strong on him on Night 5, which stopped Olivia's ignite. She promised Heidi protection in public but protected Frank, and Heidi died on Night 6.

tip: When an Enforcer is likely to visit your holder (or a suspect publicly asks to be Enforced), skip the Katana attack that night. Also, an Enforcer can visit two suspected holders at once, so don't let two exposed members both act on one night.
evidence: On Night 2 Dave's two-target Enforce on Frank and Erin killed Erin, the holder. On Night 3 Frank skipped the Katana while Dave Enforced Frank and Alice, so the Strong attack went to Alice (saved by Narrow Escape) and Frank survived.

tip: Use the structure of a Profiler result. Of the two fake roles, one is in play and one isn't. Once the true role and one other role on a list are confirmed in play, the third role is not in play. Any later claim of that role is false. Run this check as soon as roles are confirmed.
evidence: Alice's list was Arsonist/Eavesdropper/Hitman. She left as the Hitman, and Niaj was killed by an Arsonist, so Eavesdropper wasn't in play and Frank's Eavesdropper claim was false. Heidi only worked this out on Day 6, after the vote lock.

tip: Choose a cover that a common investigator is unlikely to contradict, and keep made-up results bland. Once a cover breaks, a second claim is rarely believed. If a teammate is exposed, cast doubt with a forged will rather than by defending them openly.
evidence: Ivan's Lookout cover collided with the real Lookout (Judy) and Niaj's profile, and his switch to Census Taker got him hanged. Frank's forged Bob will ('don't hang Frank on my N1 alone') gave Mallory a reason others could accept for her Day 3 Innocent.
